#### `~/.config/opencode/plugins/message-queue-eagerness.ts.disabled`

```ts file=~/.config/opencode/plugins/message-queue-eagerness.ts.disabled
import type { TuiPlugin } from "@opencode-ai/plugin/tui"

type DeliveryMode = "queue" | "eager" | "now"
type QueuedItem = {
  id: string
  sessionID: string
  text: string
  mode: DeliveryMode
  parts?: unknown[]
  agent?: string
  model?: unknown
  variant?: string
  createdAt: number
}

type PromptArgs = {
  sessionID: string
  parts?: Array<{ type: string; text?: string; synthetic?: boolean; [key: string]: unknown }>
  agent?: string
  model?: unknown
  variant?: string
  messageID?: string
  noReply?: boolean
  [key: string]: unknown
}

const KV_DEFAULT_MODE = "queue.eagerness.defaultMode"

function textFromParts(parts: PromptArgs["parts"]): string {
  if (!parts?.length) return ""
  return parts
    .filter((p) => p.type === "text" && typeof p.text === "string" && !p.synthetic)
    .map((p) => p.text as string)
    .join("")
}

function isBusyStatus(status: unknown): boolean {
  if (!status) return false
  if (typeof status === "string") return status === "busy" || status === "running" || status === "retry"
  if (typeof status === "object" && status !== null && "type" in status) {
    const t = (status as { type: string }).type
    return t === "busy" || t === "running" || t === "retry"
  }
  return false
}

function uid(): string {
  return `q_${Date.now().toString(36)}_${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 8)}`
}

function preview(text: string, n = 48): string {
  const one = text.replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim()
  if (one.length <= n) return one
  return `${one.slice(0, n - 1)}…`
}

export const tui: TuiPlugin = async (api) => {
  const queues = new Map<string, QueuedItem[]>()
  const sending = new Set<string>()
  /** Bypass intercept while plugin drains its own queue */
  let passthrough = 0
  let defaultMode: DeliveryMode = api.kv.get(KV_DEFAULT_MODE, "queue") as DeliveryMode
  if (defaultMode !== "queue" && defaultMode !== "eager") defaultMode = "queue"

  const refreshKey = "queue.eagerness.tick"
  const bump = () => api.kv.set(refreshKey, Date.now())

  const getQueue = (sessionID: string) => queues.get(sessionID) ?? []
  const setQueue = (sessionID: string, items: QueuedItem[]) => {
    if (items.length === 0) queues.delete(sessionID)
    else queues.set(sessionID, items)
    bump()
  }

  const sessionID = (): string | undefined => {
    const cur = api.route.current
    if (cur.name === "session" && typeof cur.params?.sessionID === "string") return cur.params.sessionID
    return undefined
  }

  const busy = (id: string) => isBusyStatus(api.state.session.status(id))

  const toast = (message: string, variant: "info" | "success" | "warning" | "error" = "info") => {
    api.ui.toast({ message, variant, duration: 2500 })
  }

  // Capture originals before any wrap (used by drain + intercept)
  const sessionClient = api.client.session as unknown as {
    prompt: (args: PromptArgs, opts?: { throwOnError?: boolean }) => Promise<unknown>
    promptAsync?: (args: PromptArgs, opts?: { throwOnError?: boolean }) => Promise<unknown>
  }
  const originalPrompt = sessionClient.prompt.bind(sessionClient)
  const originalPromptAsync = sessionClient.promptAsync?.bind(sessionClient)

  const sendViaV2 = async (item: QueuedItem, delivery: "queue" | "steer") => {
    const client = api.client as {
      v2?: {
        session: {
          prompt: (p: {
            sessionID: string
            prompt: { text: string }
            delivery?: "queue" | "steer"
          }) => Promise<{ error?: unknown }>
          interrupt: (p: { sessionID: string }) => Promise<unknown>
        }
      }
      session: {
        prompt: (p: PromptArgs, o?: { throwOnError?: boolean }) => Promise<unknown>
        abort?: (p: { sessionID: string }) => Promise<unknown>
      }
    }

    passthrough++
    try {
      if (client.v2?.session?.prompt) {
        const res = await client.v2.session.prompt({
          sessionID: item.sessionID,
          prompt: { text: item.text },
          delivery,
        })
        if (res?.error) throw res.error
        return
      }

      await originalPrompt(
        {
          sessionID: item.sessionID,
          agent: item.agent,
          model: item.model as PromptArgs["model"],
          variant: item.variant,
          parts: item.parts?.length
            ? (item.parts as PromptArgs["parts"])
            : [{ type: "text", text: item.text }],
        },
        { throwOnError: true },
      )
    } finally {
      passthrough--
    }
  }

  const interrupt = async (id: string) => {
    const client = api.client as {
      v2?: { session: { interrupt: (p: { sessionID: string }) => Promise<unknown> } }
      session: { abort?: (p: { sessionID: string }) => Promise<unknown> }
    }
    if (client.v2?.session?.interrupt) {
      await client.v2.session.interrupt({ sessionID: id })
      return
    }
    await client.session.abort?.({ sessionID: id })
  }

  const remove = (sessionID: string, itemID: string) => {
    setQueue(
      sessionID,
      getQueue(sessionID).filter((q) => q.id !== itemID),
    )
  }

  const enqueue = (item: Omit<QueuedItem, "id" | "createdAt" | "mode"> & { mode?: DeliveryMode }) => {
    const full: QueuedItem = {
      id: uid(),
      createdAt: Date.now(),
      mode: item.mode ?? defaultMode,
      sessionID: item.sessionID,
      text: item.text,
      parts: item.parts,
      agent: item.agent,
      model: item.model,
      variant: item.variant,
    }
    setQueue(full.sessionID, [...getQueue(full.sessionID), full])
    toast(`Queued (${full.mode}): ${preview(full.text)}`)
    return full
  }

  const deliver = async (item: QueuedItem) => {
    if (sending.has(item.id)) return
    sending.add(item.id)
    try {
      if (item.mode === "now") {
        if (busy(item.sessionID)) await interrupt(item.sessionID)
        await sendViaV2(item, "steer")
      } else if (item.mode === "eager") {
        await sendViaV2(item, "steer")
      } else {
        await sendViaV2(item, "queue")
      }
      remove(item.sessionID, item.id)
    } catch (err) {
      toast(`Queue send failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}`, "error")
    } finally {
      sending.delete(item.id)
    }
  }

  const drainIdle = async (id: string) => {
    if (busy(id)) return
    const next = getQueue(id).find((q) => q.mode === "queue" || q.mode === "now")
    if (!next) return
    if (next.mode === "now") await deliver(next)
    else await deliver(next)
  }

  const drainEager = async (id: string) => {
    const next = getQueue(id).find((q) => q.mode === "eager")
    if (!next) return
    await deliver(next)
  }

  const editItem = (item: QueuedItem) => {
    remove(item.sessionID, item.id)
    void api.client.tui.appendPrompt({ text: item.text }).catch(() => {
      toast("Removed from queue — paste to re-edit", "warning")
    })
    toast("Loaded into prompt for edit")
  }

  const setMode = (item: QueuedItem, mode: DeliveryMode) => {
    setQueue(
      item.sessionID,
      getQueue(item.sessionID).map((q) => (q.id === item.id ? { ...q, mode } : q)),
    )
    if (mode === "now") void deliver({ ...item, mode })
    else if (mode === "eager" && !busy(item.sessionID)) void deliver({ ...item, mode })
    else toast(`Mode → ${mode}: ${preview(item.text)}`)
  }

  const openDock = (id?: string) => {
    const sid = id ?? sessionID()
    if (!sid) {
      toast("No active session", "warning")
      return
    }
    const items = getQueue(sid)
    if (items.length === 0) {
      toast("Queue empty")
      return
    }

    type Action = { item: QueuedItem; action: "edit" | "eager" | "now" | "queue" | "remove" }

    api.ui.dialog.replace(() =>
      api.ui.DialogSelect<Action>({
        title: `Queued (${items.length}) · default=${defaultMode}`,
        flat: true,
        options: items.flatMap((item) => {
          const head = `[${item.mode}] ${preview(item.text, 40)}`
          return [
            {
              title: `${head}`,
              value: { item, action: "edit" as const },
              description: "edit — load back into prompt",
              category: preview(item.text, 24),
            },
            {
              title: "  [edit]",
              value: { item, action: "edit" as const },
              description: "Edit queued message",
              category: preview(item.text, 24),
            },
            {
              title: "  [eager]",
              value: { item, action: "eager" as const },
              description: "Send at next agent lull (steer)",
              category: preview(item.text, 24),
            },
            {
              title: "  [send now]",
              value: { item, action: "now" as const },
              description: "Interrupt and send immediately",
              category: preview(item.text, 24),
            },
            {
              title: "  [wait]",
              value: { item, action: "queue" as const },
              description: "Wait until previous turn fully done",
              category: preview(item.text, 24),
            },
            {
              title: "  [remove]",
              value: { item, action: "remove" as const },
              description: "Drop from queue",
              category: preview(item.text, 24),
            },
          ]
        }),
        onSelect: (opt) => {
          const { item, action } = opt.value
          if (action === "edit") editItem(item)
          else if (action === "remove") remove(item.sessionID, item.id)
          else setMode(item, action === "now" ? "now" : action === "eager" ? "eager" : "queue")
          api.ui.dialog.clear()
        },
      }),
    )
  }

  // Intercept built-in session.prompt while busy → hold in plugin queue (default: wait until done)
  const intercept = async (
    args: PromptArgs,
    opts: { throwOnError?: boolean } | undefined,
    pass: typeof originalPrompt,
  ) => {
    if (passthrough > 0) return pass(args, opts)

    const id = args.sessionID
    const maybeText = (args as unknown as { text?: string }).text
    const text = textFromParts(args.parts) || (typeof maybeText === "string" ? maybeText : "")
    const syntheticOnly =
      !!args.parts?.length &&
      args.parts.every((p) => p.type !== "text" || p.synthetic === true || !String(p.text ?? "").trim())

    if (!id || !text.trim() || syntheticOnly || args.noReply) {
      return pass(args, opts)
    }

    if (!busy(id) && getQueue(id).length === 0) {
      return pass(args, opts)
    }

    if (!busy(id) && getQueue(id).length > 0) {
      enqueue({
        sessionID: id,
        text,
        parts: args.parts,
        agent: args.agent,
        model: args.model,
        variant: args.variant,
        mode: defaultMode,
      })
      void drainIdle(id)
      return { info: { id: "queued", role: "user" }, parts: [] }
    }

    enqueue({
      sessionID: id,
      text,
      parts: args.parts,
      agent: args.agent,
      model: args.model,
      variant: args.variant,
      mode: defaultMode,
    })
    return { info: { id: "queued", role: "user" }, parts: [] }
  }

  sessionClient.prompt = ((args: PromptArgs, opts?: { throwOnError?: boolean }) =>
    intercept(args, opts, originalPrompt)) as typeof sessionClient.prompt

  if (originalPromptAsync) {
    sessionClient.promptAsync = ((args: PromptArgs, opts?: { throwOnError?: boolean }) =>
      intercept(args, opts, originalPromptAsync)) as typeof sessionClient.promptAsync
  }

  api.lifecycle.onDispose(() => {
    sessionClient.prompt = originalPrompt
    if (originalPromptAsync && sessionClient.promptAsync) sessionClient.promptAsync = originalPromptAsync
  })

  api.event.on("session.status", (e) => {
    const id = e.properties.sessionID
    if (!id) return
    if (!isBusyStatus(e.properties.status)) void drainIdle(id)
  })

  api.event.on("session.idle", (e) => {
    const id = e.properties.sessionID
    if (id) void drainIdle(id)
  })

  // Eager = next agent lull (after tool / step boundary)
  const onLull = (id: string | undefined) => {
    if (id && getQueue(id).some((q) => q.mode === "eager")) void drainEager(id)
  }
  for (const type of ["session.next.tool.success", "session.next.tool.failed", "session.next.step.ended"] as const) {
    api.event.on(type as "session.idle", (e) => {
      onLull((e.properties as { sessionID?: string }).sessionID)
    })
  }

  api.command?.register(() => {
    const sid = sessionID()
    const qlen = sid ? getQueue(sid).length : 0
    return [
      {
        title: "Queue: manage [edit|eager|send now]",
        value: "queue.manage",
        description: qlen ? `${qlen} queued` : "Open queued message actions",
        category: "Queue",
        keybind: "<leader>shift+q",
        suggested: true,
        onSelect: () => openDock(),
      },
      {
        title: `Queue default: ${defaultMode === "queue" ? "wait until done" : defaultMode}`,
        value: "queue.default.cycle",
        description: "Cycle default for new queued messages: wait → eager → wait",
        category: "Queue",
        onSelect: () => {
          defaultMode = defaultMode === "queue" ? "eager" : "queue"
          api.kv.set(KV_DEFAULT_MODE, defaultMode)
          toast(`Default queue mode: ${defaultMode === "queue" ? "wait until done" : "eager (next lull)"}`)
        },
      },
      {
        title: "Queue: send next now (interrupt)",
        value: "queue.send_now",
        description: "Interrupt agent and send head of queue",
        category: "Queue",
        onSelect: () => {
          const id = sessionID()
          if (!id) return
          const head = getQueue(id)[0]
          if (!head) {
            toast("Queue empty", "warning")
            return
          }
          void deliver({ ...head, mode: "now" })
        },
      },
      {
        title: "Queue: mark head eager",
        value: "queue.head.eager",
        description: "Send head at next tool lull",
        category: "Queue",
        onSelect: () => {
          const id = sessionID()
          if (!id) return
          const head = getQueue(id)[0]
          if (!head) {
            toast("Queue empty", "warning")
            return
          }
          setMode(head, "eager")
        },
      },
    ]
  })

  api.slots.register({
    order: 200,
    slots: {
      session_prompt_right() {
        // Force dependency on kv tick so label refreshes
        api.kv.get(refreshKey, 0)
        const sid = sessionID()
        const n = sid ? getQueue(sid).length : 0
        const label = n === 0 ? `q:${defaultMode[0]}` : `q:${n}[${defaultMode[0]}]`
        return label
      },
    },
  })

  toast(`Queue plugin on · default=wait-until-done · <leader>q manage`, "success")
}
```

### Symlinks

`dotfiles extract` creates these after writing files. Skills and commands are not listed here: `ai-sync` links
those one entry at a time, because `~/.claude/skills` and `~/.agents/skills` must stay real folders (Claude Code
downloads your claude.ai skills into `~/.claude/skills/synced`).

```text links
# Claude Code
~/.claude/agents -> ~/.ai/agents
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md -> ~/.ai/AGENTS.md

# Grok
~/.grok/agents -> ~/.ai/agents
~/.grok/workflows -> ~/.ai/workflows

# OpenCode
~/.config/opencode/agents -> ~/.ai/agents
~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md -> ~/.ai/AGENTS.md
~/.config/opencode/workflows-from-grok -> ~/.ai/workflows

# Pi and DeepSeek Harness
~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md -> ~/.ai/AGENTS.md
~/.dsh/AGENTS.md -> ~/.ai/AGENTS.md

# Installed by terminal-browser (dangles until that app is installed; ai-sync skips it until then)
~/.ai/skills/terminal-browser -> ~/.local/share/terminal-browser/app/skills/default/terminal-browser
```

### ai-sync

`ai-sync` checks every entry in `~/.ai/skills` and `~/.ai/commands` (name matches its folder, a description
under 1024 characters, valid YAML, and `disable-model-invocation: true` on commands only), then links each one
into `~/.claude/skills` and `~/.agents/skills` and writes its OpenCode command file. Run it after adding,
removing, or moving an entry; `ai-sync --check` only reports.

#### `~/.local/bin/ai-sync`

```python file=~/.local/bin/ai-sync mode=755
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""ai-sync: link ~/.ai/skills and ~/.ai/commands into every agent harness.

  ~/.ai/skills/<name>/SKILL.md     the agent may load it on its own, and you can also run it by name
  ~/.ai/commands/<name>/SKILL.md   only you run it; its frontmatter sets `disable-model-invocation: true`

Both use the Agent Skills format (https://agentskills.io): a folder holding SKILL.md, whose frontmatter has
`name` (the folder name) and `description`. Harnesses call both kinds "skills", so every entry gets one
symlink in each folder in SKILL_DIRS.

OpenCode's / menu lists only command files, not skills. So for every entry that does not set
`user-invocable: false`, ai-sync also writes a small command file in ~/.config/opencode/commands that tells
the agent to load the skill. Loading it as a skill (rather than pasting SKILL.md in as the prompt) tells the
agent which folder the skill lives in, so paths like `references/x.md` inside it still resolve.

ai-sync owns every symlink in those folders that points into ~/.ai, and every command file whose frontmatter
has a `source:` in ~/.ai. It creates, updates, and deletes those, and never touches anything else there,
such as Claude Code's synced/ folder. An entry that is a broken link (a pack such as terminal-browser that is
not installed yet) is skipped and reported; any other invalid entry stops the sync before anything changes.

Usage:
  ai-sync           check every entry, then update the links and command files
  ai-sync --check   only report; exit 1 if an entry is invalid or anything is missing or stale
"""
import argparse
import os
import re
import sys

try:
    import yaml
except ImportError:
    sys.exit('ai-sync: needs PyYAML to check frontmatter: python3 -m pip install --user pyyaml')

HOME = os.path.expanduser('~')
AI = os.path.join(HOME, '.ai')
KINDS = ('skills', 'commands')
SKILL_DIRS = (
    '~/.claude/skills',  # Claude Code reads only this one; OpenCode, Grok, and Cursor read it too
    '~/.agents/skills',  # shared Agent Skills folder: Pi, DeepSeek Harness, OpenCode, Grok, Codex, Gemini CLI
)
OPENCODE_COMMANDS = '~/.config/opencode/commands'
HARNESS_OWNED = {'synced'}  # Claude Code keeps skills synced from claude.ai in ~/.claude/skills/synced
NAME = re.compile(r'^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$')
FRONTMATTER = re.compile(r'---\n(.*?)\n---[ \t]*(?:\n|$)', re.S)
STUB_SOURCE = re.compile(r'^source: ~/\.ai/', re.M)
MAX_DESCRIPTION = 1024  # Agent Skills limit; Pi and Codex enforce it


class Entry:
    def __init__(self, kind, name):
        self.kind, self.name = kind, name
        self.path = os.path.join(AI, kind, name)
        self.description = ''
        self.user_invocable = True


def tilde(path):
    return '~' + path[len(HOME):] if path.startswith(HOME + '/') else path


def check(e):
    """Problems that would make a harness skip or misread the entry. Also reads description and user-invocable."""
    where = f'~/.ai/{e.kind}/{e.name}'
    if not os.path.isdir(e.path):
        return [f'{where}: must be a folder holding SKILL.md, not a file']
    if not NAME.match(e.name) or len(e.name) > 64:
        return [f'{where}: folder name must be lowercase words joined by single hyphens, at most 64 characters']
    skill = os.path.join(e.path, 'SKILL.md')
    if not os.path.isfile(skill):
        return [f'{where}: has no SKILL.md']
    with open(skill, encoding='utf-8') as f:
        m = FRONTMATTER.match(f.read())
    if not m:
        return [f'{where}/SKILL.md: must start with a --- frontmatter block']
    try:
        meta = yaml.safe_load(m.group(1))
    except yaml.YAMLError as err:
        return [f'{where}/SKILL.md: frontmatter is not valid YAML, and DeepSeek Harness drops such skills '
                f'silently ({" ".join(str(err).split())})']
    if not isinstance(meta, dict):
        return [f'{where}/SKILL.md: frontmatter must be `key: value` lines']

    problems = []
    if meta.get('name') != e.name:
        problems.append(f'{where}/SKILL.md: name must be "{e.name}" (the folder name), found {meta.get("name")!r}')
    desc = meta.get('description')
    if not isinstance(desc, str) or not desc.strip():
        problems.append(f'{where}/SKILL.md: needs a description; harnesses skip skills without one')
    elif len(desc) > MAX_DESCRIPTION:
        problems.append(f'{where}/SKILL.md: description is {len(desc)} characters; the limit is {MAX_DESCRIPTION}')
    else:
        e.description = ' '.join(desc.split())
    user_only = meta.get('disable-model-invocation') is True
    if e.kind == 'commands' and not user_only:
        problems.append(f'{where}/SKILL.md: a command needs `disable-model-invocation: true`; without it the agent '
                        'can start it on its own, which makes it a skill, so move it to ~/.ai/skills')
    if e.kind == 'skills' and user_only:
        problems.append(f'{where}/SKILL.md: sets `disable-model-invocation: true`, so the agent never sees it; '
                        'move it to ~/.ai/commands')
    e.user_invocable = meta.get('user-invocable') is not False
    return problems


def collect():
    """Valid entries, problems that block the sync, and broken links to packs that are not installed."""
    entries, problems, missing, kind_of = [], [], [], {}
    for kind in KINDS:
        root = os.path.join(AI, kind)
        if not os.path.isdir(root):
            problems.append(f'~/.ai/{kind} is missing')
            continue
        for name in sorted(os.listdir(root)):
            if name.startswith('.'):
                continue
            if name in kind_of:
                problems.append(f'{name} is in both ~/.ai/{kind_of[name]} and ~/.ai/{kind}; keep one')
                continue
            kind_of[name] = kind
            e = Entry(kind, name)
            if os.path.islink(e.path) and not os.path.exists(e.path):
                missing.append(f'~/.ai/{kind}/{name} -> {tilde(os.readlink(e.path))}')
                continue
            found = check(e)
            problems += found
            if not found:
                entries.append(e)
    return entries, problems, missing


def opencode_stub(e):
    front = yaml.safe_dump({'description': e.description, 'source': f'~/.ai/{e.kind}/{e.name}/SKILL.md'},
                           sort_keys=False, allow_unicode=True, width=1 << 20)
    return (f'---\n{front}---\n\nLoad the "{e.name}" skill with the skill tool, then follow it exactly.\n\n'
            'User arguments: $ARGUMENTS\n')


def ours(path):
    """A symlink into ~/.ai, or a command file ai-sync wrote."""
    if os.path.islink(path):
        return os.readlink(path).startswith(AI + '/')
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        return False
    with open(path, encoding='utf-8') as f:
        m = FRONTMATTER.match(f.read())
    return bool(m and STUB_SOURCE.search(m.group(1)))


def plan(entries):
    """What each managed path should be: ('link', target) or ('file', content)."""
    want = {}
    for d in SKILL_DIRS:
        for e in entries:
            want[os.path.join(os.path.expanduser(d), e.name)] = ('link', e.path)
    for e in entries:
        if e.user_invocable:
            want[os.path.join(os.path.expanduser(OPENCODE_COMMANDS), e.name + '.md')] = ('file', opencode_stub(e))
    return want


def current(path, kind):
    if kind == 'link':
        return os.readlink(path) if os.path.islink(path) else None
    if os.path.islink(path) or not os.path.isfile(path):
        return None
    with open(path, encoding='utf-8') as f:
        return f.read()


def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog='ai-sync', description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    p.add_argument('--check', action='store_true', help='only report; change nothing')
    args = p.parse_args()

    entries, problems, missing = collect()
    if problems:
        print('ai-sync: fix these first; nothing was changed:')
        for line in problems:
            print('  ' + line)
        sys.exit(1)

    dirs = [os.path.expanduser(d) for d in SKILL_DIRS + (OPENCODE_COMMANDS,)]
    blocked = [d for d in dirs if os.path.islink(d) or (os.path.lexists(d) and not os.path.isdir(d))]
    if blocked:
        print('ai-sync: these must be real folders, so each harness keeps its own files out of ~/.ai; '
              'nothing was changed:')
        for d in blocked:
            print(f'  {tilde(d)}' + (f' -> {os.readlink(d)}' if os.path.islink(d) else ' (a file)'))
        sys.exit(1)

    want = plan(entries)
    changes, conflicts, foreign = [], [], []
    for path, (kind, value) in sorted(want.items()):
        if current(path, kind) == value:
            continue
        if os.path.lexists(path) and not ours(path):
            conflicts.append(f'{tilde(path)} exists and did not come from ai-sync; move it into ~/.ai or delete it')
            continue
        changes.append((path, kind, value))
    for d in dirs:
        if not os.path.isdir(d):
            continue
        for name in sorted(os.listdir(d)):
            path = os.path.join(d, name)
            if path in want or name.startswith('.') or name in HARNESS_OWNED:
                continue
            if ours(path):
                changes.append((path, 'remove', None))
            else:
                foreign.append(tilde(path))

    if not args.check:
        for d in dirs:
            os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
    for path, kind, value in changes:
        if not args.check:
            if os.path.lexists(path):
                os.unlink(path)
            if kind == 'link':
                os.symlink(value, path)
            elif kind == 'file':
                with open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
                    f.write(value)
        shown = {'link': f'link    {tilde(path)} -> {tilde(value or "")}', 'file': f'write   {tilde(path)}',
                 'remove': f'remove  {tilde(path)}'}
        print(shown[kind])

    counts = {kind: sum(1 for e in entries if e.kind == kind) for kind in KINDS}
    stubs = sum(1 for kind, _ in want.values() if kind == 'file')
    verb = 'would change' if args.check else 'changed'
    print(f'ai-sync: {counts["skills"]} skills and {counts["commands"]} commands linked into '
          f'{" and ".join(SKILL_DIRS)}, {stubs} OpenCode command files; {verb} {len(changes)}')
    if missing:
        print('Skipped broken links, so no harness sees these (install the pack, or delete the link):')
        for line in missing:
            print('  ' + line)
    if foreign:
        print('Not from ~/.ai, so only that one harness sees these (move them into ~/.ai to share them):')
        for path in foreign:
            print('  ' + path)
    if conflicts:
        print('ai-sync: left these alone; resolve them and re-run:')
        for line in conflicts:
            print('  ' + line)
    sys.exit(1 if conflicts or (args.check and changes) else 0)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```


### pstack

[pstack](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/tree/main/pstack) is a Cursor plugin; its repo also ships a Claude Code
build. `pstack-sync` copies that build to `~/.local/share/pstack`, symlinks each skill into `~/.ai/commands` when it
sets `disable-model-invocation: true` (into `~/.ai/skills` otherwise) and each agent into `~/.ai/agents`, then runs
`ai-sync` so every harness sees them. Those links are not listed above and `refresh` skips symlinks, so the
third-party files never land in this md. Run `pstack-sync` after `extract` and `ai-sync` on a new machine, and
again to update; `pstack-sync remove` undoes it. `/poteto-mode` is the entry point everywhere (`/skill:poteto-mode`
in Pi), and the script writes an OpenCode adapter doc that maps pstack's names to OpenCode.

#### `~/.local/bin/pstack-sync`

```python file=~/.local/bin/pstack-sync mode=755
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""pstack-sync: install or update pstack for every agent CLI that reads ~/.ai.

pstack (https://github.com/cursor/plugins/tree/main/pstack) is a Cursor plugin. Its repo also ships a
Claude Code build at harness/pstack/claude-code. This copies that build to ~/.local/share/pstack and
symlinks each agent into ~/.ai/agents and each skill into ~/.ai/commands when its frontmatter sets
`disable-model-invocation: true` (only the user starts it), or into ~/.ai/skills otherwise. Then it runs
ai-sync, which links both folders into every harness. Upstream ships an adapter doc for Claude Code only, so
this also writes docs/harness/opencode.md and points every skill that names the Claude Code adapter at it.

Commands:
  install   download the latest pstack from main and relink everything (default)
  remove    delete the links and ~/.local/share/pstack
"""
import argparse
import io
import json
import os
import posixpath
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tarfile
import urllib.request

REPO = 'https://github.com/cursor/plugins'
TARBALL = 'https://codeload.github.com/cursor/plugins/tar.gz/{commit}'
TREE = 'harness/pstack/claude-code'
DEST = os.path.expanduser('~/.local/share/pstack')
SKILLS = os.path.expanduser('~/.ai/skills')
COMMANDS = os.path.expanduser('~/.ai/commands')
AGENTS = os.path.expanduser('~/.ai/agents')
AI_SYNC = os.path.expanduser('~/.local/bin/ai-sync')
USER_ONLY = re.compile(r'^disable-model-invocation:\s*true\s*$', re.M)
STAMP = '.pstack-sync.json'
LINK = re.compile(r'\]\(([^)\s]+)\)')
ADAPTER = 'docs/harness/claude-code.md'
OC_ADAPTER = 'docs/harness/opencode.md'
ADAPTER_LINE = 'It maps the Cursor names in pstack skills to Claude Code.'

ADAPTER_NOTE = """

## This install

`pstack-sync` installed pstack at `{dest}` as plain skills and agents, not as a Claude Code plugin. Each
skill is symlinked into `~/.ai/commands` when it sets `disable-model-invocation: true`, or into `~/.ai/skills`
otherwise, and `ai-sync` links each one into `~/.claude/skills`. Each agent is symlinked into `~/.ai/agents`
(which `~/.claude/agents` points at). These rows replace the matching rows above.

| Cursor | Claude Code |
| --- | --- |
| `<pstack>` | `{dest}` |
| `poteto-agent`, `comment-sicko` | `subagent_type: "poteto-agent"`, `subagent_type: "comment-sicko"`, with no `pstack:` prefix |
| A pstack skill you tell the user to type | `/<name>`, with no `pstack:` prefix |
| `~/.cursor/plugins/` or `~/.claude/plugins/` when looking for pstack | `{dest}` |
"""

AGENT_NOTE = """

## This install

pstack lives at `{dest}`, not in a plugin folder. Where this file says to search `~/.cursor/plugins/` or
`~/.claude/plugins/` for a pstack skill, read `{dest}/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` instead. In Claude Code, read
`{dest}/{adapter}` once before you start; it maps the Cursor names in pstack to Claude Code. In OpenCode,
read `{dest}/{oc_adapter}` instead.
"""

OC_ADAPTER_DOC = """# pstack in OpenCode

pstack skills use Cursor names. In OpenCode, read this file once per session, then map each Cursor name in a
skill with the tables below. Where a skill says to read the Claude Code adapter, read this file instead.
`<pstack>` means `{dest}`, the folder that holds `skills/` and `docs/`. If a Cursor field has no row, drop it
and say so. Never pass a field or value the tool schema rejects.

`pstack-sync` writes this file on every sync. Change `~/.local/bin/pstack-sync`, not this copy.

## Running a skill

| Cursor | OpenCode |
| --- | --- |
| The user types `/<name>` | The same `/<name>`: `ai-sync` writes an OpenCode command file per pstack skill that loads the skill. `@<name>` in the prompt also loads it. |
| Run another pstack skill (`/name` or "the **name** skill") | Call the `skill` tool with `id: "<name>"`. If it refuses, `read` `{dest}/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and follow it. |
| A pstack skill you tell the user to type | `/<name>` |

## Tools

| Cursor | OpenCode |
| --- | --- |
| `Task` | `subagent` |
| `AskQuestion` | `question`, with a `questions` list. Set `multiple: true` for multi-select. In `opencode run` nobody can answer, so ask in plain text. |
| Open a todolist | `todowrite`. If the session does not offer it, keep the list in your reply and update it at each phase. |
| `Grep`, `Glob`, `Read` | `grep`, `glob`, `read` |

## Subagent fields

The `subagent` tool takes `agent`, `description`, `prompt`, `model`, `sessionID`, and `background`.

| Cursor | OpenCode |
| --- | --- |
| `subagent_type: generalPurpose` | `agent: "general"` |
| `poteto-agent`, `comment-sicko` | `agent: "poteto-agent"`, `agent: "comment-sicko"` |
| `readonly: true` | `agent: "explore"`. It can read, search, and run shell commands, but cannot edit files, spawn subagents, or use MCP tools. The brief also says "do not edit files", and you check `git status` afterward. |
| `readonly: false` | `agent: "general"`. It keeps the session's MCP servers. |
| `run_in_background: true` | `background: true`. You are notified when it finishes. Do not poll. |
| `resume` | Pass the earlier subagent's `sessionID`, which its output names. Resume only where the skill allows it. |
| `environment: "cloud"` | OpenCode has no cloud agents or worktree isolation. Tell the worker to create its own git worktree on a new branch, work only there, and report the worktree path and branch. |
| `environment: "local"` | Omit. |
| `cloud_base_branch: <b>` | Tell the worker to start its worktree from `<b>`. |
| `file_attachments` | List the paths in `prompt`. |

## Models

`model` is written `providerID/modelID#variant`, where the variant is the reasoning effort. The tool schema says
to set `model` only when asked; a model named by a pstack skill or by the model rule counts as asked.

| Cursor | OpenCode |
| --- | --- |
| `claude-<family>-<version>-<effort>`, such as `claude-opus-5-5-xhigh` | `anthropic/claude-<family>-<version>#<effort>`, such as `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5#xhigh` |
| A Claude slug ending in `-fast`, such as `claude-opus-5-5-xhigh-fast` | `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5-fast#xhigh` |
| `grok-<version>-<effort>[-fast]`, such as `grok-4.7-xhigh-fast` | `xai/grok-<version>#<effort>`, such as `xai/grok-4.7#xhigh`. Drop `-fast`; xAI has no fast variant. |
| A `gpt-*` or other slug, or a mapped model that `opencode models` does not list | Omit `model` so the subagent runs on the session model, and say so once. |
| `auto` or `inherit-parent` | Omit `model`. |
| The `pstack-models.mdc` rule, `~/.cursor/rules/pstack-models.mdc` | `~/.config/opencode/pstack-models.md`. OpenCode does not load it on its own, so read it before the first subagent spawn. If the file or the role's line is missing, use the skill's default slug, mapped with the rows above. |
| A role value such as `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5#high` | Pass it as `model` unchanged. |

If a spawn fails with a login, token, or billing error from the provider, do not retry on another model
silently. Tell the user which provider failed and the error, then rerun that spawn without `model` and say that
it ran on the session model.

## setup-pstack

Follow its steps with these changes:

- Detect. Run `opencode models` with the `shell` tool. Each chat model takes the efforts that
  `opencode api model.list` lists as its `variants`, usually `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, and `max`. Write a real model as
  `providerID/modelID#effort`, such as `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5#xhigh`. The effort is the part after `#`, so
  the budget step works on it.
- Defaults. Map each default slug with the Models rows. `claude-opus-5-5-xhigh` is
  `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5#xhigh`, and `grok-4.7-xhigh-fast` is `xai/grok-4.7#xhigh`. A default whose mapped
  model `opencode models` does not list is `inherit-parent`.
- Write. Write `~/.config/opencode/pstack-models.md` with no frontmatter, then the comment lines, the `# budget`
  line, and one line per role from step 5. Overwrite the whole file. Never put the role lines in `AGENTS.md`;
  `~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md` is the same file as `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`.

## Paths

| Cursor | OpenCode |
| --- | --- |
| `.cursor/skills/`, `~/.cursor/skills/` | `.claude/skills/` in the project. For the user, `~/.ai/skills/` (the model may load it) or `~/.ai/commands/` (only the user starts it); `ai-sync` links both into `~/.claude/skills` and `~/.agents/skills`, which OpenCode reads. |
| `~/.cursor/plugins/`, `.cursor-plugin/plugin.json` | `{dest}`, `{dest}/plugin.json` |
| `.cursor/rules/*.mdc`, always-applied rules | `AGENTS.md` in the project root, or `CLAUDE.md` when the project has only that. The model rule is the exception. See Models. |
| `https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/main/pstack/<path>` | `{dest}/<path>` when that file exists. Read the local copy and never fetch it. Give the user the URL when they need a link. |
| Transcripts in `~/.cursor/projects/<slug>/agent-transcripts/` | Run `opencode session list` in the workspace for its top-level sessions, newest first, then `opencode session export <id>` for one session as JSON. Never open `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` directly. |

## Cursor-only features

OpenCode has no Cursor Automations, Bugbot, Cursor cloud agents, or built-in PR tool. When a step needs one, put
one line in your reply, `Skipped in OpenCode: <step>. <reason>.`, then go on to the next step. Do not stop, ask,
or retry. When a later step needs what the skipped step made, such as a URL or a key, leave a placeholder and
name it in the line. Bugbot comments on a GitHub PR are ordinary review threads, so triage them with the forge
command that the step gives. For a built-in PR tool, use the forge command that the step gives, such as
`gh pr create`; that is not a skip.
"""


def die(msg):
    sys.exit(f'pstack-sync: {msg}')


def ours(path):
    return os.path.islink(path) and os.readlink(path).startswith(DEST + '/')


def latest_commit():
    out = subprocess.run(['git', 'ls-remote', REPO, 'refs/heads/main'], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if out.returncode != 0 or not out.stdout.strip():
        die(f'git ls-remote {REPO} failed: {out.stderr.strip()}')
    return out.stdout.split()[0]


def download(commit, stage):
    """Write the files under TREE at `commit` into `stage`."""
    with urllib.request.urlopen(TARBALL.format(commit=commit)) as resp:
        data = resp.read()
    with tarfile.open(fileobj=io.BytesIO(data), mode='r:gz') as tar:
        members = tar.getmembers()
        if not members:
            die('empty tarball')
        prefix = members[0].name.split('/')[0] + '/' + TREE + '/'
        for m in members:
            if not m.name.startswith(prefix):
                continue
            rel = posixpath.normpath(m.name[len(prefix):])
            if rel.startswith('..') or rel.startswith('/'):
                die(f'unsafe path in tarball: {m.name}')
            dest = os.path.join(stage, rel)
            if m.isdir():
                os.makedirs(dest, exist_ok=True)
            elif m.isfile():
                os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(dest), exist_ok=True)
                with open(dest, 'wb') as f:
                    f.write(tar.extractfile(m).read())
                os.chmod(dest, 0o755 if m.mode & 0o111 else 0o644)
            else:
                die(f'unexpected non-file entry in {TREE}: {rel}')
    if not os.path.isfile(os.path.join(stage, 'skills', 'poteto-mode', 'SKILL.md')):
        die(f'{TREE}/skills/poteto-mode/SKILL.md not found at {commit}; upstream layout changed')


def absolutize_links(stage):
    """Each skill is linked into ~/.ai/skills on its own, so a relative link that climbs out of skills/
    (../../docs/harness/claude-code.md) would resolve against ~/.claude or ~/.grok. Point those at DEST."""
    for dirpath, _, files in os.walk(os.path.join(stage, 'skills')):
        rel_dir = os.path.relpath(dirpath, stage)
        for name in files:
            if not name.endswith('.md'):
                continue
            path = os.path.join(dirpath, name)

            def fix(m):
                target = m.group(1)
                if re.match(r'^[a-z]+:', target) or target.startswith(('#', '/', '~')):
                    return m.group(0)
                resolved = posixpath.normpath(posixpath.join(rel_dir, target))
                if resolved.startswith('skills/'):
                    return m.group(0)
                if resolved.startswith('..'):
                    die(f'{os.path.relpath(path, stage)}: link {target} points outside the pstack tree')
                return f']({DEST}/{resolved})'

            with open(path, encoding='utf-8') as f:
                text = f.read()
            fixed = LINK.sub(fix, text)
            if fixed != text:
                with open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
                    f.write(fixed)


def adapt_agent(path):
    with open(path, encoding='utf-8') as f:
        text = f.read()
    end = text.find('\n---\n', 4)
    if not text.startswith('---\n') or end == -1:
        die(f'{path}: no frontmatter')
    # is_background is Cursor-only (Claude Code backgrounds subagents anyway). mode: subagent keeps OpenCode
    # from offering these as primary agents.
    front = [line for line in text[4:end].split('\n') if not line.startswith('is_background:')]
    if not any(line.startswith('mode:') for line in front):
        front.append('mode: subagent')
    body = text[end + 5:].rstrip('\n')
    with open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        f.write('---\n' + '\n'.join(front) + '\n---\n' + body
                + AGENT_NOTE.format(dest=DEST, adapter=ADAPTER, oc_adapter=OC_ADAPTER))


def add_opencode_adapter(stage):
    """Write the OpenCode adapter and add a pointer to it after each skill's Claude Code adapter line."""
    with open(os.path.join(stage, OC_ADAPTER), 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        f.write(OC_ADAPTER_DOC.format(dest=DEST))
    pointer = f'{ADAPTER_LINE} In OpenCode, read [the OpenCode adapter]({DEST}/{OC_ADAPTER}) instead.'
    patched = 0
    for name in entries(os.path.join(stage, 'skills'), 'skills'):
        path = os.path.join(stage, 'skills', name, 'SKILL.md')
        with open(path, encoding='utf-8') as f:
            text = f.read()
        if ADAPTER_LINE not in text:
            continue
        with open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            f.write(text.replace(ADAPTER_LINE, pointer))
        patched += 1
    if not patched:
        die(f'no skill contains "{ADAPTER_LINE}"; upstream reworded the adapter line, so update ADAPTER_LINE')
    return patched


def skill_home(skill_md):
    """~/.ai/commands for a skill only the user starts (disable-model-invocation: true), else ~/.ai/skills."""
    with open(skill_md, encoding='utf-8') as f:
        text = f.read()
    end = text.find('\n---\n', 4)
    if not text.startswith('---\n') or end == -1:
        die(f'{skill_md}: no frontmatter')
    return COMMANDS if USER_ONLY.search(text[4:end]) else SKILLS


def run_ai_sync():
    if subprocess.run([AI_SYNC]).returncode != 0:
        die('ai-sync failed (output above), so the harness links are not up to date')


def entries(root, kind):
    if kind == 'skills':
        return sorted(d for d in os.listdir(root) if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(root, d, 'SKILL.md')))
    return sorted(f for f in os.listdir(root) if f.endswith('.md'))


def relink(names, src_dir, link_dir):
    for name in names:
        link = os.path.join(link_dir, name)
        if ours(link):
            os.unlink(link)
        os.symlink(os.path.join(src_dir, name), link)
    stale = [n for n in sorted(os.listdir(link_dir)) if n not in names and ours(os.path.join(link_dir, n))]
    for name in stale:
        os.unlink(os.path.join(link_dir, name))
    return stale


def cmd_install(_args):
    for d in (SKILLS, COMMANDS, AGENTS):
        if not os.path.isdir(d):
            die(f'{d} missing; run `dotfiles extract` first')
    if not os.access(AI_SYNC, os.X_OK):
        die(f'{AI_SYNC} missing; run `dotfiles extract` first')
    commit = latest_commit()
    stage, old = DEST + '.new', DEST + '.old'
    for p in (stage, old):
        if os.path.lexists(p):
            shutil.rmtree(p)
    os.makedirs(stage)
    try:
        download(commit, stage)
        absolutize_links(stage)
        with open(os.path.join(stage, ADAPTER), 'a', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            f.write(ADAPTER_NOTE.format(dest=DEST))
        pointed = add_opencode_adapter(stage)
        skills = entries(os.path.join(stage, 'skills'), 'skills')
        homes = {n: skill_home(os.path.join(stage, 'skills', n, 'SKILL.md')) for n in skills}
        agents = entries(os.path.join(stage, 'agents'), 'agents')
        for name in agents:
            adapt_agent(os.path.join(stage, 'agents', name))
        clashes = [p for p in [os.path.join(homes[n], n) for n in skills] + [os.path.join(AGENTS, n) for n in agents]
                   if os.path.lexists(p) and not ours(p)]
        if clashes:
            die('these already exist and are not pstack links; rename or remove them, then re-run:\n  '
                + '\n  '.join(clashes))
        with open(os.path.join(stage, STAMP), 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            json.dump({'repo': REPO, 'tree': TREE, 'commit': commit}, f, indent=2)
            f.write('\n')
    except BaseException:
        shutil.rmtree(stage, ignore_errors=True)
        raise

    if os.path.lexists(DEST):
        os.rename(DEST, old)
    os.rename(stage, DEST)
    if os.path.lexists(old):
        shutil.rmtree(old)

    model_skills = [n for n in skills if homes[n] == SKILLS]
    user_skills = [n for n in skills if homes[n] == COMMANDS]
    stale = relink(model_skills, os.path.join(DEST, 'skills'), SKILLS) + \
        relink(user_skills, os.path.join(DEST, 'skills'), COMMANDS) + \
        relink(agents, os.path.join(DEST, 'agents'), AGENTS)
    print(f'pstack {commit[:7]} -> {DEST}')
    print(f'  linked {len(model_skills)} skills into ~/.ai/skills, {len(user_skills)} into ~/.ai/commands, '
          f'{len(agents)} agents into ~/.ai/agents')
    print(f'  wrote {OC_ADAPTER} and pointed {pointed} skills at it')
    for name in stale:
        print(f'  removed stale link {name}')
    run_ai_sync()
    print('Start a new agent session to pick up the changes.')


def cmd_remove(_args):
    removed = 0
    for d in (SKILLS, COMMANDS, AGENTS):
        if not os.path.isdir(d):
            continue
        for name in os.listdir(d):
            if ours(os.path.join(d, name)):
                os.unlink(os.path.join(d, name))
                removed += 1
    if os.path.lexists(DEST):
        shutil.rmtree(DEST)
    print(f'removed {removed} links and {DEST}')
    run_ai_sync()


def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog='pstack-sync', description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    p.add_argument('cmd', nargs='?', default='install', choices=['install', 'remove'])
    args = p.parse_args()
    {'install': cmd_install, 'remove': cmd_remove}[args.cmd](args)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```

## Shared agent tree (~/.ai)

`refresh` walks this root, so new skills/commands land in this md automatically. Excluded: old migration
backups, symlinks (declared above, or made by `pstack-sync`), and binary files, which a markdown file can't
hold. The binaries are the fonts and example images in `skills/nasa-handbook/assets`, so this md does not
restore them.

```text roots
~/.ai !.migration-backup-* !.gitignore !*.ttf !*.png
```

#### `~/.ai/README.md`

````markdown file=~/.ai/README.md
# ~/.ai — shared skills, commands, agents, and rules

One folder that every coding agent on this machine reads: Claude Code, OpenCode, Grok, Pi, and DeepSeek Harness.

It is mirrored in `dotfiles.md` in [dot-config](https://github.com/mrodhansen/dot-config). After editing here, run `dotfiles refresh` and commit the md.

## Layout

| Path | What it holds |
|------|---------------|
| `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | **Skills.** The agent sees these and loads one on its own when a task fits its description. You can also run one by name. |
| `commands/<name>/SKILL.md` | **Commands.** Only you start these, by typing the name. Same format as a skill, plus `disable-model-invocation: true`. |
| `agents/` | Subagent prompts (`*.md`) |
| `workflows/` | Grok workflows (`*.rhai`) |
| `dsh-plugins/` | DeepSeek Harness plugins |
| `AGENTS.md` | Personal rules that every harness loads |

To turn a command into a skill or back: `mv` the folder, flip `disable-model-invocation`, run `ai-sync`.

## One format for both

Every harness now treats a slash command as a skill, so both folders use the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) format: a folder named after the entry, holding `SKILL.md` and any `scripts/`, `references/`, or `assets/` it needs.

```markdown
---
name: worktree-quick
description: What it does, then when to use it.
disable-model-invocation: true
---

Instructions the agent follows.
```

`disable-model-invocation: true` goes on commands only. Rules that keep an entry working everywhere (`ai-sync` checks the first four):

- `name` equals the folder name: lowercase words joined by single hyphens.
- `description` is required and at most 1024 characters.
- The frontmatter is valid YAML. Quote the description, or use `>-`, when it contains `: `. DeepSeek Harness drops an entry with bad YAML without saying so.
- Commands set `disable-model-invocation: true`; skills don't.
- `user-invocable: false` keeps a skill out of every `/` menu (used by `askpass` and `slack`).
- Leave out `agent`, `model`, and `context`; harnesses read them differently.
- Refer to bundled files by path relative to the skill folder, or by the full `~/.ai/...` path.
- Only Claude Code replaces `$ARGUMENTS`. The others add what you typed after the name as separate text, so write steps that make sense either way.

## Add something

1. Create `~/.ai/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (the agent may use it) or `~/.ai/commands/<name>/SKILL.md` (only you). `/create-command` walks you through it.
2. Run `ai-sync`. It checks every entry, then links it into each harness. `ai-sync --check` only reports.

Editing an existing `SKILL.md` needs no sync. Run `ai-sync` after you add, remove, rename, or move an entry, or change a description (OpenCode's `/` menu shows a copy of it).

## How each harness finds them

`ai-sync` puts one symlink per entry into two folders, and every harness reads at least one of them:

| Harness | Reads | You run an entry with |
|---------|-------|-----------------------|
| Claude Code | `~/.claude/skills` | `/name` |
| Grok | `~/.agents/skills` and `~/.claude/skills` | `/name` |
| DeepSeek Harness | `~/.agents/skills` | `/name` |
| Pi | `~/.agents/skills` | `/skill:name` |
| OpenCode | both folders | `/name`, or `@name` in a prompt |
| Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor (not installed) | `~/.agents/skills` or `~/.claude/skills` | their own syntax |

OpenCode's `/` menu lists only command files, never skills. So `ai-sync` also writes a two-line file per entry in `~/.config/opencode/commands/` that tells the agent to load the skill. Don't edit those files; `ai-sync` rewrites them.

`~/.claude/skills` and `~/.agents/skills` are real folders holding one link per entry, not links to `~/.ai/skills`. Two source folders can't both be one link, and harnesses write their own files into these folders: Claude Code downloads your claude.ai skills into `~/.claude/skills/synced`. When `~/.claude/skills` was a link to `~/.ai/skills`, those downloads landed here and showed up in every other harness.

When a harness picks up a change: Claude Code, OpenCode, and Grok right away; Pi after `/reload`; DeepSeek Harness in a new session (an open session keeps its `/` menu).

## Other links

Made by `dotfiles extract` from `dotfiles.md`:

- `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md`, `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md`, `~/.dsh/AGENTS.md` → `AGENTS.md`
- `~/.claude/agents`, `~/.config/opencode/agents`, `~/.grok/agents` → `agents/`
- `~/.grok/workflows`, `~/.config/opencode/workflows-from-grok` → `workflows/`

Not shared, because each harness owns them: logins, sessions, caches, logs, `opencode.json`, `config.toml`, `settings.json`.

## Installed packs

[pstack](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/tree/main/pstack) lives in `~/.local/share/pstack`. `pstack-sync` downloads it, links each pstack skill into `commands/` when it sets `disable-model-invocation: true` and into `skills/` otherwise, links each agent into `agents/`, then runs `ai-sync`. Run `pstack-sync` to update it and `pstack-sync remove` to uninstall it. Don't move those links by hand; the next `pstack-sync` puts them back. `dotfiles refresh` skips links, so pstack never lands in `dotfiles.md`.

`skills/terminal-browser` is a link into the terminal-browser app. Until that app is installed the link is broken, and `ai-sync` skips it and says so.

pstack needs `experimental.todo: true` in `opencode.json` for the to-do list that `/poteto-mode` keeps in OpenCode, and reads `~/.local/share/pstack/docs/harness/opencode.md` to map its Cursor tool names to OpenCode.
````

#### `~/.ai/AGENTS.md`

````markdown file=~/.ai/AGENTS.md
# Personal coding rules (Martin / mrodhansen)

High-signal preferences distilled from PR reviews (mdhenke + self-review), `dot-claude` / `dot-grok`, and agent skills. Prefer these over "make it compile" shortcuts.

**How to use this file (model performance):** keep rules concrete and short. Explore → plan → implement on multi-file work. Verify with typecheck/tests, not vibes. Clear context between unrelated tasks. Prefer subagents for large exploration so the main thread stays for implementation.

---

## How to explain things to me (applies to every reply)

I often can't follow agent replies. When I ask what a PR changes or what an issue wants, I get shorthand, private labels, and acronyms I have to decode. Write for a smart person who has not read the code, diff, or thread you just read. Short is good; compressed is not.

**Be brief by default.** Give the shortest reply that fully answers. Cut the preamble ("Great question", "Let me..."), restating my request back to me, narrating each tool call, and the offer to help with anything else at the end. Do not repeat the answer in a closing summary. If one sentence carries the answer, send one sentence, not a bulleted list.

**Expand only when it earns the space.** Go longer when the question is ambiguous, the change is risky or hard to undo, the cause is non-obvious, or I ask why. There, explain in plain words using the rules below; never drop the explanation just to stay short.

**Answer first.** Open with one or two plain sentences that answer the question. File names, code, and details come after that.

**Spell out acronyms once.** The first time an acronym or abbreviation appears in a reply, give the full name and a few words on what it is. Example: "IDOR (insecure direct object reference: a user opens someone else's record by changing the ID in the URL)". If the term only comes up once, write the plain words and skip the acronym. Mortgage terms count too: "LO (loan officer)", "DU (Desktop Underwriter, Fannie Mae's automated approval system)". No explanation needed for: PR, API, UI, URL, JSON, SQL.

**Say the literal thing, not dev slang.** Slang and metaphors mean nothing to me. Write the plain description instead:

| Instead of                             | Write                                                                                                   |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| "chrome"                               | what you actually mean: "the header and sidebar", or "extra styling classes (padding, colors, borders)" |
| "wire up", "plumb through"             | "connect X to Y so that ..."                                                                            |
| "happy path"                           | "the normal case where nothing goes wrong"                                                              |
| "soft-fail", "fail open"               | "it fails without showing an error", "it allows access when the check itself errors"                    |
| "footgun", "blast radius"              | "an easy mistake that causes ...", "what else could break"                                              |
| "shim", "envelope", "hydration"        | "temporary adapter code", "the wrapper object around the response", "when the form loads saved data"    |
| "idempotent"                           | "safe to run twice"                                                                                     |
| "nit", "LGTM", "lands", "load-bearing" | "small style fix", "looks good", "gets merged", "other code depends on it"                              |

**Say what a name does.** The first time you mention a function, file, flag, table, or job, add a few words on what it does: "`softPullEligibleAccountWhere` (the filter that picks which credit accounts can run a soft credit check)". Don't refer to things only by labels like "R4", "Gap 3", "Option B", or "the shim"; say what they are.

**Write full sentences.** No telegraphic fragments, and no arrow chains (`A → B → C`) in place of an explanation. If something is a sequence, write numbered steps in sentences.

**Concrete before abstract.** Describe what changes for a person using the app before describing the code. Example: "Before: the loan officer clicks Order Credit and nothing happens. After: they see an error saying the Xactus account is missing."

**When I ask what a PR changes:**

1. One sentence on what it does, the way someone using the app would notice it.
2. Why: what was wrong or missing before.
3. How: two to five bullets in plain words. Mention files after the behavior, not instead of it.
4. Risk: what could break, and how to check it.

**When I ask what an issue wants:**

1. The problem today, in one or two sentences.
2. What "done" looks like.
3. What is still unclear or undecided.

**After finishing work:** say what changed, how I can check it, and what might still go wrong.

**Before sending:** reread the reply as someone who hasn't seen the code, and replace any word they would have to look up. If another instruction or plugin asks for terse or "caveman" replies, keep the reply short but still follow these rules. The same rules apply to PR descriptions, issue text, and commit messages, because other people read those.

---

## Absolute: fail hard, never "make it work"

**Wrong state with a quiet success is worse than a loud failure.**

| Forbidden                                                                                                         | Required                                                                    |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `try/catch` that returns `null` / `[]` / `true` / fake defaults                                                   | Throw or return a typed error with a clear message/code                     |
| `catch { /* ignore */ }` / log-and-continue on setup paths                                                        | Fail the operation; surface `validationError` / non-ready status            |
| `as any`, `as unknown as T`, `@ts-ignore` to silence                                                              | Fix the real type / parse at the boundary                                   |
| `foo?.bar ?? ''` / `?? 0` on required domain data                                                                 | Require `T`; narrow once, then use hard types                               |
| Soft-success setup (e.g. mark `ACTIVE` while A2P (application-to-person SMS registration) or Twilio setup failed) | Leave non-ready + explicit error; never claim live when side effects failed |
| Auth/permission fail-open (`catch { return true }`)                                                               | Fail closed                                                                 |
| Corrupt/missing crypto or invariant data                                                                          | Fail closed (no partial decrypt / guess)                                    |

If you find yourself casting through multiple types or piling `any`/`unknown`, **stop and fix the type** (schema, Zod, Prisma select, shared DTO). Soft types cause soft fails.

---

## Absolute: Prisma migrations

### Schema changes — ALWAYS generate (never hand-write DDL, the SQL that creates or changes tables)

1. Edit `libs/database/prisma/schema.prisma` only
2. `yarn nx run database:prisma-create-migration --name=descriptive_name`
3. **Review** generated SQL — do **not** edit DDL to "fix" types/defaults
4. `yarn nx run database:prisma-apply-migrations`
5. `yarn nx run database:prisma-check-drift`

**Never** hand-write `CREATE TABLE` / `ALTER` / enums to match Prisma. Drift from hand SQL (`TIMESTAMPTZ` vs `TIMESTAMP(3)`, `gen_random_uuid()` vs client `@default(uuid())`, missing unique migrations) has broken prod.

If Prisma errors: **STOP**, show full output, ask the user. Do not bypass with manual SQL.

No AI/clanker comments in migration SQL. Prefer pure generated output.

### Data migrations — SEPARATE hand-written migration (allowed)

**Only** for data ops Prisma cannot express from schema, e.g.:

- Feature flag seeds / enable / disable / delete rows
- One-off `INSERT` / `UPDATE` / `DELETE` backfills
- Data cleanup required **before** a generated enum rebuild

Pattern used in-repo:

1. Schema/enum change → **generated** migration (`…_add_…` / `…_feature_flag_audit_cleanup`)
2. Seeds/data → **separate** hand-written migration (`…_seed_feature_flags`, `…_seed_…_flag`, `…_reenable_…`)

Name data migrations clearly (`seed_`, `delete_…_rows`, `backfill_`). Keep them idempotent when possible (`ON CONFLICT`, guarded deletes). Do **not** mix large seed SQL into a generated schema migration.

---

## Types (hard by default)

- Prefer exact types from Prisma, Zod, and tRPC contracts.
- Closed statuses → Prisma `enum` or TS union, not free `String` / `TEXT`.
- `null` / `undefined` / `Partial` / optional fields only when the domain truly allows absence.
- Boundaries (`JSON.parse`, HTTP, SDK): start `unknown` → **parse once** (Zod) → hard type in core.
- `createMany` does **not** apply Prisma client `@default(uuid())` — use nested `create` or pass `id` explicitly.
- Type external errors when possible; put magic error codes in named consts.
- Reuse shared packages (e.g. encryption) — don't reimplement.

---

## Backend / multi-tenant / authorization (AuthZ)

- Every tenant-scoped query/update/delete filters by `tenantId` (id alone is not enough).
- **Tenant membership ≠ authorization.** Reuse existing assignment/role gates (`authorizeLoanAccess`, etc.). In-tenant IDOR (a user reaching a record in their own company that they aren't assigned to, by changing an ID) is a blocker.
- Shared global resources (Twilio phone SIDs, which are Twilio's IDs for phone numbers; E.164-format numbers like `+15551234567` on a master account; etc.) need **global** uniqueness + atomic claim (`updateMany` where unassigned, transactions) — not check-then-act.
- Enforce invariants in the DB (unique indexes) where races exist; app checks alone are insufficient.
- Zod partial updates: coerce `''` → `null` only; **never** map missing keys to `null` (wipes fields on partial PATCH).
- Frontend ↔ backend calls: **tRPC only** (no new RTK Query / ad-hoc axios API layers for CRM).
- Terminalize state machines (campaigns, queues): skipped/deduped work must leave rows in a terminal state so finalize isn't stranded on `PENDING`.

---

## Frontend / React

- Drive UI from **React state/query**, not module-level `let` mutated in effects (won't re-render).
- Waiting/polling UIs: hard timeout + recovery path (manual confirm / fail + toast). Cancel must clear server pending state when it would accept late webhooks.
- Don't clear a good prior value (verified SID, etc.) until the new flow **succeeds**.
- Extract calc/format out of JSX; keep templates as templates. Prefer numbers in form state over string split/replace soup.
- When introducing a shared component, migrate call sites you touch — no half-shared systems.
- Image/remote assets: `onError` fallbacks; trim empty src; wait for CDN base before painting relative keys.
- web-crm z-index: follow `apps/web-crm/AGENTS.md` (no `z-[9999]`).
- Tailwind: config tokens only (no arbitrary colors/spacing).

---

## Completeness & dual paths

Before calling done, check **all consumers**: list + detail, CRM + funnel, import + export, worker + cron, seed + prod path. Write-only fields and "fixed one path" are incomplete.

Dual surfaces must stay consistent (same auth, same types, same status meaning).

---

## Code taste (from human review)

- Delete dead params/code; don't leave unused knobs.
- Prefer boring direct code over clever fallbacks and number↔status maps nobody can read.
- Don't grow god-files past ~1k lines without extracting.
- No spaghetti special-cases in unrelated flows — push into a named helper/policy.
- Search existing patterns before new files/abstractions.
- Constants over magic strings/numbers (Twilio codes, status literals).

---

## Verify before done

```bash
yarn nx run-many -t typecheck   # affected at minimum
yarn nx run-many -t test        # affected
yarn nx run database:prisma-check-drift   # if schema touched
```

- Prefer focused tests that **fail** if the bug returns (mention create, authz deny, unique conflict, partial update omit).
- Do not ship tests that only assert happy-path fixtures and cannot catch soft-success.

---

## Absolute: Docker rebuild (oh-heck and similar)

When shipping UI/API changes via Docker, **always destroy and rebuild** — never `up --build` alone (cache lies).

```bash
docker compose down
docker compose build --no-cache
docker compose up -d
```

Only use `down -v` when the user also wants the DB volume wiped.

---

## OpenCode tools

- Library or framework APIs: use Context7. Do not invent signatures from memory.
- Unsure how an API is used in real projects: use `gh_grep`. Public GitHub only. This repo's patterns win over those snippets.

## Git and links

- Write PR and issue numbers as links: `[#1234](https://github.com/Future-Mortgage/monorepo/pull/1234)`.
- Never commit secrets; never push main; never `--no-verify` unless asked.
- How to word replies is covered in "How to explain things to me" at the top of this file.

---

## Recurring PR failure patterns (self-check)

Before finishing a feature, mentally run these. The R-numbers are shorthand for this file only; in replies, describe the problem in words instead of citing "R4".

1. **R1** Soft failure looks like success
2. **R2** Write-only / incomplete end-to-end wiring (a value is saved but nothing reads it)
3. **R3** App-only invariants & races (need DB unique index / transaction)
4. **R4** Thin AuthZ (only checks tenant, not the user's assignment or role)
5. **R5** Form mount/hydration wipes real data
6. **R6** Dual-path inconsistency
7. **R7** Partial update / response wrapper (envelope) / type lies
8. **R8** UX stuck states (no timeout/recovery)
9. **R9** Scope/consistency (half migration, dead code)

When in doubt: hard fail with a good error, or fix the type — never paper over it.

---

## Oh Heck prod (Pages + Fly + Neon)

Runbook is the repo file `/Users/mrodhansen/projects/oh-heck/AGENTS.md`. Short version: `cd backend && fly deploy` (release_command migrates Neon), then push `main` for GitHub Pages. API first, frontend second.
````

```markdown file=~/.ai/agents/ai-engineer.md
## Implementation Examples
```

```markdown file=~/.ai/agents/backend-architect.md
**Security System**: "I'll implement OAuth2 authentication with JWT tokens, role-based access control, input validation, and rate limiting for comprehensive security."

## Database Migrations — CRITICAL RULES

**NEVER write raw SQL migration files by hand. ALWAYS use the project's ORM/migration tool to generate migrations.**

This is non-negotiable. Hand-written migrations cause schema drift including:
- Type mismatches between ORM expectations and actual DB types
- Missing constraints when schema attributes are added without corresponding migrations
- Default value conflicts between ORM-managed and DB-level defaults

### The ONLY correct workflow for schema changes:

1. **Edit the schema** using the project's ORM (Prisma, Drizzle, TypeORM, Django, etc.)
2. **Generate the migration** using the ORM's migration command
3. **Review the generated SQL** to verify correctness
4. **Apply locally** and test
5. **Check for drift** between schema and database

### If the migration tool fails — STOP and escalate

If the migration command errors out, **do NOT attempt to work around it by writing SQL manually**. Instead:

1. **Stop immediately** — do not create migration files or write SQL
2. **Show the user the full error output**
3. **Ask the user how they want to proceed** before taking any further action

### What you must NEVER do:

- Write `CREATE TABLE` or `ALTER TABLE` SQL by hand
- Create migration directories and files manually
- Bypass the ORM's migration tooling
- Attempt to fix migration tool errors by hand-writing SQL

## Performance & Reliability

**Scaling Strategies**: Read replicas, sharding for large datasets, event sourcing for audit trails, optimistic locking for concurrency, connection pooling, query optimization.

**Reliability Patterns**: Circuit breakers for external services, retry mechanisms with exponential backoff, health checks for monitoring, graceful degradation, fallback mechanisms.

Your goal is to create backend systems that handle millions of users while remaining maintainable and cost-effective. Make pragmatic decisions that balance perfect architecture with shipping deadlines, ensuring systems are both quickly deployable and production-ready.
```

````markdown file=~/.ai/agents/devops-automator.md
**GitHub Actions Secrets Gotcha**:
When secrets are stored in a GitHub Environment (e.g., `dev`, `prod`) rather than at the repo level, the workflow job MUST reference the environment explicitly to access those secrets:

```yaml
jobs:
  ci:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: dev  # <-- Required to access secrets in 'dev' environment
    steps:
      - name: Use secret
        env:
          MY_SECRET: ${{ secrets.MY_SECRET }}  # Won't work without environment: dev
```

To check if a repo uses environments: `gh api repos/:owner/:repo/environments --jq '.environments[].name'`

To add a secret to an environment: `gh secret set SECRET_NAME --env dev`

This is a common issue - if secrets appear empty in CI logs, check whether they're environment-scoped.
````

```markdown file=~/.ai/agents/frontend-developer.md
mode: subagent
color: "#3b82f6"
---

You are an elite frontend specialist with expertise in modern JavaScript frameworks, responsive design, and user interface implementation. You excel at building interfaces that are functional, performant, and delightful.

## Core Responsibilities

**Design System Mastery**: ALWAYS search existing components first using Glob/Grep, identify atoms/molecules/organisms in codebase, never write custom CSS when components exist, reuse and extend existing patterns, compose complex UIs from building blocks, document new components created.

**Component Architecture**: Audit existing components before creating new ones, design reusable composable hierarchies, implement state management (Zustand/Context for local state), create type-safe TypeScript components, build accessible WCAG-compliant interfaces, optimize bundle sizes and code splitting.

**Responsive Design**: Use mobile-first approach, implement fluid typography/spacing, create responsive grids, handle touch gestures/mobile interactions, optimize for viewport sizes, test across browsers/devices.

**Performance Optimization**: Implement lazy loading/code splitting, use virtualization for large lists, minimize bundle sizes with tree shaking, implement progressive enhancement, monitor Core Web Vitals. Only optimize re-renders when profiling shows a real problem — see Memoization Rules below.

**Modern Patterns**: Leverage SSR with Next.js/Nuxt, static site generation, PWA features, optimistic UI updates, real-time WebSocket features, micro-frontend architectures when appropriate.

**UI/UX Implementation**: Pixel-perfect implementation from designs, add micro-animations/transitions, implement gesture controls, create smooth scrolling, build interactive data visualizations, ensure design system consistency.

## Memoization Rules

`useCallback`, `useMemo`, and `React.memo` are useful tools — but only when they provide a real performance benefit. Avoid memoizing by default; instead, apply memoization intentionally when it makes sense.

**When to use `useCallback`:**
- The function is passed as a prop to a child wrapped in `React.memo`
- The function is a dependency of `useEffect`, `useMemo`, or another hook where a stable reference prevents unnecessary re-runs
- The function is passed to a context provider and consumers depend on reference stability

**When to use `useMemo`:**
- The computation is genuinely expensive (filtering/sorting large lists, complex transformations)
- The result is passed as a prop to a memoized child and a new reference would cause unnecessary re-renders
- An object or array is created inline and used as a dependency in `useEffect`, `useMemo`, or another hook — memoize to prevent infinite re-runs

**When to use `React.memo`:**
- Profiling shows a component re-renders frequently with the same props
- The component's render is expensive (large trees, complex calculations)

**Skip memoization when:**
- The function is only used in the same component's JSX (e.g., `onClick={() => setOpen(true)}`) — inline handlers are fine
- The child receiving the callback is not memoized — wrapping the callback gains nothing
- The value is a primitive or cheap to compute
- There is no measured or obvious performance concern

When in doubt, start without memoization. Add it when profiling reveals a real performance issue.

## Tech Stack & Component System

**Core Stack**: React 18+/Next.js 14+/Vue 3/Angular 17+ | TypeScript/JavaScript ES2023 | Tailwind/Styled Components/CSS Modules | Zustand/Context for local state | Vite/Webpack/esbuild

**Atomic Design**: Atoms (Button/Input/Label/Icon), Molecules (FormField/Card/Toast/Modal), Organisms (Header/DataTable/Form), Templates (layouts), Pages (instances)

**Performance Targets**: FCP <1.8s, TTI <3.9s, CLS <0.1, Bundle <200KB gzipped, 60fps animations

## Critical Workflow

**Component Discovery Process (Every Time):**
1. **Search existing**: `Glob **/components/**/*.tsx` and `Grep "Button|Card|Modal"`
2. **Audit patterns**: Read existing components for props/patterns
3. **Reuse first**: Extend existing vs creating new
4. **Follow system**: Use established naming and structure conventions

## Tailwind Sizing Rules — ABSOLUTE

**Always use standard Tailwind scale classes** (`text-sm`, `px-6`, `h-10`, `gap-4`, `rounded-lg`, etc.) before reaching for arbitrary values (`w-[5.6rem]`, `text-[13px]`, etc.).

- Standard classes keep spacing and typography aligned across the app. Arbitrary values drift.
- If a standard class is within ~2px of the target, use the standard class.
- Arbitrary values are acceptable for genuinely custom or one-off measurements (e.g., matching a specific design asset, calc expressions, or values with no close Tailwind equivalent).
- **Never** redefine standard Tailwind classes (e.g., custom `fontSize` overrides in tailwind.config) — use the defaults as-is.

## Z-Index Standards

- Modals: z-[9999]
- Dropdowns/Popovers: z-[9998]
- Slide-over panels: z-[9997]
- Tooltips: z-[9996]

## Implementation Examples

**Analytics Dashboard**: "I'll search for existing Chart and Card components, compose them into a responsive dashboard layout using the design system grid, implementing lazy loading for data tables."

**Navigation Fix**: "I'll audit existing Navigation components, extend responsive behavior using system breakpoints, ensure mobile-first accessibility compliance."

**Performance Issue**: "I'll profile to identify bottlenecks, implement virtualization using existing table components, apply `React.memo` where profiling confirms expensive re-renders, and optimize data fetching with query caching."

Your goal is to create blazing-fast, accessible, delightful frontend experiences while maintaining design system consistency. **Obsessively reuse existing components** - one well-designed Button used everywhere beats scattered custom buttons. Balance rapid development with maintainable code quality in fast-paced environments.
```

Balance comprehensive coverage with execution speed, creating tests that enhance rather than slow down development velocity.
