### Commands

Slash commands (OpenCode loads all; Claude Code links the ones with no same-named skill). Many mirror a skill: same body, command-style frontmatter.

#### `~/.ai/commands/check-shared-ui/SKILL.md`

````markdown file=~/.ai/commands/check-shared-ui/SKILL.md
---
name: check-shared-ui
description: Checks frontend diffs for native HTML controls (especially buttons) and shared-component className chrome. Replaces natives with design-system primitives, requires predefined variant/size/shape/appearance, and strips style overrides except positioning (sizing only rarely). Use when user says "/check-shared-ui", "/check-shared-ui <PR#>", "check shared components", "no native buttons", or "shared UI chrome".
disable-model-invocation: true
---

# /check-shared-ui — Shared primitives, no chrome overrides

Goal: every **changed** frontend file uses design-system primitives instead of native controls, and every shared primitive is styled **only** through its predefined `variant` / `size` / `shape` / `appearance` props. `className` / `style` on those primitives may contain **positioning** and, rarely, **sizing**. Chrome overrides are a hard fail.

**Usage:**
- `/check-shared-ui` — current branch vs `origin/main` (or detected default branch)
- `/check-shared-ui <PR-number>` / `/check-shared-ui <PR-url>` — that PR's touched files
- `/check-shared-ui --dry-run` / `preview` — report only, no edits

User arguments: $ARGUMENTS

---

## Core Rules

1. **No native interactive HTML** when a design-system primitive exists. `<button>`, raw `<input>`, `<textarea>`, `<select>`, naked checkbox/radio, hand-rolled dialog/sheet — replace with the shared component.
2. **Chrome comes from the primitive's predefined styles.** Read the component's `cva` (`variant`, `size`, `shape`, `appearance`, …). Pick the closest existing key. Do **not** invent a look via `className`.
3. **No style overrides on shared primitives.** `className` / `style` / `style={{…}}` must not set color, background, border, shadow, radius, font, opacity-as-chrome, hover/focus/active/disabled chrome, or `!` important.
4. **`className` allowlist is tiny.** Positioning is allowed. Sizing is allowed only when layout truly requires it (`w-full`, `min-w-0`, `flex-1`) — prefer the `size` prop. Padding, gap, and height that fight the size variant are **overrides** — strip them.
5. **`variant="unstyled"` (or equivalent) + restyle is cheating.** Forbidden unless the file **is** the design-system primitive.
6. **Import from the design-system**, not local clones (`components/ui/button`, `Shared/`, `AtomicDesign/`, numbered `dialog2` / `select4`).
7. **Only edit changed frontend files** (plus the import line if a replacement needs it). Do not restyle unrelated files. Do not touch `.css` / `.scss`.
8. **Idempotent.** Running twice produces no further changes.
9. **Do not run formatters.** Surgical edits only. Do not commit.

---

## Canon map (re-read the live files; this table is a start)

Discover primitives from the repo at run time:

- Future Mortgage CRM: `libs/design-system/src/ui/` imported as `@future-mortgage/design-system/src/ui/<name>`
- Call-site rules: `apps/web-crm/src/app/components/AGENTS.md`
- Runtime stripper (safety net, **looser** than this command): `libs/design-system/src/utils/layout-class-name.ts`

| Native / smell | Shared primitive | Style props |
|---|---|---|
| `<button>` | `Button` | `variant`, `size`, `shape` |
| `<input>` (text-like) | `Input` | `appearance`, `inputSize`, `shape` |
| `<textarea>` | `Textarea` | same family as Input |
| `<select>` | `Select` | `appearance` |
| `<input type="checkbox">` | `Checkbox` | size / variant on that file |
| `<input type="radio">` | `RadioGroup` | |
| `<input type="checkbox">` toggle look | `Switch` | `size` |
| hand-rolled modal | `Dialog` / `AlertDialog` / overlays (`ConfirmDialog`, `FormSheet`, `FormModal`) | |
| hand-rolled drawer | `Sheet` | `overlay` |
| ad-hoc pill / status chip | `Badge` | `variant`, `size`, `shape` |
| local `components/ui/*` clone | design-system `ui/` | |

If the repo is **not** this monorepo, find the equivalent shared UI kit (`src/components/ui`, `packages/ui`, etc.) and apply the same rules against **that** kit's `cva` variants.

---

## Execution Flow

```
1. Resolve target           -> branch OR PR# OR PR URL
2. Collect changed files    -> git diff, frontend only
3. Load primitive catalog   -> each ui/*.tsx: export name, cva keys, pickLayoutClassName?
4. Scan + classify          -> native controls, wrong imports, chrome className, rare sizing
5. Fix                      -> replace natives, set variant props, strip chrome className
6. Report                   -> per-file table + summary
```

---

## Phase 1: Resolve Target

```bash
git branch --show-current
BASE=$(git remote show origin | grep 'HEAD branch' | awk '{print $NF}')
git merge-base HEAD origin/$BASE
```

PR number/URL:

```bash
gh pr view <PR> --json headRefName,baseRefName,headRepository,number
gh pr diff <PR> --name-only
```

Edit locally only if the PR is already checked out; otherwise report from `gh pr diff` (or prompt to check out).

---

## Phase 2: Collect Changed Files

```bash
git diff --name-only $(git merge-base HEAD origin/$BASE)..HEAD \
  | grep -E '\.(tsx|jsx)$' \
  | grep -vE '(\.test\.|\.spec\.|\.stories\.|/node_modules/|/dist/|/build/)'
```

Also include unstaged/uncommitted working-tree changes on those paths (`git diff` + `git diff --cached`).

**Skip (do not "fix" primitives to use themselves):**
- `libs/design-system/src/ui/**` (or the repo's primitive directory)
- files that **are** the shared component definition

Still **scan** those primitive files if they changed: they must own chrome via `cva` and run `pickLayoutClassName` / `pickLayoutStyle` on consumer `className`/`style`. Flag primitives that merge raw `className` into chrome.

---

## Phase 3: Load the Primitive Catalog

For each shared UI module:

1. Exported component names (`Button`, `Input`, …)
2. `cva` variant keys and allowed values (`variant: primary | secondary | …`)
3. Default variants
4. Whether `className` is passed through `pickLayoutClassName`

Build a lookup: tag name / typical class smell → primitive + how to pick a variant.

---

## Phase 4: Classify Violations

Walk JSX in each changed file.

### 4.1 Native control (HIGH)

Flag:

```tsx
<button>…</button>
<input>   <!-- not type=hidden / file / csrf / radio+checkbox already mapped -->
<textarea>
<select>
```

**Allowed natives (do not replace):**
- `<input type="hidden">`, file inputs that are visually hidden behind a `Button`/`Label`
- `<input type="file">` when the visible trigger is already a shared `Button`
- SVG / math / canvas internals
- The primitive's own inner DOM (`button.tsx` rendering `<button>` / `Slot`)

`asChild` on `Button` wrapping an `<a>` is fine. A raw `<button>` wrapping an icon is **not**.

### 4.2 Wrong import (HIGH)

```ts
import { Button } from '@/app/components/ui/button';
import { Button } from '../../components/ui/button';
```

Must be the design-system (or this repo's canon path). Also flag `buttonVariants(...)` applied to a native `<button>`.

### 4.3 Chrome override on a shared primitive (HIGH)

On `<Button>`, `<Input>`, `<Textarea>`, `<SelectTrigger>`, `<Checkbox>`, `<Switch>`, `<Badge>`, and any other primitive that documents layout-only `className`:

**Forbidden tokens** (after stripping `sm:` / `md:` / `lg:` / `xl:` / `2xl:` — state variants like `hover:` / `focus:` / `active:` / `disabled:` / `data-[…]` / `aria-[…]` on chrome are also forbidden):

- Color / chrome: `bg-*`, `text-*` (except `text-left|center|right`), `border*`, `ring-*`, `outline-*`, `shadow-*`, `from-*`, `via-*`, `to-*`, `fill-*`, `stroke-*`, `opacity-*`, `backdrop-*`
- Type: `font-*`, `leading-*`, `tracking-*`, `underline`, `italic`
- Shape chrome: `rounded-*`
- Size-as-chrome: `h-*`, `px-*`, `py-*`, `p-*`, `pt-*`, `gap-*` when the primitive has a `size` / `inputSize` prop — use the prop
- `!` important on any of the above
- Inline `style` keys outside the layout set: `color`, `background*`, `border*`, `font*`, `boxShadow`, `opacity`, `borderRadius`, …

**Allowed positioning:**

`static` `relative` `absolute` `fixed` `sticky`  
`top-*` `right-*` `bottom-*` `left-*` `inset-*` `z-*`  
`m-*` `mx-*` `my-*` `mt-*` `mb-*` `ml-*` `mr-*` `ms-*` `me-*`  
`self-*` `justify-self-*` `place-self-*` `order-*`  
`col-span-*` `col-start-*` `row-span-*`  
`translate-*` `transform` (overlay alignment only)

**Rarely allowed sizing** (keep, but list under "Rare sizing" in the report — do not add new ones unless layout is broken without them):

`w-full` `w-auto` `min-w-0` `max-w-*` `flex-1` `flex-none` `grow` `shrink-0`

Any other `w-*` / `h-*` / `size-*` / `min-h-*` on a primitive → strip or map to `size` / `inputSize`. If mapping is unclear, flag and do not guess a one-off pixel size.

### 4.4 Missing / invalid predefined style (MEDIUM)

- Primitive used with no `variant` / `appearance` when the visual is clearly not the default (e.g. a ghost/icon/destructive look implemented via leftover classes)
- `variant="something-not-in-cva"`
- Closest existing variant exists but caller used chrome classes instead

Map leftover chrome to a real key (examples — **always re-read the live `cva`**):

| Smell | Typical Button fix |
|---|---|
| accent / primary fill | `variant="primary"` |
| zinc/dark fill | `variant="secondary"` |
| border + transparent | `variant="outline"` or `glass` |
| no fill, hover wash | `variant="ghost"` |
| red fill | `variant="destructive"` |
| red ghost | `variant="destructive-ghost"` |
| underline text | `variant="link"` |
| icon-only, ~24px | `size="icon-sm"` |
| icon-only, ~40px | `size="icon"` |
| compact toolbar | `size="xs"` or `sm` |
| uppercase tracking | `size="action"` |
| pill | `shape="pill"` |

### 4.5 Primitive definition regression (HIGH, only if those files changed)

Changed files under the shared UI kit must:
- Define chrome in `cva` (or a shared styles helper), not at each call site
- Pipe consumer `className` through `pickLayoutClassName`
- Pipe consumer `style` through `pickLayoutStyle`

Do **not** widen `pickLayoutClassName` to allow chrome so a call site "works".

---

## Phase 5: Apply Fixes

For each HIGH/MEDIUM finding that has a clear fix:

1. **Replace native `<button>`** with `<Button …>` (same `type`, `onClick`, `disabled`, `aria-*`, children). Add the canon import if missing. Remove now-unused imports.
2. **Same for Input / Textarea / Select / Checkbox / Switch / Badge** when the mapping is 1:1.
3. **Set** `variant` / `size` / `shape` / `appearance` from the catalog. Delete the chrome classes those props replace.
4. **Strip** remaining forbidden tokens from `className`. If `className` becomes empty, remove the prop.
5. **Strip** forbidden `style` keys. If empty, remove `style`.
6. **Rewrite** wrong imports to the canon path.

**Do not auto-fix** (report only):
- A control whose closest primitive is unclear (custom segmented control, canvas toolbar, contenteditable)
- A file that would need a **new** design-system variant — propose the variant name + `cva` snippet, do not invent it in the call site
- > 20 replacements in one file — show the plan, ask before applying

Never use `Write` to rewrite a whole file. `Edit` only.

---

## Phase 6: Report

```
### apps/web-crm/src/.../foo.tsx

| Line | Finding | Action |
|------|---------|--------|
| 42 | native `<button>` | → `<Button variant="ghost" size="icon-sm">` |
| 58 | `<Button className="bg-red-500 text-white">` | stripped chrome; `variant="destructive"` |
| 73 | `<Button className="h-12 px-8">` | stripped size override; `size="lg"` |
| 91 | `<Button className="absolute right-2">` | kept (positioning) |
| 104 | `<Button className="w-full">` | kept (rare sizing) |
```

```
## Summary
- Files scanned: N
- Files modified: M
- Natives replaced: B buttons, I inputs, …
- Chrome classNames stripped: K
- Rare sizing left in place: R
- Needs new DS variant (not invented): …
- Skipped / needs human: …
```

`--dry-run` / `preview` → report only.

---

## Safety Rails

| Situation | Action |
|---|---|
| No frontend files in the diff | Stop. Say so. |
| File is the primitive itself | Do not replace inner DOM. Check `cva` + `pickLayoutClassName` only. |
| Merge conflict markers | Skip file. |
| Hidden file input + visible Button | Leave the hidden input. |
| `asChild` + `<a>` / router `Link` | Leave the child element. |
| Unclear mapping / new look | Report + propose a DS variant. Do not chrome-override. |
| User said dry-run / preview | Report only. |

---

## What This Command Does NOT Do

- Does not run `/fix-tailwind` (token snap is a different command). After this pass, remaining layout classes should already be config tokens.
- Does not add new design-system variants unless the user explicitly asks.
- Does not restyle page-level layout wrappers (`div`, `section`, `main`) — only native controls and shared primitive call sites.
- Does not commit or push.
````

#### `~/.ai/commands/create-command/SKILL.md`

````markdown file=~/.ai/commands/create-command/SKILL.md
---
name: create-command
description: Interactively create a new slash command or skill in the shared Agent Skills format and link it into every agent harness (Claude Code, OpenCode, Grok, Pi, DeepSeek Harness). Use when the user runs /create-command.
disable-model-invocation: true
---

# /create-command

Create a new command or skill on disk, in the one format every harness reads.

## Step 1: Ask

Ask these one at a time, as plain conversation. Do not use option pickers for free-text answers.

1. **Name**: lowercase letters, digits, and single hyphens; starts and ends with a letter or digit; at most 64 characters (for example `deploy-k8s`). Run `ls ~/.ai/skills ~/.ai/commands` and reject a name that is already taken.
2. **Who starts it**:
   - **Command**: only the user, by typing `/<name>`. It goes in `~/.ai/commands/<name>/`.
   - **Skill**: the agent may also load it on its own when a task matches its description. It goes in `~/.ai/skills/<name>/`.
3. **Scope**: **User** (every project; the default) or **Project** (this repo only).
4. **What it should do**: the workflow, an example prompt, or the task to automate.

## Step 2: Draft the description

Write one or two sentences: what it does, then when to use it. For a skill, name the phrases that should trigger it, because the agent decides from this text. Keep it under 1024 characters. Show the draft and let the user approve or edit it.

## Step 3: Write SKILL.md

| Scope | Path |
|-------|------|
| User | `~/.ai/commands/<name>/SKILL.md` or `~/.ai/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` |
| Project | `<repo-root>/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` |

```markdown
---
name: <name>
description: <approved description>
disable-model-invocation: true
---

<instructions: steps, commands, code blocks>
```

Keep `disable-model-invocation: true` for a command and delete that line for a skill.

Format rules:

- Quote the description, or use `>-`, when it contains `: `. Invalid YAML makes DeepSeek Harness drop the entry without any message.
- Do not add `agent`, `model`, or `context`; harnesses read those fields differently.
- Put helper files next to SKILL.md in `scripts/`, `references/`, or `assets/`. Refer to them by path relative to the skill folder, or by the full `~/.ai/...` path.
- Only Claude Code replaces `$ARGUMENTS`. The other harnesses add what the user typed after the instructions, so write steps that work either way, such as "the PR number the user gave".

## Step 4: Link it

**User scope:** run `ai-sync`. It checks the new entry (name, description, valid YAML, and that the folder matches the `disable-model-invocation` flag), then links it into every harness and writes its OpenCode command file. If it reports a problem, fix SKILL.md and run it again.

**Project scope:** link it for Claude Code, which reads only `.claude/skills`:

```bash
mkdir -p <repo-root>/.claude/skills
ln -s ../../.agents/skills/<name> <repo-root>/.claude/skills/<name>
```

For `/<name>` in OpenCode, also write `<repo-root>/.opencode/commands/<name>.md`:

```markdown
---
description: <approved description>
---

Load the "<name>" skill with the skill tool, then follow it exactly.

User arguments: $ARGUMENTS
```

## Step 5: Confirm

Read the file back, then tell the user how to run it:

- Claude Code, OpenCode, Grok, DeepSeek Harness: `/<name> [arguments]`
- Pi: `/skill:<name> [arguments]`

Claude Code, OpenCode, and Grok pick it up right away. Pi needs `/reload`, and DeepSeek Harness needs a new session.
````

#### `~/.ai/commands/fix-merge-conflicts/SKILL.md`

````markdown file=~/.ai/commands/fix-merge-conflicts/SKILL.md
---
name: fix-merge-conflicts
description: Fetches origin/main into the current branch and resolves each conflict one file at a time, keeping this branch's style and behavior. Always creates a code-only git worktree first (same as /worktree-quick; yarn install is mandatory) so /fix-merge-conflicts does not need a prior /worktree-quick. Use when user says "/fix-merge-conflicts", "/fix-merge-conflicts 1234", "fix merge conflicts", "resolve conflicts", "merge main", or "pull main and resolve".
disable-model-invocation: true
---

# /fix-merge-conflicts - Merge Main & Resolve Conflicts

Fetches `origin/main` (or `master`) into the **current feature branch**, then resolves **each conflicted file one at a time**. Keep the style and function of **our** changes (the branch we are working on). Integrate incoming main only when it is required for the result to compile and stay correct.

**Usage:** `/fix-merge-conflicts [PR number | PR URL | branch]`

`/fix-merge-conflicts 1234` is enough — this skill creates the code-only worktree itself. Do **not** require a prior `/worktree-quick`. **Yarn install is mandatory** on every worktree (create, reuse, already-isolated).

User arguments: $ARGUMENTS

---

## Core Philosophy

- **Ours is the feature.** The current branch's intent, naming, structure, and behavior win. Do not throw away work we are shipping.
- **Main is the platform.** Take incoming API renames, shared-type changes, schema updates, and infra that our code must call. Adapt **our** code to the new platform — do not revert our feature to match old main.
- **One file at a time.** Never bulk `--ours` / `--theirs`. Read, understand both sides, write a single coherent file, then `git add` it before touching the next.
- **Fail loud.** If a hunk cannot be resolved with confidence, stop on that file and ask. Wrong quiet success is worse than a paused merge.

---

## Execution Flow

```
0. Code-only worktree     -> /worktree-quick script + yarn + session_move (always)
1. Safety checks          -> repo, branch, dirty tree, mid-merge/rebase
2. Detect default branch  -> main or master
3. Fetch + merge main     -> into current branch (not the other way around)
4. Inventory conflicts    -> list every unmerged path
5. Resolve file-by-file   -> ours style/function; adapt to main's platform
6. Verify                 -> no markers / no unmerged paths (not typecheck/tests)
7. Complete merge commit  -> only the merge commit; do not push
8. Report                 -> files, decisions, leftover risk
```

---

## Phase 0: Code-only worktree (always, before any work)

Work **never** runs in the primary checkout. Isolate first with the same script as `/worktree-quick`, then merge/resolve in that worktree. **Do not** wait for `/worktree-quick`. **Do not** use `/monorepo-worktree`. **Do not** stop after create.

**Yarn is mandatory on every worktree.** Create, reuse, and already-isolated all require `yarn install` in the worktree with exit 0 (10 min timeout). Never skip because `node_modules` exists. Never skip on reuse. If the create script already ran yarn in this turn and you watched it exit 0, that create counts; reuse / already-isolated **must still yarn**.

User arguments: `$ARGUMENTS`

### Parse target

| TARGET | Action |
|--------|--------|
| PR / URL | `~/.ai/skills/worktree-quick/scripts/quick-worktree.sh <n-or-url>` |
| Branch / ref | `…/quick-worktree.sh <ref>` |
| Empty | `gh pr view --json number -q .number`. If that fails and cwd is already `*-quick-*`, skip create. Else if current branch is not `main`/`master`, worktree that branch. Else ask for a PR number. |

Remember `PR_NUMBER`. Do **not** merge main into the primary checkout.

### Create or reuse

Do **not** hand-roll `git worktree add`. Skip create only if cwd is already a matching `*-quick-*` worktree. If path already exists: **reuse**. If reusing and **dirty**, do not `reset --hard`.

### Yarn (always)

```bash
(cd "<path>" && yarn install)
```

Reuse / already-isolated: **always** run this. Wait for exit 0.

### Move the session, then work

OpenCode: `tools.opencode.session_move` with `directory` = absolute worktree path. Continue this session. Then **immediately** continue. Do **not** destroy the worktree when finished.

---

## Phase 1: Safety Checks

```bash
git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree
git branch --show-current
git status --porcelain=v1
git rev-parse -q --verify MERGE_HEAD
git rev-parse -q --verify REBASE_HEAD
git rev-parse -q --verify CHERRY_PICK_HEAD
```

**Hard stops:**

| Condition | Action |
|-----------|--------|
| Not a git repo | Stop |
| Current branch is `main` or `master` | Stop. Never merge "our work" by updating main in place. User must be on a feature branch. |
| Detached HEAD | Stop and ask |
| Unrelated dirty files that are **not** part of an in-progress merge/rebase | Stop and ask whether to stash. Do not stash silently. |
| `REBASE_HEAD` or `CHERRY_PICK_HEAD` present | Do **not** start a new merge. Continue that operation (Phase 4+) or ask if the user meant a merge instead. |
| `MERGE_HEAD` already present | Skip fetch/merge. Resume at Phase 4. |

`$ARGUMENTS` may name a base branch (e.g. `develop`). Use that instead of main/master when given.

---

## Phase 2: Detect Default Branch

If `$ARGUMENTS` is empty:

```bash
git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD 2>/dev/null
git rev-parse --verify origin/main
git rev-parse --verify origin/master
```

Prefer `origin/HEAD` → else `origin/main` → else `origin/master`. Call this `BASE`. Never invent a remote branch.

---

## Phase 3: Fetch and Merge Base Into Current Branch

```bash
git fetch origin
git merge --no-edit "origin/<BASE>"
```

- Merge **base into current branch**. Do not checkout base. Do not reset. Do not rebase unless the user explicitly asked to rebase.
- If the merge is already complete (fast-forward or clean merge): report that there is nothing to resolve and stop. Do not create extra commits.
- If git refuses (local changes, unborn branch, etc.): show the full error and stop. Do not force.

---

## Phase 4: Inventory Conflicts

```bash
git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U
git status
```

For each unmerged path, record the conflict type:

```bash
git ls-files -u
```

| Index stages | Meaning |
|--------------|---------|
| stages 1,2,3 | both modified (normal) |
| stages 2,3 only | both added |
| stage 2 only | deleted by them, modified by us |
| stage 3 only | deleted by us, modified by them |

Build a TodoWrite list: one item per conflicted file, plus a final verify item. Mark the first file `in_progress`.

If there are zero unmerged paths after the merge, skip to Phase 7.

---

## Phase 5: Resolve One File at a Time

Process files **serially**. Finish and `git add` file N before opening file N+1.

### 5.1 Read both sides (do not guess)

For a normal both-modified file:

```bash
git show :2:"<path>"   # ours  — current branch
git show :3:"<path>"   # theirs — incoming base
git show :1:"<path>"   # base ancestor (when present)
```

Also read the working-tree file (conflict markers) and nearby non-conflicted files for style.

For delete/add special cases, inspect `git log --oneline -5 -- <path>` on both `HEAD` and `MERGE_HEAD` before choosing keep vs delete.

### 5.2 Resolution rules (ours wins on product; theirs wins on platform)

**Keep ours when the hunk is:**

- New feature code, new UI, new tests, new routes, new domain logic
- Naming, formatting, import order, component structure we introduced
- Control flow we wrote (error handling, status machines, authz)
- Comments we added or removed as part of this work

**Take or adapt to theirs when the hunk is:**

- Shared type/API/schema that our new code must call
- Import path or symbol rename on a dependency we use
- Lockfile / generated Prisma client / codegen — regenerate rather than hand-merge
- Config that would leave the branch unable to boot against current main

**Never:**

- `git checkout --ours -- <file>` or `--theirs` for a whole source file
- Leave conflict markers
- Soft-merge by concatenating both blocks "to be safe"
- Invent APIs that exist on neither side
- Hand-write Prisma DDL or "fix" a generated migration to make the merge succeed
- Resolve binary files without asking

**Prisma / migrations:** if `schema.prisma` or a generated migration conflicts, **stop and ask**. Do not edit generated SQL to paper over drift.

**Lockfiles (`yarn.lock`, `package-lock.json`, `bun.lock`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`):** pick one package manager from the repo, take a coherent tree, then regenerate the lockfile with the project's install command. Do not hand-edit lockfile conflict hunks.

**Generated files:** regenerate (`prisma generate`, nx codegen, etc.) after resolving the source of truth.

### 5.3 Write the resolved file

Produce one clean file that:

1. Preserves our feature's behavior and local style (match surrounding code on **this** branch).
2. Compiles against main's types/exports/APIs.
3. Contains no `<<<<<<<`, `=======`, `>>>>>>>`.

Then:

```bash
git add -- "<path>"
```

Mark that todo `completed` and move to the next file.

### 5.4 Stop conditions (ask the user)

Pause before `git add` if:

- Both sides added the same symbol with different contracts
- Delete vs modify and the feature still needs the file
- Binary or asset conflict
- Migration / schema conflict
- You cannot tell which side is "our feature" vs "platform"
- Resolving would require rewriting more than this file in a way you cannot verify

Show both sides briefly and wait.

---

## Phase 6: Verify

After every path is staged:

```bash
git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U
rg -n '^(<<<<<<<|=======|>>>>>>>)' .
```

If any markers or unmerged paths remain, go back to Phase 5. Do not continue.

Do **not** run typecheck, tests, lint, format, or build here. `/pr` push runs `.husky/pre-push`, which is the CI gate. If the merge would fail CI, the hook will block the push with the failing job's output.

---

## Phase 7: Complete the Merge

A merge in progress is not done until the merge commit exists. Create **only** that merge commit:

```bash
git status
git log --oneline -5
git commit --no-edit
```

- Use the default merge message unless it is empty/broken.
- Do **not** `git add` unrelated untracked files.
- Do **not** push.
- Do **not** commit extra "fixup" commits.
- No `Co-Authored-By` trailer. No `--no-verify` unless the user asked.

If `git commit` is rejected by a hook, fix the hook failure (it is often leftover markers or lint) and commit again. Do not `--no-verify`.

---

## Phase 8: Summary

```markdown
## Merge conflict summary

**Branch**: [current] ← **origin/[base]**
**Merge commit**: [sha] (or still in progress if stopped)

### Resolved
| File | Decision |
|------|----------|
| src/foo.ts | Kept our handler; updated import to main's renamed `authorizeX` |

### Stopped / needs you
| File | Why |
|------|-----|

### Verification
| Check | Result |
|-------|--------|
| Conflict markers / unmerged paths | [clean / still open] |
| CI (typecheck/test/build/format) | not run here — pre-push on `/pr` |

### Residual risk
[lockfile regenerated?, migrations? CI runs on `/pr` push]
```

---

## Error Handling

| Error | Action |
|-------|--------|
| On main/master | Stop |
| Fetch/merge refused | Show full git output; stop |
| Already merging | Resume Phase 4; do not start a second merge |
| Mid-rebase and user asked to merge | Ask which operation to finish |
| Cannot resolve a file | Leave it unmerged, report, wait |
| Hook rejects merge commit | Fix the cause; no `--no-verify` |
| Prisma/migration conflict | Stop and ask |

---

## Important Rules

1. **Never merge by checking out main and pulling the feature in.** Always merge base → current branch.
2. **Never `--ours` / `--theirs` a source file wholesale.**
3. **One file at a time.** Add it before opening the next.
4. **Keep our style and function.** Adapt callsites to main; do not rewrite the feature to look like main.
5. **No silent leftovers.** Conflict markers or unmerged paths at the end is a failed run.
6. **Do not push. Do not touch main.**
7. **Do not commit anything except the merge commit** this command creates.
8. **Fail hard** when unsure — ask.
9. **Always isolate in a code-only worktree first** (Phase 0). Never merge main into the primary checkout. **Yarn install is mandatory** on every worktree (create, reuse, already-isolated). Never skip yarn because `node_modules` exists.
````

````markdown file=~/.ai/commands/grill-me/SKILL.md
# /grill-me

Interview the user relentlessly until you reach a shared understanding. Map this as a **design tree**: every decision branches into the decisions that hang off it.

Topic: `$ARGUMENTS` (or the current conversation if arguments are empty). Do **not** implement, spec, or ticket anything until the user confirms shared understanding.

## Rounds and the frontier

Work the tree in **rounds**. The **frontier** is every decision whose prerequisites are already settled: the questions you can ask *now* without guessing at answers you have not heard yet.

Ask the **whole frontier** in one round. Number each question and give your recommended answer. Then **wait** for the user's answers before the next round.

A question whose answer depends on another question still open in this round belongs to a *later* round, not this one.

Each round the user answers reshapes the tree: settled decisions push the frontier outward and unblock questions that depended on them. Recompute the frontier and ask the next round.

## Round format

Use this markdown in the conversation. Do **not** use the structured Question tool — design questions need paragraphs and a recommended answer.

```
❓ **Q1** - **<question title>**: <question body, might be multiple paragraphs, including multiple choices>

➡️ <your recommended answer>

---

❓ **Q2** - **<question title>**: <question body, might be multiple paragraphs, including multiple choices>

➡️ <your recommended answer>
```

## Facts vs decisions

Finding **facts** is your job, never the user's. When a frontier question needs a fact from the environment (filesystem, git, code, docs), dispatch a sub-agent to find it; don't ask the user for anything you could look up yourself. Don't block on it: a running exploration is an unsettled prerequisite, so only the questions downstream of it wait for the sub-agent to report; ask the rest of the frontier now.

The **decisions** are the user's: put each to them and wait.

## Done

The session is done when the frontier is empty: every branch of the design tree visited, nothing left silently assumed.

Then:

1. Restate the settled tree in a short recap (decisions + rejected alternatives).
2. Wait for the user to confirm shared understanding.
3. Do **not** act on it until they confirm. After confirm, stop unless they ask to implement (`/peer-review`, `/pr`, etc.).
````

```markdown file=~/.ai/commands/in-my-voice/SKILL.md
# /in-my-voice

Rewrite the user's input as a LinkedIn post in **Martin's voice**, dialed up to a **hard caricature**. Do not soften. Do not generic-LinkedIn-ify. Emulate the posts below so hard it almost parodies them while still sounding like a real human who ships.

## Input

User arguments (the draft to rewrite):

$ARGUMENTS

If `$ARGUMENTS` is empty, ask once for the text block. Then rewrite. Do not chat first.

## Output rules

1. Output **only** the rewritten post. No preamble, no "here's the rewrite", no analysis, no alternatives unless asked.
2. Preserve the user's facts, links, metrics, product names, and claims. Do not invent metrics, employers, or results.
3. You may invent **rhetorical structure**, hooks, reframes, and closing questions. Not biography.
4. Length: usually 120–280 words. Shorter for OTW blurbs. Longer only if the source is dense build-log material.
5. Hashtags: only if the draft is clearly open-to-work or the user included them. Match their tag style: `hashtag#Tag` lines at the end, 4–6 max. Otherwise omit.
6. Emoji: rare. `🚨` only for multi-incident news openers. No 🚀 💪 🔥 walls.
7. No em-dash addiction. Prefer periods, colons, and short sentences. Occasional comma or semicolon is fine. Em dashes sparingly if at all.
8. No corporate sludge: "excited to share", "thrilled", "leveraging", "delve", "landscape", "robust", "seamless", "game-changer", "I'm humbled".
9. No fake vulnerability essays. Confidence with receipts. Curiosity at the end.

---

## Voice DNA (caricature dial: 11)

### Opening hook (always)

Lead with a **short, slightly wrong-sounding or counterintuitive line**. Then a staccato punch.

Patterns to steal:

- Claim. Not a little. Fundamentally.
- I built X, and its best feature is Y. (Y is the opposite of what demos show)
- I started X this week. There's no X yet.
- Every fresh session starts with total amnesia.
- X has a cruel timing problem, and I think about it constantly.
- So believe me when I say this: [uncomfortable industry claim].
- Here's the strange place [field] is in right now:
- [Person] said X. Then they said the opposite. I think that's kind of a big deal?

First line does the work. No throat-clearing.

### The reframe (the signature move)

After the hook, kill the obvious read:

- "Here's the thing most people miss:"
- "Here's what most people miss:"
- "The usual read is X. I think that's only half the story."
- "The failures aren't the story. The detection is."
- "It's not that the models don't know X. It's that X lives in the gap between..."
- "What's actually happening is..."

Name the lazy narrative. Replace it with a sharper one. This is non-negotiable in the caricature.

### Proof with dirt under the nails

Then get specific. Prefer:

- Concrete stack: Next.js, TypeScript, pgvector, Claude, local models vs cloud
- Named behaviors: refusals scored in CI, hit@5, MRR, kill switch, hash-diffed re-syncs
- Process truths: eval harness gates PRs, docs the agent must re-read, intentionally broken test messages
- Honest limits: "I don't have a clean answer", "least impressive robot ever", "honesty-boundaries doc"

Judgment > output. Taste. Evals. Documentation an amnesiac expert can execute. Encoding intent so the code is obvious.

### Sentence music

- Mix one-word-punch fragments with longer analytical sentences.
- "Not X. Y."
- "Not fewer engineering jobs. A different job."
- "Refusals aren't a failure mode here. They're a scored behavior."
- "The demo looks perfect. Ship it." (as the thing you're attacking)
- "Wrong state with a quiet success is worse than a loud failure" energy without quoting that line.
- Parenthetical asides used lightly.
- Questions that are actually questions, not engagement bait cosplay — but yes, end with one.

### Closing

Almost always:

1. One-line uncomfortable takeaway or "real shift"
2. A genuine peer question ("What's your X look like?", "What did building Y teach you that the tutorials didn't?", "Are you building now or timing the curve?")

OTW posts: clear ask, stack, clearance if relevant, DMs/referrals, hashtags. Still hook-first when possible ("Anyone else have LinkedIn fatigue?").

### Thematic obsessions (lean into these when the draft touches them)

- AI fails at intent / completeness / follow-through, not typing code
- Evals are the product; shipping on vibes is the enemy
- Refusal and hard boundaries as features
- Accessibility debt at industrial scale; checklists models can't charm past
- Repo memory beats model memory (filing cabinet / constitution)
- One brain, many bodies / orchestration is the product
- Design eng = encoding intent; Figma/spec quality mirrors output quality
- Mid-career value = taste + shipping with AI, not alongside it
- Build in public with decision logs and rejected alternatives
- Respect people who admit they were wrong out loud

### Caricature amplifiers (use freely)

Turn these knobs up past polite:

- One killer reframe per post, stated like it's obvious once said
- At least one staccato triplet or double period punch early
- At least one "most people miss" / "usual read is wrong" move
- Specificity theater: name the boring mechanism (deterministic chunk IDs, commands that expire if late, rubric item that scores refusal)
- End on craft identity, not hype
- Sound like someone who grades agents for a living and builds robots on weekends — because that is the bit

### Anti-patterns (never)

- LinkedIn-bro swagger or guru thread energy
- "5 things I learned" listicles unless the source is already a list
- Starting with "I'm excited to announce"
- Apologetic soft openers
- Over-explaining the joke
- Hashtag stuffing on thought posts
- Emoji bullet salads
- Sounding like ChatGPT wearing a flannel

---

## Worked style fragments (internal reference — do not paste these back)

Hook + punch:

> Connecting Claude Code to Figma changed how I ship UI. Not a little. Fundamentally.

Reframe:

> Here's the thing most people miss: AI coding tools don't fail because they can't write code. They fail because they're guessing at intent.

Inversion feature:

> I built a chatbot, and its best feature is refusing to answer.

Process as product:

> Evals aren't a checkbox anymore. They're the product.

Uncomfortable takeaway:

> The skill that actually determines your output quality with coding agents isn't prompting. It's writing documentation an amnesiac expert can execute perfectly.

Respect + understatement:

> I think that's kind of a big deal? Not because of who was right, but because he had to eat the earlier tweet to say it.

Build-log honesty:

> I started building a robot this week. There's no robot yet.

Industry knife:

> We are shipping accessibility debt at industrial scale.

---

## Mode selection

Infer from the draft:

| Draft smells like | Mode |
|---|---|
| Shipping a project, metrics, repo, demo link | **Build log** — hook on the surprising feature, evals/process pride, try-it CTA + craft question |
| Hot take on AI/hiring/tools/news | **Thesis** — hook, kill usual read, reframe, light proof, uncomfortable takeaway, peer question |
| Robot / physical AI / side project | **Workshop** — slightly wry, systems lesson, day-job transfer, glue-on-desk energy |
| Open to work / role search | **OTW** — human, direct, receipts (years, stack, clearance, 508 record if present), clear ask, hashtags |
| Agency / studio / accessibility pitch | **Studio** — market math opener, proof, what you build, link in comments energy |
| Short gripe / fatigue | **Blade** — keep it short, one cut, then the pitch if present |

If mixed, prefer **Thesis** skeleton with **Build log** specifics.

---

## Procedure

1. Read the draft. Extract: core claim, proof points, must-keep facts/links, mode.
2. Write a new hook that could only open this post.
3. Plant the reframe.
4. Fold proof in as lived detail, not a resume dump (unless OTW).
5. Land the takeaway + question (or OTW ask).
6. Read once as caricature check: if it could be anyone's post, punch harder. If it invents facts, strip them.
7. Output the post only.

## Optional flags in $ARGUMENTS

If the user prefixes with a flag, honor it:

- `tight:` — under ~100 words
- `otw:` — force open-to-work mode
- `thesis:` — force take mode
- `build:` — force build-log mode
- `wild:` — maximum caricature (even punchier hooks, harder reframes)

Strip the flag from the content before rewriting.
```

#### `~/.ai/commands/manual-review/SKILL.md`

````markdown file=~/.ai/commands/manual-review/SKILL.md
---
name: manual-review
description: 'Pulls a PR or branch into a code-only git worktree (same as /worktree-quick — fetch + checkout, env copy, yarn install; no DB/ports/seed), studies the diff deeply, then writes a review brief: the problem the PR solves, the fix, every change grouped by app (income app, funnel, CRM) and by backend area (Freddie Mac, Fannie Mae, messaging, income, AI, and so on), plus regressions, gaps, UI that is not wired to the backend, and schema changes. Use when the user runs /manual-review, /manual-review 1234, /manual-review <pr-url>, /manual-review <branch>, or says "manual review", "walk me through this PR", "what does this PR change", "review this PR for me by hand", or "what did this PR break". Read-only: never edits, commits, pushes, or posts to GitHub (that is /pr-review). Do not require a prior /worktree-quick.'
disable-model-invocation: true
---

# /manual-review — What this PR changes, and what to watch out for

The user is about to review this PR by hand. Read the code closely enough to explain, in plain words, what problem it solves, what it changed, and what it may have broken or left half-done.

This is **not** a code review with severity levels and GitHub comments; `/pr-review` does that. This report tells the user where to look and what to be suspicious of. Anything suspicious goes in the five closing sections.

**Usage:** `/manual-review [PR number | PR URL | branch]`

User arguments: `$ARGUMENTS`

## Hard rules

1. **Worktree first.** Read the PR's code only from a code-only worktree (Phase 0). Never read it from the primary checkout, and never require a prior `/worktree-quick`.
2. **Every changed file is accounted for.** Each path in the diff appears in at least one change bullet. Tests, lockfiles, and generated files may share one grouped bullet. Run the coverage check before sending.
3. **The summary comes from the code, not the PR description.** Use the description, commits, and tickets to understand intent and to quote why a choice was made, but confirm every claim against the diff. When the body and the code disagree, say so — that is a gap.
4. **A regression claim needs a before and after.** Name the screen or call path, what it did on the base branch, what it does now, and the file that proves it. "Might affect other screens" is not a finding.
5. **No invented reasons.** Every "why" names its source: PR description, linked issue, commit message, code comment, PRD, or _inferred from the code_. If nothing explains a choice, write "Not explained in the PR" and put it under Gaps.
6. **Write for the user.** Follow "How to explain things to me" in `~/.ai/AGENTS.md`: answer first, spell out acronyms once, no dev slang, say what each named thing does, full sentences, concrete before abstract. Terse reply modes do not apply to this report.
7. **Read-only.** Do not edit code, commit, push, post to GitHub, or destroy the worktree.

## Phase 0: Worktree and PR context (in parallel)

### Parse the target

| Token                                                 | Meaning                                                                                                                                              |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `1234` / `#1234` / `pr 1234` / GitHub `.../pull/1234` | PR                                                                                                                                                   |
| `feature/foo` / `origin/foo` / other git ref          | Branch. Look for its PR: `gh pr list --head <branch> --json number,url -q '.[0]'`                                                                    |
| Empty                                                 | `gh pr view --json number -q .number`. If that fails and cwd is already a `*-quick-*` worktree, use it (skip create). Otherwise ask for a PR number. |

Remember `PR_NUMBER`. Every later `gh` call uses it, because the local branch will be `quick/pr-N`, which GitHub does not know.

### Create the worktree (in the background)

Script: `~/.ai/skills/worktree-quick/scripts/quick-worktree.sh <target>`, run from the repo the user is talking about. It fetches, adds `../worktrees/<repo>-quick-<slug>` on branch `quick/<slug>`, copies `.env*`, and runs `yarn install`. Do not hand-roll `git worktree add`.

- **Claude Code:** run the script yourself in the background from the repo root, and keep gathering PR context while it installs. On `worktree path already exists: <path>`, reuse that path: run `git fetch origin pull/<N>/head && git -C <path> reset --hard FETCH_HEAD` (or `origin/<branch>` for a branch), then `(cd <path> && yarn install)`. Wait for exit 0 before reading code from the worktree.
- **OpenCode:** run the script in the background with `cd <repo> && ~/.ai/skills/worktree-quick/scripts/quick-worktree.sh <target>`, keep reading while it installs, and call `session_move` to the path once it exists.
- **Already isolated** (cwd is the matching `*-quick-*` worktree): fetch + `reset --hard` to the latest PR SHA, then `yarn install`.

If the create fails for any other reason, stop, show the output verbatim, and do not fall back to the primary checkout.

### Gather PR context while the worktree builds

None of this needs the worktree:

```bash
gh pr view $PR_NUMBER --json number,title,url,body,author,baseRefName,headRefName,headRefOid,closingIssuesReferences,labels,commits
gh pr view $PR_NUMBER --comments
gh api "repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/$PR_NUMBER/comments" --paginate \
  --jq '.[] | {path, line, user: .user.login, body}'
```

Then follow what the body references:

- Linked GitHub issues: `gh issue view <N> --json title,body,comments`.
- Linear tickets (`TRY-33` style IDs): fetch with the Linear MCP `get_issue` when it is available.
- PRDs or docs the body mentions (`docs/prd/...`): read them from the worktree once it exists.

From here on, every git command, Read, and Grep targets the worktree path, using absolute paths or `git -C <path>`.

## Phase 1: Diff

Diff from the **merge base**, so commits already on the base branch do not show up as the PR's work:

```bash
BASE=$(gh pr view $PR_NUMBER --json baseRefName -q .baseRefName)   # no PR: origin's default branch
git -C <path> fetch origin "$BASE"
MB=$(git -C <path> merge-base HEAD "origin/$BASE")
git -C <path> diff --stat "$MB"..HEAD
git -C <path> diff --name-status "$MB"..HEAD
git -C <path> log --reverse --format='%h %s%n%b' "$MB"..HEAD
git -C <path> diff "$MB"..HEAD -- <file or folder>
```

Read the files in this order, because later files make more sense once you have seen the earlier ones: schema and migrations → backend services and routers → worker jobs → UI → tests → config.

For a large PR (roughly 40+ files or 8+ separate frontend areas), fan out `Explore` subagents for the mechanical tracing (which screens render a component, which callers use a tRPC procedure), one per area. Give each the worktree path, its file list, `~/.ai/commands/manual-review/references/future-monorepo-frontend-map.md`, and the exact question. You still write the report.

## Phase 2: The problem and the fix

Write these before the change list; they set the frame.

**The problem** answers: who hits it, what do they do, and what goes wrong today? Derive it from the code plus the linked issue, not from the PR title. Two to four sentences. Use the shape "Before: <person> does <action> and <wrong result>."

- If the PR is a feature rather than a bug fix, describe the missing capability the same way: "Today the loan officer can see X but cannot Y."
- If the PR fixes something that only breaks under a condition (a vendor's format, a tenant type, a flag, an old record), name the condition.
- If the code and body tell different stories about the problem, say so here and repeat it under Gaps.

**The fix** answers: what happens now that did not before? Two to four sentences, user-visible behavior first, then the mechanism in plain words. Example: "The calculation page now sends Freddie Mac the same wage file its test binder expects. Internally, the request builder was rewritten to read one line per paystub row instead of the old summary fields."

Do not restate the change list here. The fix is the one idea; the list is the detail.

## Phase 3: The change inventory, grouped by project

One bullet per change a person would describe as "a thing that changed", not one per file. Include the files after the description and keep each bullet to one or two lines.

Bucket every changed path, using this repo's layout:

| Bucket       | Paths                                                                                                                          |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Income app   | `apps/web-income/**`, `libs/income/domain/*-ui/**`                                                                             |

## Phase 4: The four checks

Do these against the worktree and the base branch. Each check produces either findings or an explicit "nothing found, here is what I checked" line — silence reads as "not checked" to the user.

### 4.1 Regressions (frontend, and anything that feeds a screen)

The question is: what worked on the base branch and does not work now? Intentional behavior changes count too, marked `(intentional)` — the user wants to see them either way.

For each changed frontend file:

1. **Find every renderer, not just the changed one.** Search the exported name and the import path across `apps/` and `libs/`, including barrel re-exports and `lazy(() => import(...))`. A change to a shared component or to `libs/design-system` can hit screens the PR never mentions.
2. **Compare props and defaults against the base.** `git -C <path> show "$MB:<file>"` gives the old version. A new required prop, a changed default, a changed label, a reordered list, or a removed export can break callers that still pass the old shape.
3. **Check every caller of a changed tRPC procedure.** Grep `.routerName.procedureName` in `apps/` and `libs/`. Input that is now required, output fields that were renamed or omitted, and status values that no longer exist all break screens that were not touched.
4. **Check every reader of a changed database field.** List, detail, export, PDF, funnel, worker, analytics. A renamed or newly nullable column that a screen assumes is present is a regression even when the writer is correct.
5. **Check the old entry points.** Removed or renamed routes, tabs (`LOAN_DETAIL_TABS`, `?tab=` values), funnel steps, and modal openers. An old bookmark or a nav item that still points there is broken.
6. **Check behavior that depends on a condition.** Feature flags (on/off default), tenant type (CRM/LOS/INCOME), role, and data conditions. Say when a regression only appears in one of them.
7. **For vendor payload changes** (Freddie Mac, Fannie Mae, Twilio, email), ask what the other side used to accept. A field renamed to match a new spec can be rejected by a live endpoint or a saved fixture. Say whether the PR proves it against a sandbox and where.

Write each finding as:

```markdown
- **<Screen or feature>: <what used to work, now broken>** — Before: <behavior on the base branch>. Now: <behavior>. Where: `<file:line>`. Intentional? <Yes/No, and the evidence>.
```

Read `~/.ai/commands/manual-review/references/future-monorepo-frontend-map.md` for the app, route, and shared-component map, then confirm every entry against the worktree.

### 4.2 Gaps

A gap is something the PR is trying to do but does not finish. Sources of truth, in this order: the linked issue's acceptance criteria, the PR body's promises, code comments and TODO/FIXME added in the diff, then the change list itself.

Check these pairs, because this repo has broken on every one of them:

- **Write path and read path.** A field is saved but no screen, export, or job reads it.
- **List and detail.** Both show the new value, and both handle the empty case.
- **CRM and funnel.** The same loan or contact data shown in both places agrees.
- **Server and worker.** A status the worker sets is one the server and UI understand.
- **Schema and migration plus backfill.** Existing rows survive the new column, enum, or index.
- **Zod, Prisma, DTO, and UI.** The same field exists in all four, with the same optionality.
- **Feature flag: registered, defaulted, documented, and read in both server and client.**
- **New tRPC procedure: has a caller, has an authorization check, filters by tenant.**
- **New vendor request: has a contract test or fixture, and an error path the user can see.**
- **New UI state: loading, empty, and error.** A spinner that never resolves and a silent empty list are gaps.
- **UI text that describes the old behavior.** Dialogs, confirmations, and helper lines often promise something the PR just changed ("already read documents reuse their saved reads", "this will keep X"). Diff those strings against the new behavior and flag a stale one.
- **A changed model prompt.** Check whether saved model answers are keyed by the prompt (a fingerprint or version). If they are, changing the prompt makes every saved answer stale, so old records re-read and spend tokens; if they are not, old records keep the old answer. Either way, say which happens, because the PR body usually claims one of them.

Write each finding as: what the PR sets out to do, what is missing, and the file that proves it. If the body explicitly defers something ("not in this PR"), list it once under Gaps as a known deferral, not as a defect.

### 4.3 UI not connected to the backend or schema

Look for screens that look finished but have nothing real behind them:

- Handlers that only `console.log`, set local state, or show a toast with no mutation.
- Components seeded with hardcoded sample rows, `mock`/`demo`/`placeholder` data, or a `TODO` where the query should be.
- A prop that no parent passes, where a default hides the gap.
- Form fields absent from the mutation input, the Zod schema, or the Prisma model — they look saved and are dropped.
- A field rendered in the UI that nothing writes, or written by the server and never selected.
- Mutations that do not invalidate or refetch the query the screen reads, so the change disappears on reload.
- `as any`, `data!`, and optional chaining used to paper over a field that is not actually returned.
- New routes or buttons that lead to a placeholder page or an empty panel.
- New enum or status values the UI never handles (default branch of a switch renders nothing).

Write each finding as: what the user sees, what is actually behind it, and what is missing (procedure, schema field, persistence, invalidation).

### 4.4 Schema changes

For every change in `libs/database/prisma/schema.prisma` and every new folder in `libs/database/prisma/migrations/`:

- **What:** model and table, column name and type, nullability, default, enum values, indexes, unique constraints, relations added or removed.
- **How:** the migration folder name and whether the SQL was generated by Prisma or hand-written (data-only migrations are allowed to be hand-written; DDL written by hand is a finding).
- **Existing rows:** is there a backfill? Would a `NOT NULL` without a default fail on current data? Does a renamed column have a matching data migration?
- **Why:** the reason from the PR body, ticket, or the code that reads the new value. If nothing reads it yet, say so — that is a write-only field.
- **Blast radius:** every reader and writer in the diff, plus any code outside the diff that selects the model with `include`/`select` and will now see the new field.

Then state one of: "No schema changes." or a list in the form below.

```markdown
- **`Model.column`** — `<type, nullable/default>`, added in `<migration_folder>`. Why: <reason>. Existing rows: <backfill or none>. Read by: `<file:line>`; written by: `<file:line>`.
```

Keep the changes list concise: one line per change, files in parentheses. The five closing sections carry the detail.

Omit any group with no changes. If none of the three frontend apps changed, replace those headings with one line: "No frontend code changed." A backend change that alters a screen still gets a line in Regressions saying what changes on screen.

Before sending:

1. **Coverage check.** Compare `git -C <path> diff --name-only "$MB"..HEAD` against the paths named in the report; add anything missing. Files that are only reformatted or generated can go in one grouped bullet.
2. **Claim check.** Every regression, gap, and unconnected-UI bullet names a file. Delete any bullet you cannot point at a line for.
3. **Style check.** Reread as someone who has not seen the code: expand acronyms, replace slang, and make each bullet a sentence.
4. **Link check.** PR and issue numbers are links, e.g. `[#1234](https://github.com/Future-Mortgage/monorepo/pull/1234)`.

Then stop. In later turns, answer questions about the PR from the worktree. If the user wants to click through the app, a quick worktree has no port remap and serving it collides with the primary checkout. Point them to `/monorepo-worktree <PR>` for a runnable second stack instead. Do not start a dev server here.

## Errors

| Error                               | Action                                                                                     |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Branch with no PR                   | Skip the `gh pr` calls; take intent from commits, code comments, and any linked ticket     |
| Empty diff against the merge base   | Say so and stop                                                                            |
| Linear MCP unavailable              | Note the ticket ID and say it was not read                                                 |
| Can't trace a component to a screen | Say how far the trace got (the last file that renders it) and what blocked it. Never guess |
| Worktree install fails              | Show the output verbatim and stop                                                          |

User arguments: $ARGUMENTS
````

```markdown file=~/.ai/commands/manual-review/references/future-monorepo-frontend-map.md
## 2. web-crm routes

`apps/web-crm/src/app/index.tsx` is the only router (`createBrowserRouter`). `pages/User/UsageDashboard/all-routes.ts` is **not** the router. It's a list only the Usage dashboard reads, and it can drift from the real routes.

### Guards, outermost first (under `apps/web-crm/src/app/`)

1. `components/ProtectedRoute/index.tsx`: not logged in → `/login`; status PENDING → `/onboarding`. Wraps `FeatureFlagProvider` and `AdminLayout` (top header + PrimaryNav).
2. `config/feature-flags/FeatureRouteGuard.tsx` + `route-config.ts`:
   - `routeFeatureMap` maps a path to the flag that must be on. Prefixes ending in `/` match by prefix, and the longest match wins.
   - `CRM_ONLY_BLOCKED_ROUTE_PREFIXES` blocks loan and other LOS-only routes when `tenantType === 'CRM'`.
   - A blocked route redirects to `/admin/contacts`.
3. `components/AdminRouteGuard`: ADMIN or SUPER_ADMIN only; others → `/user/user-settings/personal-info`.
4. `components/TeamRouteGuard`: admins or LOAN_OFFICER.
5. `components/SuperAdminRoute`: `role === SUPER_ADMIN`, else → `/admin/contacts`. It sits outside ProtectedRoute, so super admin pages have no AdminLayout header.

After login (`getPostLoginPath` in `apps/web-crm/src/utils/constants.ts`): UNDERWRITER → `/user/underwriter-queue`; everyone else → `/admin/contacts`.

### Main routes (components under `apps/web-crm/src/app/pages/`; "(!)" means the name is misleading)

- **Contacts**
  - `/admin/contacts` → `Admin/Contacts/components/contact-page.tsx`
  - `/admin/contacts/:id` → `Admin/Contacts/ContactDetail.tsx`. It opens a side sheet over the list; its tabs are in §4.
- **Loan detail:** `/user/loan/:loanId` → `components/AdminLayout/LoanPropertySidebar/sidebar-layout.tsx` → `User/Loan-Property/index.tsx`. See §3.
- **Loan Center**
  - `/user/file-view` → `User/Applications` (the Loan Applications list)
  - `/user/my-pipeline` → `User/MyPipeline`
  - `/user/loan-pipeline` and `/pricing` → `User/Loans-Pipeline`
  - `/user/lenders-page`, `/user/lenders-new` → `User/Lenders/{lenders,lender-new}.tsx`
  - `/user/price-loan` → `User/Inbox/components/pricing-loan.tsx` (!)
  - `/user/underwriter-queue` → `User/UnderwriterQueue`
  - `/user/{compliance,closings,active-pipeline,broker-approval,loan-timer,loan-ticket,compare-lenders,refinance-tracker,pricing-engine,underwriting,opportunities,refiScanner}` → the `User/` folder with the same name
- **Dashboards** (folder spelled `User/Dasboard/`)
  - `/dashboard`, `/user/plans-billing-dashboard` → `PlansAndBillingDashboard`
  - `/user/lead-management` → `LeadManagement`; `/user/pipeline` → `Pipeline`; `/user/rankings-dashboard` → `RankingsBoard`; `/user/agents-dashboard` → `AgentsBoard`; `/user/pipeline-dashboard` → `pipeline-dashboard-new.tsx`; `/user/lead-dashboard` → `lead-dashboard.tsx`
  - Separate pages: `/user/kpi-dashboard`, `/user/financial-dashboard`, `/user/ai-dashboard` (folder `AI Dashboard`, with a space), `/user/ai-usage`
- **Communication and tasks:** `/user/inbox`, `/user/crm-task` (`CRM-Task`), `/user/task-hub`, `/user/dialer`, `/user/crm-message`
- **Marketing**
  - `/user/campaigns` → `User/Outreach` (!)
  - `/user/outreach` → `User/Campaings` (!), plus `/user/outreach/add-campaigns` and `/user/outreach/edit-campaign/:campaignId` → `Campaings/components/campaign-new`
  - `/user/{social-media,reviews,articles,video-library,print}`
- **IncomeIQ** (the income calculation tool inside CRM): `/parser`, `/parser/income-calculation/:loanId`, `/parser/income-calculations/:calculationId`. Small wrappers in `index.tsx` render parser-ui pages. The Bank, Wage, or SelfEmployed page is picked by `data.method`.
- **Settings**
  - `/user/user-settings/personal-info` → `User/UserSettings`, tabs via `?tab=info|application|credit|communications|password` (`profile-tabs.ts`)
  - Behind TeamRouteGuard: `/user/user-settings/funnel-automation`, `/user/user-settings/my-teams` and `/my-teams/:loanOfficerId` (→ `Admin/MyTeams`)
  - Behind AdminRouteGuard: `/user/company-settings/{organization-info, login-settings, integrations, webhooks, documents-forms, smart-conditions, automated-emails (+ /:templateKey), automations-rules, licenses, company-users, locations, closing-costs, lender-comp, commission-plans, funnel-automation}`, `/user/sponsors`, `/user/brokerage-partners`, `/admin/rate-management`, `/admin/payroll`

## 3. Loan detail page (web-crm)

- **URL:** `/user/loan/:loanId?tab=<key>&section=<sub>`
- **Allowed tabs and sections:** `apps/web-crm/src/app/components/AdminLayout/LoanPropertySidebar/loan-tab-url.ts` (`LOAN_DETAIL_TABS`). Sections: `property` → `loan-info|property-info|title-info`; `borrower` → `basic-detail|declaration|demographics|additional-questions`.
- **Tab state:** `.../LoanPropertySidebar/LoanTabContext.tsx`. The starting tab comes from `?tab` (default `property`; unknown values fall back to Property). Changing tabs rewrites `?tab`, clears `section`, and goes through `requestNavigation`, which shows the unsaved-changes dialog.

- **Tab content:** `apps/web-crm/src/app/pages/User/Loan-Property/index.tsx`, one `TabsContent` per tab.

  8. **Settings ▾**: a grid (Company / People & Payroll / Lending / Automation & Integrations / My Account) with admin-only items, My Team for loan officers, Funnel Automation, payroll, My Profile, and Super Admin (SUPER_ADMIN only)
- Items are gated by `Features.isFeatureEnabled(...)`, `isAdminRole`, role checks, `isCrmOnly = tenantType !== 'LOS'`, or `isRateManagementTenant(hostname)` (`app/config/tenant-features.ts`: subdomains fm, future, app).
- **Header extras:** global search (`components/GlobalSearch`), notifications (`AdminLayout/Notifications/notifications-new.tsx`), user menu `user-dropdown.tsx` (copies the funnel invite link `/apply/invite/<nmls>`).
- **Dashboard switcher:** `pages/User/Dasboard/PlansAndBillingDashboard/dashboard-switchers.tsx`.
- **Pitfall:** the menu and the route guards are maintained separately. A menu item can be visible but its route blocked (for example, "Company Details" for admins on CRM tenants redirects to `/admin/contacts`). Check both when a PR touches either.

## 6. Shared UI libraries

There are no `tsconfig.base.json` path aliases. Packages resolve through yarn workspaces, and each lib's `package.json` points straight at `src/*.ts`. web-crm also has local aliases `app/`, `utils/`, `store/` (rooted at `apps/web-crm/src`).

| Package | Folder | Rendered in |
|---|---|---|
| `@future-mortgage/design-system` | `libs/design-system` (`src/ui` primitives, `src/widgets`, `src/components`, `src/auth`, `src/customer-auth`, `theme`) | every app. A change here can show up on many screens: list the main ones, don't claim all |
| `@future-mortgage/design-system-widgets` | `libs/design-system-widgets` (re-exports `libs/design-system/src/widgets`) | web-crm, funnel-ui, parser-ui, web-funnel |
| `@future-mortgage/client-portal-domain-funnel-ui` | `libs/client-portal/domain/funnel-ui` | web-funnel only |
| `@future-mortgage/crm-domain-parser-ui` | `libs/crm/domain/parser-ui` | **both** web-crm (`/parser*`) **and** web-income. Report both locations |
| `@future-mortgage/auth-ui`, `customer-auth-ui`, `client-portal-design-system` | `libs/auth-ui`, `libs/customer-auth-ui`, `libs/client-portal/design-system` | nothing (old re-export files with no importers) |
| `@future-mortgage/crm-domain-loans-ui` | `libs/crm/domain/loans-ui` | nothing (one stub, no importers) |

`libs/income/domain/*` has no UI.

## 7. Feature flags, tenants, roles

- **Flag names:** Prisma enum `FeatureFlagName` in `libs/database/prisma/schema.prisma`, re-exported in `libs/shared/feature-flags/src/lib/constants.ts`. Values are per tenant, loaded by `trpc.featureFlags.getAll` in `apps/web-crm/src/app/config/feature-flags/FeatureFlagProvider.tsx`. Toggled in Super Admin → Feature Flags.
- **Checking a flag in code:** `useFeatureFlag(FLAG)` / `useFeatureFlags([...])` (React hooks), or `isFeatureEnabled` / `isAnyFeatureEnabled` from `libs/shared/feature-flags/src/lib/config.ts` (used by PrimaryNav, `route-config.ts`, `<FeatureGate feature=…>`, `withFeatureGate`). Route-level flags are in `route-config.ts` `routeFeatureMap`.
- **Is a flag on locally?** Look at the tenant's row in the feature flag table (find the table name from the Prisma model that uses `FeatureFlagName`), or Super Admin → Feature Flags. Say "not checked" if you didn't.
- **Tenant type:** `user.tenant.tenantType` is `CRM`, `LOS`, or `INCOME`. CRM tenants lose loan routes (`CRM_ONLY_BLOCKED_ROUTE_PREFIXES`) and LOS-only nav items.
- **Roles:** `USER_ROLES` in `apps/web-crm/src/utils/constants.ts` (SUPER_ADMIN, ADMIN, BRANCH_MANAGER, LOAN_OFFICER, ASSISTANT, PROCESSOR, UNDERWRITER, CLOSER, PAYROLL, RECRUITER, LOCK_DESK, BORROWER). Helpers in the same file: `isAdminRole`, `isAdminOrLoanOfficerRole`, `isLoanOfficerRole`. Hook `useIsAdmin` (`apps/web-crm/src/utils/hooks/useIsAdmin.ts`). The user comes from redux `useSelector(selectUser)`.
- **Permission scopes:** `<PermissionsWrapper scopes={[...]}>` (`app/components/features/permissions/PermissionWrapper.tsx`) checks `ROLE_PERMISSIONS` (`libs/shared/validation/src/lib/authorization.ts`; admins have `all_permissions`) plus the user's role permissions from the database.
- **web-funnel and web-income** have no flag checks; their guards are login-only (`AuthRouteGuard`).

## 8. web-funnel (borrower application)

Router `apps/web-funnel/src/app/app.tsx`. Every URL starts with `/apply`. Pages live in `libs/client-portal/domain/funnel-ui/src/lib/`.

- **Public:** `/login`, `/signup`, `/forgot-password`, `/reset-password`, `/verification/done`, `/welcome/:nmls` (landing page branded for one loan officer), `/welcome/:nmls/apply`, `/invite/:nmls` (redirects to `/welcome/...`), `/`.
- **Logged in (borrower):** `/start`, `/dashboard`, `/loan/:loanId` (borrower task tiles, `dashboard/LoanDashboardPage.tsx`), `/loan/:loanId/report`, `/loan-application/:loanId/:stepName`, `/loan-application/:loanId/borrower/:borrowerIndex/:stepName`.
- **Steps:** no route per step. `app.tsx` switches on `stepName` and renders `loan-application/<Name>Page.tsx`.
- **Step order:** `libs/client-portal/domain/funnel-ui/src/lib/loan-application/loan-application-pages.ts`, `FUNNEL_STEP_SEQUENCE`: account → loan-purpose → first-time-buyer → loan-term → property-type → property-occupancy → years-in-home → property-address → property-value → applicants → identity → contact → va → demographics → employment → assets → real-estate-owned → real-estate-agent → referral-source → declarations → credit-check → review → submitting → pre-approved.
  - `getFunnelStepSequence()` drops property-type, property-address, property-value, years-in-home, and real-estate-agent for refinances, and repeats the per-borrower steps for each co-borrower.
  - `loan-type`, `va-eligibility`, and `loan-amount` can be opened by URL but aren't in the sequence.
  - `RefinancePropertyPage` only renders inside `PropertyOccupancyPage` for refinances.
- **How to describe a funnel location:** "Borrower app, step N of the application (`<step>`), reached by starting an application at `/apply/welcome/<nmls>` and clicking through." Name the conditions (refinance vs purchase, co-borrower, VA).

## 9. web-income

Router `apps/web-income/src/app/app.tsx`.

- **Logged out only:** `/login`, `/request-access`, `/signup`, `/verify`, `/forgot-password`; also `/reset-password`.
- **Logged in (AppShell nav: Home, Calculations):** `/home` → HomePage; `/parser` → `ParserListPage` (wraps parser-ui `LoanRequestsPage`); `/parser/income-calculations/:calculationId` → `ParserDetailPage` (parser-ui Bank, Wage, or SelfEmployed page).
- **Account dialog:** `ProfileDialog.tsx`, tabs `profile` and `billing` (kept in component state, not the URL). Billing UI: `apps/web-income/src/billing/`.
- ACTIVE users land on `/home`; everyone else on `/login` (`auth/home-path.ts`).

## 10. Tracing a changed file to its screen

1. Walk importers upward until you hit a router file (§1). Search the file's basename and its exported names across `apps` and `libs`, excluding `*.spec.*`, `*.test.*`, `*.stories.*`.
2. **Lazy loading:** web-crm routes import `pages/User/X/Loadable`, which calls `lazyLoad(() => import('./index'), m => m.X)` (`apps/web-crm/src/utils/loadable.tsx`). Search for both `X/Loadable` and `/X'`.
3. **Barrels** (`index.ts` files that re-export others): `pages/User/LoanDetail/index.ts`, `pages/SuperAdmin/index.tsx`, `components/overlays/index.ts`, `config/feature-flags/index.ts`, and each lib's `src/index.ts`. Being exported is not the same as being rendered: keep going until something renders it in JSX.
4. Many `pages/User/*` folders are **loan-detail tabs, not routes**: Financial-info, Borrower-info, NeedDocs, Client-needs, Review-fees, Product-Pricing, Dual, Processing, LoanCenter, Audit-Dates, Disclosure-Packages. Use the §3 table.
5. **Misleading names:** Campaings and Outreach routes are swapped; `Inbox/components/pricing-loan` is `/user/price-loan`; tab `pre-approval` renders AIUnderwriter; tab `ai-underwriter` renders the conditions tab; folder typos `Dasboard` and `AI Dashboard`.
6. **Known dead code:** `Financial-info/index.tsx` + `Loadable.ts`, `Borrower-info/index.tsx`, `NeedDocs/index.tsx` + `Loadable.ts`, `Admin/Contacts/index.tsx` + `Loadable.ts`, `Dasboard/Loadable.ts`, the 14 `LoanPropertySidebar` files in §3, and the libs marked "nothing" in §6. A PR that edits one of these changes nothing on screen: say so under Risk.
7. **One change, several apps:** parser-ui → CRM `/parser*` and web-income; design-system → every app; funnel-ui → web-funnel only.
8. **Deep links:** loan detail `?tab=&section=`, contact detail `?tab=&taskId=`, user settings `?tab=`, CRM-Task.
9. **Placeholders:** `/user/usage-report/*` except `all-system-pages`, and the `closing-center` loan tab, render placeholder or blank content.
```
