````markdown file=~/.ai/skills/fix-shipyard-tests/references/shipyard-workflows.md
# Shipyard workflows reference

Source of truth: https://github.com/Future-Mortgage/shipyard/actions

## Active workflows (typical)

| Workflow | Path | Role for this skill |
|----------|------|---------------------|
| Deploy Dev (GCP) | `.github/workflows/deploy-dev-gcp.yml` | **Primary** — runs integration + e2e after deploy |
| Deploy Prod (GCP) | `.github/workflows/deploy-prod-gcp.yml` | Prod deploy; not the default test target |
| Deploy Infrastructure (GCP) | `.github/workflows/deploy-infra-gcp.yml` | Infra only |
| Deploy Ephemeral Preview (GCP) | `.github/workflows/deploy-ephemeral-gcp.yml` | Preview deploys |

## Deploy Dev job chain

1. `prepare` — tag + monorepo/verification refs, actor/Slack mapping  
2. `build_images` — build container images from monorepo ref  
3. `deploy` — deploy to dev GCP  
4. `integration_tests` — Vitest API/integration suite  
5. `e2e_tests` — Playwright server-crm + web-crm suites  

## Commands executed in shipyard (monorepo checkout)

```bash
# integration_tests
yarn vitest run --config apps/server-crm-e2e/vitest.config.ts --no-file-parallelism

# e2e_tests
npx playwright test --config=apps/server-crm-e2e/playwright.config.ts
npx playwright test --config=apps/web-crm-e2e/playwright.config.ts
```

Env: `TEST_BASE_URL` from shipyard vars (dev host).

## Artifacts

- Name: `e2e-test-results`
- Paths: `apps/server-crm-e2e/test-results/`, `apps/web-crm-e2e/test-results/`

## Useful gh commands

```bash
gh run list --repo Future-Mortgage/shipyard --workflow "Deploy Dev (GCP)" --status failure --limit 10
gh run view <id> --repo Future-Mortgage/shipyard --json jobs
gh run view <id> --repo Future-Mortgage/shipyard --log-failed
gh run download <id> --repo Future-Mortgage/shipyard --name e2e-test-results --dir /tmp/shipyard-e2e-<id>
```

## Fix ownership

| Failure shape | Likely repo |
|---------------|-------------|
| Test assertion / selector / playwright setup | monorepo (`apps/*-e2e` or product UI) |
| API contract / server behavior | monorepo (`apps/server-crm`, shared libs) |
| Wrong image tag, secrets, workflow step, URL var | shipyard |
````

#### `~/.ai/skills/fix-tailwind/SKILL.md`

````markdown file=~/.ai/skills/fix-tailwind/SKILL.md
---
name: fix-tailwind
description: Normalizes all Tailwind classes in a PR's touched .tsx/.jsx files to use ONLY values defined in the project's tailwind.config (colors, spacing, fontSize, fontFamily, borderRadius, etc.). Replaces arbitrary values (e.g. `text-[#abc123]`, `p-[13px]`, `bg-[rgb(...)]`), off-scale tokens (e.g. `text-blue-50`, `bg-gray-700`), and any class that doesn't resolve to a config value with the closest available default. Also collapses raw hex/rgb to the nearest configured palette entry. Always creates a code-only git worktree first (same as /worktree-quick; yarn install is mandatory) so /fix-tailwind 1234 does not need a prior /worktree-quick. Use when user says "/fix-tailwind", "/fix-tailwind <PR#>", "fix tailwind in this PR", "normalize tailwind classes", or "snap tailwind to config".
---

# /fix-tailwind — Snap Tailwind classes in a PR to config defaults

Make every Tailwind class in the PR's changed `.tsx` / `.jsx` / `.ts` / `.js` frontend files resolve against the app's `tailwind.config.{js,ts}`. Arbitrary, off-scale, and undefined values become the **closest matching config value**; nothing else in the file changes.

**Usage:** `/fix-tailwind` works on the current branch's diff vs. `origin/main`. `/fix-tailwind <PR-number>` or `<PR-url>` works on that PR's touched files, read via `gh pr diff` or a local checkout.

`/fix-tailwind 1234` is enough: this skill creates the code-only worktree itself. Do **not** require a prior `/worktree-quick`. **Yarn install is mandatory** on every worktree (create, reuse, already-isolated).

## Core Rules

1. **No arbitrary values.** Any utility containing `[...]` (`text-[#abc123]`, `p-[13px]`, `bg-[rgb(0,0,0)]`, `w-[42%]`, `gap-[7px]`) **must** be rewritten to the closest config token. Leave it only when the scale has no analog at all (a one-off `grid-cols-[1fr_auto_2fr]`, a custom `clip-path-[...]`, an `animate-[...]` with no named keyframe), and list it under "Skipped — no config analog".
2. **No off-scale named tokens either.** `bg-gray-100` (no `gray` in the palette), `text-blue-50`, `bg-blue-900` (outside 100–800), `rounded-md` when `md` is not configured — all snap to the closest configured value.
3. **Config is the source of truth.** Allowed values come from `theme` + `theme.extend` plus Tailwind's built-in defaults for anything not fully overridden. Read `tailwind.config.{js,ts,cjs,mjs}` and any theme files or CSS variables it imports.
4. **Scope: only changed class strings.** Work only on files the PR touched (`git diff --name-only` against the base, filtered to `.tsx` / `.jsx` / `.ts` / `.js`, and only those containing `className=` / `class=` / `clsx(` / `cn(` / `cva(` / `` tw` ``). Never modify TS logic, imports, props, types, or non-class literals, and never commit or push: edits stay in the working tree for review.
5. **Closest, not creative.** Pick the numerically or perceptually closest entry in the same property family. Do not guess intent, do not swap a hue token for a semantic token, and never invent a class that was not there.
6. **Keep variants, change nothing else.** `dark:`, `hover:`, `md:`, group/peer, `[&>...]`, `data-[state=open]:` stay verbatim; only the trailing utility is rewritten. Bracketed variants are not arbitrary values, so rule 1 does not touch them. Do not reorder, dedupe, or reformat classes, and do not run `prettier` or `eslint --fix`. Running the skill twice changes nothing.

## Phase 0: Code-only worktree (always, before any work)

Work never runs in the primary checkout. Isolate with the same script as `/worktree-quick`, then continue there — do **not** wait for `/worktree-quick`, do **not** use `/monorepo-worktree`, and do **not** stop after create.

**Yarn is mandatory on every worktree:** `(cd "<path>" && yarn install)` with exit 0 (10 min timeout), on create, reuse, and already-isolated alike. Never skip because `node_modules` exists, and never skip on reuse. If the create script already ran yarn this turn and you watched it exit 0, that create counts; reuse and already-isolated worktrees **must still yarn**.

### Parse target

PR numbers / `#N` / `pr N` / GitHub `.../pull/N` / git refs are worktree targets. Do **not** hand-roll `git worktree add`.

| TARGET       | Action                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| PR / URL     | `~/.ai/skills/worktree-quick/scripts/quick-worktree.sh <n-or-url>`                                                                                                                                |
| Branch / ref | `…/quick-worktree.sh <ref>`                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Empty        | `gh pr view --json number -q .number`. If that fails and cwd is already `*-quick-*`, skip create. Else if the current branch is not `main`/`master`, worktree that branch. Else ask for a PR number. |

Remember `PR_NUMBER`; later calls use `gh pr view ${PR_NUMBER}`.

### Create, reuse, then move the session

Skip create only if cwd is already a matching `*-quick-*` worktree. If the path exists, **reuse** it: fetch + reset to latest when clean, and do not `reset --hard` when dirty. Then call `tools.opencode.session_move` (OpenCode) with `directory` = absolute worktree path, continue this session immediately, and do **not** destroy the worktree when finished.

## Phase 1: Resolve Target

```bash
# No arg → current branch diff vs base
git branch --show-current
BASE=$(git remote show origin | grep 'HEAD branch' | awk '{print $NF}')
git merge-base HEAD origin/$BASE
```

If a PR number or URL was given:

```bash
# Get PR head SHA + base, fetch, build a diff range
gh pr view <PR> --json headRefName,baseRefName,headRepository,number
gh pr diff <PR> --name-only        # quick file list
gh pr checkout <PR>                 # only if user wants edits committed locally
```

If the user only wants a report (no edits) for a remote PR, work on `gh pr diff <PR>` content instead of checked-out files. Otherwise edit locally only when the PR is already checked out, and prompt if it is not.

## Phase 2: Collect Changed Files

```bash
git diff --name-only $(git merge-base HEAD origin/$BASE)..HEAD \
  | grep -E '\.(tsx|jsx|ts|js)$' \
  | grep -vE '(\.test\.|\.spec\.|\.stories\.|/node_modules/|/dist/|/build/)'
```

For each candidate, confirm it contains class strings (`grep -lE 'className=|class=|clsx\(|cn\(|cva\(|tw\`'`); skip pure-logic files. If a repo has **multiple `tailwind.config`** files, take the one whose `content` glob matches the file being edited, and if none matches, skip the file and note it.

## Phase 3: Load the Tailwind Config

Read `tailwind.config.{js,ts,cjs,mjs}` for the relevant app and resolve it statically — do not execute it.

| Family        | Where to look                                                                                                                                      | Build set of                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Colors        | `theme.colors`, `theme.extend.colors`                                                                                                              | `{<color>-<shade>}` keys, including `DEFAULT`, plus semantic tokens (`primary`, `muted`, etc.). Resolve hex values for distance comparisons. CSS-variable-backed colors (`hsl(var(--x))`) stay opaque — match by name only. |
| Spacing       | `theme.spacing`, `theme.extend.spacing` (Tailwind defaults if absent)                                                                              | px/rem values per key                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Font size     | `theme.fontSize`, `theme.extend.fontSize`                                                                                                          | sizes per key                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Font family   | `theme.fontFamily`, `theme.extend.fontFamily`                                                                                                      | family names                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Border radius | `theme.borderRadius`, `theme.extend.borderRadius`                                                                                                  | sizes per key                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Other scales  | `theme.<prop>`, `theme.extend.<prop>` for `borderWidth`, `boxShadow`, `zIndex`, `opacity`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`, `animation`, `keyframes` | widths, named shadows, numeric or name keys, percent keys, sizes, animation and keyframe names                                                                                                                              |

If a property is **not extended**, fall back to Tailwind's built-in defaults (allowed = defaults ∪ extend). If it is **fully overridden** (declared in `theme.<prop>`, not `theme.extend.<prop>`), only the override values are allowed.

> This monorepo's scales run `100…800`, so `bg-blue-50`, `bg-blue-900`, and `bg-gray-*` (no `gray` in config) are all **off-scale**.

## Phase 4: Tokenize and Rewrite

For each extracted class string:

### 4.1 Split utilities

Split on whitespace, then peel the variant prefixes off each utility (everything before the final `:`, including `[&>div]:`, `data-[state=open]:`, `dark:`, `group-hover:`). Keep prefixes verbatim and rewrite only the trailing utility, preserving `!` (`!text-red-500`) and `-` (`-mt-4`).

### 4.2 Classify the utility

| Prefix examples                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Family                                                    |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `text-`, `bg-`, `border-`, `ring-`, `from-`, `via-`, `to-`, `fill-`, `stroke-`, `placeholder-`, `accent-`, `caret-`, `divide-`, `outline-`, `decoration-`, `shadow-` (color form)                                                                                                               | color                                                     |
| `p-`, `px-`, `py-`, `pt-`, `pr-`, `pb-`, `pl-`, `m-`, `mx-`, `my-`, `mt-`, `mr-`, `mb-`, `ml-`, `gap-`, `gap-x-`, `gap-y-`, `space-x-`, `space-y-`, `inset-`, `top-`, `right-`, `bottom-`, `left-`, `w-`, `h-`, `min-w-`, `min-h-`, `max-w-`, `max-h-`, `size-`, `translate-x-`, `translate-y-` | spacing                                                   |
| `text-` (with size keys xs/sm/base/lg/xl/…/9xl, or arbitrary)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | fontSize                                                  |
| `font-` (sans/serif/mono/custom names)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | fontFamily                                                |
| `font-` (thin/normal/bold/…/numeric)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | fontWeight (Tailwind defaults; rarely extended)           |
| `rounded-`, `rounded-{side}-`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | borderRadius                                              |
| `border-`, `border-{side}-` (numeric)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | borderWidth                                               |
| `shadow-` (non-color)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | boxShadow                                                 |
| `z-` / `opacity-` / `leading-` / `tracking-` / `animate-` (and `bg-opacity-`, `text-opacity-`, etc.)                                                                                                                                                                                            | zIndex / opacity / lineHeight / letterSpacing / animation |

`text-*` is ambiguous, so check the suffix against the config: `text-center` is alignment (always allowed), `text-blue-500` is color, `text-sm` is size, `text-[14px]` is an arbitrary fontSize, `text-[#abc]` is an arbitrary color.

### 4.3 Decide if a rewrite is needed

Leave alone when the utility is not parameterized (`flex`, `grid`, `block`, display, alignment, layout) or its suffix exactly matches a configured key and uses no `[…]`.

Rewrite when:

- It uses arbitrary `[…]` of any kind: `[#hex]`, `[rgb(...)]`, `[hsl(...)]`, `[var(--…)]`, `[Npx]`, `[Nrem]`, `[N%]`, `[Nch]`, `[calc(...)]`. Skip only when the scale has no analog.
- Its arbitrary value equals a configured token anyway: `text-[#0968F6]` with `blue.500 = #0968F6` still becomes `text-blue-500`, because removing brackets is the goal.
- Its suffix is not a config key: `bg-gray-100` (no `gray`), `text-blue-50` / `text-blue-900` (outside 100–800), `rounded-md` when not in the radius set.

### 4.4 Pick the closest config value

**Colors:** resolve the input to hex/rgb/hsl (for `text-blue-50`, resolve against Tailwind's built-in palette), convert to Lab, and take the smallest ΔE (CIE76 is fine). Break ties by family name, so `blue-*` prefers a `blue-*` entry. Never introduce a semantic token (`primary`, `muted`) unless the input was also semantic, and allow a CSS-variable-backed match (e.g. `neutral-*`) only when the input was neutral or gray.

**Spacing / sizes:** convert to px (1rem = 16px unless `theme.fontSize.base` says otherwise), take the smallest absolute px delta, and on a tie pick the smaller value so layout is not silently inflated.

**Font size:** same as spacing, against the fontSize scale only, including custom keys (`xxs: 10px`, `tiny: 13px`).

**Border radius / border width / line height / letter spacing / opacity / z-index:** numeric closest match; for named-only scales (`shadow-sm/md/lg`), infer from the value the config resolves to.

**Animations / keyframes / fontFamily:** exact match only, never "closest". If nothing matches, leave the class alone and note it in the report.

### 4.5 Construct the replacement

Rebuild as `<variants>:<new-suffix>`, keeping `!` and `-`, and reassemble the class string with its original whitespace. If the rebuilt token equals the original, make no edit.

## Phase 5: Apply Edits

For each file with at least one substitution:

1. Use the `Edit` tool with `replace_all: true` only when the old class string appears several times **and** the substitution is identical for all of them; otherwise edit each occurrence with enough context to be unique.
2. Never use `Write` to rewrite a whole file.
3. After the edits, re-read the file and verify only class strings changed.

Class forms to handle:

- **`className={cn(...)}` / `clsx(...)`**: walk every string-literal argument; for object-key forms (`{ 'text-red-500': cond }`), rewrite the key.
- **`cva(...)`**: rewrite strings inside `variants` / `compoundVariants` / `defaultVariants`.
- **Tagged templates** (`` tw`...` ``, `` styled`...` ``) and template literals with `${...}`: rewrite static segments only.
- **Variants on arbitrary values** (`md:bg-[#abc]`): keep `md:`, rewrite the suffix.
- **Out of scope:** JSX spread (`{...props}`), inline styles (`style={{ color: '#abc' }}`), `.css` / `.scss` files, and `@apply`. Layout, components, and non-class code are never refactored.
- **Empty classes** (`className=""`, `className={undefined}`): no-op.

## Phase 6: Report

One markdown table per file:

```
### apps/web-crm/src/.../foo.tsx

| Line | Before | After | Reason |
|------|--------|-------|--------|
| 42 | text-[#0968F6] | text-blue-500 | exact hex match in config |
| 58 | bg-gray-100 | bg-neutral-100 | gray not in palette; closest neutral |
| 73 | p-[13px] | p-3 | 13px → 12px (closest spacing, Δ1px) |
| 91 | text-blue-50 | text-blue-100 | 50 not in scale (100–800) |
| 104 | rounded-md | rounded-default | md not in config; default=0.6125rem closest |
```

Then a summary:

```
## Summary
- Files scanned: N
- Files modified: M
- Total substitutions: K
- Skipped (no closest match): J
  - <list any unresolved utilities>
- Off-scale colors collapsed: …
- Arbitrary values normalized: …
```

If `--dry-run` was passed (or the user said "preview" / "don't apply"), produce the report only and make no edits.

## Safety Rails

| Situation                                                        | Action                                                        |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tailwind config missing or unparseable                           | Stop. Report which config was sought and where it's expected. |
| File has merge conflict markers                                  | Skip the file. Report.                                        |
| File would change > 50 utilities                                 | Show the proposed diff first and ask before applying.         |
| Multiple tailwind configs and no `content` glob matches the file | Skip the file. Report.                                        |
| Animation/keyframe/fontFamily with no exact match                | Leave alone. Report under "Skipped".                          |
| User passes `--dry-run` or `preview`                             | Report only. No edits.                                        |

## Quick Reference: Common Substitutions in This Repo

Built from `apps/web-crm/tailwind.config.js`: color scales run **100–800**, neutral runs **100–900**.

| Off-config                                | Likely fix                                         |
| ----------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `text-blue-50`                            | `text-blue-100`                                    |
| `bg-blue-900`                             | `bg-blue-800`                                      |
| `text-gray-*`                             | `text-neutral-*` (closest shade)                   |
| `bg-slate-*` / `bg-zinc-*` / `bg-stone-*` | `bg-neutral-*` (closest shade)                     |
| `text-[#0968F6]`                          | `text-blue-500`                                    |
| `rounded-md`                              | `rounded-default` or the closest configured radius |
| `text-[10px]`                             | `text-xxs`                                         |
| `text-[13px]`                             | `text-tiny`                                        |
| `font-DM_Sans` / `font-['DM_Sans']`       | `font-sans`                                        |

These are illustrative — always re-derive from the actual config at run time.
````

````markdown file=~/.ai/skills/fix-types/SKILL.md
---
name: fix-types
description: Scans all TypeScript/types in a PR or branch diff for soft types (`any`, unnecessary `null`/`undefined`, optional fields that are required, `Partial`, unvalidated JSON, over-wide unions) and hardens them against Prisma/DB schemas, API contracts, and domain invariants — then fixes call sites so the code compiles with those hard types. Prefer exact definitions over `any` or nullish escape hatches. Always creates a code-only git worktree first (same as /worktree-quick; yarn install is mandatory) so /fix-types 1234 does not need a prior /worktree-quick. Use when the user runs /fix-types, /fix-types 1234, /fix-types <pr|branch>, "harden types", "fix soft types", "remove any types", "make types strict", or "hard types on this PR/branch".
---

# /fix-types - Harden Soft Types on a PR / Branch

Scans every type that is part of the current PR or branch (not the whole monorepo), finds soft types, grounds the correct hard shape in schema, contracts, and domain code, rewrites the types to be exact, and fixes all call sites so the branch typechecks with those hard definitions.

**Usage:**

- `/fix-types` — current branch against the detected base (`main`/`master`)
- `/fix-types <branch>` — that branch against its merge-base with the origin default branch, or against current if the user asked to compare
- `/fix-types pr` / `/fix-types <pr-number>` — the open PR, or that PR's head against its base

`/fix-types 1234` is enough — this skill creates the code-only worktree itself. Do not require a prior `/worktree-quick`.

Use a short todo list for multi-file work. Prefer direct edits and spawn agents only when the package fan-out is large. The scope is the PR or branch only: touch files outside the diff only to export a shared hard type the branch already depends on. Hard types are the default — prefer an exact shape over `any`, over-wide unions, or a nullish maybe — and softening a type so a call site compiles is forbidden.

## Phase 0: Code-only worktree (always, before any work)

Work never runs in the primary checkout. Isolate first with the same script as `/worktree-quick`, then continue in that worktree. Do not wait for the user to run `/worktree-quick`, do not use `/monorepo-worktree`, and do not stop after create.

**Yarn is mandatory on every worktree.** Create, reuse, and already-isolated all require `yarn install` in the worktree with exit 0 (10 minute timeout). Never skip because `node_modules` exists, and never skip on reuse. If the create script already ran yarn this turn and you watched it exit 0, that create counts; reuse and already-isolated must still yarn.

User arguments: `$ARGUMENTS`

### Parse target

PR numbers, `#N`, `pr N`, GitHub `.../pull/N`, and git refs are worktree targets.

| TARGET       | Action                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| PR / URL     | `~/.ai/skills/worktree-quick/scripts/quick-worktree.sh <n-or-url>`                                                                                                                                |
| Branch / ref | `…/quick-worktree.sh <ref>`                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Empty        | `gh pr view --json number -q .number`. If that fails and cwd is already `*-quick-*`, skip create. Else if the current branch is not `main`/`master`, worktree that branch. Else ask for a PR number. |

Remember `PR_NUMBER`. Later use `gh pr view ${PR_NUMBER}`.

### Create, reuse, yarn

Do not hand-roll `git worktree add`. Skip create only if cwd is already a matching `*-quick-*` worktree. If the path already exists, reuse it. If reusing and clean, fetch and reset to the latest; if dirty, do not `reset --hard`. Then always run:

```bash
(cd "<path>" && yarn install)
```

Reuse and already-isolated always run this. Wait for exit 0.

### Move the session, then work

Call `tools.opencode.session_move` with `directory` = absolute worktree path, then continue this session immediately. Do not destroy the worktree when finished.

## Phase 1: Resolve Scope

```bash
git branch --show-current
git remote show origin | grep 'HEAD branch' | awk '{print $NF}'
git merge-base HEAD origin/main   # or origin/master / the detected default
git diff --name-only $(git merge-base HEAD origin/<base>)..HEAD
git diff --stat $(git merge-base HEAD origin/<base>)..HEAD
git diff $(git merge-base HEAD origin/<base>)..HEAD
gh pr view --json number,url,title,baseRefName,headRefName,files
# or: gh pr view ${PR_NUMBER} --json ...
```

Use the PR's `baseRefName` as the base in PR mode. Read these type-bearing files:

- `*.ts`, `*.tsx`, `*.d.ts`.
- Schema sources the branch touches: `**/schema.prisma`, Zod schemas, GraphQL SDL, OpenAPI, tRPC routers.
- Generated types only when the branch owns the generator input: fix the source of truth, then regenerate with the repo's standard command.

Skip pure assets, lockfiles, migration SQL (unless types or enums are defined there), and docs unless they embed type contracts.

Stop when:

| Condition                         | Action                                  |
| --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| Empty diff                        | Stop: nothing to harden                 |
| No TS or schema files in the diff | Stop and report no type-bearing changes |
| Cannot detect the base            | Ask the user for the base branch        |

## Phase 2: Inventory Soft Types

Scan only the changed files and the new symbols they introduce. Read the full file when the diff is not enough context; types often live above the hunk.

### Soft-type smells

| Smell                 | Examples                                                                                                    |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Explicit `any`        | `any`, `Array<any>`, `Record<string, any>`, `Promise<any>`                                                  |
| Type erasure          | `as any`, `as unknown as T`, double casts, `// @ts-ignore`, unjustified `@ts-expect-error`                  |
| Lazy non-null         | `foo!` used to silence instead of proving presence                                                          |
| Unnecessary nullish   | `T \| null`, `T \| undefined`, `T \| null \| undefined` when the domain always has `T` after success        |
| Fake optionals        | `foo?: Bar` or `foo: Bar \| undefined` when the flow always provides it                                     |
| `Partial` abuse       | `Partial<Entity>` for fully loaded entities or API responses                                                |
| Loose bags            | `object`, `{}`, `Record<string, unknown>` inside the domain; acceptable only at a raw boundary before parse |
| Un-narrowed `unknown` | `unknown` returned or stored without a type guard or schema parse                                           |
| Over-wide primitives  | `string` for closed enums and statuses; `number` for fixed unions                                           |
| Soft JSON             | A `JSON.parse` result used without a schema; `any` from an HTTP client                                      |
| Soft returns          | A function returning `T \| undefined` when a miss should throw or return an error                           |
| Soft params           | Optional parameters added so call sites compile                                                             |
| Soft Prisma usage     | Selecting fewer fields then defaulting; ignoring generated nullability                                      |
| Soft React props      | Optional props the parent always passes; `children?:` when the layout requires it                           |

```bash
rg -n '\bany\b|as any|as unknown as|@ts-ignore|@ts-expect-error' --glob '*.ts' --glob '*.tsx' <files>
rg -n '\|\s*null|\|\s*undefined|\?:|Partial<|Record<string,\s*(any|unknown)>' --glob '*.ts' --glob '*.tsx' <files>
```

Also read the full diff for soft types the regex misses: `any` inferred from untyped parameters, missing return types that widen. Record each finding with file and line, the current form, the symbol, why it is soft, the suspected hard type, and whether it sits at an I/O boundary (HTTP, env, raw DB, form).

## Phase 3: Ground Truth

### 3.1 Lookup order

Stop at the first definitive source; do not guess from local convenience.

1. **Database / Prisma** — model fields, `?` nullability, enums, relations in `schema.prisma` and its generators.
2. **Validation schemas** — Zod, Yup, class-validator, or custom parsers colocated with the API.
3. **API contracts** — tRPC procedures, OpenAPI, GraphQL, shared DTO packages.
4. **Domain types** — existing entities in `libs/**`, branded types, event payloads.
5. **Auth / session** — what middleware guarantees, for example `orgId` is always present when authenticated.
6. **Call graph on this branch** — who constructs the value, and what is proven after a successful path.

### 3.2 Nullability rules

| Reality                                      | Hard type                                                                  |
| -------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Field required in the DB and always selected | `T`, not `T \| null`                                                       |
| Column nullable in the DB                    | `T \| null` at the DB and result layer only                                |
| Lookup may miss                              | `T \| null` or `Result` at the lookup; `T` after the guard or throw        |
| Authenticated context field always set       | Required on `AuthenticatedSession`, not optional on a generic session      |
| Form draft vs submitted entity               | Two types, `DraftX` and `X`, never one soft type for both                  |
| JSON column with a known shape               | Parse to an exact interface; do not leave `Prisma.JsonValue` in the domain |

- **Boundaries** (HTTP body, query, env, `JSON.parse`, third-party SDK) may start as `unknown` or soft, and must parse once into a hard type.
- **Core domain and UI after load** use hard types only: no `any`, no cascading `?.` or `??` for required invariants.

## Phase 4: Plan Hard Types

State the plan before editing. Show it for large PRs, keep it internal for small ones. For each finding:

1. **Exact hard type**, field by field if needed: `{ id: string; email: string }`, `LoanStatus`, `AuthenticatedSession`.
2. **Where it is defined** — reuse an existing type or add a named one; prefer reuse.
3. **Where to narrow** — a single validation boundary.
4. **Call-site impact** — files that must drop `??`, `?.`, `!`, `as any`, or optional chaining.
5. **Intentional soft?** — only if the product truly allows absence, with the reason documented.

### 4.1 Forbidden fixes

Never ship any of these as the solution:

- `any`, `as any`, or `as unknown as T` without a real refine.
- Widening to `string | number | boolean | null | undefined` to silence errors.
- Making more fields optional so call sites compile.
- A blanket `!` without a proven invariant.
- `@ts-ignore` or an empty `@ts-expect-error`.
- Replacing a hard error with `?? default` for required data.

### 4.2 Preferred patterns

| Situation                 | Pattern                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Resource may be missing   | `findX(): Promise<X \| null>` then `if (!x) throw` or 404; `X` afterwards                                        |
| Create vs entity          | `CreateXInput` vs `X`                                                                                            |
| Patch endpoint            | `PatchX` or `Partial<Pick<X, ...>>`, only at the patch boundary                                                  |
| Status and kind fields    | String literal unions or enums matching the DB enum                                                              |
| Lists that are never null | `T[]`, empty array allowed; not `T[] \| null` unless the API distinguishes                                       |
| Errors                    | Throw, or a discriminated union `{ ok: true; data: T } \| { ok: false; error: E }`; never a silent empty success |

## Phase 5: Apply Type Fixes

Edit in this order to avoid rework:

1. **Schema and shared contracts** — Prisma enum usage, Zod, shared DTO packages the branch already touches.
2. **Domain type definitions** — interfaces, types, branded IDs.
3. **Function signatures** — explicit, hard parameters and return types.
4. **Component props** — required vs optional matched to real usage.

- **Mechanics.** Prefer named types over large inline unions repeated everywhere, and match existing conventions: `type` vs `interface`, `z.infer<typeof Schema>`, Prisma generated types.
- If Prisma nullability is wrong against the DB, do not lie in TypeScript. Fix the schema or migration only if the branch already owns that; otherwise type the query result honestly and narrow.
- Remove optional markers from types used only after validation.

Generated clients: change the source (schema, Zod, OpenAPI). Run the repo's standard generate command only when needed (`yarn prisma:sync`, project codegen). Do not hand-edit generated files.

## Phase 6: Fix Call Sites and Runtime

Hard types will surface real errors. That is the point; fix them properly.

| Before (soft)                         | After (hard)                                                         |
| ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `user?.orgId ?? ''`                   | `user: AuthenticatedUser` with `orgId: string`, then `user.orgId`    |
| `as SomeType`                         | Parse or validate, or fix the producer type                          |
| `data: any` from `fetch`              | A typed client, or a Zod parse of the response                       |
| `fn(x?: T)`                           | `fn(x: T)` and fix the callers                                       |
| `return null` on an impossible branch | `throw new Error(...)` or an exhaustive `never` check                |
| `Partial<User>` state for a full form | `UserFormState` with optional fields only where the draft needs them |

- **Exhaustiveness.** Prefer `switch` over unions with `default: const _exhaustive: never = x` where the codebase already does this.
- Do not add a `default` that silently swallows new enum values unless the product requires it.
- Fixtures must satisfy the hard types: full objects, not partials, unless the test covers the draft path.
- Add or adjust tests so invalid boundary input is rejected instead of soft-succeeding.

## Phase 7: Verify

Prefer Nx, per the monorepo AGENTS.md. If there is no typecheck target, use the package's `tsc --noEmit` or its existing CI script.

```bash
# Identify projects from the changed paths, then:
yarn nx run-many -t typecheck -p <projects>
# or project-specific: yarn nx run web-crm:typecheck / tsc -p ...
```

While errors caused by this hardening remain: classify each one (still a soft type, a real logic bug, or an intentional optional), fix it hard without re-introducing `any`, and re-run the typecheck. If ESLint enforces `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` or similar, leave the changed files clean.

Stop when the only errors left are pre-existing on the base and untouched here. Note them in the report.

## Phase 8: Report

```markdown
## fix-types Report

**Scope**: [branch / PR #] vs [base]
**Files scanned**: [N type-bearing]
**Soft types found**: [N]
**Hardened**: [N]
**Intentional soft left**: [N]
**Call sites updated**: [N]
**Typecheck**: [pass / pass with notes / blocked]

### Hardened

| File      | Before           | After                                     | Ground truth                    |
| --------- | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| path:line | `orgId?: string` | `orgId: string` on `AuthenticatedSession` | Auth middleware always sets org |

### Call-site / runtime fixes

| File | Change                                              |
| ---- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| path | Removed `?? ''`; throws when the session has no org |

### Intentional soft types (kept)

| File | Type                      | Why allowed                     |
| ---- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| path | `deletedAt: Date \| null` | Nullable column for soft delete |

### Skipped / out of scope

| Item                             | Reason              |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------- |
| Soft types in unrelated packages | Outside the PR diff |

### Follow-ups (if any)

- [ ] e.g. regenerate the Prisma client in CI; product decision needed on optional field X
```

## Severity Order

1. **`any` and type erasure** — always fix.
2. **Required domain fields typed optional or nullish** — fix the type and its call sites.
3. **`Partial` and loose records in the domain** — replace with exact types.
4. **Over-wide `string` / `number`** — literal unions or enums.
5. **Missing explicit return types** that hide soft inference — add hard returns.
6. **Cosmetic** — only when it affects safety.

On a huge PR, fix every `any` and every required-nullish first, then continue until the typecheck is clean or the user stops.

## Interaction Rules

1. Do not ask permission for routine hardening inside the PR scope: `any` to an exact type, removing a bogus `| undefined`, fixing call sites.
2. Do ask when hardening would change an external API contract, a public package export, or DB schema nullability. Present the proposed hard type and wait.
3. Do ask when the product meaning of null vs missing is unclear, for example whether "no avatar" is `null`, an omitted field, or an empty string.
4. Never expand scope into drive-by refactors unrelated to types on this branch.
5. Follow the monorepo rules: Nx targets, the existing validation libraries, no hand-editing generated clients.

## Error Handling

| Error                                                           | Action                                                                          |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Schema file missing, ground truth not findable                  | Read the producers and consumers; if still ambiguous, ask the user with options |
| Typecheck fails for unrelated reasons                           | Isolate the errors this change caused, fix only those, and report the rest      |
| Hardening breaks a public API the branch did not mean to change | Revert that surface; propose a follow-up or a versioned type                    |
| The user wants one file only                                    | Limit the inventory and the fixes to that path                                  |

User arguments: $ARGUMENTS
````

#### `~/.ai/skills/peer-review/SKILL.md`

`````markdown file=~/.ai/skills/peer-review/SKILL.md
---
name: peer-review
description: Builds a feature with a three-round peer review loop. The main agent plans and implements, then three FRESH review rounds run in sequence. Within each round, specialist agents (security, silent-failure/soft-types, recurring patterns, correctness/plan-fit, testing, dead-code/stale-comments, duplication/extract-to-shared, architecture sense-check) spawn in parallel with no prior-round context. After each round, the main agent merges actionable comments, triages every comment as accept / reject / defer with reasoning, then implements accepted changes before the next round. Architecture sense-check notes are advisory only (never trigger a redo mid-loop) and surface to the user only at the end if the agent has a clear concern. Use when user says "/peer-review <task>", "/peer-review <prd-file>", "/peer-review #42", or asks for a "reviewed" / "triple-reviewed" / "peer-reviewed" implementation.
allowed-tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Edit, Write, Task, TaskCreate, TaskUpdate, TaskList, WebFetch
permissionMode: acceptEdits
---

# /peer-review — Plan, Implement, Review x3, Triage

> **Prefer the workflow when possible.** Run `/peer-review` as a **workflow** (`.grok/workflows/peer-review.rhai` or `~/.grok/workflows/peer-review.rhai`) when you want durable orchestration: a fresh independent judge instead of the implementer triaging, adversarial verification that requires evidence, 2 rounds by default with an early exit and a delta-only round 2, structured schemas with a resumable `/workflows` UI, and budget caps (`MAX_VERIFY=12`, 6 findings per specialty). Run it as `/workflow peer-review` with `{ "task": "<description | prd path | #issue>", "rounds": 1|2, "base": "main" }`, or from the tool as `workflow(name: "peer-review", args: #{ task: "..." })`. Use **this skill** when you want the interactive main agent to plan and implement in-conversation.

## Usage

`/peer-review <task-description | prd-file-path | github-issue>`

- `/peer-review add rate limiting to the public API` — free-form task
- `/peer-review docs/prd/user-dashboard.md` — reads a PRD file
- `/peer-review #42` — fetches GitHub issue #42 from the repo of the current working directory
- `/peer-review https://github.com/org/repo/issues/42`

Three independent rounds stress-test one implementation; each round runs its specialists in parallel with no prior-round context, and the main agent merges, triages, and implements before the next round.

## Core Invariants

These must hold for every run. If you cannot satisfy them, stop and tell the user why.

1. **Three rounds, in sequence.** Not two, not four. Round N+1 does not start until round N is fully triaged and its accepted changes are implemented.
2. **Specialists run in parallel inside a round.** Spawn one agent per concern type in a single tool-call batch. Never run them one at a time or as sequential main-agent work.
3. **Reviewers see no prior rounds.** Specialist prompts carry the plan and the current code only — never prior comments, prior decisions, or any hint that earlier rounds happened.
4. **Specialists stay in their lane.** Overlap is fine; the main agent deduplicates when merging.
5. **Every actionable comment is triaged.** For S1–S5 and S7–S8 the main agent picks `accept` (implement now), `reject` (with reasoning), or `defer` (with reasoning and a scope note). Nothing is silently ignored.
6. **S6 architecture sense-check is advisory.** It never produces accept/reject/defer items and **must never** cause a mid-loop re-architecture or redo. Persist its notes quietly; surface them in Phase 3 only if it has a clear concern.
7. **Accepted changes are implemented before the next round**, so the next round reads the updated code. Earlier feedback shows up in the code, not in side text.
8. **All artifacts are persisted** in `.peer-review/` so the user can audit the loop: plan, per-round comments, per-round decisions, architecture notes, final summary.
9. **Never stall on a missing reviewer.** A specialist that errors, times out, hangs, or never returns usable output counts as a failure: retry that specialty once, then continue.

## Phase 0 — Resolve Input

The single argument takes one of three forms. Detect and dispatch:

1. **GitHub issue** — matches `^#?\d+$` or contains `github.com/.*/issues/\d+`:
   - `#NNN` or bare `NNN`: detect the repo from `git remote get-url origin` in the CWD, then `gh issue view <NNN> --repo <owner>/<repo>`
   - Full URL: parse repo and issue number, then `gh issue view`
   - If the issue body references a PRD path, read that too
2. **File path** — the argument exists on disk (`Read`): treat the contents as the spec
3. **Free-form description** — anything else: treat the argument as the task

If detection is ambiguous, prefer the most concrete reading: filesystem first, then issue pattern, then free-form.

Save the resolved spec to `.peer-review/spec.md` (verbatim for files and issues; the user's text as a one-paragraph spec for free-form input).

## Phase 1 — Plan and Implement

The MAIN agent (you, in this conversation) does this phase directly. Do not delegate the plan.

1. **Create the plan** in `.peer-review/plan.md`, covering:
   - **Goal** — one paragraph restating the task in your own words
   - **Approach** — the design choice and the main tradeoff you accept
   - **Files to create or modify** — explicit paths
   - **Consumer / dual-path map** — for every new or moved field or abstraction, who must read or honor it (API schema, DB, list/read UI, exporters and transformers for **each** pipeline, importers, jobs). Mark any intentionally deferred consumer under Out of scope.
   - **Invariants & concurrency** — what must be unique or atomic, and whether a DB constraint or transaction enforces it
   - **AuthZ** — who can call new procedures, and which existing gate (role/assignment/tenant helper) is reused
   - **Failure modes** — what hard-fails versus what degrades visibly; no silent ACTIVE/success on failed setup
   - **Out of scope** — what you deliberately are not doing, so reviewers don't churn on it
   - **Open questions** — anything you are unsure about
2. **Track tasks.** Use `TaskCreate` to list the implementation steps from the plan and update them as you go.
3. **Implement.** Use specialized agents (`backend-architect`, `frontend-developer`, etc.) through `Task` when the work clearly fits their domain; otherwise write it yourself. Verify it builds and type-checks before declaring Phase 1 done.
   - Self-check the recurring patterns while implementing (soft success, write-only wiring, races, thin authZ, mount wipes, dual-path drift, envelope casts, tests that assert failure paths) so round 1 does not rediscover basics.
4. **Snapshot the file set.** Write the created and modified paths to `.peer-review/files-touched.md`, one per line. Specialists review exactly these files.

Do not announce "ready for review". Move directly into Phase 2.

## Phase 2 — Three Sequential Rounds (Parallel Specialists Inside Each Round)

Loop exactly three times with `N` = 1, 2, 3, running 2.N.a through 2.N.e in order.

### 2.N.a — Spawn parallel specialist agents

Spawn **eight** independent agents in **one tool-call batch** (same turn), using the platform's multi-agent tool (`Task` / `spawn_subagent` / equivalent).

| Specialist ID | Concern                             | subagent_type                                     | description              | Actionable?            |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ | ---------------------- |
| **S1**        | Correctness / plan-fit / edge cases | `general-purpose`                                 | `Peer R{N}: correctness` | Yes — triage           |
| **S2**        | Security / authZ / secrets          | `backend-architect` (fallback: `general-purpose`) | `Peer R{N}: security`    | Yes — triage           |
| **S3**        | Silent failure / soft types         | `general-purpose`                                 | `Peer R{N}: silent fail` | Yes — triage           |
| **S4**        | Recurring PR patterns R1–R10        | `general-purpose`                                 | `Peer R{N}: recurring`   | Yes — triage           |
| **S5**        | Testing gaps                        | `test-writer-fixer` (fallback: `general-purpose`) | `Peer R{N}: testing`     | Yes — triage           |
| **S6**        | Architecture sense-check            | `general-purpose` (or `plan` if available)        | `Peer R{N}: arch sense`  | **No** — advisory only |
| **S7**        | Dead code / unused / stale comments | `general-purpose`                                 | `Peer R{N}: dead code`   | Yes — triage           |
| **S8**        | Duplication / extract-to-shared     | `general-purpose`                                 | `Peer R{N}: duplication` | Yes — triage           |

Prefer `capability_mode: read-only` (or equivalent) so specialists cannot edit code.

Do not spawn one mega-reviewer, do not wait for S1 before launching S2–S8, and do not treat S6 output as work for the main agent.

### Shared prefix for every specialist (round N)

Interpolate the plan and file list, never prior-round artifacts. Every specialty block below appends to this prefix.

````
You are an independent specialist code reviewer for ONE concern only (stated below).
You have no prior context about this work — review what you see, not what you assume.
You do not know about other specialists or other review rounds.

## The plan

The implementing engineer wrote this plan before coding:

---
{contents of .peer-review/plan.md}
---

## Files implemented

{contents of .peer-review/files-touched.md}

## Shared rules (all specialists)

1. Read the plan carefully. Do not raise comments about what it marks OUT OF SCOPE.
2. Read every listed file in full, not just the changed regions.
3. Stay in your specialty. Skip issues owned by other specialists unless inseparable from your finding.
4. Do not modify code. Review only.
5. Do not read `.peer-review/round-*` files. Your review must be independent.
6. Be specific: cite file:line and a concrete change, not "add error handling".
7. Nothing substantive for your specialty? Return an empty Comments section with Summary: "clean for this specialty". Do not pad.
8. Severity: blocker | major | minor | nit

## Comment format (local IDs S1, S2, ... within your own output)

Return structured markdown in your final message:

```markdown
# Specialist: <SPECIALTY_NAME> (round N)

## Summary
One paragraph: overall impression for THIS specialty only.

## Comments

### S1 — <short title>
- **Severity**: blocker | major | minor | nit
- **File**: path/to/file.ts:LINE (or "general")
- **Observation**: what you see
- **Why it matters**: concrete consequence
- **Suggested change**: specific change, not a vague direction

### S2 — ...
```

This is round: N
Your specialty: <SPECIALTY_NAME>

````

### S1 — Correctness / plan-fit / edge cases

```

## Your specialty: Correctness / plan-fit / edge cases

Review ONLY for: mismatches between the plan and the implementation; logic bugs, edge cases,
off-by-one, null derefs, race and async ordering; incomplete error handling that is pure correctness
(not the soft-fail catalog); maintainability issues that meaningfully hurt this change; missing
cleanup, wrong status codes, copy-paste bugs.

Do NOT deep-dive: injection/auth catalogs, silent-fallback catalogs, R1–R10 checklists,
unused-import/dead-symbol cleanup, extract-to-shared DRY, or test-suite design (other specialists).

```

### S2 — Security / authZ / secrets

```

## Your specialty: Security / authZ / secrets

Review ONLY for: injection (SQL/NoSQL/command/XSS/template); missing or weak auth checks and broken
access control; thin tenant checks without the assignment/role gates used elsewhere; over-broad
procedures (PENDING/onboarding doing privileged side effects); identity mixed with capability filters;
auth that fails open (`catch { return true }`); secrets or PII in logs and responses; env names in
user-facing errors; cross-tenant leakage; missing input validation on new endpoints; crypto and
session/JWT issues.

Do NOT deep-dive: performance, silent-fallback type hardening (except fail-open auth), test coverage, or plan-fit nits.

```

### S3 — Silent failure / soft types

```

## Your specialty: "Just make it work" / silent-failure / soft types

Prefer hard failures with clear errors over continuing in a wrong state, unless the fallback is
intentional, documented, user-visible graceful degradation. Many fallbacks exist because of soft
types: prefer a hard, exact type plus one validation boundary — never `any` or type erasure.

Silent or swallowed failures: an empty catch, or one that only logs and continues as success;
`.catch(() => undefined|null|[]|{})`; try/catch returning a default "success" on failure;
fire-and-forget async where failure should affect the caller.

Fallbacks that should hard-fail: critical config/env defaults that hide misconfiguration; empty
arrays, objects, or `null` where required data is missing; `|| []`, `?? []`, `?? {}`, `?? ''` papering
over unexpected null/undefined; long optional chains on required paths; production mock, stale, or
placeholder fallbacks without a product requirement; parse failures converted to silent defaults;
retries that "succeed" with partial or empty data.

Soft types that force soft fails — for every fallback you flag: trace the type of the defaulted
value; name the **exact** expected hard type (field-by-field if needed); prefer fixing the type so
the fallback disappears; never suggest `any`, `as any`, double casts, blanket `!`, or `@ts-ignore`.
Flag optional fields that should be required, `Partial<T>` for loaded entities, unvalidated JSON deep
in domain code, empty success where absence is an error, optional params added only so call sites
compile, and DB selects that omit fields the code then defaults.

Type papering and soft-fail behavior: `as any`, double casts, or non-null `!` used to silence the
compiler; partial success reported as full success; validation that warns and continues; auth
fail-open (report it too; the security specialist may overlap).

For each finding state what happens on failure today, what should happen instead, the soft-type root
cause with the exact hard type and boundary if there is one, and the concrete fix (not more defaults,
not `any`).

Severity: auth fail-open and data-loss soft-fails = blocker/major; silent config or required-data
defaults and soft-type fallback cascades = major; suggesting `any` = major; non-critical swallows = minor.

```

### S4 — Recurring PR patterns (R1–R10)

```

## Your specialty: Recurring PR failure patterns (R1–R10)

Walk this checklist against the touched files. Flag hits with blocker/major when they can cause data
loss, wrong money/credit/AUS/messaging behavior, cross-tenant issues, or "looks healthy while broken".
For R2/R6, read consumers outside the touched list when needed.

R1 — Soft failure that looks like success: catch/log-and-continue while status claims ACTIVE / ready /
success; empty fallbacks on **required** export or vendor payloads instead of a preflight throw; setup
failures swallowed so the feature looks live; tests that skip or pass when fixtures are missing;
polling-only UIs with no recovery if webhooks never land.

R2 — Incomplete end-to-end wiring (write-only): UI → API/schema → DB → read/list → export transformers
(each pipeline) → import → jobs → shared sites. Partial shared-component adoption; clear/reset without
a live side-effect update; deleted write path without re-home. If deferred, the plan must say so;
else blocker/major.

R3 — App-only invariants and races: uniqueness only in app code; check-then-act without atomicity;
counter without unique+retry; tenant-scoped unique on a globally unique vendor resource; multi-step
writes missing a transaction.

R4 — Thin authZ / tenant / secret boundaries: weaker gates than siblings; over-broad callers; identity
mixed with capability filters; env names in user errors; PII or secrets logged; dual-pipeline redaction gaps.

R5 — Form hydration / mount wipes: useEffect mount write without a hydration sentinel; auto-flip
nulling persisted enums or booleans; partial updates nulling omitted fields.

R6 — Dual-path inconsistency: parallel transformers with different predicates; CRM vs funnel or admin
vs LO rule drift; dual schemas; sticky columns vs live derivation; actor identity changing across steps.

R7 — Envelopes / partial updates / type lies: casts to guessed shapes vs real envelopes; omitted fields
set to null; `as any` to compile.

R8 — Tests that do not protect the change: no unit test on new branches or guards; happy-path-only
fixtures; no-op when inputs are absent. Prefer a test that would fail if a silent-success or
write-only bug returned (overlap with the testing specialist is OK — focus on whether the test
protects the failure mode).

R9 — UX recovery and edge states: missing loading/error/cancel/retry/stale handling; double-submit;
broken image fallback; eager per-row work without cleanup or virtualization.

R10 — Consistency with codebase patterns: reinventing existing helpers; arbitrary design tokens or
z-index; incomplete a11y for tab-like UI.

In **Why it matters**, name the production failure mode. In **Suggested change**, prefer DB constraints,
existing auth helpers, hard preflight throws, full consumer wiring, and tests that pin the failure
path — not more `??` defaults.

```

### S5 — Testing gaps

```

## Your specialty: Testing gaps

Review ONLY for missing or weak tests. Do not redesign product logic except to say what assertion
would catch a bug.

Cover: new branches or logic without unit tests (especially refusal, guard, migration, backfill);
modified behavior without updated tests; fixtures that hardcode the happy path so assertions always
pass; tests that no-op green when fixtures or reference files are missing; missing tests that assert
**failure** paths; behavior or UI contract changes without e2e/integration updates. Prefer at least
one test that would **fail** if a silent-success or write-only bug returned.

For each comment: where the test should live, what to assert, and what bug it would catch.

```

### S7 — Dead code / unused / stale comments

```

## Your specialty: Dead code / unused / stale comments

Remove refactor leftovers. Prove unused with grep/read — do not guess.

Unused imports and symbols: unused imports (named, default, type-only, unneeded side-effect); unused
locals, params, private helpers, types, constants; exports or re-exports with no in-repo consumers
(unless an intentional public package API); dead or unreachable branches after condition changes;
assigned-never-read variables; leftover feature-flag or env reads.

Stale or useless comments (prefer delete): comments narrating removed behavior ("used to",
"previously", "was", "no longer", "removed X", "old path"); large commented-out code blocks; JSDoc
that contradicts current signatures; TODOs/FIXMEs already done or pointing at deleted code; leftover
section banners for deleted code; obvious narrating comments that add no non-obvious intent.

Do NOT flag: symbols used via types, decorators, DI, or framework reflection; WHY, invariant, or
security comments that still apply; WIP blocks with an active tracking TODO and issue; broad cleanups
outside this change's reach.

Severity: unused import = nit; dead private helper or misleading stale comment = minor/major; stale
comment that contradicts auth or security behavior = major/blocker.
For each: proof of zero refs (or quote the stale comment) and the exact delete.

```

### S8 — Duplication / extract-to-shared

```

## Your specialty: Duplication / extract-to-shared

Flag repeated logic only when ALL hold:

1. **≥ 3 real occurrences** after this change, in the touched files and/or the existing codebase
2. **Would realistically be used more** (sibling features, list+detail+export, dual pipelines, repeated fields)
3. **Stable enough to name** — not a coincidental similar shape with different invariants
4. **Extraction reduces drift risk** — not a premature helper that obscures intent

Scope of the shared home (required on every finding):

| Fan-out                            | Scope                                                   |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| 3+ in one file                     | Private helper in that file                             |
| 3+ in one feature/module           | Module `utils` / `helpers` beside the feature           |
| 3+ across one app                  | App-level shared module already used for similar things |
| 3+ across apps / FE+BE domain rule | Existing monorepo `libs/` domain package                |
| Near-match to an existing helper   | Extend or reuse that helper — no parallel utility       |

Always include: occurrence count, file:line list, proposed symbol and path, params vs identical core.
Search the repo, not only the touched list.

Do NOT flag: only 2 weak lookalikes; intentional test-fixture duplication; trivial one-liners;
similar control flow with different business meaning; huge unrelated DRY refactors disproportionate
to this change.

Severity: easy local 3-copy helper = minor/nit; drifting copies or a dual-path same-domain rule =
major; reinvented existing helper = major. Suggested change must be a concrete signature and home
path — not "consider DRY".

```

### S6 — Architecture sense-check (advisory only)

Append to the shared prefix, but **override** the comment format: S6 does **not** emit C#/S# triage items.

```

## Your specialty: Architecture sense-check (advisory)

Answer one question: does the way this is implemented actually make sense as it is now?

Look at the plan's stated approach and tradeoffs, the implemented files end to end, and the
surrounding codebase patterns (related modules, existing helpers, how similar features are built).
Ask whether the architecture fits this codebase and the problem, and whether a competent engineer
reading it in six months would understand why it was built this way.

Stance — default to "fine": do not rush to demand a re-architecture, because most working designs
that fit local patterns are fine. Speak up only when a **very clear** better way fits this codebase,
or the current approach is **clearly poor** (wrong layer, fights existing abstractions, invents a
parallel system for something already solved, forces painful follow-ups). Style preferences,
micro-optimizations, naming preferences, and preferable-but-not-clearly-better alternatives are NOT
findings. Silence is correct when the design is acceptable.

| Verdict               | When                                                                    | What you write                                                    |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **fine**              | Design is reasonable for this codebase                                  | `Verdict: fine` only — no explanation                             |
| **clear-better-path** | A clearly better architecture fits this change and the surrounding code | Current approach, why a better path is obvious, what that path is |
| **poor-fit**          | Wrong layer, fights patterns, invents parallel systems                  | What is poor, why, and the coherent alternative                   |

Constraints: **never** tell the implementing agent to redo or re-architect the work; **never** emit
Severity, Suggested change, or C# comments for triage. Your output is a **user-facing advisory note**
collected until the end of the loop — half a page at most, one line when fine.

Output format (return this only):

# Specialist: Architecture sense-check (round N)

## Verdict

fine | clear-better-path | poor-fit

## Note

(Omit entirely when Verdict is fine.) When not fine, 2–6 sentences: what was built and why it took
this shape, why that shape is a poor fit or why a better path is clearly preferable, and the concrete
alternative that fits this codebase. Do not instruct anyone to rewrite now.

```

### 2.N.b — Merge specialist outputs into one comments file

Wait until **all eight** specialists finish (or their one retry does).

For the actionable specialists (S1–S5, S7–S8), write `.peer-review/round-N-comments.md`:

1. Start with a round header and a 1–3 sentence summary you synthesize.
2. Renumber all comments globally as **C1, C2, C3, ...** in stable order: S1, S2, S3, S4, S5, S7, S8.
3. Preserve Severity / File / Observation / Why it matters / Suggested change.
4. Add `- **Specialty**: Correctness | Security | SilentFailure | RecurringPattern | Testing | DeadCode | Duplication`.
5. Deduplicate near-identical findings: keep one comment, note both specialties, keep the stronger severity and the more specific fix.
6. Note clean specialists under a "Clean specialists" line; do not invent padding comments.
7. Never put S6 content in this file as triageable comments.

```markdown
# Review round N

## Summary
One paragraph: overall impression and the single most important thing the engineer should address.
Specialists run: Correctness, Security, SilentFailure, RecurringPattern, Testing, DeadCode, Duplication, ArchitectureSense (advisory).

## Comments

### C1 — <short title>
- **Specialty**: Security
- **Severity**: blocker | major | minor | nit
- **File**: path/to/file.ts:LINE (or "general")
- **Observation**: ...
- **Why it matters**: ...
- **Suggested change**: ...

### C2 — ...

## Clean specialists
- Testing: no findings

## Architecture sense-check (advisory — not triaged)
- Round N verdict: fine | clear-better-path | poor-fit
- (Full note lives in round-N-architecture-note.md; do not implement from this)
```

**S6 — stash only.** Write `.peer-review/round-N-architecture-note.md` with S6's raw output (or `Verdict: fine` if clean or empty). Then:

- Do not triage it.
- Do not implement, re-architect, or open follow-up work because of it during the loop.
- Do not stream its notes to the user mid-loop.
- After three rounds keep the strongest verdict (poor-fit > clear-better-path > fine). If all rounds said fine, the summary omits architecture entirely.

### 2.N.c — Triage every comment (actionable only)

Read `.peer-review/round-N-comments.md` and decide each comment C1, C2, ... **Skip S6 entirely** — architecture notes are never accept / reject / defer.

- **accept** — the comment is correct and you will implement it now
- **reject** — the comment is wrong, already handled elsewhere, or based on a misreading; explain why
- **defer** — reasonable but out of scope; explain why and note where it should be tracked (follow-up issue, TODO, etc.)

Write `.peer-review/round-N-decisions.md`:

```markdown
# Round N decisions

## C1 — <title from comment>

- **Decision**: accept | reject | defer
- **Reasoning**: 1-3 sentences. For reject/defer this is mandatory.
- **Implementation note**: (only if accepted) the specific edit you will make

## C2 — ...
```

**Severity is informational, not binding.** A `nit` can be worth accepting if cheap; a `blocker` can be worth rejecting if the reviewer misunderstood. Use judgment.

### 2.N.d — Implement accepted changes

Apply every `accept` decision before the next round begins, using `Edit` / `Write` / specialist Task agents as appropriate. Verify the code still builds and type-checks.

When the accepted fix concerns a soft-fail, fallback, or soft type:

1. Determine the **exact** expected type (domain, API contract, DB schema, caller guarantees) at field level.
2. Introduce or tighten that hard type; validate and narrow once at the right boundary.
3. Remove the silent fallback, empty default, or type papering that prompted the comment.
4. Do not "fix" with `any`, `as any`, `as unknown as T`, blanket `!`, or by making more fields optional. If the compiler complains, the call sites or boundary validation are wrong — fix those.

If applying an accepted change proves it wrong (a test fails, an unexpected type error), change the decision file from `accept` to `reject` and document what you learned. Do not silently drop it. A type error after removing a fallback usually means hardening more call sites, not restoring soft types.

### 2.N.e — Update files-touched

If accepted changes added files, append them to `.peer-review/files-touched.md` so round N+1 sees the full surface area.

## Phase 3 — Final Summary

After round 3 is fully triaged and implemented, write `.peer-review/summary.md`:

```markdown
# Peer review summary

**Spec source**: <path / issue # / "free-form">
**Files created**: <count>
**Files modified**: <count>
**Review model**: 3 sequential rounds × 8 parallel specialists (Correctness, Security, SilentFailure, RecurringPattern, Testing, DeadCode, Duplication, ArchitectureSense-advisory)

## What was built

<2-4 sentences describing the final implementation>

## Review rounds

### Round 1

- Specialists: 8 parallel (7 actionable + architecture advisory)
- Comments raised: <N> (after merge/dedupe; actionable only)
- Accepted: <N> | Rejected: <N> | Deferred: <N>
- Architecture sense-check: fine | clear-better-path | poor-fit
- Notable changes from this round: <bullets>

### Round 2

(same structure)

### Round 3

(same structure)

## Deferred items

<every deferred comment across all rounds, with where it should be tracked>

## Architecture sense-check (user advisory)

<!-- ONLY include this section if the strongest verdict across rounds is NOT fine.
     If all rounds said fine: OMIT this entire section — say nothing about architecture. -->

**Verdict**: clear-better-path | poor-fit

<Synthesize the strongest non-fine note(s) from round-*-architecture-note.md into a short
user-facing paragraph. Do not re-implement. Do not present this as work the agent will do.
Frame as: "For your consideration — the architecture sense-check thought…" >

## Open risks

<anything the reviewers didn't catch but you noticed during the loop, or known limitations>
```

Then send a short message pointing at `.peer-review/summary.md` and listing the deferred items inline.

Architecture in that message: if the strongest S6 verdict is `fine`, say nothing about architecture. If it is `clear-better-path` or `poor-fit`, add a short final paragraph so the user sees what the sense-check thinks — and do not offer to rewrite unless the user asks.

## Output Discipline

- Do not stream specialist comments as they arrive; the files are the record. Give one status line per phase ("plan + implementation done", "round 1: 8 specialists done, 4 comments — 2 accepted, 1 rejected, 1 deferred").
- Do not ask for approval between rounds. The loop is autonomous.
- If the user interrupts mid-loop, the state in `.peer-review/` is enough to resume — say so.
- If a specialist batch is incomplete, merge what you have and proceed. Never leave the user waiting on a hung reviewer.

## Error Recovery

- **Spawn specialists as one foreground parallel batch** so they return together. Do not background them and wait for a later notification — that is how this loop stalls.
- **One specialist fails** (error, empty output, capacity/timeout, or never returns): retry **that specialty only**, once, immediately. If the retry also fails, log `reviewer-failed (<specialty>)` as a `major` comment and continue the round with whoever finished. If S6 fails twice, write `Verdict: fine` with a one-line note that it failed; never block the loop.
- **Silent or hung specialist**: treat it as a failure. Do not poll, do not wait.
- **All specialists fail**: stop the loop and tell the user; do not invent comments.
- **An accepted change breaks the build**: revert that change, flip the decision to `reject` with reasoning `"applying this broke <X>"`, continue.
- **Specialists contradict each other**: both comments survive the merge (dedupe only if identical). Triage each on its merits.
- **A reviewer contradicts a change accepted in a prior round**: allowed and expected, since rounds are fresh. Triage on merits; if you reject, note that round M's accepted change was deliberate.

## Checklist Before Marking Complete

- [ ] `.peer-review/plan.md` exists and covers consumer map, invariants, authZ, failure modes
- [ ] `.peer-review/files-touched.md` exists and lists every changed file
- [ ] `round-1-comments.md`, `round-2-comments.md`, `round-3-comments.md` exist, and each round's merged comments cover silent-failure, recurring patterns, dead-code, and duplication (S3, S4, S7, S8)
- [ ] Each round spawned **eight parallel specialists** (Correctness, Security, SilentFailure, RecurringPattern, Testing, DeadCode, Duplication, ArchitectureSense) — not one mega-reviewer
- [ ] `round-1-decisions.md`, `round-2-decisions.md`, `round-3-decisions.md` exist, and every actionable comment (S1–S5, S7–S8) has a decision
- [ ] All `accept` decisions are reflected in the code, which builds and type-checks
- [ ] S6 notes are in `round-N-architecture-note.md`, were **never** triaged, and did **not** cause a re-architecture during the loop
- [ ] `.peer-review/summary.md` exists, and its architecture section plus the user message mention architecture only when the strongest S6 verdict is not fine
- [ ] The user got a short status message pointing at the summary

If any item is unchecked, the loop is not done.
`````

#### `~/.ai/skills/pr/SKILL.md`

````markdown file=~/.ai/skills/pr/SKILL.md
---
name: pr
description: Commits, pushes the feature branch (never main; never --no-verify), and creates or updates the PR. If the repo pre-push hook fails, fix those errors, commit, and retry the push. Use when user says "/pr", "create pr", "ship it", or "prepare pr".
---

# /pr - Automated PR Workflow

Quality checks (format, lint, typecheck, test, build) run in the repo **pre-push** hook (`.husky/pre-push`; there is no pre-commit hook). Prisma stays in GitHub Actions only. Do not run them here before push. Stop if any step fails.

## Critical safety rules

- Never push directly to `main` or `master`. Create a feature branch first.
- Never `git push --no-verify`. It skips the CI gate.

## Workflow steps

### Step 1: Check the branch (safety check)

```bash
git branch --show-current
```

If the branch is `main` or `master`, stop the push and create a feature branch with `git checkout -b <branch-name>`, named descriptively such as `fix/openai-api-key-deployment` or `feat/user-authentication`. Proceed only on a feature branch.

### Step 2: Check git status

```bash
git status
git diff --stat
```

If the working tree is clean and up to date with remote, go to step 5 to check whether a PR exists. If there are changes, commit them. Do not run typecheck, format, lint, test, or build here; pre-push is the gate.

### Step 3: Stage and commit

```bash
git diff --staged
git diff
git log --oneline -5
git add -A
```

Write a conventional commit message: `feat:` new feature, `fix:` bug fix, `refactor:` refactor, `style:` formatting only, `docs:` docs, `test:` tests, `chore:` maintenance. For formatting-only work use `git commit -m "style: format code"`; otherwise say what changed and why. No `Co-Authored-By` trailer (Claude, Grok, or otherwise).

### Step 4: Push (never to main, never `--no-verify`)

Confirm `git branch --show-current` is not main/master; if it is, go back to step 1.

```bash
git push -u origin HEAD
```

The pre-push hook runs format/sync, lint, typecheck, test, and build. This can take minutes; wait and capture the full output.

#### If the hook blocks the push: fix and retry (max 3 loops)

Do not `--no-verify` and do not skip ahead to the PR.

1. Read the hook banner and the errors above it: `CI job :` (which job failed), `Command:` (exact command), `Fix    :` (hint), and the nx / prettier / jest errors.
2. Fix the **root cause**:
````
