```python file=~/.ai/skills/watch-pr/tests/test_diff.py
    diff,
)

ME = "martin"
OTHER = "marcus"


def snap(**kw) -> Snapshot:
    base = dict(
        me=ME,
        number=7,
        url="https://github.com/o/r/pull/7",
        title="t",
        author=ME,
        state="OPEN",
        is_draft=False,
        is_cross_repo=False,
        mergeable="MERGEABLE",
        merge_state="BLOCKED",
        review_decision="REVIEW_REQUIRED",
        head_ref="feat/x",
        base_ref="main",
        head_oid="a" * 40,
        head_author=ME,
        checks=[],
        reviews=[],
        threads=[],
        issue_comments=[],
        review_requests=[],
        truncated=[],
    )
    base.update(kw)
    return Snapshot(**base)


def review(id: str, author: str, state: str = "COMMENTED", at: str = "2026-10-14T10:00:00Z", commit: Optional[str] = "a" * 40, body: bool = True) -> Review:
    return Review(id=id, author=author, is_bot=False, state=state, submitted_at=at, commit_oid=commit, has_body=body)


def comment(id: str, author: str, at: str, review_id: Optional[str], reply: bool) -> ThreadComment:
    return ThreadComment(id=id, author=author, created_at=at, review_id=review_id, is_reply=reply)


def thread(id: str, comments: List[ThreadComment], resolved: bool = False, resolved_by: Optional[str] = None) -> Thread:
    return Thread(id=id, path="src/a.ts", line=3, is_resolved=resolved, resolved_by=resolved_by, is_outdated=False, started_by=comments[0].author, comments=comments)


def kinds(events: List[str]) -> List[str]:
    return [e.split(" ", 1)[0] for e in events]


def step(prev: Optional[State], cur: Snapshot, role: str):
    return diff(prev, cur, role)


class AuthorTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_baseline_surfaces_existing_conflict_and_failures(self):
        s = snap(mergeable="CONFLICTING", merge_state="DIRTY", checks=[Check("typecheck", "fail", "FAILURE"), Check("lint", "pass", "SUCCESS")])
        events, state = step(None, s, "author")
        self.assertEqual(kinds(events), ["BASELINE", "CONFLICT", "CI_FAILED"])
        self.assertIn("attempt=1", events[2])
        self.assertEqual(state.known_mergeable, "CONFLICTING")

    def test_conflict_fires_once_and_unknown_does_not_reset(self):
        _, s1 = step(None, snap(), "author")
        e2, s2 = step(s1, snap(mergeable="CONFLICTING"), "author")
        self.assertEqual(kinds(e2), ["CONFLICT"])
        e3, s3 = step(s2, snap(mergeable="UNKNOWN"), "author")
        self.assertEqual(e3, [])
        e4, _ = step(s3, snap(mergeable="CONFLICTING"), "author")
        self.assertEqual(e4, [], "UNKNOWN in between must not re-fire CONFLICT")

        _, s2 = step(s1b, snap(head_oid="b" * 40, checks=[Check("test", "pending", "IN_PROGRESS")]), "author")
        e3, _ = step(s2, snap(head_oid="b" * 40, checks=fail), "author")

    def test_thread_resolved_by_author(self):
        _, s1 = step(None, self.reviewed(), "reviewer")
        t = thread("T1", [comment("C1", ME, "2026-10-14T10:00:00Z", "R1", False)], resolved=True, resolved_by=OTHER)
        e2, _ = step(s1, self.reviewed(threads=[t]), "reviewer")
        self.assertEqual(kinds(e2), ["MY_THREAD_RESOLVED"])


class WatchLoopTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """`watch --exit-on-event`: OpenCode only wakes the session when the process exits."""

    def setUp(self):
        self.real_poll, self.real_sleep = watch_pr.poll, watch_pr.time.sleep
        self.addCleanup(setattr, watch_pr, "poll", self.real_poll)
        self.addCleanup(setattr, watch_pr.time, "sleep", self.real_sleep)
        self.sleeps = 0
        watch_pr.time.sleep = self.count_sleep

    def count_sleep(self, _seconds: float) -> None:
        self.sleeps += 1

    def run_watch(self, results: list, exit_on_event: bool) -> int:
        queue = iter(results)

        def fake_poll(_args, save):
            item = next(queue)
            if isinstance(item, Exception):
                raise item
            return item

        watch_pr.poll = fake_poll
        return watch_pr.cmd_watch(argparse.Namespace(pr=7, interval=300, exit_on_event=exit_on_event))

    def test_returns_after_first_poll_with_events(self):
        open_state = State(role="author", snapshot=snap(), known_mergeable="MERGEABLE")
        rc = self.run_watch([([], open_state), ([], open_state), (["CONFLICT pr=7"], open_state)], exit_on_event=True)
        self.assertEqual((rc, self.sleeps), (0, 2))

    def test_returns_on_watch_error(self):
        rc = self.run_watch([watch_pr.GhError("boom")] * 3, exit_on_event=True)
        self.assertEqual((rc, self.sleeps), (1, 2))

    def test_without_flag_keeps_polling_until_closed(self):
        open_state = State(role="author", snapshot=snap(), known_mergeable="MERGEABLE")
        merged = State(role="author", snapshot=snap(state="MERGED"), known_mergeable="MERGEABLE")
        rc = self.run_watch([(["CONFLICT pr=7"], open_state), (["PR_MERGED pr=7"], merged)], exit_on_event=False)
        self.assertEqual((rc, self.sleeps), (0, 1))


class PingTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """`ping`: @-mentions in a PR comment instead of a Slack DM."""

    def setUp(self):
        self.real_gh = watch_pr.gh
        self.addCleanup(setattr, watch_pr, "gh", self.real_gh)
        self.posted: List[List[str]] = []
        watch_pr.gh = self.fake_gh
        self.state_dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
        self.addCleanup(shutil.rmtree, self.state_dir)

    def fake_gh(self, args: List[str]) -> str:
        self.posted.append(args)
        return "https://github.com/o/r/pull/7#issuecomment-1\n"

    def ping(self, to: List[str], text: str = "needs a re-review") -> int:
        return watch_pr.cmd_ping(argparse.Namespace(repo="o/r", pr=7, state_dir=self.state_dir, to=to, text=text, dry_run=False))

    def test_mentions_everyone_in_one_comment(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.ping(["marcus", "ben"]), 0)
        self.assertEqual(len(self.posted), 1)
        body = self.posted[0][self.posted[0].index("--body") + 1]
        self.assertTrue(body.startswith("@marcus @ben needs a re-review"))
        self.assertIn(watch_pr.PING_MARKER, body)

    def test_same_ping_within_window_is_skipped_per_person(self):
        self.ping(["marcus"])
        self.ping(["marcus", "ben"])
        self.assertEqual(len(self.posted), 2)
        second = self.posted[1][self.posted[1].index("--body") + 1]
        self.assertTrue(second.startswith("@ben needs a re-review"))
        self.ping(["marcus", "ben"])
        self.assertEqual(len(self.posted), 2)

    def test_refuses_bots_ghost_and_me(self):
        for login in ("github-actions[bot]", "ghost", "@me"):
            with self.assertRaises(SystemExit):
                self.ping([login])
        self.assertEqual(self.posted, [])

    def test_failed_post_is_not_logged_as_sent(self):
        def failing_gh(_args: List[str]) -> str:
            raise watch_pr.GhError("HTTP 403")

        watch_pr.gh = failing_gh
        self.assertEqual(self.ping(["marcus"]), 1)
        watch_pr.gh = self.fake_gh
        self.assertEqual(self.ping(["marcus"]), 0)
        self.assertEqual(len(self.posted), 1)

    def test_my_ping_is_hidden_but_my_real_answer_is_not(self):
        me = {"login": ME, "__typename": "User"}
        self.assertTrue(watch_pr.is_my_ping({"author": me, "body": f"@marcus needs a re-review\n\n{watch_pr.PING_MARKER}"}, ME))
        self.assertFalse(watch_pr.is_my_ping({"author": me, "body": "Fixed both points in 3ef83f3."}, ME))
        other = {"login": OTHER, "__typename": "User"}
        self.assertFalse(watch_pr.is_my_ping({"author": other, "body": f"@martin hi\n\n{watch_pr.PING_MARKER}"}, ME))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
```

#### `~/.ai/skills/monorepo-worktree/SKILL.md`

````markdown file=~/.ai/skills/monorepo-worktree/SKILL.md
---
name: monorepo-worktree
description: Create or destroy an isolated git worktree of the Future Mortgage monorepo that runs front-end and back-end on alternate ports (own Postgres DB + Redis DB index) so multiple full stacks can run at once. Remaining args after create are a follow-on coding task — do that immediately in the worktree, do not stop after setup. Use when the user runs /monorepo-worktree, /monorepo-worktree destroy|remove|teardown, asks to "spin up a worktree", "run a second stack", "parallel monorepo", "worktree on new ports", or needs a second seeded local environment without stopping the primary checkout. Do NOT use for a code-only PR/branch checkout — that is /worktree-quick.
---

# /monorepo-worktree

Create **or destroy** a parallel monorepo checkout beside the primary stack (`:3000` / `:3001` / `:4201`). For a code-only PR/branch checkout with no env/DB/seed, use `/worktree-quick`.

User arguments: `$ARGUMENTS`

## Commands

| User says                                                   | Action                                                                 |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/monorepo-worktree` / `create` / `setup`                   | Create + seed + report how to serve                                    |
| `/monorepo-worktree <task>`                                 | Create with defaults, then **immediately do the task** in the worktree |
| `/monorepo-worktree destroy` / `remove` / `teardown` / `rm` | Stop processes, drop DB, remove worktree                               |
| `/monorepo-worktree list`                                   | Show worktrees, slots, ports, what is listening                        |

## Parse `$ARGUMENTS` — then do not stall

Classify the first tokens; leftover text is the follow-on task.

| Pattern                                                                                     | Action                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `destroy` / `remove` / `teardown` / `rm` …                                                  | Destroy. No create. No coding task.                 |
| `list`                                                                                      | List only.                                          |
| `create` / `setup` (optional), optional slot int, optional git ref, optional name, **rest** | Create. `rest` is the task.                         |
| Anything else (multi-word, or a single non-verb token)                                      | Create with defaults; the whole string is the task. |

Examples: `implement fees page polish` → slot `1`, ref `HEAD`, name slug from task, then implement it. `2 feature/foo my-feature fix login OTP` → slot 2, that ref/name, task `fix login OTP`. Empty → create slot 1, report URLs, **stop**.

Defaults: slot `1`, ref `HEAD`, name `slot-1` **or** a `[a-z0-9-]{1,32}` slug from the task. **Do not ask** for slot/branch/name. Ask only if the chosen slot's ports are busy (then next free slot ≥1) or a destroy target is ambiguous.

### HARD RULE: setup is a prefix, not the job

If a follow-on task exists, you (this same session) start it the moment `setup-worktree.sh` exits 0. After setup succeeds:

1. Start `./serve-worktree.sh` **background only** (`background: true`; do not wait for exit). Never foreground; coding does not depend on serve.
2. Optional health check: poll the API **≤90s**, then continue even if still warming. Never poll forever.
3. `cd` to the worktree path and **immediately implement the task**. All edits / git / yarn / nx happen in `$WT`, not the primary checkout.
4. One-line URL/path note is fine, then keep working.

**Forbidden** when a follow-on task exists:

- Ending the turn after create with only URLs, credentials, or a destroy command
- Asking "want me to start on X?" / "should I continue?"
- Asking for slot, branch, or name
- Spawning a subagent for the task and then idling
- Waiting on `serve-worktree.sh`, webpack compile, or health as if that were the deliverable

## Default ports (primary = slot 0)

| Service      | Primary    | Slot 1         | Slot 2     | Slot N         |
| ------------ | ---------- | -------------- | ---------- | -------------- |
| web-crm      | 3000       | 3100           | 3200       | 3000 + N×100   |
| server-crm   | 3001       | 3101           | 3201       | 3001 + N×100   |
| web-funnel   | 4201       | 4301           | 4401       | 4201 + N×100   |
| web-income   | 4202       | 4302           | 4402       | 4202 + N×100   |
| Postgres     | dbname     | dbname_wt1     | dbname_wt2 | dbname_wtN     |
| Redis DB #   | 0          | 1              | 2          | N              |
| Cookie       | auth-token | auth-token-wt1 | …          | auth-token-wtN |
| Node inspect | 9229       | 9230           | 9231       | 9229 + N       |

CRM URL for slot N: `http://fm.futurewholesale.local:{WEB_PORT}`.
Income URL for slot N: `http://income.futurewholesale.local:{WEB_PORT}` (same host:port shape as the CRM, like prod `income.trygenius.ai`). `web-income` is its own vite app on `4202 + N×100`; the worktree-local `income-host-proxy` patch makes the CRM dev server forward every `income.*` request (including the Vite HMR websocket) to it. The raw vite port also works.

### Slot rules (non-negotiable)

- **Income opens on the CRM port.** `income.futurewholesale.local:{WEB_PORT}` must render IncomeOS, not the CRM. `webpack-dev-middleware` runs before `devServer.proxy`, so a host-matched proxy entry never sees `/` (CRM `index.html` wins). `scripts/patch-income-host-proxy.py` prepends a host-filtered proxy via `setupMiddlewares`, using the `http-proxy-middleware` that `webpack-dev-server` ships (v2; the hoisted v3 is not a declared dependency). Its fallback target is the slot's own income port, never the shared `4202`.
- **Own income port per slot.** `serve-worktree.sh` exports `WEB_INCOME_PORT=4202 + N×100`. Unset, vite silently drifts to the next free port (4203…) and you end up on another checkout's income app.
- **Income seed every time.** Setup runs `database:seed-income` after the CRM/DU/LPA seeds; without it the income app has no login.
- **Env must be bash-sourceable.** `serve-worktree.sh` does `set -a; source .env; source .env.local`. Primary `.env.local` has `GENIUS_BYTEPRO_ORG_NAME=002 Genius API` unquoted (dotenv fine, bash dies with `Genius: command not found`, exit 127). Setup quotes known keys in the WORKTREE copy only and hard-fails if sourcing still breaks. Never blanket-regex the env files; never edit the primary copy.
- **OTP is 6 digits** (`111111`) for CRM and income logins.
- **Verify income in a browser**, not only curl: log in at `income.futurewholesale.local:{WEB_PORT}`, open Calculations, confirm `income.*` tRPC calls hit `localhost:{API_PORT}` with 200 and the console shows `[vite] connected.` (`playwright-cli console debug`).

## Create (setup)

Use for a second or third local stack beside a running primary, a clean seeded DB for feature work, or side-by-side UI comparison across branches.

### Prerequisites

1. Primary monorepo has working `.env` + `.env.local` (source of secrets), and Docker is running `future-mortgage-postgres` and `future-mortgage-redis`.
2. Hosts file already has the tenant subdomains (same as primary): `127.0.0.1 fm.futurewholesale.local` (and others as needed).
3. Slot ports are free (`lsof -nP -iTCP:3100 -sTCP:LISTEN` etc.).

### Fast path (preferred)

Run from inside the **primary** monorepo (or any of its worktrees). The skill is user-scoped at `~/.ai/skills/monorepo-worktree/`, not in the repo.

```bash
# Slot 1 from current HEAD, name "slot-1"
~/.ai/skills/monorepo-worktree/scripts/setup-worktree.sh 1

# Slot 2 from a branch, custom name
~/.ai/skills/monorepo-worktree/scripts/setup-worktree.sh 2 feature/foo my-feature

# Or pin the repo explicitly:
MONOREPO_ROOT=/path/to/monorepo ~/.ai/skills/monorepo-worktree/scripts/setup-worktree.sh 1
```

The script:

1. `git worktree add` under `../worktrees/monorepo-<name>`
2. Copy env files from primary
3. Create Postgres DB `dbname_wt{N}`
4. Rewrite port / DB / Redis / cookie / FRONTEND_URL values
5. Patch webpack + vite + `web-crm` project.json for env-aware ports, plus the `income-host-proxy`, all worktree-local; quote bash-hostile env values and hard-fail if `.env`/`.env.local` do not source
6. `yarn install` (own `node_modules`; husky postinstall wires pre-push; do not skip yarn; do not symlink from primary) → `yarn prisma:sync` → `yarn nx run database:seed` → `yarn nx run database:seed-du-test-cases` (Fannie Mae) → `yarn nx run database:seed-lpa-test-cases` (Freddie Mac) → `yarn nx run database:seed-income` (Genius Income user + waitlist fixtures)
7. Write `serve-worktree.sh` and the `.worktree-slot` marker

Then start it **in the background** (never wait for the process to exit):

```bash
cd ../worktrees/monorepo-slot-1   # or the path printed by the script
./serve-worktree.sh
```

If a follow-on task exists, start serve in the background and **begin the task immediately**; do not wait for compile/health. While primary is up, `Starting inspector on localhost:9229 failed` is expected; `NODE_OPTIONS=--inspect=9230` avoids it (the setup script sets this).

Verify:

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:3101/health   # slot 1 API
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://localhost:3100/
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://localhost:4301/apply/
curl -s http://income.futurewholesale.local:3100/ | grep -o '<title>[^<]*'   # must be IncomeOS (proxied)
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://income.futurewholesale.local:4302/   # direct vite
# Primary must still be up:
curl -s http://localhost:3001/health
```

### Agent checklist — create

1. **Parse** `$ARGUMENTS` (see above). Do **not** ask for slot/branch/name; default them.
2. **Confirm** the target slot's ports are free (`lsof` / curl). If busy, use the next free slot ≥1.
3. **Run** `~/.ai/skills/monorepo-worktree/scripts/setup-worktree.sh` (preferred) **or** the manual steps below.
4. **Start** `./serve-worktree.sh` in the worktree **in the background**. Never foreground; never wait for exit.
5. **Health** (optional, ≤90s): new API port, `income.futurewholesale.local:{WEB_PORT}` returns IncomeOS, and primary `:3001` still responds. On timeout, continue.
6. **No follow-on task:** report URLs, credentials, path, destroy command, then **stop**.
7. **Follow-on task:** one line with path + URLs, then **immediately implement the task in `$WT`** (this session, not a subagent). Do not stop. Do not ask.

## Destroy / remove / teardown

Use when the user says `destroy`, `remove`, `teardown`, `rm`, `clean up worktree`, `kill the worktree stack`, or `shut down slot N`.

### Fast path (preferred)

Run from inside the monorepo, or set `MONOREPO_ROOT`. Scripts live at `~/.ai/skills/monorepo-worktree/scripts/`.

```bash
# List what exists (no changes)
~/.ai/skills/monorepo-worktree/scripts/destroy-worktree.sh list

# Destroy slot 1 (stops ports, flushes redis DB 1, drops dbname_wt1, removes worktree + branch)
~/.ai/skills/monorepo-worktree/scripts/destroy-worktree.sh destroy 1 --yes

# Same aliases
~/.ai/skills/monorepo-worktree/scripts/destroy-worktree.sh remove 1 --yes
~/.ai/skills/monorepo-worktree/scripts/destroy-worktree.sh teardown --name slot-1 --yes
~/.ai/skills/monorepo-worktree/scripts/destroy-worktree.sh --path ../worktrees/monorepo-slot-1 --yes

# Destroy every monorepo-* under ../worktrees/
~/.ai/skills/monorepo-worktree/scripts/destroy-worktree.sh --all --yes
```

### Flags

| Flag            | Effect                                                |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `--yes` / `-y`  | Required in non-interactive agent shells; skip prompt |
| `--force`       | `git worktree remove --force` (discard dirty files)   |
| `--keep-db`     | Do not `DROP DATABASE dbname_wtN`                     |
| `--keep-branch` | Do not delete the `worktree/<name>` branch            |
| `--keep-redis`  | Do not `FLUSHDB` the slot's Redis logical DB          |

Default destroy is **full cleanup**: stop processes + flush the redis slot + drop the DB + remove the worktree dir + delete the `worktree/*` branch.

### Destroy order (the script guarantees this order)

1. **Resolve target(s)** from slot / name / path / `--all`, using the `.worktree-slot` marker when present
2. **Safety checks** (refuse the primary path, primary ports, primary DB name `dbname`)
3. **Stop listeners** on worktree ports only (`WEB` / `API` / `FUNNEL` / inspect)
4. **Best-effort kill** node/yarn/nx processes whose cwd is under the worktree (covers parent `nx run-many`)
5. **Redis** `FLUSHDB` on logical DB `N`, then **Postgres** terminate backends on `dbname_wtN` and `DROP DATABASE`
6. **`git worktree remove`** (retry with `--force` if needed; prune)
7. **Delete local branch** `worktree/<name>` if it exists and is not checked out elsewhere
8. **Verify** primary ports are untouched; print the remaining `git worktree list`

### Hard safety rules (never violate)

- **Never** kill ports `3000`, `3001`, `4201`, `4202` (primary stack)
- **Never** `DROP DATABASE dbname` (only `dbname_wt[1-9]…`)
- **Never** remove the primary monorepo checkout path
- **Never** flush Redis logical DB `0`
- If `.worktree-slot` is missing, still allow destroy when the path is under `../worktrees/monorepo-*` and ports can be inferred from a `slot-N` name

### Agent checklist — destroy

1. **Parse intent**: `destroy` / `remove` / `teardown` / `list`.
2. **Identify the target**: slot number, name, path, or `--all`. If ambiguous, run `list` and ask.
3. **If the user has uncommitted feature work** only in that worktree, warn and prefer `--keep-branch`, or confirm `--force`.
4. **Run** `~/.ai/skills/monorepo-worktree/scripts/destroy-worktree.sh … --yes`.
5. **Verify**: worktree ports no longer listening; `git worktree list` no longer shows the path; `dbname_wtN` gone (unless `--keep-db`); primary `:3001/health` still OK if it was running.
6. **Report** what was stopped, dropped, and removed.

### Manual destroy (if the script is unavailable)

```bash
PRIMARY="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
# if already inside a worktree, use git common dir:
# PRIMARY="$(dirname "$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir)")"
WT="$(dirname "$PRIMARY")/worktrees/monorepo-slot-1"
SLOT=1
WEB=$((3000 + SLOT*100)); API=$((3001 + SLOT*100)); FUNNEL=$((4201 + SLOT*100))
DB="dbname_wt${SLOT}"

# 1) Stop serve processes on worktree ports ONLY
for p in $WEB $API $FUNNEL; do
  lsof -nP -iTCP:$p -sTCP:LISTEN -t | xargs -r kill -TERM 2>/dev/null || true
done
sleep 1
for p in $WEB $API $FUNNEL; do
  lsof -nP -iTCP:$p -sTCP:LISTEN -t | xargs -r kill -KILL 2>/dev/null || true
done

# 2) Flush redis logical DB for slot (not 0)
docker exec future-mortgage-redis redis-cli -n "$SLOT" FLUSHDB

# 3) Drop isolated DB only
docker exec -e PGPASSWORD=dbpassword future-mortgage-postgres \
  psql -U dbuser -d postgres -c \
  "SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE datname='${DB}' AND pid<>pg_backend_pid();"
docker exec -e PGPASSWORD=dbpassword future-mortgage-postgres \
  psql -U dbuser -d postgres -c "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS ${DB};"

# 4) Remove worktree + branch
git -C "$PRIMARY" worktree remove --force "$WT" || {
  rm -rf "$WT"
  git -C "$PRIMARY" worktree prune
}
git -C "$PRIMARY" branch -D "worktree/slot-${SLOT}" 2>/dev/null || true

# 5) Confirm primary still up
curl -s http://localhost:3001/health || true
git -C "$PRIMARY" worktree list
```

## Manual create process (if the setup script is unavailable)

### 1. Create worktree

```bash
PRIMARY="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$PRIMARY")/worktrees"
# Cannot check out the same branch in two worktrees — use a new branch name
git worktree add -b worktree/slot-1 \
  "$(dirname "$PRIMARY")/worktrees/monorepo-slot-1" HEAD
WT="$(dirname "$PRIMARY")/worktrees/monorepo-slot-1"
```

### 2. Copy env files from primary

```bash
cp "$PRIMARY/.env" "$WT/.env"
cp "$PRIMARY/.env.local" "$WT/.env.local"
cp "$PRIMARY/apps/web-crm/.env.local" "$WT/apps/web-crm/.env.local"
cp "$PRIMARY/apps/web-funnel/.env.local" "$WT/apps/web-funnel/.env.local"
cp "$PRIMARY/apps/server-crm/.env.local" "$WT/apps/server-crm/.env.local"
```

### 3. Create isolated database

```bash
docker exec -e PGPASSWORD=dbpassword future-mortgage-postgres \
  psql -U dbuser -d postgres \
  -c "CREATE DATABASE dbname_wt1 OWNER dbuser;"
```

Reuse the same Postgres **container** and Redis **container**; only change the DB name / Redis logical DB index so data and job queues do not collide.

### 4. Rewrite env for slot ports

In `$WT/.env` (slot 1 example):

```bash
PORT=3101
ADMIN_URL=http://localhost:3100/admin
WEB_FUNNEL_URL=http://localhost:4301
WEB_CRM_PORT=3100
WEB_FUNNEL_PORT=4301
REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379/1
DB_NAME=dbname_wt1
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://dbuser:dbpassword@localhost:5432/dbname_wt1
NX_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:3101
NX_PUBLIC_SERVER_CRM_SOCKET_URL=http://localhost:3101
SESSION_COOKIE_NAME=auth-token-wt1
```

In `$WT/.env.local`:

```bash
FRONTEND_URL=http://fm.futurewholesale.local:3100
# Leave BASE_URL (ngrok) alone unless you open a second tunnel to :3101
```

Write app-local env (Vite only loads env from the app directory).

`apps/web-crm/.env.local`:

```bash
PORT=3100
WEB_CRM_PORT=3100
WEB_FUNNEL_URL=http://localhost:4301
WEB_FUNNEL_PORT=4301
NX_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:3101
NX_PUBLIC_SERVER_CRM_SOCKET_URL=http://localhost:3101
NX_PUBLIC_ENV=local
```

`apps/web-funnel/.env.local`:

```bash
WEB_FUNNEL_PORT=4301
PORT=4301
NX_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:3101
NX_PUBLIC_ENV=local
```

### 5. Make front-end ports env-aware (worktree-local)

**Do not commit these with feature work** unless promoting env-aware defaults.

`apps/web-crm/webpack.config.js` — `devServer.port` and the `/apply` proxy:

```js
port: Number(process.env.PORT || process.env.WEB_CRM_PORT || 3000),
// ...
target:
  process.env.WEB_FUNNEL_PROXY_TARGET ||
  process.env.WEB_FUNNEL_URL ||
  'http://localhost:4201',
```

`apps/web-crm/webpack.config.js` — income host proxy (run the patch; do not hand-write it):

```bash
~/.ai/skills/monorepo-worktree/scripts/patch-income-host-proxy.py "$WT" 4302
```

`apps/web-funnel/vite.config.ts` — `server.port` / `preview.port`:

```ts
port: Number(process.env.WEB_FUNNEL_PORT || process.env.PORT || 4201),
```

`apps/web-crm/project.json` serve env:

```json
"PORT": "3100",
"WEB_CRM_PORT": "3100",
"WEB_FUNNEL_URL": "http://localhost:4301",
"WEB_FUNNEL_PORT": "4301"
```

### 6. Install, migrate, seed

```bash
cd "$WT"
# If leftover node_modules symlink from older setup: rm -f node_modules
yarn install   # own node_modules; husky postinstall — do not skip
yarn prisma:sync
yarn nx run database:seed
yarn nx run database:seed-du-test-cases   # Fannie Mae DU test loans
yarn nx run database:seed-lpa-test-cases  # Freddie Mac LPA test loans
yarn nx run database:seed-income          # Genius Income user + waitlist fixtures
```

### 7. Serve

```bash
export PORT=3101 WEB_CRM_PORT=3100 WEB_FUNNEL_PORT=4301
export WEB_FUNNEL_URL=http://localhost:4301
export WEB_INCOME_PORT=4302
export NX_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:3101
export NX_PUBLIC_SERVER_CRM_SOCKET_URL=http://localhost:3101
export DATABASE_URL=postgresql://dbuser:dbpassword@localhost:5432/dbname_wt1
export REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379/1
export SESSION_COOKIE_NAME=auth-token-wt1
export FRONTEND_URL=http://fm.futurewholesale.local:3100
export NODE_OPTIONS="--inspect=9230"

yarn nx run-many --target=serve
```

---

## Do not

- Point the worktree at the primary `DATABASE_URL` (`dbname`) if you plan to seed or migrate
- Commit worktree-only port patches / `.env*` / `serve-worktree.sh` / `.worktree-slot` as feature commits
- Use preview_* tools (subdomain tenancy requires `*.futurewholesale.local`)
- Reuse `SESSION_COOKIE_NAME=auth-token` across slots, leave `WEB_INCOME_PORT` unset, point the income proxy at `4202`, or hand out the raw vite port as the income URL
- Edit files in the primary checkout after create — work in `$WT`

## Why each isolation knob

| Knob                       | Why                                                                              |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Ports                      | Avoid EADDRINUSE against primary webpack/vite/node                               |
| Separate Postgres DB       | Safe migrate/seed without wiping primary data                                    |
| Redis DB index             | BullMQ / cache keys do not steal jobs from primary                               |
| SESSION_COOKIE_NAME        | Browser cookies ignore port; the same name collides on `*.futurewholesale.local` |
| FRONTEND_URL               | Server redirects / emails must hit this slot's web port                          |
| NX_PUBLIC_API_URL / SOCKET | Browser must talk to this slot's API                                             |
| WEB_FUNNEL_URL             | web-crm `/apply` proxy + server funnel links                                     |
| Node inspect port          | Primary already binds `9229`                                                     |
| WEB_INCOME_PORT            | web-income vite defaults to 4202 and silently drifts when it is taken            |

## Optional: promote env-aware ports to main

If the team wants worktrees without patching configs every time, land this on main with backwards-compatible defaults: read `PORT` / `WEB_CRM_PORT` / `WEB_FUNNEL_URL` in `apps/web-crm/webpack.config.js`, and `WEB_FUNNEL_PORT` / `PORT` in `apps/web-funnel/vite.config.ts`. Then the setup script only needs env rewrites + DB create + install/seed.
````

#### `~/.ai/skills/monorepo-worktree/scripts/destroy-worktree.sh`

```bash file=~/.ai/skills/monorepo-worktree/scripts/destroy-worktree.sh mode=755
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# destroy-worktree.sh — Tear down an isolated monorepo worktree cleanly.
#
# Usage:
#   ./destroy-worktree.sh <slot>                 # e.g. 1 → monorepo-slot-1
#   ./destroy-worktree.sh --name <name>          # e.g. my-feature → monorepo-my-feature
#   ./destroy-worktree.sh --path <abs-or-rel>    # explicit worktree path
#   ./destroy-worktree.sh --all                  # every monorepo-* under ../worktrees/
#   ./destroy-worktree.sh list                   # show discoverable worktrees (no destroy)
#
# Aliases accepted as $1: destroy | remove | teardown | rm | clean | list
#   ./destroy-worktree.sh destroy 1
#   ./destroy-worktree.sh remove --name slot-1
#
# Options:
#   --keep-db       Do not DROP the isolated Postgres database
#   --keep-branch   Do not delete the worktree/* git branch
#   --keep-redis    Do not FLUSHDB the slot's Redis logical DB
#   --force         git worktree remove --force (discard uncommitted worktree files)
#   --yes           Skip interactive confirmation (still prints plan)
#
# Safety (hard rules — script will refuse otherwise):
#   - Never touch primary ports 3000 / 3001 / 4201 / 4202
#   - Never DROP database "dbname" (primary)
#   - Never remove the primary monorepo checkout
#   - Only kill listeners on the worktree's own ports (or PIDs rooted in WT path)
#   - Only DROP databases matching dbname_wt{N}

set -euo pipefail

KEEP_DB=0
KEEP_BRANCH=0
KEEP_REDIS=0
FORCE=0
YES=0
MODE=""          # slot | name | path | all | list
SLOT=""
NAME=""
WT_PATH_ARG=""
ACTION="destroy" # destroy | list

usage() {
  sed -n '2,35p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \?//'
  exit 1
}

# --- parse args ---
ARGS=()
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    destroy|remove|teardown|rm|clean)
      ACTION="destroy"
      shift
      ;;
    list|ls)
      ACTION="list"
      shift
      ;;
    --name)
      MODE="name"
      NAME="${2:-}"
      [[ -n "${NAME}" ]] || usage
      shift 2
      ;;
    --path)
      MODE="path"
      WT_PATH_ARG="${2:-}"
      [[ -n "${WT_PATH_ARG}" ]] || usage
      shift 2
      ;;
    --all)
      MODE="all"
      shift
      ;;
    --keep-db) KEEP_DB=1; shift ;;
    --keep-branch) KEEP_BRANCH=1; shift ;;
    --keep-redis) KEEP_REDIS=1; shift ;;
    --force) FORCE=1; shift ;;
    --yes|-y) YES=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help) usage ;;
    --*)
      echo "Unknown option: $1"
      usage
      ;;
    *)
      ARGS+=("$1")
      shift
      ;;
  esac
done

if [[ ${#ARGS[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
  if [[ -z "${MODE}" && "${ARGS[0]}" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]; then
    MODE="slot"
    SLOT="${ARGS[0]}"
  elif [[ -z "${MODE}" ]]; then
    # treat bare token as name
    MODE="name"
    NAME="${ARGS[0]}"
  fi
fi

if [[ "${ACTION}" == "list" ]]; then
  MODE="list"
fi

if [[ -z "${MODE}" ]]; then
  usage
fi

# --- resolve primary + worktrees root ---
# User-scoped skill — do NOT resolve monorepo from script path.
# Priority: MONOREPO_ROOT env → cwd git main worktree → fail
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
resolve_primary() {
  if [[ -n "${MONOREPO_ROOT:-}" && -d "${MONOREPO_ROOT}" ]]; then
    echo "$(cd "${MONOREPO_ROOT}" && pwd)"
    return 0
  fi
  if ! git rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "ERROR: not inside a monorepo git checkout. cd into it or set MONOREPO_ROOT." >&2
    return 1
  fi
  local main_wt
  main_wt="$(git worktree list --porcelain 2>/dev/null | awk '/^worktree /{print $2; exit}')"
  if [[ -n "${main_wt}" && -d "${main_wt}" ]]; then
    echo "${main_wt}"
    return 0
  fi
  git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null
}
PRIMARY="$(resolve_primary)"
PRIMARY="$(cd "${PRIMARY}" && pwd)"
WORKTREES_ROOT="$(dirname "${PRIMARY}")/worktrees"

is_primary_path() {
  local p
  p="$(cd "$1" 2>/dev/null && pwd || echo "$1")"
  [[ "${p}" == "${PRIMARY}" ]]
}

# --- discovery helpers ---
read_marker() {
  # sets SLOT NAME WEB_PORT API_PORT FUNNEL_PORT INCOME_PORT DB_NAME REDIS_URL INSPECT_PORT from .worktree-slot
  local marker="$1/.worktree-slot"
  SLOT="" NAME="" WEB_PORT="" API_PORT="" FUNNEL_PORT="" INCOME_PORT="" DB_NAME="" REDIS_URL="" INSPECT_PORT=""
  if [[ -f "${marker}" ]]; then
    # shellcheck disable=SC1090
    set -a
    # only allow KEY=VALUE lines
    # shellcheck disable=SC1091
    source <(grep -E '^[A-Z_]+=.*' "${marker}" || true)
    set +a
  fi
}

infer_from_path() {
  local path="$1"
  read_marker "${path}"
  if [[ -z "${NAME}" ]]; then
    NAME="$(basename "${path}" | sed 's/^monorepo-//')"
  fi
  if [[ -z "${SLOT}" && "${NAME}" =~ ^slot-([1-9][0-9]*)$ ]]; then
    SLOT="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
  fi
  if [[ -n "${SLOT}" ]]; then
    WEB_PORT="${WEB_PORT:-$((3000 + SLOT * 100))}"
    API_PORT="${API_PORT:-$((3001 + SLOT * 100))}"
    FUNNEL_PORT="${FUNNEL_PORT:-$((4201 + SLOT * 100))}"
    INCOME_PORT="${INCOME_PORT:-$((4202 + SLOT * 100))}"
    DB_NAME="${DB_NAME:-dbname_wt${SLOT}}"
    REDIS_URL="${REDIS_URL:-redis://localhost:6379/${SLOT}}"
    INSPECT_PORT="${INSPECT_PORT:-$((9229 + SLOT))}"
  fi
}

list_worktrees() {
  echo "Primary: ${PRIMARY}"
  echo "Worktrees root: ${WORKTREES_ROOT}"
  echo ""
  git -C "${PRIMARY}" worktree list
  echo ""
  if [[ -d "${WORKTREES_ROOT}" ]]; then
    echo "Discovered monorepo-* dirs:"
    for d in "${WORKTREES_ROOT}"/monorepo-*; do
      [[ -d "$d" ]] || continue
      if is_primary_path "$d"; then
        continue
      fi
      infer_from_path "$d"
      local ports="?"
      if [[ -n "${WEB_PORT:-}" ]]; then
        ports="${WEB_PORT}/${API_PORT}/${FUNNEL_PORT}/${INCOME_PORT}"
      fi
      local listening=""
      for p in ${WEB_PORT:-} ${API_PORT:-} ${FUNNEL_PORT:-} ${INCOME_PORT:-}; do
        [[ -n "$p" ]] || continue
        if lsof -nP -iTCP:"$p" -sTCP:LISTEN >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          listening+="${p} "
        fi
      done
      echo "  - $d"
      echo "      name=${NAME:-?} slot=${SLOT:-?} ports=${ports} db=${DB_NAME:-?} listening=${listening:-none}"
    done
  else
    echo "(no ${WORKTREES_ROOT} directory)"
  fi
}

if [[ "${MODE}" == "list" || "${ACTION}" == "list" ]]; then
  list_worktrees
  exit 0
fi

# --- build target list ---
TARGETS=()

resolve_one() {
  local path="$1"
  path="$(cd "${path}" 2>/dev/null && pwd || true)"
  if [[ -z "${path}" || ! -d "${path}" ]]; then
    echo "ERROR: worktree path not found: $1" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  if is_primary_path "${path}"; then
    echo "ERROR: refusing to destroy primary monorepo: ${path}" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  # Prefer paths under worktrees/ or registered git worktrees that are not primary
  TARGETS+=("${path}")
}

case "${MODE}" in
  slot)
    NAME="slot-${SLOT}"
    resolve_one "${WORKTREES_ROOT}/monorepo-${NAME}"
    ;;
  name)
    resolve_one "${WORKTREES_ROOT}/monorepo-${NAME}"
    ;;
  path)
    resolve_one "${WT_PATH_ARG}"
    ;;
  all)
    shopt -s nullglob
    found=0
    for d in "${WORKTREES_ROOT}"/monorepo-*; do
      if is_primary_path "$d"; then
        continue
      fi
      TARGETS+=("$(cd "$d" && pwd)")
      found=1
    done
    shopt -u nullglob
    if [[ ${found} -eq 0 ]]; then
      echo "No monorepo-* worktrees found under ${WORKTREES_ROOT}"
      exit 0
    fi
    ;;
  *)
    usage
    ;;
esac

if [[ ${#TARGETS[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: nothing to destroy."
  exit 1
fi

# --- kill helpers ---
PRIMARY_PORTS=(3000 3001 4201 4202)

is_primary_port() {
  local p="$1"
  for pp in "${PRIMARY_PORTS[@]}"; do
    [[ "$p" == "$pp" ]] && return 0
  done
  return 1
}

kill_port() {
  local port="$1"
  if is_primary_port "${port}"; then
    echo "  REFUSE kill primary port ${port}"
    return 0
  fi
  local pids
  pids="$(lsof -nP -iTCP:"${port}" -sTCP:LISTEN -t 2>/dev/null || true)"
  if [[ -z "${pids}" ]]; then
    echo "  port ${port}: nothing listening"
    return 0
  fi
  echo "  port ${port}: killing PIDs ${pids//$'\n'/ }"
  # kill process group leaders gently then hard
  for pid in ${pids}; do
    kill -TERM "${pid}" 2>/dev/null || true
  done
  sleep 1
  for pid in ${pids}; do
    if kill -0 "${pid}" 2>/dev/null; then
      kill -KILL "${pid}" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
  done
}

kill_tree_by_cwd() {
  # Best-effort: kill node/yarn/nx processes whose cwd is under the worktree
  local wt="$1"
  local pid cwd cmd
  # macOS: lsof +cwd; Linux: /proc
  if [[ "$(uname -s)" == "Darwin" ]]; then
    while read -r pid; do
      [[ -n "${pid}" ]] || continue
      cwd="$(lsof -a -p "${pid}" -d cwd -Fn 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^n//p' | head -1 || true)"
      if [[ -n "${cwd}" && "${cwd}" == "${wt}"* ]]; then
        cmd="$(ps -p "${pid}" -o comm= 2>/dev/null || true)"
        case "${cmd}" in
          node|yarn|npm|nx|vite|webpack*|esbuild)
            echo "  cwd-match PID ${pid} (${cmd}) under ${wt}"
            kill -TERM "${pid}" 2>/dev/null || true
            ;;
        esac
      fi
    done < <(pgrep -u "$(id -u)" -f 'node|yarn|nx|vite|webpack' 2>/dev/null || true)
    sleep 1
  fi
}

drop_db() {
  local db="$1"
  if [[ -z "${db}" ]]; then
    echo "  skip DB drop (unknown name)"
    return 0
  fi
  if [[ "${db}" == "dbname" || ! "${db}" =~ ^dbname_wt[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]; then
    echo "  REFUSE to drop non-worktree database: ${db}"
    return 1
  fi
  if ! docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -qx 'future-mortgage-postgres'; then
    echo "  WARN: future-mortgage-postgres not running; cannot drop ${db}"
    return 0
  fi
  echo "  dropping database ${db}..."
  # terminate backends then drop
  docker exec -e PGPASSWORD=dbpassword future-mortgage-postgres \
    psql -U dbuser -d postgres -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -c \
    "SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE datname = '${db}' AND pid <> pg_backend_pid();" \
    >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  docker exec -e PGPASSWORD=dbpassword future-mortgage-postgres \
    psql -U dbuser -d postgres -c "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS ${db};"
}

flush_redis_db() {
  local slot="$1"
  if [[ -z "${slot}" || ! "${slot}" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]; then
    echo "  skip redis flush (unknown slot)"
    return 0
  fi
  if ! docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -qx 'future-mortgage-redis'; then
    echo "  WARN: future-mortgage-redis not running; skip flush db ${slot}"
    return 0
  fi
  echo "  redis FLUSHDB on logical DB ${slot}..."
  docker exec future-mortgage-redis redis-cli -n "${slot}" FLUSHDB >/dev/null
}

remove_git_worktree() {
  local path="$1"
  local force_flag=()
  [[ "${FORCE}" -eq 1 ]] && force_flag=(--force)

  if git -C "${PRIMARY}" worktree list --porcelain | grep -q "^worktree ${path}$"; then
    echo "  git worktree remove ${path} ${force_flag[*]:-}"
    # If dirty and not forced, try force after unlock
    if ! git -C "${PRIMARY}" worktree remove ${force_flag[@]+"${force_flag[@]}"} "${path}" 2>/tmp/wt-rm-err.$$; then
      echo "  worktree remove failed, retrying with --force..."
      cat /tmp/wt-rm-err.$$ >&2 || true
      git -C "${PRIMARY}" worktree remove --force "${path}" || {
        echo "  WARN: git worktree remove failed; removing directory manually"
        rm -rf "${path}"
        git -C "${PRIMARY}" worktree prune
      }
    fi
    rm -f /tmp/wt-rm-err.$$
  elif [[ -d "${path}" ]]; then
    echo "  path not registered as git worktree; removing directory ${path}"
    rm -rf "${path}"
    git -C "${PRIMARY}" worktree prune 2>/dev/null || true
  else
    echo "  path already gone: ${path}"
  fi
}

delete_branch() {
  local path="$1"
  local branch name
  # Prefer branch currently (or was) associated via marker name
  infer_from_path "${path}" 2>/dev/null || true
  name="${NAME:-$(basename "${path}" | sed 's/^monorepo-//')}"
  branch="worktree/${name}"
  if git -C "${PRIMARY}" show-ref --verify --quiet "refs/heads/${branch}"; then
    # refuse if checked out elsewhere
    if git -C "${PRIMARY}" worktree list | grep -q "\[${branch}\]"; then
      echo "  branch ${branch} still checked out elsewhere; skip delete"
      return 0
    fi
    echo "  deleting branch ${branch}"
    git -C "${PRIMARY}" branch -D "${branch}" || true
  else
    echo "  no local branch ${branch}"
  fi
}

destroy_one() {
  local path="$1"
  echo ""
  echo "───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────"
  echo " Destroying: ${path}"
  echo "───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────"

  if is_primary_path "${path}"; then
    echo "ERROR: refusing primary path"
    return 1
  fi

  infer_from_path "${path}"

  echo "  slot=${SLOT:-?} name=${NAME:-?} web=${WEB_PORT:-?} api=${API_PORT:-?} funnel=${FUNNEL_PORT:-?} income=${INCOME_PORT:-?}"
  echo "  db=${DB_NAME:-?} redis=${REDIS_URL:-?}"

  # 1) Stop services on worktree ports
  echo "→ Stopping listeners"
  for p in ${WEB_PORT:-} ${API_PORT:-} ${FUNNEL_PORT:-} ${INCOME_PORT:-} ${INSPECT_PORT:-}; do
    [[ -n "${p}" ]] || continue
    kill_port "${p}"
  done
  # Also stop anything still rooted in this cwd (nx parent, etc.)
  if [[ -d "${path}" ]]; then
    kill_tree_by_cwd "${path}"
  fi
  sleep 0.5

  # Verify ports free
  for p in ${WEB_PORT:-} ${API_PORT:-} ${FUNNEL_PORT:-} ${INCOME_PORT:-}; do
    [[ -n "${p}" ]] || continue
    if lsof -nP -iTCP:"${p}" -sTCP:LISTEN >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "  WARN: port ${p} still listening after kill; retrying KILL"
      kill_port "${p}"
    fi
  done

  # 2) Redis flush for slot
  if [[ "${KEEP_REDIS}" -eq 0 && -n "${SLOT:-}" ]]; then
    echo "→ Redis cleanup"
    flush_redis_db "${SLOT}"
  else
    echo "→ Redis cleanup skipped"
  fi

  # 3) Drop isolated DB
  if [[ "${KEEP_DB}" -eq 0 ]]; then
    echo "→ Postgres cleanup"
    drop_db "${DB_NAME:-}"
  else
    echo "→ Postgres cleanup skipped (--keep-db)"
  fi

  # 4) Remove git worktree + files
  echo "→ Git worktree remove"
  # Capture branch name before path disappears
  local branch_name="${NAME:-}"
  remove_git_worktree "${path}"

  # 5) Delete worktree/* branch
  if [[ "${KEEP_BRANCH}" -eq 0 ]]; then
    echo "→ Branch cleanup"
    # path may be gone; use captured name
    if [[ -n "${branch_name}" ]]; then
      local branch="worktree/${branch_name}"
      if git -C "${PRIMARY}" show-ref --verify --quiet "refs/heads/${branch}"; then
        if git -C "${PRIMARY}" worktree list | grep -q "\[${branch}\]"; then
          echo "  branch ${branch} still checked out; skip"
        else
          echo "  deleting branch ${branch}"
          git -C "${PRIMARY}" branch -D "${branch}" || true
        fi
      else
        echo "  no local branch ${branch}"
      fi
    fi
  else
    echo "→ Branch cleanup skipped (--keep-branch)"
  fi

  echo "✓ Destroy complete for ${NAME:-$path}"
}

# --- plan + confirm ---
echo "═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
echo " Monorepo worktree DESTROY"
echo "═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
echo "  primary:      ${PRIMARY}"
echo "  targets:      ${#TARGETS[@]}"
echo "  keep-db:      ${KEEP_DB}"
echo "  keep-branch:  ${KEEP_BRANCH}"
echo "  keep-redis:   ${KEEP_REDIS}"
echo "  force:        ${FORCE}"
for t in "${TARGETS[@]}"; do
  infer_from_path "$t"
  echo "  - $t  (slot=${SLOT:-?} db=${DB_NAME:-?} ports=${WEB_PORT:-?}/${API_PORT:-?}/${FUNNEL_PORT:-?})"
done
echo "═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"

if [[ "${YES}" -ne 1 ]]; then
  if [[ -t 0 ]]; then
    read -r -p "Proceed with destroy? [y/N] " ans
    case "${ans}" in
      y|Y|yes|YES) ;;
      *) echo "Aborted."; exit 1 ;;
    esac
  else
    echo "Non-interactive shell: pass --yes to confirm destroy."
    exit 1
  fi
fi

for t in "${TARGETS[@]}"; do
  destroy_one "$t"
done

echo ""
echo "→ Verifying primary stack still intact"
for p in 3000 3001 4201; do
  if lsof -nP -iTCP:"$p" -sTCP:LISTEN >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "  primary port $p: still listening (ok)"
  else
    echo "  primary port $p: not listening (ok if primary wasn't running)"
  fi
done
if curl -s -m 2 http://localhost:3001/health >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "  primary API :3001 health OK"
fi

echo ""
echo "→ Remaining worktrees"
git -C "${PRIMARY}" worktree list
echo ""
echo "Done."
```

#### `~/.ai/skills/monorepo-worktree/scripts/patch-income-host-proxy.py`

```python file=~/.ai/skills/monorepo-worktree/scripts/patch-income-host-proxy.py mode=755
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Worktree-local patch: serve web-income on the CRM dev-server port for income.* hosts.

webpack-dev-middleware runs before devServer.proxy, so a host-matched proxy entry
never sees `/` (the CRM index.html wins). This prepends a host-filtered proxy via
setupMiddlewares instead. ws:true carries Vite's HMR socket; webpack-dev-server's
own socket only claims `/ws`, so the two never collide.

Usage: patch-income-host-proxy.py <worktree-path> <income-port>
Idempotent; exits non-zero if the devServer anchor is missing.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import sys

MARKER = "income-host-proxy"
ANCHOR = "    historyApiFallback: {\n"

wt, income_port = Path(sys.argv[1]), int(sys.argv[2])
wp = wt / "apps/web-crm/webpack.config.js"
t = wp.read_text()

if MARKER in t:
    print(f"  webpack.config.js already has {MARKER}")
    sys.exit(0)
if t.count(ANCHOR) != 1:
    sys.exit(f"ERROR: expected one devServer `historyApiFallback: {{` in {wp}; patch by hand")

block = f"""    // Worktree-local ({MARKER}): income.<domain> on the CRM port → this slot's
    // web-income vite. Do not commit.
    setupMiddlewares: middlewares => {{
      const {{ createProxyMiddleware }} = require(
        require.resolve('http-proxy-middleware', {{
          paths: [require.resolve('webpack-dev-server')],
        }})
      );
      middlewares.unshift({{
        name: '{MARKER}',
        middleware: createProxyMiddleware(
          (_pathname, req) => (req.headers.host || '').startsWith('income.'),
          {{
            target: `http://localhost:${{Number(process.env.WEB_INCOME_PORT || {income_port})}}`,
            ws: true,
          }}
        ),
      }});
      return middlewares;
    }},
"""
wp.write_text(t.replace(ANCHOR, block + ANCHOR, 1))
print(f"  patched apps/web-crm/webpack.config.js ({MARKER} → :{income_port})")
```

#### `~/.ai/skills/monorepo-worktree/scripts/setup-worktree.sh`

```bash file=~/.ai/skills/monorepo-worktree/scripts/setup-worktree.sh mode=755
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# setup-worktree.sh — Create an isolated monorepo worktree on alternate ports.
#
# Usage:
#   ./setup-worktree.sh <slot> [branch] [worktree-name]
#
# Examples:
#   ./setup-worktree.sh 1
#   ./setup-worktree.sh 2 feature/my-branch my-feature
#   ./setup-worktree.sh 1 HEAD immutable-email
#
# Slot 0 is reserved for the primary checkout (ports 3000/3001/4201).
# Slot N (>=1) uses:
#   web-crm     = 3000 + N*100
#   server-crm  = 3001 + N*100
#   web-funnel  = 4201 + N*100
#   postgres DB = dbname_wt{N}
#   redis DB #  = N
#   cookie name = auth-token-wt{N}
#
# Prerequisites: docker postgres (future-mortgage-postgres), redis, yarn, git.
# Env sources: copies .env / .env.local from the primary monorepo checkout.

set -euo pipefail

SLOT="${1:-}"
BRANCH_OR_REF="${2:-HEAD}"
NAME="${3:-slot-${SLOT}}"

if [[ -z "${SLOT}" || ! "${SLOT}" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]; then
  echo "Usage: $0 <slot>=1..N [branch|ref=HEAD] [name=slot-N]"
  echo "  Slot must be an integer >= 1 (slot 0 = primary checkout)."
  exit 1
fi

# Resolve primary monorepo (user-scoped skill — do NOT use script path).
# Priority: MONOREPO_ROOT env → cwd git common dir → cwd toplevel
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
resolve_primary() {
  if [[ -n "${MONOREPO_ROOT:-}" && -d "${MONOREPO_ROOT}" ]]; then
    echo "$(cd "${MONOREPO_ROOT}" && pwd)"
    return 0
  fi
  local common
  if common="$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null)"; then
    # common dir is <repo>/.git (or .git file target); primary checkout is parent of .git
    local root
    root="$(dirname "${common}")"
    # If we're inside a linked worktree, common dir still points at main .git
    # Prefer the main worktree path from worktree list (first entry)
    local main_wt
    main_wt="$(git worktree list --porcelain 2>/dev/null | awk '/^worktree /{print $2; exit}')"
    if [[ -n "${main_wt}" && -d "${main_wt}" ]]; then
      echo "${main_wt}"
      return 0
    fi
    echo "${root}"
    return 0
  fi
  echo "ERROR: cannot resolve monorepo root. cd into the monorepo or set MONOREPO_ROOT." >&2
  return 1
}
PRIMARY="$(resolve_primary)"

WORKTREES_ROOT="$(dirname "${PRIMARY}")/worktrees"
WT_PATH="${WORKTREES_ROOT}/monorepo-${NAME}"
BRANCH_NAME="worktree/${NAME}"

WEB_PORT=$((3000 + SLOT * 100))
API_PORT=$((3001 + SLOT * 100))
FUNNEL_PORT=$((4201 + SLOT * 100))
INCOME_PORT=$((4202 + SLOT * 100))
DB_NAME="dbname_wt${SLOT}"
REDIS_URL="redis://localhost:6379/${SLOT}"
COOKIE="auth-token-wt${SLOT}"
INSPECT_PORT=$((9229 + SLOT))

echo "═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
echo " Monorepo worktree setup"
echo "═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
echo "  slot:        ${SLOT}"
echo "  name:        ${NAME}"
echo "  path:        ${WT_PATH}"
echo "  base ref:    ${BRANCH_OR_REF}"
echo "  branch:      ${BRANCH_NAME}"
echo "  web-crm:     http://fm.futurewholesale.local:${WEB_PORT}"
echo "  server-crm:  http://localhost:${API_PORT}"
echo "  web-funnel:  http://localhost:${FUNNEL_PORT}/apply/"
echo "  web-income:  http://income.futurewholesale.local:${INCOME_PORT}"
echo "  database:    ${DB_NAME}"
echo "  redis:       ${REDIS_URL}"
echo "  cookie:      ${COOKIE}"
echo "  inspect:     ${INSPECT_PORT}"
echo "═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"

# --- port free check ---
for p in "${WEB_PORT}" "${API_PORT}" "${FUNNEL_PORT}" "${INCOME_PORT}"; do
  if lsof -nP -iTCP:"${p}" -sTCP:LISTEN >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "ERROR: port ${p} is already in use. Pick another slot or free the port."
    lsof -nP -iTCP:"${p}" -sTCP:LISTEN || true
    exit 1
  fi
done

# --- create worktree ---
mkdir -p "${WORKTREES_ROOT}"
if [[ -d "${WT_PATH}" ]]; then
  echo "Worktree path already exists: ${WT_PATH}"
  echo "Reusing it (will re-apply env / config patches)."
else
  cd "${PRIMARY}"
  # If BRANCH_OR_REF is an existing local branch name and we want a new worktree branch from it:
  git worktree add -b "${BRANCH_NAME}" "${WT_PATH}" "${BRANCH_OR_REF}"
fi

# --- copy env files from primary ---
copy_env() {
  local src="$1" dest="$2"
  if [[ -f "${src}" ]]; then
    cp "${src}" "${dest}"
    echo "  copied $(basename "${src}") → ${dest}"
  else
    echo "  WARN: missing ${src}"
  fi
}

# Yarn installs a real node_modules in the worktree. Drop a leftover symlink
# from older setup so install does not write into the primary tree.
drop_node_modules_symlink() {
  local dest="${1}/node_modules"
  if [[ -L "${dest}" ]]; then
    rm -f "${dest}"
    echo "  removed leftover node_modules symlink"
  fi
}
echo "Copying env files from ${PRIMARY}..."
copy_env "${PRIMARY}/.env" "${WT_PATH}/.env"
copy_env "${PRIMARY}/.env.local" "${WT_PATH}/.env.local"
copy_env "${PRIMARY}/apps/web-crm/.env.local" "${WT_PATH}/apps/web-crm/.env.local"
copy_env "${PRIMARY}/apps/web-funnel/.env.local" "${WT_PATH}/apps/web-funnel/.env.local"
copy_env "${PRIMARY}/apps/server-crm/.env.local" "${WT_PATH}/apps/server-crm/.env.local"

# --- create isolated postgres database ---
echo "Ensuring postgres database ${DB_NAME}..."
if ! docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -qx 'future-mortgage-postgres'; then
  echo "ERROR: container future-mortgage-postgres is not running."
  echo "Start it with: docker compose -f docker-compose.database.yml up -d"
  exit 1
fi
EXISTS=$(docker exec -e PGPASSWORD=dbpassword future-mortgage-postgres \
  psql -U dbuser -d postgres -tc "SELECT 1 FROM pg_database WHERE datname = '${DB_NAME}'" | tr -d '[:space:]')
if [[ "${EXISTS}" != "1" ]]; then
  docker exec -e PGPASSWORD=dbpassword future-mortgage-postgres \
    psql -U dbuser -d postgres -c "CREATE DATABASE ${DB_NAME} OWNER dbuser;"
  echo "  created ${DB_NAME}"
else
  echo "  ${DB_NAME} already exists"
fi

# --- patch root .env / .env.local ---
python3 - "${WT_PATH}" "${WEB_PORT}" "${API_PORT}" "${FUNNEL_PORT}" "${DB_NAME}" "${SLOT}" "${COOKIE}" <<'PY'
import re, sys
from pathlib import Path

wt, web, api, funnel, db, slot, cookie = sys.argv[1:8]
web, api, funnel, slot = int(web), int(api), int(funnel), int(slot)

def set_kv(text: str, key: str, value: str) -> str:
    pat = re.compile(rf"^{re.escape(key)}=.*$", re.M)
    line = f"{key}={value}"
    if pat.search(text):
        return pat.sub(line, text)
    if text and not text.endswith("\n"):
        text += "\n"
    return text + line + "\n"

env_path = Path(wt) / ".env"
env = env_path.read_text() if env_path.exists() else ""
for k, v in {
    "PORT": str(api),
    "ADMIN_URL": f"http://localhost:{web}/admin",
    "WEB_FUNNEL_URL": f"http://localhost:{funnel}",
    "WEB_CRM_PORT": str(web),
    "WEB_FUNNEL_PORT": str(funnel),
    "REDIS_URL": f"redis://localhost:6379/{slot}",
    "DB_NAME": db,
    "DATABASE_URL": f"postgresql://dbuser:dbpassword@localhost:5432/{db}",
    "NX_PUBLIC_API_URL": f"http://localhost:{api}",
    "NX_PUBLIC_SERVER_CRM_SOCKET_URL": f"http://localhost:{api}",
    "SESSION_COOKIE_NAME": cookie,
}.items():
    env = set_kv(env, k, v)
env_path.write_text(env)

local_path = Path(wt) / ".env.local"
local = local_path.read_text() if local_path.exists() else ""
local = set_kv(local, "FRONTEND_URL", f"http://fm.futurewholesale.local:{web}")
local_path.write_text(local)

# App-local env so Vite/webpack pick up ports without relying on cwd
(Path(wt) / "apps/web-crm/.env.local").write_text(
    f"""PORT={web}
WEB_CRM_PORT={web}
WEB_FUNNEL_URL=http://localhost:{funnel}
WEB_FUNNEL_PORT={funnel}
NX_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:{api}
NX_PUBLIC_SERVER_CRM_SOCKET_URL=http://localhost:{api}
NX_PUBLIC_ENV=local
"""
)
(Path(wt) / "apps/web-funnel/.env.local").write_text(
    f"""WEB_FUNNEL_PORT={funnel}
PORT={funnel}
NX_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:{api}
NX_PUBLIC_ENV=local
"""
)
print("  patched .env, .env.local, app .env.local files")
PY

# --- serve-worktree.sh sources .env/.env.local as bash; dotenv tolerates unquoted spaces, bash does not ---
# Targeted keys only (a blanket regex pass once mangled every line). Never edits the primary copy.
python3 - "${WT_PATH}" <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import sys

KEYS = ("GENIUS_BYTEPRO_ORG_NAME",)
p = Path(sys.argv[1]) / ".env.local"
lines = p.read_text().split("\n")
quoted = []
for i, ln in enumerate(lines):
    key, sep, val = ln.partition("=")
    if sep and key in KEYS and val and val[0] not in "\"'" and any(c.isspace() for c in val):
        lines[i] = f'{key}="{val}"'
        quoted.append(key)
if quoted:
    p.write_text("\n".join(lines))
print(f"  quoted in worktree .env.local: {', '.join(quoted) or 'nothing needed'}")
PY
if ! (cd "${WT_PATH}" && bash -ec 'set -a; source .env; source .env.local') >/dev/null; then
  echo "ERROR: worktree .env/.env.local are not bash-sourceable; serve-worktree.sh would exit immediately."
  echo "       Quote the offending line in the WORKTREE copy only (add its key to KEYS above)."
  exit 1
fi

# --- make webpack + vite + project.json env-aware / slot-ported ---
python3 - "${WT_PATH}" "${WEB_PORT}" "${FUNNEL_PORT}" <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import sys, re

wt, web, funnel = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
web, funnel = int(web), int(funnel)

# webpack.config.js
wp = Path(wt) / "apps/web-crm/webpack.config.js"
t = wp.read_text()
t2 = re.sub(
    r"port:\s*Number\(process\.env\.PORT \|\| process\.env\.WEB_CRM_PORT \|\| 3000\),|port:\s*3000,",
    "port: Number(process.env.PORT || process.env.WEB_CRM_PORT || 3000),",
    t,
    count=1,
)
t2 = re.sub(
    r"target:\s*\n\s*process\.env\.WEB_FUNNEL_PROXY_TARGET \|\|\n\s*process\.env\.WEB_FUNNEL_URL \|\|\n\s*'http://localhost:4201',|target:\s*'http://localhost:4201',",
    "target:\n          process.env.WEB_FUNNEL_PROXY_TARGET ||\n          process.env.WEB_FUNNEL_URL ||\n          'http://localhost:4201',",
    t2,
    count=1,
)
if t2 != t:
    wp.write_text(t2)
    print("  patched apps/web-crm/webpack.config.js (env-aware ports)")
else:
    # force simple replace if still plain
    if "port: 3000" in t:
        t = t.replace("port: 3000,", "port: Number(process.env.PORT || process.env.WEB_CRM_PORT || 3000),", 1)
        t = t.replace(
            "target: 'http://localhost:4201',",
            "target:\n          process.env.WEB_FUNNEL_PROXY_TARGET ||\n          process.env.WEB_FUNNEL_URL ||\n          'http://localhost:4201',",
            1,
        )
        wp.write_text(t)
        print("  patched apps/web-crm/webpack.config.js")
    else:
        print("  webpack.config.js already env-aware (or unexpected format)")

# vite.config.ts
vt = Path(wt) / "apps/web-funnel/vite.config.ts"
v = vt.read_text()
v2 = v.replace(
    "port: 4201,",

)
if v2 != v:

else:
    print("  vite.config.ts already env-aware (or unexpected format)")

# web-crm project.json — set PORT env for serve target
pj = Path(wt) / "apps/web-crm/project.json"
p = pj.read_text()
p2 = re.sub(r'"PORT":\s*"\d+"', f'"PORT": "{web}"', p)
if '"WEB_FUNNEL_URL"' not in p2:
    p2 = p2.replace(
        f'"PORT": "{web}"',
        f'"PORT": "{web}",\n          "WEB_CRM_PORT": "{web}",\n          "WEB_FUNNEL_URL": "http://localhost:{funnel}",\n          "WEB_FUNNEL_PORT": "{funnel}"',
    )
else:
    p2 = re.sub(r'"WEB_CRM_PORT":\s*"\d+"', f'"WEB_CRM_PORT": "{web}"', p2)
    p2 = re.sub(r'"WEB_FUNNEL_PORT":\s*"\d+"', f'"WEB_FUNNEL_PORT": "{funnel}"', p2)
    p2 = re.sub(
        r'"WEB_FUNNEL_URL":\s*"[^"]*"',
        f'"WEB_FUNNEL_URL": "http://localhost:{funnel}"',
        p2,

if p2 != p:

    print("  patched apps/web-crm/project.json serve ports")
else:

print(

)
```

#### `~/.ai/skills/nasa-handbook/SKILL.md`

````markdown file=~/.ai/skills/nasa-handbook/SKILL.md
---
name: nasa-handbook
description: Make printable technical documents in the style of Apollo-era NASA paperwork. The model is an Apollo Operations Handbook "Systems Data" page with a typed running head, numbered paragraphs, Leroy-lettered line drawings and schematics, a performance data table, NOTE/CAUTION/WARNING notices, a Flight Data File checklist card, a black thumb tab and a dated footer, rendered to an A4 or US Letter PDF. Use this whenever someone asks for NASA-style, Apollo-style, retro aerospace or "mission manual" documentation. Also use it for a technical explainer, spec sheet or one-pager that should look like vintage engineering paperwork, for a handbook page explaining a product, codebase, system or fictional gadget, or for "another one of those NASA pages", even if they never say Apollo or handbook.
compatibility: opencode
metadata:
  opencode/slash: "true"
---

# NASA handbook page

This skill makes one-page (or few-page) technical documents that read like a
1969 Apollo Operations Handbook page. A typed running head sits over numbered
paragraphs, followed by a hero line drawing, a second figure, a data table, a
caution and a crew checklist. The thumb tab and the dated footer finish the
page. It suits real subjects (a codebase, a product, a protocol) and fictional
ones (a portal gun). For real subjects, the page should leave the reader
understanding the technical idea. For fiction, it should be convincing.

Finished pages ship with the skill. Look at the PNGs before you start;
they are the bar:
- `assets/examples/portal-gun-device.png` (+ `.html`): a fictional device. It
  has a general arrangement drawing with callouts, dimensions and a section
  view, an electrical schematic, and a deadpan WARNING.
- `assets/examples/espresso-fluid-system.png` (+ `.html`): a fictional machine
  built on real physics (brewing at lunar-habitat cabin pressure). It has a
  general arrangement with a section view, a fluid and electrical schematic
  with station tags, and a computed chart. A fresh agent made it from this
  skill alone in six render passes.

## Resource paths

Paths here are relative to this skill's directory (the base directory reported
when the skill loads):

- `assets/template.html`: the page with all CSS, shared SVG markers and
  patterns, a skeleton of every block and a fit check. Start every page from it.
- `assets/fonts/`: Routed Gothic (Leroy lettering), Letter Gothic and their
  licences. Copy the folder next to the page.
- `scripts/render.sh`: renders a PDF (print) and a 2x PNG (preview) with
  headless Chrome. It prints the room left above the footer and exits 3 when
  the page overflows.
- `scripts/check.py`: checks for one page, the page size, black and white
  only, and the fonts. It also cuts 300 dpi half-width tiles for the visual
  review (`--out DIR` to choose where). It can't see overflow; `render.sh`
  catches that.
- `references/style-guide.md`: anatomy, space budget, typography, writing
  voice, which figures to draw, drawing taste, pitfalls and variants. Read it
  in full for your first page in a session.
- `references/svg-parts.md`: copy-paste drawing parts (boxes, drums, wires,
  breakers, switches, talkbacks, callouts, dimensions, section views,
  timelines, sequence and parts strips, valves, pumps, gauges, sensors,
  station tags, charts).
- `references/sources.md`: the scanned originals and what each taught.

## Workflow

1. **Understand the subject and find its one idea.** This is the sentence the
   reader must leave with ("the coffee brews at sea-level pressure in a sealed circuit"). For a real
   system, read its spec or README and the code. Grep every number you intend
   to print (limits, sizes, intervals, retries, key bindings, UI strings) and
   prefer the code when docs disagree. For fiction, invent a consistent
   specification first: name, what it does, five to eight numbers with units,
   its controls and its one dangerous failure mode.

2. **Plan the page on paper before drawing.** Decide the blocks in the order
   they appear: intro (3 lines), hero figure, functional description
   (4 lines), one underlined mechanism (2 lines), secondary figure (with
   optional DETAIL insets), data table (6–8 rows), one notice, a checklist
   (6–7 steps). Pick figure types from the table in style guide §5. Write the
   text now; it is short, and writing it shows what the figures must explain.

3. **Set up the folder.** Use the folder the user names. Otherwise use a new
   folder in the current project or working directory.
   ```sh
   mkdir -p <out> && cp <skill>/assets/template.html <out>/<name>.html && cp -R <skill>/assets/fonts <out>/fonts
   ```

4. **Fill the template.** Replace every `[BRACKETED]` placeholder. Draw the
   figures from `svg-parts.md` parts in millimetre coordinates. Keep the shared
   `nh-*` defs. Don't add colours, logos or texture.

5. **Render and fit.** Run `sh <skill>/scripts/render.sh <out>/<name>.html`.
   The `fit:` line reports the space left above the footer; aim for 4–10 mm.
   It exits 3 on overflow. Then cut words or a table row, not type size. In
   the lower band, trim whichever column is taller (style guide §2).

6. **Check and look.** Run
   `uv run --no-project --with pymupdf python <skill>/scripts/check.py <out>/<name>.pdf`.
   It must report one page and black and white only. Then open every tile it
   lists and look for:
   - a line or leader crossing or touching text (keep 0.6 mm clear)
   - labels touching each other or a box edge
   - a dimension value sitting on its line
   - a clipped word
   - a pattern used with two meanings
   - an arrow pointing at the wrong thing

   Fix them, then repeat steps 5 and 6. Most of the quality comes from this
   loop; expect three to six passes.

7. **Deliver.** Give the PDF as the print file and the PNG as the preview, and
   show it if you have a preview tool. Say what the page explains. For real
   subjects, list the files you checked the numbers against. Mention anything
   deliberately simplified.

## What makes it look right

These are the calls that separate a convincing page from a costume.
`style-guide.md` has the full reasoning.

- **Structure over texture.** The genre is carried by the running head,
  numbered paragraphs, figure codes, change bar, thumb tab and dated footer.
  Leave out coffee stains, noise, rotated stamps and NASA insignia.
- **Three typefaces, three jobs.** Letter-spaced serif typewriter text for
  prose. Leroy caps for everything inside a drawing. Letter Gothic only on the
  checklist card. All caps is the genre here, not a style mistake.
- **One idea, two figures.** The hero figure draws the one idea; the secondary
  shows how it behaves over time or in detail. Everything else supports them.
- **Flat, exact voice.** Third person, present tense, numbers with units,
  controls in caps as placarded, UI strings quoted exactly.
- **Text is never crossed by a line.** Leaders start just outside their label
  and end on the part. Move a label rather than shrink it.
- **Drafting-sized details.** Line weights from 0.16 to 0.5 mm, arrowheads
  about 2 mm long, labels 2.05 to 2.5 mm. The template's classes and markers
  already encode this; use them instead of ad-hoc strokes.
- **Pure black on pure white.** Differentiate with hatching and dotted
  outlines. Printers turn any tint or grey into dots.
- **Truth first on real subjects.** A precise-looking page with a wrong number
  is worse than one row fewer.

## Variants

US Letter, multi-page sections, controls-and-displays pages, engineering
drawing sheets, Technical Note covers and the 1975 Helvetica look are all
covered in style guide §9. The page structure, the drawing rules and the check
loop stay the same.

## Requirements

- Google Chrome or Chromium, for `render.sh` (set `CHROME=/path` if it isn't
  found).
- `uv` (or a Python with `pymupdf`), for `check.py`.
- Iowan Old Style ships with macOS. Elsewhere the body falls back to Georgia,
  which is acceptable. Helvetica Neue (or Arial) supplies the flagged "1" in
  drawing labels.
````

```text file=~/.ai/skills/nasa-handbook/assets/template.html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<title>[DOC NUMBER] [PROGRAM] Operations Handbook, page [2.1-1]</title>
<style>
  /* ---------- fonts (files in ./fonts, copied from the skill's assets/fonts) ---------- */
  /* Leroy-template lettering for every drawing label. */
  @font-face { font-family: "Routed Gothic"; src: url("fonts/routed-gothic.ttf"); unicode-range: U+0000-0030, U+0032-FFFF; }
  @font-face { font-family: "Routed Gothic Narrow"; src: url("fonts/routed-gothic-narrow.ttf"); unicode-range: U+0000-0030, U+0032-FFFF; }
  /* Leroy's plain "1" reads as "I" (API V1, T1). Borrow a flagged one. Delete these two
     rules for a strictly period look on pages without versions or subscripts. */
  @font-face { font-family: "Routed Gothic"; src: local("Helvetica Neue"), local("HelveticaNeue"), local("Arial"); unicode-range: U+0031; }
  @font-face { font-family: "Routed Gothic Narrow"; src: local("Helvetica Neue"), local("HelveticaNeue"), local("Arial"); unicode-range: U+0031; }
  /* IBM Selectric Letter Gothic: crew checklists only. */
  @font-face { font-family: "Letter Gothic"; src: url("fonts/LetterGothicCode-R.ttf"); font-weight: 400; }
  @font-face { font-family: "Letter Gothic"; src: url("fonts/LetterGothicCode-B.ttf"); font-weight: 700; }

  @page { size: A4; margin: 0; }
  * { box-sizing: border-box; }
  html, body { margin: 0; padding: 0; background: #8a8a86; }
  body { -webkit-print-color-adjust: exact; print-color-adjust: exact; }
  @media print { html, body { background: none; } }

  :root {
    --ink: #000000;
    --paper: #fbfaf5;   /* screen only; print is pure white (below) */
    --type: "Iowan Old Style", "Iowan", Georgia, serif;
    --leroy: "Routed Gothic Narrow", "Routed Gothic", sans-serif;
    --selectric: "Letter Gothic", "Courier", monospace;
  }
  /* Must come after :root. A printed off-white tint is halftoned into dots. */
  @media print { :root { --paper: #ffffff; } }

  .page {
    position: relative;
    width: 210mm;
    height: 297mm;
    margin: 0 auto;
    padding: 9mm 15mm 0 16mm;
    background: var(--paper);
    color: var(--ink);
    font-family: var(--type);
    font-size: 8pt;
    line-height: 1.33;
    letter-spacing: 0.055em;   /* the Selectric typewriter spacing */
    overflow: hidden;
  }

  /* ---------- running head / foot ---------- */
  .head { text-align: center; line-height: 1.25; }
  .head .doc { font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.6pt; letter-spacing: 0.06em; }
  .head .title { font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.6pt; letter-spacing: 0.08em; }
  .head .part { margin-top: 2.2mm; font-size: 8.2pt; letter-spacing: 0.1em; }
  .rule { height: 0; border-top: 1.5pt solid var(--ink); margin: 1.4mm -2mm 0; }

  .foot { position: absolute; left: 16mm; right: 15mm; bottom: 8mm; }
  .foot .rule { margin: 0 -2mm 1.6mm; }
  .foot .sub { text-align: center; letter-spacing: 0.1em; font-size: 8.2pt; }
  .foot .line { display: flex; align-items: baseline; justify-content: space-between; margin-top: 2.2mm; font-size: 8.2pt; }
  .foot .fill { display: inline-block; border-bottom: 0.6pt solid var(--ink); text-align: center; padding: 0 1mm; font-size: 8.8pt; letter-spacing: 0.03em; }

  /* ---------- section opener ---------- */
  .opener { text-align: center; letter-spacing: 0.12em; margin: 3.4mm 0 2mm; line-height: 1.6; }

  /* ---------- numbered paragraphs ---------- */
  .para { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 19mm 1fr; position: relative; }
  .para .num { letter-spacing: 0.08em; }
  .para h2, .para h3 { margin: 0 0 0.8mm; font: inherit; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: 0.08em; }
  .para h3 { text-decoration: underline; text-underline-offset: 1.6pt; text-decoration-thickness: 0.5pt; letter-spacing: 0.06em; }
  .para p { margin: 0 0 1mm; text-indent: 9mm; text-align: left; }
  .para p.flush { text-indent: 0; }
  .changebar { position: absolute; left: -9mm; width: 1.3mm; background: var(--ink); }
  .nowrap { white-space: nowrap; }

  /* ---------- figures ---------- */
  figure { margin: 1.6mm 0 0; }
  figure svg { display: block; width: 100%; height: auto; }
  figcaption { text-align: center; margin-top: 0.6mm; letter-spacing: 0.07em; }
  figcaption .n { margin-right: 3mm; }

  /* SVG units are millimetres on paper: a figure 180 units wide fills the 179 mm column. */
  svg text { font-family: var(--leroy); fill: var(--ink); letter-spacing: 0.04px; }
  svg .o    { fill: none; stroke: var(--ink); stroke-width: 0.42; stroke-linejoin: round; stroke-linecap: round; } /* object line */
  svg .of   { fill: var(--paper); stroke: var(--ink); stroke-width: 0.42; stroke-linejoin: round; }               /* object, opaque */
  svg .t    { fill: none; stroke: var(--ink); stroke-width: 0.17; stroke-linecap: round; }                        /* thin detail */
  svg .hid  { fill: none; stroke: var(--ink); stroke-width: 0.22; stroke-dasharray: 1.3 0.7; }                     /* hidden */
  svg .cl   { fill: none; stroke: var(--ink); stroke-width: 0.16; stroke-dasharray: 5 0.8 0.9 0.8; }               /* centerline */
  svg .cut  { fill: none; stroke: var(--ink); stroke-width: 0.5; stroke-dasharray: 5 1 1 1; }                      /* section cut */
  svg .ld   { fill: none; stroke: var(--ink); stroke-width: 0.16; marker-end: url(#nh-leader); }                   /* leader */
  svg .dim  { fill: none; stroke: var(--ink); stroke-width: 0.16; marker-start: url(#nh-dim); }                    /* dimension half */
  svg .w    { fill: none; stroke: var(--ink); stroke-width: 0.3; stroke-linejoin: round; }                         /* wire */
  svg .wa   { fill: none; stroke: var(--ink); stroke-width: 0.3; stroke-linejoin: round; marker-end: url(#nh-arrow); } /* wire with arrow */
  svg .box  { fill: var(--paper); stroke: var(--ink); stroke-width: 0.45; }
  svg .panel{ fill: none; stroke: var(--ink); stroke-width: 0.3; stroke-dasharray: 2 1; }
  svg .ev   { fill: none; stroke: var(--ink); stroke-width: 0.18; stroke-dasharray: 1 0.7; }                       /* timeline event */
  svg .vid  { fill: url(#nh-hatch); stroke: var(--ink); stroke-width: 0.35; }                                      /* hatched bar */
  svg .aud  { fill: var(--paper); stroke: var(--ink); stroke-width: 0.35; }                                        /* plain bar */
  svg .gap  { fill: var(--paper); stroke: var(--ink); stroke-width: 0.35; stroke-dasharray: 0.6 0.5; }             /* dotted bar */
  svg .grain{ fill: url(#nh-dots); stroke: var(--ink); stroke-width: 0.35; }                                       /* granular, powder, fill */
  svg .dot  { fill: var(--ink); }
  svg .lbl   { font-size: 2.35px; }                                         /* callouts, box titles */
  svg .lbl-s { font-size: 2.05px; }                                         /* secondary lines, wire names */
  svg .lbl-b { font-size: 2.5px; font-family: "Routed Gothic", sans-serif; } /* view titles, big letters */
  svg .code  { font-size: 2.4px; font-family: "Routed Gothic", sans-serif; } /* figure code, bottom right */

  /* ---------- lower band: data table + notice + checklist ---------- */
  .lower { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 64mm; column-gap: 6mm; margin-top: 2.8mm; }
  .tcap { text-align: center; letter-spacing: 0.07em; margin: 0 0 0.8mm; }
  table { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 7.3pt; line-height: 1.2; }
  th, td { border: 0.6pt solid var(--ink); padding: 0.35mm 1.6mm; text-align: left; vertical-align: top; font-weight: 400; }
  thead th { text-align: center; letter-spacing: 0.1em; padding: 0.5mm 1.6mm; }
  td.v { white-space: nowrap; }

  .notice { text-align: left; margin-bottom: 1.8mm; }
  .notice .tag { display: block; text-align: center; letter-spacing: 0.18em; font-weight: 700; text-decoration: underline; text-underline-offset: 1.6pt; text-decoration-thickness: 0.6pt; margin-bottom: 0.8mm; }
  .notice p { margin: 0; font-size: 7.4pt; line-height: 1.28; }

  .card { border: 0.8pt solid var(--ink); font-family: var(--selectric); font-size: 7.1pt; line-height: 1.3; letter-spacing: 0; }
  .card .bar { background: var(--ink); color: var(--paper); font-weight: 700; padding: 0.5mm 1.8mm; display: flex; justify-content: space-between; }
  .card ol { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0.8mm 1.8mm 1mm; }
  .card li { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 3.2mm 1fr; white-space: pre; }

  /* black thumb tab, bleeds off the trim edge */
  .tab { position: absolute; right: 0; top: 112mm; width: 8.5mm; height: 17mm; background: var(--ink); color: var(--paper);
    font-family: "Routed Gothic", sans-serif; font-size: 8pt; letter-spacing: 0.08em; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; }
</style>
</head>
<body>

    <div class="line">
      <span>Mission <span class="fill" style="width:20mm">&nbsp;</span></span>
      <span>Basic Date <span class="fill" style="width:30mm">[1 January 1970]</span></span>
      <span>Change Date <span class="fill" style="width:30mm">&nbsp;</span></span>
      <span>Page <span class="fill" style="width:18mm">2.1-1</span></span>
    </div>
  </footer>

</div>

<script>
  // Fit check: room left between the last content block and the footer.
  // .page hides overflow, so without this an overfull page fails silently.
  // render.sh prints the result from <html data-fit>.
  document.fonts.ready.then(() => {
    const page = document.querySelector('.page')
    const foot = page.querySelector('.foot')
    let bottom = 0
    for (const el of page.children) {
      if (el === foot || el.classList.contains('tab')) continue
      bottom = Math.max(bottom, el.getBoundingClientRect().bottom)
    }
    const free = (foot.getBoundingClientRect().top - bottom) * 25.4 / 96
    document.documentElement.dataset.fit = free >= 0 ? `ok, ${free.toFixed(1)} mm free above the footer` : `OVERFLOW by ${(-free).toFixed(1)} mm`
  })
</script>
</body>
</html>
```
