```markdown file=~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/commands/plan-review.md
---
name: plan-review
description: Compare an implementation plan against the current codebase, with each fix to accept or reject in the page
---

Load the visual-explainer skill and make a visual plan review.

Input: `$@` is a plan path or plan text. If it is empty, ask for the plan.

Read the whole plan, every file it references, and the code that depends on them. For each proposed change, check that the file, function, or type exists, that current behavior matches the plan, which ripple effects it misses, and whether its tests fit the repo style. Cite the plan section and `file:line`.

Write the review as a plan page (`references/plans.md`), so the reader accepts or rejects each fix in place:

- **Header**: h1 "Review: <plan name>"; the lead gives the verdict (approve, revise, or reject) and why.
- **Hero**: `<ve-flow>` of the planned design, the parts a finding touches marked `gone` or `new` and linked to its claim.
- **Claims**: one level-1 claim per finding, as a sentence that can be false ("Step 3 edits a function that no longer exists."), most serious first, at most 5; smaller findings as child claims. Each proves itself with `<ve-code src=… lines=…>` or a quote of the plan. Unconfirmed findings get `evidence="guess"`.
- **Decisions**: each finding gets `<ve-ask id="f1" q="Fix the plan this way?">` (then `f2`, …) with `<ve-opt value="accept" default>` describing the fix and `<ve-opt value="reject">Keep the plan as written</ve-opt>`, plus any real alternative.
- **End** with `aux="scope"`: what the plan gets right.

Hand over in one line. When the response arrives, edit the plan file: apply accepted fixes and leave rejected ones as written.
```

#### `~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/commands/state-machine.md`

```markdown file=~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/commands/state-machine.md
---
name: state-machine
description: Draw a state machine from the code itself, walk every state, and show each rule it breaks as a path to replay
---

Load the visual-explainer skill, read `references/machines.md`, and draw the state machine in `$@` (a file, a reducer, or a feature). With no argument, ask which machine.

1. Gather: find the step (a reducer, an XState config, a `transition()`), the shape of its state, and every event that reaches it. Cite each with `file:line`.
2. Model: import the step from the repo. Copy a step as a hand model (`when`, `then`, `at:`) only when it does I/O, and say which steps are copied.
3. Rules: before drawing, propose 1–3 rules in the user's words, each with the state it must reject, and agree them in the chat.
4. Render. Fix every ✗, then read the machine's Page line: states, broken rules, dead ends, events that never fire. Place up to about 12 states by hand; past that, use `auto`.
5. Prove each broken rule against the real code: replay its path (the last replay caption lists the events) as a one-line script or a test file the user can keep, and run it. The replay shows the rule that breaks soonest; to see another rule's path, render with that rule alone. A path that does not reproduce is a bug in the model: fix the model, never the rule.
6. Hand off one line per broken rule (the rule, the path, the test), the dead ends and events that never fire, and what the model leaves out (timers, retries, a second user, the network).
```

#### `~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/kit/ask.js`

```js file=~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/kit/ask.js
// <ve-ask> on a kit page (kit/render.mjs inlines this only when the page has one, after kit/reply.js).
// An answer the reader gives counts toward Reply (N) and goes into the reply; a question left alone is listed with its default, or as no answer.
{
const R = window.veReply, asks = R ? R.$$("main fieldset.ask[data-ask]") : [];
if (asks.length) {
  const KEY = `ve-page-ask:${location.pathname}`;
  const inputs = (a) => R.$$("input", a);
  const read = (a) => { const ins = inputs(a); return ins[0]?.type === "checkbox" ? ins.filter((i) => i.checked).map((i) => i.value) : ins.find((i) => i.checked)?.value ?? null; };
  const write = (a, v) => { for (const i of inputs(a)) i.checked = Array.isArray(v) ? v.includes(i.value) : i.value === v; };
  const defaults = new Map(asks.map((a) => [a, read(a)]));
  const clean = (s) => s.trim().replace(/\s+/g, " ");
  const label = (a, v) => clean(inputs(a).find((i) => i.value === v)?.closest("label").querySelector(".opt-label").textContent ?? v);
  const pick = (a, v = read(a)) => (Array.isArray(v) ? v.map((x) => label(a, x)).join(", ") || "none" : v == null ? "no answer" : label(a, v));
  const q = (a) => clean(R.$(".ask-q", a).textContent);
  let done = {};
  try { done = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(KEY) || "{}"); } catch { /* storage can be off for file:// pages */ }
  const answered = (a) => Object.hasOwn(done, a.dataset.ask);
  // a saved answer whose options are gone (the page was revised) is dropped
  for (const a of asks) if (answered(a)) { const v = done[a.dataset.ask]; if ([v].flat().every((x) => inputs(a).some((i) => i.value === x))) write(a, v); else delete done[a.dataset.ask]; }
  const save = () => { try { if (Object.keys(done).length) localStorage.setItem(KEY, JSON.stringify(done)); else localStorage.removeItem(KEY); } catch { /* see above */ } };
  const record = (a) => { done[a.dataset.ask] = read(a); save(); R.refresh(); };
  for (const a of asks) {
    a.addEventListener("change", () => record(a));
    // a click, Space, or Enter on the option already selected is an answer too, though no change fires;
    // where a change does follow, it records the final value
    a.addEventListener("click", (e) => { if (e.target.matches("input")) record(a); });
    a.addEventListener("keydown", (e) => { if ((e.key === "Enter" || e.key === " ") && e.target.matches("input:checked")) record(a); });
  }
  const state = (a) => (answered(a) ? pick(a) : [read(a) ?? []].flat().length ? `${pick(a)} (default)` : "no answer");
  R.parts.push({
    count: () => asks.filter(answered).length,
    lines: () => asks.map((a) => `- ${a.dataset.ask} (${q(a)}): ${state(a)}`),
    rows: () => R.h("section", { class: "r-sec" }, R.h("p", { class: "ve-label caps" }, `Questions · ${asks.filter(answered).length} of ${asks.length} answered`),
      asks.map((a) => R.h("div", { class: "r-row" }, R.h("span", { class: "k" }, answered(a) ? "✓" : "·"), R.h("span", {}, state(a), R.h("small", {}, q(a))),
        R.h("span", { class: "acts" }, R.h("button", { type: "button", onclick: () => { R.close(); a.scrollIntoView({ block: "center" }); (inputs(a).find((i) => i.checked) || inputs(a)[0]).focus({ preventScroll: true }); } }, answered(a) ? "Change" : "Answer"))))),
    clear: () => { done = {}; save(); for (const a of asks) write(a, defaults.get(a)); },
  });
}
}
```

#### `~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/kit/ask.mjs`

```text file=~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/kit/ask.mjs
// <ve-ask>: a question the reader answers in the page, with <ve-opt> options. Plans and kit pages share it; ctx:
//   ids        Map from an id to where it was first used, shared by the page's asks
//   k, total   this ask's number and how many the page has
//   claims     plans: the claim numbers an option's removes= may name
//   page       pages: default is optional, removes= is an error, and the legend says Question
import { esc, inner, kids, textOf, words } from "./html.mjs";

export function expandAsk(n, { errors, warnings, where, ids, k, total, claims = new Set(), page = false }) {
  const at = where(n);
  const id = n.attrs.id;
  if (!id || !/^[\w-]+$/.test(id)) errors.push(`${at}: needs id="word" (letters, digits, - or _)`);
  else if (id in Object.prototype) errors.push(`${at}: id="${id}" is a reserved name; pick another`);
  else if (ids.has(id)) errors.push(`${at}: id="${id}" is already used at ${ids.get(id)}`);
  ids.set(id, at);
  const q = n.attrs.q || "";
  if (!q) errors.push(`${at}: needs q="the question"`);
  else if (words(q) > 15) warnings.push(`${at}: the question is ${words(q)} words; keep it to about 15`);
  const multi = "multi" in n.attrs;
  const opts = kids(n).filter((k) => k.name === "ve-opt");
  if (opts.length < 2) errors.push(`${at}: needs at least two <ve-opt>`);
  const defaults = opts.filter((o) => "default" in o.attrs);
  if (!multi && !page && defaults.length !== 1) errors.push(`${at}: mark exactly one <ve-opt default>, the option you would build`);
  if (!multi && page && defaults.length > 1) errors.push(`${at}: mark at most one <ve-opt default>`);
  const values = new Set();
  for (const o of opts) {
    if (!o.attrs.value) errors.push(`${where(o)}: needs value=""`);
    else if (values.has(o.attrs.value)) errors.push(`${where(o)}: value="${o.attrs.value}" is used twice`);
    values.add(o.attrs.value);
    if (page && o.attrs.removes) errors.push(`${where(o)}: removes= belongs to plan pages`);
    else for (const no of (o.attrs.removes || "").split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean)) if (!claims.has(no)) errors.push(`${where(o)}: removes="${no}", but there is no claim ${no}`);
    if (o.attrs.note && words(o.attrs.note) > 12) warnings.push(`${where(o)}: note is ${words(o.attrs.note)} words; keep it to about 12`);
  }
  const row = opts.every((o) => textOf(o).trim().length <= 18 && !o.attrs.note && !o.attrs.removes);
  const body = opts.map((o) => {
    const cost = [];
    for (const [k, sign, word] of [["new", "+", "new"], ["changed", "~", "changed"], ["deleted", "−", "deleted"]]) {
      const v = +(o.attrs[k] || 0);
      if (v) cost.push(`${v > 0 ? sign : "−"}${Math.abs(v)} ${word} file${Math.abs(v) === 1 ? "" : "s"}`);
    }
    for (const no of (o.attrs.removes || "").split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean)) cost.push(`<span class="goes">claim ${esc(no)} goes</span>`);
    const data = ["new", "changed", "deleted", "removes"].filter((k) => o.attrs[k]).map((k) => ` data-${k}="${esc(o.attrs[k])}"`).join("");
    const def = "default" in o.attrs;
    return `<label class="opt"><input type="${multi ? "checkbox" : "radio"}" name="${esc(id)}" value="${esc(o.attrs.value ?? "")}"${def ? " checked" : ""}${data}><span class="opt-body"><span class="opt-label">${inner(o).trim()}</span>${def ? '<span class="sug">Suggested</span>' : ""}${o.attrs.note ? `<small>${esc(o.attrs.note)}</small>` : ""}${cost.length ? `<span class="opt-cost">${cost.join(" · ")}</span>` : ""}</span></label>`;
  }).join("");
  const legend = page ? (total > 1 ? `Question <b>${k}</b> of ${total}` : "Question") : `Decision <b>${k}</b> of ${total}`;
  return `<fieldset class="ask${row ? " row" : ""}" id="ask-${esc(id)}" data-ask="${esc(id)}"><legend class="ask-n">${legend}</legend><p class="ask-q">${esc(q)}</p><div class="ask-opts">${body}</div></fieldset>`;
}
```

```text file=~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/kit/files.mjs
// Reading cited files from the repo, shared by the plan renderer (code exhibits, at="path:line") and the state-machine model
// (its imports and the at: of a hand-written step). Only files under the root, and never one named like a secrets file.
import { readFileSync, realpathSync, statSync } from "node:fs";
import { relative, resolve, sep } from "node:path";

const SECRET_NAME = /(^|\/)\.(git|ssh|aws|gnupg|kube)(\/|$)|(^|\/)(\.env(\.[^/]*)?|\.npmrc|\.netrc|\.pypirc|\.pgpass|\.git-credentials|id_(rsa|dsa|ecdsa|ed25519)[^/]*|credentials[^/]*|secrets?(\.[^/]*)?)$|\.(pem|key|p12|pfx|tfstate|kdbx|keystore)$/i;

/** A cached reader for paths relative to realRoot: { text, abs } or { error } (plus missing: true when nothing is there). */
export function fileReader(realRoot) {
  const cache = new Map();
  return (path) => {
    if (cache.has(path)) return cache.get(path);
    let out;
    try {
      const requested = relative(realRoot, resolve(realRoot, path)).split(sep).join("/");
      const real = realpathSync(resolve(realRoot, path));
      const rel = relative(realRoot, real);
      if (rel.startsWith("..") || rel.startsWith(sep) || /^[a-z]:/i.test(rel)) out = { error: `${path} is outside ${realRoot}` };
      // check the cited name and the link target both, so a link named .env cannot pass as config.txt
      else if (SECRET_NAME.test(requested) || SECRET_NAME.test(rel.split(sep).join("/"))) out = { error: `${path} looks like a secrets file; not reading it` };
      else if (!statSync(real).isFile()) out = { error: `${path} is not a file` };
      else out = { text: readFileSync(real, "utf8").replace(/\r\n/g, "\n"), abs: real };
    } catch {
      out = { missing: true, error: `${path} not found under ${realRoot}` };
    }
    cache.set(path, out);
    return out;
  };
}

/** Checks at="path" or at="path:line": { error } when it is malformed or names nothing, and abs when the file exists.
 * A path alone may name a file that does not exist yet (a plan creates it); a line must exist. */
export function checkAt(at, read) {
  const [path, line] = at.split(":");
  const r = read(path);
  if (line !== undefined && !/^[1-9]\d*$/.test(line)) return { error: `at="${at}"; write at="path" or at="path:line" with a line number from 1` };
  if (r.error && (!r.missing || line)) return { error: `at="${at}": ${r.error}` };
  if (!r.missing && line && +line > r.text.split("\n").length) return { error: `at="${at}", but ${path} has ${r.text.split("\n").length} lines`, abs: r.abs };
  return { abs: r.abs };
}
```

```text file=~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/kit/flow.mjs
// <ve-flow>: boxes on a grid and arrows between them. The layout is computed here, so no coordinates are written by hand.
// Plans and ordinary pages share it; ctx says how a part links to the rest of its page:
//   ref(k)              attributes for a box or arrow (plans: claim refs; pages: data-ref and data-s as written)
//   callout(k, x, y)    marks drawn over a box (plans: one numbered callout per claim)
//   page                pages: an arrow with data-s also gets a replay token, and the drawing keeps its labels between 12 px and 1.3× as rendered
//   root, models        a <script type="text/plain" model> child is walked from root's code (models: false refuses it; references/machines.md)
// A <ve-region> holds the <ve-node>s of one part of the model's state and draws as a dashed boundary around them.
import { esc, hasClass, kids, textOf } from "./html.mjs";
import { drawAuto, drawModel } from "./machine.mjs";

const W = 140, H = 64, GY = 56, PAD = 16;
const RX = 14, RT = 30; // a region's padding beside and below its nodes, and above them, where its label sits; two regions in adjacent rows keep GY − RX − RT apart
const CH = 8.4; // one mono character of a 14-unit label
export const ifAttrs = (k, cls = "") => `${k.attrs["data-if"] ? ` data-if="${esc(k.attrs["data-if"])}"` : ""}${cls || k.ifOff ? ` class="${cls}${k.ifOff ? `${cls ? " " : ""}is-if-off` : ""}"` : ""}`;
const flags = (k, base) => [base, ...["key", "new", "gone", "hot", "async", "breaks", "may-break", "bug-path"].filter((f) => f in k.attrs).map((f) => `is-${f}`)].join(" ");

export function expandFlow(n, { errors, warnings, where, ref, callout = () => "", page = false, root = process.cwd(), models = true }) {
  // plans keep three columns near the 560×340 hero; a page has room for longer arrow labels between columns
  const GX = page ? 124 : 84;
  const boxes = new Map(), edges = [], scripts = [], regions = new Map(), before = errors.length;
  const place = (k, region) => {
    const m = (k.attrs.at || "").match(/^(\d+(?:\.5)?)[\s,]+(\d+(?:\.5)?)$/);
    if (!k.attrs.id || !m) errors.push(`${where(k)}: needs id="name" and at="column row", for example at="2 1"`);
    else if (boxes.has(k.attrs.id)) errors.push(`${where(k)}: id="${k.attrs.id}" is used twice`);
    else { boxes.set(k.attrs.id, { k, x: PAD + (m[1] - 1) * (W + GX), y: PAD + (m[2] - 1) * (H + GY) }); region?.ids.push(k.attrs.id); }
  };
  for (const k of kids(n)) {
    if (k.name === "ve-node") place(k);
    else if (k.name === "ve-region") {
      const g = { k, ids: [] };
      if (!k.attrs.id || regions.has(k.attrs.id)) errors.push(`${where(k)}: needs its own id="part", the part of state() it draws`);
      else regions.set(k.attrs.id, g);
      for (const c of kids(k)) if (c.name === "ve-node") place(c, g); else errors.push(`${where(c)}: only <ve-node> belongs in <ve-region>`);
      if (!kids(k).some((c) => c.name === "ve-node")) errors.push(`${where(k)}: a <ve-region> holds the <ve-node>s of its part; this one has none`);
    } else if (k.name === "ve-edge") edges.push(k);
    else if (k.name === "script" && "model" in k.attrs) { if (scripts.length) errors.push(`${where(k)}: one model per <ve-flow>`); scripts.push(k); }
    else errors.push(`${where(k)}: only <ve-node>, <ve-region>, <ve-edge>, and one <script type="text/plain" model> belong in <ve-flow>`);
  }
  // auto: the whole walk, laid out by Pele; render.mjs draws the Mermaid this leaves on n.auto
  if ("auto" in n.attrs) {
    // a plan has no Pele step to draw it, so it would be an empty exhibit
    if (!page) errors.push(`${where(n)}: auto draws only on a page; in a plan, place the states by hand with <ve-node>`);
    else if (boxes.size || regions.size || edges.length) errors.push(`${where(n)}: auto draws the whole walk; remove the nodes, or drop auto`);
    else if (!scripts.length) errors.push(`${where(n)}: auto draws the walk of one <script type="text/plain" model>; add it`);
    else if (!n.attrs.label) errors.push(`${where(n)}: add label="…", one sentence a screen reader can read instead of the picture`);
    else if (errors.length === before) {
      const a = drawAuto(scripts[0], { root, models, where });
      if (a.errors) errors.push(...a.errors);
      else { n.auto = a; n.machine = { line: a.line }; }
    }
    return "";
  }
  for (const [id, { k }] of regions) if (boxes.has(id)) errors.push(`${where(k)}: id="${id}" is also a <ve-node>; an arrow could not tell them apart`);
  for (const e of edges) for (const end of ["from", "to"]) if (!boxes.has(e.attrs[end])) errors.push(`${where(e)}: ${end}="${e.attrs[end] ?? ""}" names no <ve-node>`);
  if (!n.attrs.label) warnings.push(`${where(n)}: add label="…", one sentence a screen reader can read instead of the picture`);
  if (!boxes.size) { errors.push(`${where(n)}: needs at least one <ve-node>`); return ""; }
  // a model draws the arrows and sets the steps: the walk replaces what an author would write by hand
  // (after a node or region error the drawing is incomplete, and the walk would only repeat it as "not drawn")
  if (scripts.length && errors.length === before) {
    for (const e of edges) errors.push(`${where(e)}: a flow with a model draws its arrows from the walk; remove this <ve-edge>`);
    for (const { k } of boxes.values()) if ("data-s" in k.attrs) errors.push(`${where(k)}: a flow with a model takes its steps from the walk; remove data-s`);
    const m = drawModel(scripts[0], new Map([...boxes].map(([id, b]) => [id, b.k])), { root, models, where, regions });
    if (m.errors) { errors.push(...m.errors); return ""; }

  }
  const pairs = new Set(edges.map((e) => `${e.attrs.from}>${e.attrs.to}`));
  const toks = [];
  const lifts = new Map(); // region id → the sides its lifted arrows already leave from
  const width = Math.max(...[...boxes.values()].map((b) => b.x)) + W + PAD, height = Math.max(...[...boxes.values()].map((b) => b.y)) + H + PAD;
  const rects = new Map([...regions].filter(([, g]) => g.ids.length).map(([id, g]) => {
    const bs = g.ids.map((i) => boxes.get(i)), x = Math.min(...bs.map((b) => b.x)) - RX, y = Math.min(...bs.map((b) => b.y)) - RT;
    return [id, { k: g.k, ids: g.ids, x, y, w: Math.max(...bs.map((b) => b.x)) + W + RX - x, h: Math.max(...bs.map((b) => b.y)) + H + RX - y }];

  // a label beside a vertical arrow can reach past the outer boxes; the drawing widens to hold it
  let lo = 0, hi = width;
  const edgeSvg = edges.filter((e) => (boxes.has(e.attrs.from) || rects.has(e.attrs.from)) && boxes.has(e.attrs.to) && e.attrs.from !== e.attrs.to).map((e) => {
    const a = boxes.get(e.attrs.from) ?? rects.get(e.attrs.from), b = boxes.get(e.attrs.to), lift = !boxes.has(e.attrs.from);
    let side = 0;
    if (lift) {
      // a lifted arrow comes back in along its node's row, so it leaves from a side with no other node of the region in that row,
      // and not one another lifted arrow of the region already uses

      const clear = [-1, 1].filter((s) => !between(s));
      side = clear.find((s) => !used.has(s)) ?? clear[0] ?? -1;
      if (!clear.length) warnings.push(`${where(e)}: the arrow "${e.attrs.label}" lifted to ${e.attrs.to} would run under ${between(-1)}; put ${e.attrs.to} at the end of its row in region "${e.attrs.from}"`);
      else if (used.has(side)) warnings.push(`${where(e)}: two lifted arrows leave region "${e.attrs.from}" on its ${side < 0 ? "left" : "right"}; put ${e.attrs.to} at the other end of its row`);

    }

    const off = pairs.has(`${e.attrs.to}>${e.attrs.from}`) ? (e.attrs.from < e.attrs.to ? -12 : 12) : 0;
    const [ax, ay, bx, by] = [a.x + W / 2, a.y + H / 2, b.x + W / 2, b.y + H / 2];
    const x1 = bx > ax ? a.x + W : a.x, y2 = by > ay ? b.y : b.y + H;
    let d, mx, my, vertical = false;
    if (lift) {

      const out = Math.abs(a.y + a.h / 2 - by) < 20 ? a.y + a.h - 8 : a.y + a.h / 2, edge = side < 0 ? a.x : a.x + a.w;
      d = `M${edge} ${out}H${edge + side * 32}V${by}H${side < 0 ? b.x : b.x + W}`; mx = edge + side * 32; my = (out + by) / 2; vertical = true;
    }
    else if (ay === by) { const x2 = bx > ax ? b.x : b.x + W; d = `M${x1} ${ay + off}H${x2}`; mx = (x1 + x2) / 2; my = ay + off; }
    else if (ax === bx) { const y1 = by > ay ? a.y + H : a.y; d = `M${ax + off} ${y1}V${y2}`; mx = ax + off; my = (y1 + y2) / 2; vertical = true; }

    const r = ref(e);
    // an arrow that appears at a step draws in; one drawn from the start (step 0) just lights
    const draw = page && e.attrs["data-s"] && !/^\s*0\b/.test(e.attrs["data-s"]) ? ' pathLength="1"' : "";
    if (page && e.attrs["data-s"]) toks.push(`<circle class="ve-tok" data-s="${esc(e.attrs["data-s"])}" r="5" style="offset-path: path('${d}')"/>`);
    if (page && e.attrs.label && !vertical && e.attrs.label.length * CH > Math.abs(bx - ax) - W - 8) warnings.push(`${where(e)}: label="${e.attrs.label}" is wider than the gap between its boxes; shorten it`);

  });

  for (const { k, x, y } of boxes.values()) {

    const ty = (subs.length ? 25 : 32) + (db ? 6 : 0);
    const shape = db ? `<path class="sh" d="M0 8V56A${W / 2} 8 0 0 0 ${W} 56V8"/><ellipse class="sh lid" cx="${W / 2}" cy="8" rx="${W / 2}" ry="8"/>` : `<rect class="sh" width="${W}" height="${H}" rx="6"/>`;

  const regionSvg = [...rects].map(([id, r]) => `<rect class="ve-bnd" x="${r.x}" y="${r.y}" width="${r.w}" height="${r.h}" rx="8"/><text class="ve-bnd-t" x="${r.x + 12}" y="${r.y + 20}">${esc(r.k.attrs.label || id)}</text>`);

  const size = page ? ` ve-flow" style="--min: ${Math.ceil((w * 12) / 14)}px; --max: ${Math.round(w * 1.3)}px` : "";
```

```text file=~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/kit/html.mjs
// A small HTML tree, shared by the page and plan renderers: enough to find tags and attributes. Untouched parts serialize byte for byte.
const VOID = new Set("area base br col embed hr img input link meta source track wbr".split(" "));
const RAW_TEXT = new Set(["script", "style", "textarea", "title"]);
const ENTITIES = { amp: "&", lt: "<", gt: ">", quot: '"', apos: "'", nbsp: " " };
export const decode = (s) => s.replace(/&(#x[\da-f]+|#\d+|\w+);/gi, (m, e) => (e[0] === "#" ? String.fromCodePoint(e[1].toLowerCase() === "x" ? parseInt(e.slice(2), 16) : +e.slice(1)) : ENTITIES[e.toLowerCase()] ?? m));
export const esc = (s) => String(s).replace(/[&<>"]/g, (c) => ({ "&": "&amp;", "<": "&lt;", ">": "&gt;", '"': "&quot;" })[c]);
const TAG = /<!--[\s\S]*?-->|<!doctype[^>]*>|<\/([a-zA-Z][\w:-]*)\s*>|<([a-zA-Z][\w:-]*)((?:\s+[^\s=\/>"']+(?:\s*=\s*(?:"[^"]*"|'[^']*'|[^\s>]+))?)*)\s*(\/?)>/gi;

function parseAttrs(src) {
  const attrs = {};
  for (const m of src.matchAll(/([^\s=\/>"']+)(?:\s*=\s*(?:"([^"]*)"|'([^']*)'|([^\s>]+)))?/g)) attrs[m[1].toLowerCase()] = decode(m[2] ?? m[3] ?? m[4] ?? "");
  return attrs;
}

export function parseHtml(html) {
  const root = { name: "#root", attrs: {}, children: [] };
  const stack = [root];
  const top = () => stack[stack.length - 1];
  const text = (raw) => raw && top().children.push({ text: raw });
  let last = 0;
  let m;
  TAG.lastIndex = 0;
  while ((m = TAG.exec(html))) {
    text(html.slice(last, m.index));
    last = TAG.lastIndex;
    if (m[0].startsWith("<!")) { top().children.push({ text: m[0], comment: true }); continue; }
    if (m[1]) {
      const i = stack.findLastIndex((n) => n.name === m[1].toLowerCase());
      if (i > 0) { stack[i].closeRaw = m[0]; stack.length = i; } else text(m[0]);
      continue;
    }
    const name = m[2].toLowerCase();
    const node = { name, attrs: parseAttrs(m[3]), openRaw: m[0], children: [], pos: m.index, selfClose: !!m[4] || VOID.has(name) };
    top().children.push(node);
    if (node.selfClose) continue;
    if (RAW_TEXT.has(name)) {
      // only "</script" followed by space, / or > ends the text; "</scripture>" inside a string does not
      const closer = new RegExp(`</${name}(?=[\\s/>])`, "gi");
      closer.lastIndex = last;
      const end = closer.exec(html)?.index ?? -1;
      const stop = end < 0 ? html.length : end;
      node.children.push({ text: html.slice(last, stop) });
      node.closeRaw = end < 0 ? "" : html.slice(end).match(/^<\/[^>]*>/)[0];
      last = stop + node.closeRaw.length;
      TAG.lastIndex = last;
      continue;
    }
    stack.push(node);
  }
  text(html.slice(last));
  return root;
}

export const serialize = (n) => n.html ?? n.text ?? (n.openRaw ?? "") + n.children.map(serialize).join("") + (n.closeRaw ?? "");
export const inner = (n) => n.children.map(serialize).join("");
export const kids = (n) => n.children.filter((c) => c.name);
function* walk(n) { for (const c of n.children ?? []) if (c.name) { yield c; yield* walk(c); } }

export const hasClass = (n, c) => (n.attrs?.class ?? "").split(/\s+/).includes(c);
```

```text file=~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/kit/kit.css
/* visual-explainer kit. The renderer inlines this file at <link rel="stylesheet" data-ve-kit>.
   Tokens sit in :where(), so a page's own :root rules (topic motif, a named palette) always win.
   A page picks its register with <html data-register="instrument|blueprint|paper|editorial">; Instrument is the default. */

/* scale, shared by every register */
:where(:root) {

}

  --bg: #0b0d0c; --surface: #121614; --border: #1f2522; --border-bright: #5e6662;
  --text: #e6ebe8; --text-dim: #919d97; --accent: #f2a93b; --accent-dim: rgba(242,169,59,.14);

/* base */
html { font-size: 17px; }
* { box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0; }
body { background: var(--bg); color: var(--text); font: 400 var(--t-body)/1.6 var(--font-body); text-wrap: pretty; font-kerning: normal; font-synthesis: none; -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased; }

@media (min-width: 52rem) { .sec-head { grid-template-columns: 3fr 9fr; } }
/* the other opener, a bare label above the h2, gets the same gaps, so the h2 never sits on the figure below */

h3 { font-size: var(--t-body); line-height: 1.3; font-weight: 600; }

.eyebrow::before { content: ''; width: 1.25rem; height: 2px; background: currentColor; }
.ve-label { font: 500 var(--t-label) var(--font-mono); color: var(--text-dim); }

:where(pre) { font: 500 var(--t-small)/1.55 var(--font-mono); font-variant-ligatures: none; background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--r-2); padding: var(--s-4); overflow-x: auto; }

   kit.js marks the section in view */

.ve-axis { fill: none; stroke: var(--border-bright); stroke-width: 1; }

/* KPI strip: one frame, cells split by hairlines, each number with its picture. Flex, so a wrapped last row stretches instead of leaving an empty gray cell. */
.kpis { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 1px; background: var(--border); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--r-2); overflow: hidden; }
.kpi { flex: 1 1 14rem; background: var(--surface); padding: var(--s-5); display: grid; grid-template-rows: auto auto 1fr; gap: var(--s-3); min-width: 0; }

.ve-waffle { align-self: end; width: 11rem; height: auto; font: 500 13px var(--font-mono); overflow: visible; }
.ve-waffle text { fill: var(--text-dim); dominant-baseline: central; }
.ann { fill: none; stroke: var(--text-dim); stroke-width: 1; }
.ve-bars { align-self: end; width: 100%; max-width: 16rem; height: auto; font: 500 13px var(--font-mono); overflow: visible; }

.ve-bars rect { fill: var(--border-bright); transform-box: fill-box; transform-origin: left; transition: transform 900ms var(--ease) 150ms; }

.cases { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(14.5rem, 1fr)); gap: var(--s-4); }
.case { background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--r-2); padding: var(--s-4); display: grid; gap: var(--s-3); align-content: start; transition: border-color var(--fast) var(--ease); }
.case[data-st=ok] { --st: var(--ok); } .case[data-st=warn] { --st: var(--warn); } .case[data-st=risk] { --st: var(--risk); }
.ve-mini { width: 100%; height: auto; font: 600 15px var(--font-body); }
.ve-mini .ve-n .sh { filter: none; }
/* a .cases column is never under 14.5rem, so a mini is ≥ 211 px and 14 units render ≥ 12.3 px */
.ve-mini .ve-n .sub { font-size: 14px; }
.ve-mini .is-st.ve-e { stroke: var(--st); stroke-width: 2.75; }
.ve-mini .is-st .sh { stroke: var(--st); stroke-width: 2; }
.ve-mini .is-st .sub { fill: var(--st); }
.ve-mini .is-off { stroke-dasharray: 5 4; }
.ve-mini .ve-e.is-off { opacity: .35; }

/* chips */
.chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--s-2); font: 600 var(--t-label) var(--font-mono); padding: 2px var(--s-2); border: 1px solid currentColor; border-radius: var(--r-1); white-space: nowrap; justify-self: start; }
.chip::before { content: ''; width: .5rem; height: .5rem; background: currentColor; }
.chip.ok { color: var(--ok); } .chip.ok::before { border-radius: 50%; }
.chip.warn { color: var(--warn); } .chip.warn::before { clip-path: polygon(50% 0, 100% 100%, 0 100%); }
.chip.risk { color: var(--risk); }

/* a table: a scroll frame, the header in the label style, row rules only; .num cells are right-aligned numbers */

.ve-table table { border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; font-size: var(--t-body); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }

.ve-table thead th { background: var(--surface); font: 600 var(--t-label)/1.3 var(--font-mono); letter-spacing: .08em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--text-dim); }
.ve-table tbody th { font-weight: 600; }
.ve-table tbody tr:last-child > * { border-bottom: 0; }
.ve-table .num { text-align: right; font-family: var(--font-mono); }

details { border-top: 1px solid var(--border); padding-top: var(--s-4); color: var(--text-dim); font-size: var(--t-body); }

  :where(:root[data-register="editorial"]) { --border: #e2e0da; --border-bright: #8c8a85; --text: #111111; --text-dim: #5a5853; --accent: #cc3418; --ok: #1d7443; --warn: #836000; --risk: #a01d48; --info: #1b6a94; }
```

```js file=~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/kit/kit.js
// One block scope, so the kit's names never clash with a page's own script.
{
const still = matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches;

// Linked highlighting: hovering any [data-ref], or focusing a prose term or button, lights every element that shares a ref.
// Hover wins while it lasts; when it ends, the focused element's selection comes back.
const linked = [...document.querySelectorAll('[data-ref]')], refs = (el) => el.dataset.ref.split(' ');
let hovered = null, focused = null;
const paint = () => {
  const keys = (hovered || focused)?.dataset.ref.split(' ') ?? [];
  for (const t of linked) t.classList.toggle('is-lit', refs(t).some((k) => keys.includes(k)));
  for (const svg of document.querySelectorAll('svg')) svg.classList.toggle('has-lit', !!svg.querySelector('.is-lit'));
};
for (const el of linked) {
  el.addEventListener('pointerenter', () => { hovered = el; paint(); });
  el.addEventListener('pointerleave', () => { hovered = null; paint(); });
  el.addEventListener('focus', () => { focused = el; paint(); });
  el.addEventListener('blur', () => { focused = null; paint(); });
}

// Stepper / scene player. Range and Play are optional: a plain stepper needs only data-go buttons.
for (const root of document.querySelectorAll('.ve-steps')) {
  const parts = [...root.querySelectorAll('[data-s]')], caps = [...root.querySelectorAll('.ve-cap li')];
  const range = root.querySelector('input[type=range]'), play = root.querySelector('[data-play]');
  const n = caps.length; let i = 0, timer = null;
  if (range) range.max = n - 1;
  const show = (k) => {
    i = Math.max(0, Math.min(n - 1, k));
    root.classList.remove('is-still');
    // data-s lists the steps a part takes part in: it appears at the first ("0" = from the start) and is .now on each.
    for (const el of parts) { const s = el.dataset.s.trim().split(' ').map(Number); el.classList.toggle('on', s[0] <= i + 1); el.classList.toggle('now', s.includes(i + 1)); }
    caps.forEach((c, j) => c.hidden = j !== i);
    root.classList.toggle('is-full', i === n - 1);
    root.dispatchEvent(new Event('ve:step'));
    if (range) range.value = i;
  };
  const stop = () => { clearInterval(timer); timer = null; if (play) play.textContent = 'Play'; };
  root.addEventListener('click', (e) => { const b = e.target.closest('[data-go]'); if (b) { stop(); show(i + +b.dataset.go); } });
  range?.addEventListener('input', () => { stop(); show(+range.value); });
  play?.addEventListener('click', () => {
    if (timer) return stop();
    if (i === n - 1) show(0);
    play.textContent = 'Pause';
    timer = setInterval(() => (i < n - 1 ? show(i + 1) : stop()), 3500);
  });
  show(n - 1); // open on the full picture; Play replays from step 1
  root.classList.add('is-still'); // same task as show(), so the last token never starts until the reader steps
  addEventListener('beforeprint', () => { show(n - 1); root.classList.add('is-still'); }); // print shows the end state
}

// Section nav: the link of the section in view gets aria-current, and .pos counts it.
for (const nav of document.querySelectorAll('.ve-toc')) {
  const links = [...nav.querySelectorAll('a[href^="#"]')], pos = nav.querySelector('.pos');
  const targets = links.map((a) => {
    const t = document.getElementById(decodeURIComponent(a.hash.slice(1)));
    if (!t) throw new Error(`the section nav links to ${a.hash}, but no element has that id`);
    return t;
  });

  const seen = new Set();
  const io = new IntersectionObserver((entries) => {
    for (const e of entries) e.isIntersecting ? seen.add(e.target) : seen.delete(e.target);
    const i = targets.findLastIndex((t) => seen.has(t));

}

if (!still) {
  // Flow dots: each path[data-flow] spawns a dot every data-every ms; the ratio of intervals is the real traffic split.
  // Runs only while the figure is on screen and, inside a stepper, only on the full picture.

  document.documentElement.classList.add('js-motion');

    for (const e of entries) {

        const step = (t) => {

window.veReply?.page();

// Last statement: kit/look.mjs reads this to tell that the whole script ran.
document.documentElement.dataset.veKit = "ready";
}
```

```text file=~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/kit/look.mjs
// Opens a rendered kit page in headless Chrome and looks at it the way a reader would, so the agent does not script its own browser:
// script errors, sideways scrolling, labels under 12 px, text that overlaps or runs out of its drawing, headings that sit on what
// follows, every stepper step, and a contact sheet of the first screen, the figures, and the steps. playwright-core is an optional peer.
import { createRequire } from "node:module";
import { readdirSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { basename, dirname, join, resolve } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath, pathToFileURL } from "node:url";

const WIDTHS = [390, 1280];
const MIN_LABEL = 12;
const MIN_HEADING_GAP = 8;

// a font still downloading after load must not hold the render; a late font only shifts glyphs slightly
const fontsReady = () => Promise.race([document.fonts.ready, new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 5000))]);

async function launch() {
  let chromium;
  try {
    ({ chromium } = await import("playwright-core"));
  } catch (e) {
    if (e.code !== "ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND") throw e;
    // import() never looks in global installs, so it goes beside the plugin
    const plugin = dirname(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)));
    return { skipped: `playwright-core is not installed. Run: npm install --no-save --prefix "${plugin}" playwright-core (in a repository checkout, npm install is enough)` };
  }
  try {
    return { browser: await chromium.launch() };
  } catch (e) {
    try {
      return { browser: await chromium.launch({ channel: "chrome" }) };
    } catch {
      const { version } = createRequire(import.meta.url)("playwright-core/package.json");
      return { skipped: `no browser started (${e.message.split("\n")[0]}). Install Google Chrome, or run: npx playwright-core@${version} install chromium-headless-shell` };
    }
  }
}

// Runs in the page: the smallest rendered SVG label, overflow, figure and prose counts, and whether the kit's script finished.
function measure(minLabel) {

  for (const t of document.querySelectorAll("svg text")) {
    if (!t.textContent.trim() || !t.checkVisibility({ visibilityProperty: true })) continue;

      if (edged) for (let s = 0; s <= len; s += step) { const p = e.getPointAtLength(s); pts.push(new DOMPoint(p.x, p.y).matrixTransform(m)); }

      if (shapes.some((o) => later(t, o.e) && probe.every((p) => covers(o, p)))) continue;

}

// Runs in the page: an h2 closer than minGap to what follows it.
function headings(minGap) {
  const found = [];
  for (const h of document.querySelectorAll("main h2")) {
    const block = h.parentElement.matches(".sec-head") ? h.parentElement : h;
    const next = block.nextElementSibling;
    if (!next || !next.checkVisibility()) continue;
    const gap = next.getBoundingClientRect().top - h.getBoundingClientRect().bottom;
    if (gap < minGap) found.push(`the heading "${h.textContent.trim().replace(/\s+/g, " ").slice(0, 40)}" sits ${Math.max(0, Math.round(gap))} px from the ${next.tagName.toLowerCase()} below it`);

}

// Runs in the page: moves stepper r to step k (0-based) with its own controls. False when it has none.
function goStep([r, k]) {
  const root = document.querySelectorAll(".ve-steps")[r];
  const n = root.querySelectorAll(".ve-cap li").length;
  const range = root.querySelector("input[type=range]");
  if (range) { range.value = k; range.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", { bubbles: true })); return true; }
  const go = [...root.querySelectorAll("[data-go]")];

const pngSize = (png) => ({ w: png.readUInt32BE(16), h: png.readUInt32BE(20) });

// Lays the crops out in rows on sheets of at most SHEET_W × SHEET_H: the first screens, then each figure, then each stepper's steps
// as thumbnails. A page with more than fits on MAX_SHEETS is drawn smaller before anything is left out.
function layout(items) {
  const inner = SHEET_W - 2 * PAD, tallest = SHEET_H - 2 * PAD - LABEL;
  const pack = (figScale, stepCols) => {
    const rows = [];
    for (const it of items) {
      const scaled = it.cells.map((c) => {
        const s = it.kind === "overview" ? 0.62 : it.kind === "steps" ? (inner - GAP * (stepCols - 1)) / stepCols / c.w : figScale;
        return { ...c, s: Math.min(1, s, inner / c.w, tallest / c.h) };

      // each group starts a row; its cells flow left to right
      let row = [], width = -GAP;
      for (const c of scaled) {
        const w = Math.round(c.w * c.s) + GAP;
        if (row.length && width + w > inner) { rows.push(row); row = []; width = -GAP; }
        row.push(c); width += w;

    rows = pack(figScale, stepCols);

function toSheets(rows) {
  const sheets = [];
  let cur = [], height = 2 * PAD - GAP;
  const rowH = (row) => LABEL + Math.max(...row.map((c) => Math.round(c.h * c.s)));
  for (const row of rows) {
    const h = rowH(row) + GAP;
    if (cur.length && height + h > SHEET_H) { sheets.push(cur); cur = []; height = 2 * PAD - GAP; }
    cur.push(row); height += h;
  }

async function drawSheets(browser, sheets, outBase) {
  const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width: SHEET_W, height: SHEET_H } });
  const paths = [];

    for (const [n, rows] of sheets.entries()) {
      // the sheet is only as wide as its widest row: blank pixels cost the model as much as drawn ones
      const html = `<!doctype html><body style="margin:0;background:#fff"><div id="s" style="width:max-content;max-width:${SHEET_W}px;box-sizing:border-box;padding:${PAD}px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:${GAP}px;font:600 13px/18px system-ui,sans-serif;color:#333">${rows.map((row) => `<div style="display:flex;gap:${GAP}px;align-items:flex-start">${row.map((c) => `<div><div style="height:${LABEL - 4}px;margin-bottom:4px">${c.label}</div><img src="data:image/png;base64,${c.png.toString("base64")}" width="${Math.round(c.w * c.s)}" height="${Math.round(c.h * c.s)}" style="display:block;outline:1px solid #ccc"></div>`).join("")}</div>`).join("")}</div></body>`;

/**
 * Looks at a rendered page. Returns { problems, sheets, widths, errors } or { skipped } when there is no browser.

export async function lookAt(file, { sheet = true } = {}) {

    ...result.problems,
    ...shapes,
  ];
  return result;
}

/** The lines every host prints after a render: problems as ✗, or the smallest label; then the sheet to look at. */
export function lookLines(r) {
  if (r.skipped) return [`Visual check skipped: ${r.skipped}`];
  const shown = r.problems.slice(0, 12);
  const lines = shown.length
    ? [...shown.map((p) => `✗ ${p}`), ...(r.problems.length > shown.length ? [`✗ … and ${r.problems.length - shown.length} more`] : [])]
    : [`✓ Visual check: no problems · smallest label ${WIDTHS.map((w) => `${r.widths[w].smallest?.px ?? "—"}px at ${w}`).join(", ")}`];
  if (r.sheets.length) lines.push(`Look at: ${r.sheets.join(", ")}${r.omitted ? ` (${r.omitted} more crops left out)` : ""}`);
  return lines;
}
```

```text file=~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/kit/machine.mjs
const ids = (v) => (Array.isArray(v) ? v.length > 0 && v.every((x) => typeof x === "string" && x) : typeof v === "string" && v);

/** Loads, checks, and walks a model: { errors } when it is not a model or the walk fails, else { errors: [], events, rules, form, walk, proof }.
 * events: [{ name, at? }] (at marks a hand-written step); rules: names; form: flat | regions | nested;
 * walk: see walk(); proof: { kind: "code" | "model", files } for the caption ("walked from src/player.ts" or "walked from a model of mixer.ts").
 * One timeout covers loading and walking. */
export function loadModel({ text, root, timeoutMs = 10_000, cap = 2000 }) {

  const read = fileReader(realRoot);

  const msg = plain(message(e));
  if (e?.code === "ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND") return `an import cannot be found: ${msg}. Node runs .ts files by stripping their types, so every relative import needs the file's real extension (.ts, not .js), path aliases do not resolve, and packages must be installed under the root; fix the import, or write a hand model (when, then, at)`;
  // Node puts the file and line of unstrippable syntax on the first line of the stack
  if (e?.code === "ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX") return `${/:\d+$/.test(e.stack?.split("\n")[0]) ? e.stack.split("\n")[0] : "the code"} uses TypeScript that Node cannot strip (an enum, a namespace, or parameter properties): ${msg}; write a hand model (when, then, at)`;
  if (e?.code === "ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION") return `Node ${process.version} cannot import ${msg.match(/"([^"]+)"/)?.[1] ?? "a .ts file"}; use Node 22.6 or later, or write a hand model (when, then, at)`;
  const declared = msg.match(/^Identifier '(init|events|rules|state)' has already been declared/)?.[1];
  if (declared) return `the model script declares ${declared}; write ${declared} = …, not const or let`;
  if (e instanceof SyntaxError) return `the model script does not parse: ${msg}`;
  return `the model threw while loading: ${msg}`;
}

/** Walks a checked model breadth-first from init: every event at every state, at most cap distinct states (compared as
 * stable JSON). It returns { error } or, by drawn id (state(): an id, or the JSON of a regions or nested value):
 *   states: drawn ids in the order reached · depths: { id: fewest events from init }
 *   edges: [{ from, to, events, depth }] between different drawn ids, events merged; depth: fewest events to first take it
 *   breaks: { rule: drawn ids where holds is false } · paths: { rule: the shortest [{ event, to }] from init to a break }
 *   first: the rule that breaks in the fewest steps, or null · mayBreak: ids from which a break is reachable, not breaking
 *   deadEnds: ids of states no event leaves · neverFired: events that change no reachable state
 *   counts: { states, full, edges, broken, rules, steps } for the Page line (steps: to the first break, or null) */
function walk({ init, events, rules = {}, state }, { cap = 2000 } = {}) {
  const NONE = Symbol("none");
  const steps = Object.entries(events).map(([name, ev]) => [name, typeof ev === "function" ? ev : (s) => (ev.when && !ev.when(s) ? NONE : ev.then(s))]);
  const form = formOf(state(init));
  const nodes = new Map(); // full key → { s, id, from, event, next: keys }
  const add = (s, from, event, depth) => {
    const v = state(s);
    if (formOf(v) !== form) throw new Error(`state() returns ${JSON.stringify(v)} at ${stable(s)}, but a ${form} value at init; return one form for every state`);
    nodes.set(stable(s), { s, id: typeof v === "string" ? v : stable(v), from, event, depth, next: new Set() });
  };
  const edges = new Map(), fired = new Set();
  try {
    add(init, null, null, 0);
    for (const [key, node] of nodes) { // a Map iterates entries added during the loop, so this is the BFS queue
      for (const [name, step] of steps) {
        let next;
        // a step that changes its input and returns it would rewrite a state already walked; states are plain data
        try { next = step(structuredClone(node.s)); } catch (e) { return { error: `event "${name}" throws at ${node.id}: ${message(e)}` }; }
        if (next === NONE) continue;
        if (!isData(next)) return { error: `event "${name}" at ${node.id} returns ${String(next)}, which is not plain data` };
        const k = stable(next);
        if (k === key) continue;
        fired.add(name);
        node.next.add(k);
        if (!nodes.has(k)) {
          if (nodes.size >= cap) return { error: `the walk has more than ${cap} states; model less (fewer events, or fewer fields in the state)` };
          add(next, key, name, node.depth + 1);
        }
        const to = nodes.get(k).id, pair = `${node.id}\n${to}`;
        if (to === node.id) continue;
        if (!edges.has(pair)) edges.set(pair, { from: node.id, to, events: [], depth: node.depth + 1 });
        if (!edges.get(pair).events.includes(name)) edges.get(pair).events.push(name);
      }
    }
  } catch (e) {
    return { error: message(e) };
  }

  const uniq = (xs) => [...new Set(xs)];
  // keyed by rule names and state ids, so no prototype: a state named constructor is not Object's
  const breaks = Object.create(null), paths = Object.create(null), broken = new Set();
  for (const [rule, { holds }] of Object.entries(rules)) {
    const bad = [];
    for (const [key, n] of nodes) {
      let ok;
      try { ok = holds(n.s); } catch (e) { return { error: `rule "${rule}" throws at ${n.id}: ${message(e)}` }; }
      if (!ok) bad.push(key);
    }
    breaks[rule] = uniq(bad.map((k) => nodes.get(k).id));
    bad.forEach((k) => broken.add(k));
    if (!bad.length) continue;
    // nodes are in BFS order, so the first breaking state is the nearest, and its parents give the shortest path
    const path = [];
    for (let n = nodes.get(bad[0]); n.from !== null; n = nodes.get(n.from)) path.unshift({ event: n.event, to: n.id });
    paths[rule] = path;
  }
  // reverse reachability: out from every breaking state along the steps backwards
  const prev = new Map([...nodes.keys()].map((k) => [k, []]));
  for (const [k, n] of nodes) for (const t of n.next) prev.get(t).push(k);
  const reach = new Set(broken), queue = [...broken];
  for (const k of queue) for (const p of prev.get(k)) if (!reach.has(p)) { reach.add(p); queue.push(p); }
  const breakIds = new Set([...broken].map((k) => nodes.get(k).id));
  const first = Object.keys(paths).reduce((a, r) => (a === null || paths[r].length < paths[a].length ? r : a), null);
  const states = uniq([...nodes.values()].map((n) => n.id));
  const depths = Object.create(null);
  for (const n of nodes.values()) depths[n.id] ??= n.depth; // BFS order, so the first state drawn as an id is its nearest
  return {
    states,
    depths,
    edges: [...edges.values()],
    breaks,
    paths,
    first,
    mayBreak: uniq([...nodes].filter(([k]) => reach.has(k)).map(([, n]) => n.id)).filter((id) => !breakIds.has(id)),
    deadEnds: uniq([...nodes.values()].filter((n) => !n.next.size).map((n) => n.id)),
    neverFired: steps.map(([name]) => name).filter((name) => !fired.has(name)),
    counts: { states: states.length, full: nodes.size, edges: edges.size, broken: Object.keys(paths).length, rules: Object.keys(rules).length, steps: first === null ? null : paths[first].length },
  };
}

export const plural = (n, one) => `${n} ${n === 1 ? one : `${one}s`}`;
// this many states the walk reached but nobody drew is a chart to draw with auto, not a list of nodes to add
const FLOOD = 6;
const flood = (w, k, at) => `${at}: the walk has ${w.states.length} states and ${w.edges.length} arrows, and ${k} are not drawn; set auto, or model less`;

/** The walk as drawn: each drawn id's depth, the arrows, the marks, and the shortest path to the first broken rule.
 * drawn is null for auto, which draws every state the walk reached. */
function flatView(w, drawn, { at, where }) {
  if (drawn) {
    const undrawn = w.states.filter((id) => !drawn.has(id));
    const errors = [
      ...(undrawn.length >= FLOOD ? [flood(w, undrawn.length, at)] : undrawn.map((id) => `${at}: the walk reached ${id}, which is not drawn; add <ve-node id="${id}">`)),
      ...[...drawn].filter(([id]) => !w.states.includes(id)).map(([id, k]) => `${where(k)}: ${id} is drawn, but no path from init reaches it`),
    ];
    if (errors.length) return { errors };
  }
  const path = w.first !== null ? w.paths[w.first] : [];
  const along = [w.states[0], ...path.map((p) => p.to)];
  return {
    depths: new Map(w.states.map((id) => [id, w.depths[id]])), edges: w.edges, path,
    breaking: new Set(Object.values(w.breaks).flat()), may: new Set(w.mayBreak),
    onPath: new Set(along), pathEdges: new Set(path.map((p, i) => `${along[i]}\n${p.to}`)),
  };
}

/** The same, per region: a state is an object of part → value, a value is the id of a node in its part's <ve-region>, and
 * each step draws one arrow in every part it changes. A step that every node of a region takes to the same node lifts to
 * one arrow from the region (its from is the region id). Marks go to the parts of each marked state. regions is null for
 * auto, which takes them from the walk. */
function regionView(w, drawn, regions, { at, where }) {
  const states = new Map(w.states.map((id) => [id, JSON.parse(id)]));
  const keys = Object.keys(states.get(w.states[0]));
  const errors = [];
  if (regions) {
    for (const [r, { k }] of regions) if (!keys.includes(r)) errors.push(`${where(k)}: region "${r}" is not a part of state() (${keys.join(", ")})`);
    for (const r of keys) if (!regions.has(r)) errors.push(`${at}: state() has a part "${r}" with no <ve-region id="${r}">`);
    const inRegion = new Set([...regions.values()].flatMap((g) => g.ids));
    for (const [id, k] of drawn) if (!inRegion.has(id)) errors.push(`${where(k)}: ${id} is in no <ve-region>; state() returns parts, so every node belongs to one`);
    if (errors.length) return { errors };
  }
  const depths = new Map(), part = new Map();
  for (const [id, s] of states) {
    if (Object.keys(s).join() !== keys.join()) return { errors: [`${at}: state() returns the parts ${Object.keys(s).join(", ")} at ${id}, but ${keys.join(", ")} at init; return the same parts for every state`] };
    for (const r of keys) {
      if (typeof s[r] !== "string") return { errors: [`${at}: part "${r}" of state() is ${JSON.stringify(s[r])}; a part's value is one ve-node id (nested states draw only as a whole-state array under auto)`] };
      if (part.has(s[r]) && part.get(s[r]) !== r) return { errors: [`${at}: "${s[r]}" is a value of both "${part.get(s[r])}" and "${r}"; a value names its node, so give each part its own`] };
      part.set(s[r], r);
      if (!depths.has(s[r])) depths.set(s[r], w.depths[id]); // the walk's order is by depth, so the first is the nearest
    }
  }
  if (regions) {
    const undrawn = [...part].filter(([v, r]) => !regions.get(r).ids.includes(v));
    if (undrawn.length >= FLOOD) errors.push(flood(w, undrawn.length, at));
    else for (const [v, r] of undrawn) errors.push(`${at}: the walk reached ${r} · ${v}, which is not drawn in region "${r}"; add <ve-node id="${v}"> inside it`);
    for (const [r, g] of regions) for (const id of g.ids) if (part.get(id) !== r) errors.push(`${where(drawn.get(id))}: ${id} is drawn in region "${r}", but no path from init reaches it there`);
    if (errors.length) return { errors };
  } else regions = new Map(keys.map((r) => [r, { ids: [...part].filter(([, p]) => p === r).map(([v]) => v) }]));

  const arrows = new Map();
  const add = (from, to, events, depth) => {
    // the walk's arrows come in the order it reached them, so the first depth an arrow gets is its least
    const key = `${from}\n${to}`;
    if (!arrows.has(key)) arrows.set(key, { from, to, events: [], depth });
    const e = arrows.get(key);
    for (const ev of events) if (!e.events.includes(ev)) e.events.push(ev);
  };
  for (const e of w.edges) for (const r of keys) if (states.get(e.from)[r] !== states.get(e.to)[r]) add(states.get(e.from)[r], states.get(e.to)[r], e.events, e.depth);
  const path = w.first !== null ? w.paths[w.first] : [];
  const onPath = [w.states[0], ...path.map((p) => p.to)].map((id) => states.get(id));
  // each step of the path, per part it changes; a lifted arrow is on the path only when the path takes its event
  const moves = onPath.slice(1).flatMap((s, i) => keys.filter((r) => s[r] !== onPath[i][r]).map((r) => ({ r, from: onPath[i][r], to: s[r], event: path[i].event })));
  const pathEdges = new Set();
  const lifted = [];
  for (const [r, g] of regions) {
    const own = [...arrows.values()].filter((e) => part.get(e.from) === r);
    for (const ev of new Set(own.flatMap((e) => e.events))) {
      const taking = own.filter((e) => e.events.includes(ev)), to = taking[0].to, from = new Set(taking.map((e) => e.from));
      if (taking.length < 2 || taking.some((e) => e.to !== to) || g.ids.some((id) => id !== to && !from.has(id))) continue;
      for (const e of taking) e.events = e.events.filter((x) => x !== ev);
      const prior = lifted.find((e) => e.from === r && e.to === to);
      if (prior) { prior.events.push(ev); prior.depth = Math.min(prior.depth, ...taking.map((e) => e.depth)); }
      else lifted.push({ from: r, to, events: [ev], depth: Math.min(...taking.map((e) => e.depth)), lifted: true });
      if (moves.some((p) => p.r === r && p.to === to && p.event === ev)) pathEdges.add(`${r}\n${to}`);
    }
  }
  const partsOf = (ids) => ids.flatMap((id) => keys.map((r) => states.get(id)[r]));
  // a plain arrow is on the path only if it still carries the event the path took (a lifted event left it above)
  for (const p of moves) if (arrows.get(`${p.from}\n${p.to}`)?.events.includes(p.event)) pathEdges.add(`${p.from}\n${p.to}`);
  const breaking = new Set(partsOf(Object.values(w.breaks).flat()));
  return {
    depths, path, breaking, pathEdges, regions,
    edges: [...[...arrows.values()].filter((e) => e.events.length), ...lifted],
    may: new Set(partsOf(w.mayBreak).filter((v) => !breaking.has(v))),
    onPath: new Set(onPath.flatMap((s) => keys.map((r) => s[r]))),
  };
}

/** The model loaded and walked, or { errors } that each start with the script's line (the MCP opt-in first). */
function walked(script, { root, models, where }) {
  const at = where(script);
  if (!models) return { errors: [`${at}: models run only when the MCP server starts with VISUAL_EXPLAINER_RUN_MODELS=1`] };
  const m = loadModel({ text: rawText(script), root });
  return m.errors.length ? { errors: m.errors.map((e) => `${at}: ${e}`) } : m;
}

/** The machine's Page line and the "walked from" caption under its drawing. */
function summary(m) {
  const w = m.walk, c = w.counts;
  const line = [
    `machine from ${m.proof.kind === "model" ? "a model of " : ""}${m.proof.files.join(", ")}`,
    plural(c.states, "state"),
    c.rules && (c.broken ? `${c.broken} of ${plural(c.rules, "rule")} ${c.broken === 1 ? "breaks" : "break"} ${c.steps ? `in ${plural(c.steps, "step")}` : "at the start"}` : `${plural(c.rules, "rule")} ${c.rules === 1 ? "holds" : "hold"}`),
    w.deadEnds.length && plural(w.deadEnds.length, "dead end"),
    w.neverFired.length && `${w.neverFired.map((e) => `"${e}"`).join(", ")} never ${w.neverFired.length === 1 ? "fires" : "fire"}`,
  ].filter(Boolean).join(" · ");
  const proof = `<p class="ve-label">walked from ${m.proof.kind === "model" ? "a model of " : ""}${m.proof.files.map((f) => `<code>${esc(f)}</code>`).join(", ")}</p>`;
  return { line, proof };
}

/** A <ve-flow auto>: the whole walk as Mermaid for Pele to draw, { errors } or { mermaid, bugEdges, line, proof }. */
export function drawAuto(script, ctx) {
  const m = walked(script, ctx);
  if (m.errors.length) return { errors: m.errors };
  const t = toMermaid(m.walk, m.form, ctx.where(script));
  return t.errors ? t : { ...t, ...summary(m) };
}

/** A walk as a Mermaid state diagram: { mermaid, bugEdges } or { errors }. A flat state() draws one state per id, nested ids
 * draw composites from the outermost in, and each part of an object draws its own composite, with lifted arrows from the
 * composite (Pele draws a concurrent `--` region as an empty box, so parts are separate). Marks are classes on the states.
 * Pele numbers a diagram's transitions in source order, [*] first; bugEdges are the numbers of those on the bug path. */
export function toMermaid(w, form, at = "") {
  const v = form === "regions" ? regionView(w, null, null, { at }) : flatView(w, null, { at });
  if (v.errors) return v;
  const alias = new Map(), name = (key) => alias.get(key) ?? alias.set(key, `s${alias.size}`).get(key);
  // Pele reads these as character references; a raw " ends the label
  const text = (s) => s.replace(/\s+/g, " ").replace(/[;&"<>]/g, (c) => ({ ";": "#59;", "&": "#amp;", '"': "#quot;", "<": "#lt;", ">": "#gt;" })[c]);
  const lines = ["stateDiagram-v2"], bugEdges = [];
  let n = 0;
  const go = (indent, from, to, events, lit) => { lines.push(`${indent}${from} --> ${to}${events ? ` : ${text(events.join(" · "))}` : ""}`); if (lit) bugEdges.push(n); n++; };
  const lit = (e) => v.pathEdges.has(`${e.from}\n${e.to}`);
  if (form === "regions") {
    const init = JSON.parse(w.states[0]);
    for (const [r, g] of v.regions) {
      lines.push(`  state "${text(r)}" as ${name(`region\n${r}`)} {`);
      go("    ", "[*]", name(init[r]));
      for (const id of g.ids) lines.push(`    state "${text(id)}" as ${name(id)}`);
      for (const e of v.edges.filter((e) => (e.lifted ? e.from === r : g.ids.includes(e.from)))) go("    ", name(e.lifted ? `region\n${r}` : e.from), name(e.to), e.events, lit(e));
      lines.push("  }");
    }
  } else {
    const paths = [...v.depths.keys()].map((id) => [id, form === "nested" ? JSON.parse(id) : [id]]);
    const states = (prefix, indent) => {
      const here = paths.filter(([, p]) => p.length > prefix.length && prefix.every((x, i) => p[i] === x));
      for (const head of new Set(here.map(([, p]) => p[prefix.length]))) {
        const below = [...prefix, head];
        if (here.some(([, p]) => p.length > below.length && p[prefix.length] === head)) {
          lines.push(`${indent}state "${text(head)}" as ${name(`${JSON.stringify(below)}\n`)} {`);
          states(below, `${indent}  `);
          lines.push(`${indent}}`);
        }
        const leaf = here.find(([, p]) => p.length === below.length && p[prefix.length] === head);
        if (leaf) lines.push(`${indent}state "${text(head)}" as ${name(leaf[0])}`);
      }
    };
    states([], "  ");
    go("  ", "[*]", name(w.states[0]));
    for (const e of v.edges) go("  ", name(e.from), name(e.to), e.events, lit(e));
  }
  const dead = new Set(form === "regions" ? [] : w.deadEnds), path = w.first !== null ? v.onPath : new Set();
  for (const id of v.depths.keys()) for (const [cls, on] of [["breaks", v.breaking], ["may-break", v.may], ["bug-path", path], ["dead-end", dead]]) if (on.has(id)) lines.push(`  class ${name(id)} ${cls}`);
  return { mermaid: lines.join("\n"), bugEdges };
}

/** What a <ve-flow> draws from its <script model>, given its drawn nodes (id → element): { errors } or
 *   edges: <ve-edge>-like parts for flow.mjs's arrow loop · nodes: id → attributes to add (data-s and the mark flags)
 *   steps: one caption per replay step · proof: the "walked from" line under the drawing · line: the machine's Page line.
 * The replay steps through the walk's depths (step k: what k − 1 events reach), then, when a rule breaks, one step that
 * lights the shortest path to it. */
export function drawModel(script, drawn, { root, models, where, regions }) {
  const at = where(script);
  const m = walked(script, { root, models, where });
  if (m.errors.length) return { errors: m.errors };
  const w = m.walk;
  if (m.form === "nested") return { errors: [`${at}: state() returns an array of nested ids, which only <ve-flow auto> draws; set auto, or return a ve-node id or an object of region → id`] };
  if (m.form === "flat" && regions.size) return { errors: [`${where([...regions.values()][0].k)}: a <ve-region> draws one part of state(), so state() must return an object of region → id`] };
  const v = m.form === "flat" ? flatView(w, drawn, { at, where }) : regionView(w, drawn, regions, { at, where });
  if (v.errors) return v;

  const { depths, edges: arrows, breaking, may, onPath, pathEdges, path } = v;
  const depthSteps = Math.max(...depths.values(), ...arrows.map((e) => e.depth)) + 1;
  // a rule that already fails at init has an empty path: the last step marks init alone
  const last = w.first !== null ? ` ${depthSteps + 1}` : "";
  const nodes = new Map([...depths].map(([id, d]) => [id, {
    "data-s": `${d + 1}${onPath.has(id) ? last : ""}`,
    ...(breaking.has(id) && { breaks: "" }), ...(may.has(id) && { "may-break": "" }), ...(last && onPath.has(id) && { "bug-path": "" }),
  }]));
  const edges = arrows.map((e) => {
    const lit = last && pathEdges.has(`${e.from}\n${e.to}`);
    return { name: "script", pos: script.pos, children: [], attrs: { from: e.from, to: e.to, label: e.events.join(" · "), "data-s": `${e.depth + 1}${lit ? last : ""}`, ...(lit && { "bug-path": "" }) } };
  });
  const steps = [];
  for (let k = 1, before = ""; k <= depthSteps; k++) {
    const s = [...depths.values()].filter((d) => d < k).length, a = arrows.filter((e) => e.depth < k).length;
    const text = `${plural(s, "state")}${a ? ` · ${plural(a, "arrow")}` : ""}`;
    steps.push(text === before ? `${text} · nothing new` : text);
    before = text;
  }
  if (last) steps.push(path.length ? `breaks “${w.first}” in ${plural(path.length, "step")}: ${path.map((p) => p.event).join(" → ")}` : `breaks “${w.first}” at the start`);
  return { edges, nodes, steps, ...summary(m) };
}

/** The child: evaluates the model module from stdin and writes its checked shape as JSON, the only thing on stdout. */
async function child() {
  console.log = console.info = console.debug = console.error;
  // code that writes to stdout itself (a logger) goes to stderr; the result is the only thing on the real stdout
  const write = process.stdout.write.bind(process.stdout);
  process.stdout.write = process.stderr.write.bind(process.stderr);
  const out = { errors: [], events: [], rules: [], form: null };
  const done = () => write(JSON.stringify(out), () => process.exit(0));
  const err = (e) => out.errors.push(e);
  let m;
  try {
    m = (await import(`data:text/javascript,${encodeURIComponent(readFileSync(0, "utf8"))}`)).default;
  } catch (e) {
    err(loadError(e));
    return done();
  }
  const { init, events, rules = {}, state } = m;

  if (init === undefined) err("the model sets no init; write init = the first state");
  else if (!isData(init)) err("init is not plain data (objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans, null); the walk compares states as JSON");

  if (!isObj(events) || !Object.keys(events).length) err('events is not an object of named events; write events = { "you press play": s => … }');
  else for (const [name, ev] of Object.entries(events)) {
    if (typeof ev === "function") out.events.push({ name });
    else if (isObj(ev) && typeof ev.then === "function" && (ev.when === undefined || typeof ev.when === "function")) {
      if (typeof ev.at === "string") out.events.push({ name, at: ev.at });
      else err(`event "${name}" has no at:"file:line"; a hand-written step cites the code it copies`);
    } else err(`event "${name}" is neither a function nor { when, then, at }`);
  }

  // a rule that holds on the state it must reject would pass on every machine, so it proves nothing
  if (!isObj(rules)) err('rules is not an object of named rules; write rules = { "never loud while stopped": { holds, fails } }');
  else for (const [name, r] of Object.entries(rules)) {
    if (!isObj(r) || typeof r.holds !== "function") { err(`rule "${name}" has no holds: s => true while the rule holds`); continue; }
    if (!("fails" in r) || !isData(r.fails)) { err(`rule "${name}" has no fails: the state, as plain data, that it must reject`); continue; }
    let held;
    try { held = r.holds(r.fails); } catch (e) { err(`rule "${name}" throws on its fails state: ${message(e)}`); continue; }
    if (held) err(`rule "${name}" cannot fail; it is not a rule`);
    else out.rules.push(name);
  }

  if (typeof state !== "function") err("the model sets no state; write state = s => the ve-node id that draws s");
  else if (isData(init)) {
    try {
      const id = state(init);
      out.form = formOf(id);
      if (!out.form) err(`state(init) returned ${JSON.stringify(id)}; return a ve-node id, an array of ids from the outermost state in, or an object of region → id`);
    } catch (e) {
      err(`state(init) throws: ${message(e)}`);
    }
  }
  if (!out.errors.length) {
    const w = walk(m, { cap: +process.argv[2] });
    if (w.error) err(w.error);
    else out.walk = w;
  }
  done();
}

if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(realpathSync(process.argv[1])).href) await child();
```

```text file=~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/kit/mermaid.css
/* Mermaid drawn by Pele at render time: kit colors and fonts, and a phone layout below 640 px when the renderer made one */
.ve-mermaid > svg { display: block; margin-inline: auto; }
.ve-mermaid > .is-narrow { display: none; }
@media (max-width: 640px) {
  .ve-mermaid > .is-wide { display: none; }
  .ve-mermaid > .is-narrow { display: block; }
}
@media print { .ve-mermaid > svg { min-width: 0 !important; } }
.pele {
  --pele-bg: var(--surface); --pele-fg: var(--text); --pele-muted: var(--text-dim); --pele-line: var(--text-dim);
  --pele-surface: var(--surface); --pele-surface-alt: var(--bg); --pele-border: var(--border-bright); --pele-accent: var(--accent);
  --pele-critical: var(--risk); --pele-font: var(--font-body); --pele-font-mono: var(--font-mono); --pele-radius: 6px;
  --pele-series-1: var(--accent); --pele-series-2: var(--info); --pele-series-3: var(--ok); --pele-series-4: var(--warn); --pele-series-5: var(--risk);
  --pele-series-6: var(--text-dim); --pele-series-7: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 55%, var(--surface)); --pele-series-8: color-mix(in srgb, var(--info) 55%, var(--surface));
}
/* a walked machine drawn with <ve-flow auto> (references/machines.md): a state that can still reach a broken rule, the shortest way
   there, a state no event leaves, and the state that breaks the rule; later rules win, so the breaking state stays red on the path */
.pele-node.may-break > rect { stroke: var(--warn); stroke-width: 1.75; fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--warn) 10%, var(--surface)); }
.pele-node.bug-path > rect, .pele-edge.bug-path > path:not(.pele-marker) { stroke: var(--accent); stroke-width: 2.25; } .pele-edge.bug-path > .pele-marker { fill: var(--accent); }
.pele-node.dead-end > rect { stroke: var(--text-dim); stroke-dasharray: 3 3; }
.pele-node.breaks > rect { stroke: var(--risk); stroke-width: 2.5; stroke-dasharray: 6 3; }
```
