```text file=~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/kit/render.mjs
#!/usr/bin/env node
// Turns a page source into one self-contained page. A page that links the kit (<link rel="stylesheet" data-ve-kit>)
// gets the kit's CSS, fonts, SVG defs, and script inlined at that marker; a plan source goes to plan/render.mjs.
// Only the marker elements change, so a rendered page renders to itself. No installed dependencies (Pele is vendored), so it runs
// from a copied skill folder.
import { lstatSync, readFileSync, realpathSync, renameSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { spawn } from "node:child_process";
import { basename, dirname, join, resolve, sep } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath, pathToFileURL } from "node:url";
import { decode, esc, find, hasClass, inner, kids, parseHtml, serialize, textOf, words } from "./html.mjs";
import { expandFlow } from "./flow.mjs";
import { plural } from "./machine.mjs";
import { expandAsk } from "./ask.mjs";
import { TAGS } from "./tags.mjs";
import { PeleError, render as drawMermaid } from "./vendor/pele.mjs";
import { hasPlan, renderPlan, renderPlanForHost } from "../plan/render.mjs";

const here = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));

// Each register's families, at the weights the kit uses.
const FONTS = {
  instrument: "family=Geist:wght@400;500;600;700&family=Geist+Mono:wght@400;500;600",
  blueprint: "family=IBM+Plex+Sans:wght@400;500;600&family=IBM+Plex+Mono:wght@400;500;600",
  paper: "family=Newsreader:opsz,wght@6..72,400..600&family=Atkinson+Hyperlegible+Next:wght@400;600&family=Atkinson+Hyperlegible+Mono:wght@400;500;600",
  editorial: "family=Instrument+Serif&family=Instrument+Sans:wght@400;500;600&family=JetBrains+Mono:wght@400;500;600",
};

/** Figures, figures without a caption, expanded tags and flows, prose words outside figures, and a line per walked machine. */
function count(doc, tags) {
  const r = { figures: 0, uncaptioned: 0, dataTags: tags.filter((t) => t.name !== "ve-flow").length, flows: tags.filter((t) => t.name === "ve-flow").length, proseWords: 0 };
  const machines = tags.filter((t) => t.machine).map((t) => t.machine.line);
  if (machines.length) r.machines = machines;
  // a <p> inside an <li> is counted once, with its <li>
  const visit = (n, quiet) => {
    for (const c of kids(n)) {
      if (c.name === "figure") { r.figures++; if (!kids(c).some((k) => k.name === "figcaption")) r.uncaptioned++; }
      const prose = !quiet && (c.name === "p" || c.name === "li");
      if (prose) r.proseWords += words(textOf(c));
      visit(c, quiet || prose || c.name === "figure");
    }
  };
  visit(doc, false);
  return r;
}

export const reportPage = (html) => count(parseHtml(html), []);

export const reportLine = (r) => `Page: ${plural(r.figures, "figure")}${r.uncaptioned ? ` (${r.uncaptioned} without a caption)` : ""}${r.dataTags ? ` · ${plural(r.dataTags, "data tag")}` : ""}${r.flows ? ` · ${plural(r.flows, "flow")}` : ""} · ${plural(r.proseWords, "prose word")} outside figures${(r.machines ?? []).map((m) => `\n${m}`).join("")}`;

/**
 * Inlines the kit at its marker and expands the data tags, <ve-flow>, and <ve-ask>. A page with none returns unchanged, with `kit: false`.
 * `sendBack` marks a page Pi opens in Glimpse, so the reader's reply goes to the agent instead of being copied.
 * `root` is the repo a <ve-flow> model imports from; `models: false` refuses to run one (the MCP server, unless opted in).
 */
export function renderPage(source, { sendBack = false, root = process.cwd(), models = true } = {}) {
  const errors = [], warnings = [];
  const doc = parseHtml(source);
  const links = find(doc, (n) => n.name === "link" && "data-ve-kit" in n.attrs);
  const tags = find(doc, (n) => Object.hasOwn(TAGS, n.name) || n.name === "ve-flow" || n.name === "ve-ask");
  const asks = tags.filter((t) => t.name === "ve-ask"), charts = tags.filter((t) => t.name !== "ve-ask");
  // Mermaid is drawn on kit pages only; a deck or another page without the kit keeps its <pre> as written
  const mermaids = links.length ? find(doc, (n) => n.name === "pre" && hasClass(n, "mermaid")) : [];
  if (!links.length && !tags.length && !mermaids.length) return { html: source, kit: false, errors, warnings, report: count(doc, charts) };
  const lineOf = (pos) => source.slice(0, pos).split("\n").length;
  const where = (n) => `line ${lineOf(n.pos)} <${n.name}${n.attrs.id ? `#${n.attrs.id}` : ""}>`;
  if (!links.length) errors.push(`${where(tags[0])}: tags need the kit; add <link rel="stylesheet" href="kit.css" data-ve-kit> to <head>`);
  if (links.length > 1) errors.push(`${links.length} <link data-ve-kit> elements; keep one in <head>`);
  const register = find(doc, (n) => n.name === "html")[0]?.attrs["data-register"] || "instrument";
  if (!FONTS[register]) errors.push(`data-register="${register}" is not a register; use ${Object.keys(FONTS).join(", ")}`);
  const body = find(doc, (n) => n.name === "body")[0];
  if (!body) errors.push("the page has no <body>");
  // a box or arrow keeps the data-ref and data-s it was written with, so it lights with its terms and its steps
  const ref = (k) => {
    if ("claim" in k.attrs) errors.push(`${where(k)}: claim= belongs to plan pages; link a part to its terms with data-ref`);
    return ["data-ref", "data-s"].filter((a) => k.attrs[a] !== undefined).map((a) => ` ${a}="${esc(k.attrs[a])}"`).join("");
  };
  for (const n of find(doc, (x) => "data-if" in x.attrs)) errors.push(`${where(n)}: data-if belongs to plan pages`);
  // the reader's reply is collected inside <main>, so an ask anywhere else would be answered and never reach the agent
  if (asks.length) {
    const main = find(doc, (n) => n.name === "main")[0];
    const inMain = new Set(main ? find(main, (n) => n.name === "ve-ask") : []);
    for (const a of asks) if (!inMain.has(a)) errors.push(`${where(a)}: <ve-ask> must be inside <main>, where the reader's reply is collected`);
  }
  const ids = new Map();
  for (const t of tags) {
    if (t.name === "ve-ask") t.html = expandAsk(t, { errors, warnings, where, ids, k: asks.indexOf(t) + 1, total: asks.length, page: true });
    else t.html = t.name === "ve-flow" ? expandFlow(t, { errors, warnings, where, ref, page: true, root, models }) : TAGS[t.name](t, { errors, warnings, where });
  }
  // A walked flow replays its walk: the figure's captions must match its steps, or the render writes them (and the player).
  const replayed = new Set();
  for (const t of tags.filter((x) => x.machine?.steps)) {
    const fig = find(doc, (f) => f.name === "figure" && hasClass(f, "ve-steps") && find(f, (x) => x === t).length).at(-1);
    if (!fig) continue;
    // one stepper steps through every caption in its figure, so two walks there would play as one
    if (replayed.has(fig)) { errors.push(`${where(t)}: one walked <ve-flow> per <figure class="ve-steps">; put this one in its own figure`); continue; }
    replayed.add(fig);
    const { steps } = t.machine;
    const player = find(fig, (x) => hasClass(x, "ve-player"))[0], ol = find(fig, (x) => hasClass(x, "ve-cap"))[0];
    const caps = ol ? find(ol, (x) => x.name === "li") : [];
    const lis = steps.map((s, i) => `<li data-n="${i + 1}/${steps.length}">${esc(s)}</li>`).join("");
    if (caps.length && caps.length !== steps.length) errors.push(`${where(caps[0])}: the walk replays in ${plural(steps.length, "step")} (${steps.map((s) => `“${s}”`).join(", ")}); write ${steps.length} captions, or none and the render writes them`);
    else if (caps.length) continue;
    else if (ol) ol.html = `<ol class="ve-cap">${lis}</ol>`;
    else if (player) player.children.unshift({ html: `<ol class="ve-cap">${lis}</ol>` });
    else t.html += `<div class="ve-player"><ol class="ve-cap">${lis}</ol><button data-go="-1" aria-label="Previous step">‹</button><button data-play>Play</button><input type="range" aria-label="Step"><button data-go="1" aria-label="Next step">›</button></div>`;
  }
  // Mermaid becomes plain SVG here, so the page draws offline, follows the theme through CSS, and is checked like any drawing.
  // A phone gets its own layout when Pele can make one narrower. Neither layout shrinks below its natural width (the frame
  // scrolls instead), and Pele draws some labels smaller than its base size, so the base grows until the smallest is 12 px.
  // a <ve-flow auto> becomes a diagram like one written in Mermaid, so it is drawn and checked the same way
  for (const t of tags.filter((x) => x.auto)) mermaids.push({ name: "ve-flow", attrs: { "aria-label": t.attrs.label }, pos: t.pos, children: [{ text: t.auto.mermaid }], flow: t });
  for (const [i, pre] of mermaids.entries()) {
    const label = pre.attrs["aria-label"];
    if (!label) { errors.push(`${where(pre)}: add aria-label="…" saying what the diagram shows`); continue; }
    let wide, narrow;
    try {
      const text = decode(inner(pre));
      const draw = (maxWidth, idPrefix) => {
        for (let fontSize = 14; ; fontSize++) {
          const r = drawMermaid(text, { fontSize, maxWidth, idPrefix });
          if (fontSize >= 24 || Math.min(...[...r.svg.matchAll(/font-size(?:="|:\s*)([\d.]+)/g)].map((m) => +m[1])) >= 12) return r;
        }
      };
      wide = draw(960, `ve-m${i}w`);
      narrow = draw(280, `ve-m${i}n`);
    } catch (e) {
      if (!(e instanceof PeleError)) throw e;
      errors.push(`${where(pre)}: Mermaid: ${e.message.replace(/\s*\n\s*/g, " ")}`);
      continue;
    }
    const both = narrow.width < wide.width;
    // Mermaid cannot put a class on a transition, so a walk's bug-path arrows are marked by the number Pele gives them
    const lit = new Set(pre.flow?.auto.bugEdges.map((k) => `edge${k}`));
    const svg = (r, cls) => r.svg.replace(' role="graphics-document document"', ` role="img" aria-label="${esc(label)}"`).replace('class="pele ', `class="pele${cls} `).replace('style="', `style="min-width:${r.width}px;`)
      .replace(/class="pele-edge pele-transition" data-id="(edge\d+)"/g, (m, id) => (lit.has(id) ? m.replace("pele-transition", "pele-transition bug-path") : m));
    pre.html = `<div class="ve-mermaid"${pre.attrs.id ? ` id="${esc(pre.attrs.id)}"` : ""}>${svg(wide, both ? " is-wide" : "")}${both ? svg(narrow, " is-narrow") : ""}</div>`;
    if (pre.flow) pre.flow.html = `<div class="frame">${pre.html}</div>${pre.flow.auto.proof}`;
  }
  // Each drawing says what it shows, and a viewBox wider than 816 gets the min-width that keeps 14-unit labels at 12 px.
  const drawings = [];
  const top = (n) => { for (const c of kids(n)) if (c.name === "svg") drawings.push(c); else top(c); };
  top(doc);
  for (const svg of drawings) {
    if (svg.attrs["aria-hidden"] === "true") continue;
    if (!("aria-label" in svg.attrs) && !("aria-labelledby" in svg.attrs) && !kids(svg).some((k) => k.name === "title")) errors.push(`${where(svg)}: add aria-label="…" saying what the drawing shows (aria-hidden="true" if it is decoration)`);
    if (!("role" in svg.attrs)) svg.openRaw = svg.openRaw.replace(/\s*(\/?)>$/, ' role="img"$1>');
    const min = Math.ceil(((+(svg.attrs.viewbox ?? "").trim().split(/[\s,]+/)[2]) || 0) * 12 / 14);
    if (!hasClass(svg, "ve-svg") || hasClass(svg, "ve-flow") || min <= 700 || /min-width|--ve-min/.test(svg.attrs.style ?? "")) continue;
    const style = svg.openRaw.match(/\sstyle\s*=\s*(["'])(.*?)\1/is);
    if (!style && svg.attrs.style !== undefined) continue;
    svg.openRaw = style ? svg.openRaw.replace(style[0], ` style=${style[1]}${style[2].replace(/;?\s*$/, "")}; --ve-min: ${min}px${style[1]}`) : svg.openRaw.replace(/\s*(\/?)>$/, ` style="--ve-min: ${min}px"$1>`);
  }
  if (errors.length) return { html: source, kit: true, errors, warnings };

  // a page with <ve-ask> also gets its styles and its part of the reply; a page with Mermaid gets the diagram colors
  const css = ["kit.css", ...(asks.length ? ["ask.css"] : []), ...(mermaids.length ? ["mermaid.css"] : [])].map((f) => readFileSync(join(here, f), "utf8")).join("");
  const js = ["reply.js", ...(asks.length ? ["ask.js"] : []), "kit.js"].map((f) => readFileSync(join(here, f), "utf8")).join("\n").replace(/<\/script/gi, "<\\/script");
  const script = `<script data-ve-kit${sendBack ? " data-send-back" : ""}>\n${js}</script>`;
  // without a charset, Firefox and Safari garble · and — (prepareRenderedHtml adds the viewport)
  const charset = find(doc, (n) => n.name === "meta" && ("charset" in n.attrs || /^content-type$/i.test(n.attrs["http-equiv"] ?? ""))).length ? "" : '<meta charset="utf-8">\n';
  links[0].html = `${charset}<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin>
<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?${esc(FONTS[register])}&amp;display=swap" rel="stylesheet">
<style data-ve-kit>
${css}</style>`;
  // The shared defs go first in <body>, each only if the page has no element with its id (the template has all four, so it opens raw).
  const defs = readFileSync(join(here, "defs.svg"), "utf8").trimEnd().split("\n").filter((line) => {
    const id = line.match(/^\s*<\w+ id="([^"]+)"/)?.[1];
    return !id || !find(doc, (n) => n.attrs.id === id).length;
  });
  if (defs.length > 4) body.children.unshift({ html: `\n${defs.join("\n")}` });
  const scripts = find(doc, (n) => n.name === "script" && "data-ve-kit" in n.attrs);
  if (scripts.length) {
    scripts[0].html = script;
    for (const s of scripts.slice(1)) s.html = "";
  } else body.children.push({ html: `${script}\n` });
  return { html: serialize(doc), kit: true, errors, warnings, report: count(doc, charts) };
}

const favicon = '<link rel="icon" href="data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg xmlns=\'http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\' viewBox=\'0 0 64 64\'%3E%3Crect width=\'64\' height=\'64\' rx=\'14\' fill=\'%230f172a\'/%3E%3Cpath d=\'M18 40V24l14-8 14 8v16l-14 8-14-8Z\' fill=\'none\' stroke=\'%23fbbf24\' stroke-width=\'4\' stroke-linejoin=\'round\'/%3E%3Ccircle cx=\'32\' cy=\'32\' r=\'5\' fill=\'%2338bdf8\'/%3E%3C/svg%3E">';

/** The last step before a page is written (both hosts, every page; the CLI, kit pages): a favicon, `lang`, a `<head>`, and the viewport, each only when missing. */
export function prepareRenderedHtml(html) {
  let out = html;
  if (!/<link\b[^>]*\brel=["'][^"']*(?:icon|shortcut icon)[^"']*["'][^>]*>/i.test(out)) {
    if (/<\/title>/i.test(out)) out = out.replace(/<\/title>/i, `</title>\n${favicon}`);
    else if (/<head[^>]*>/i.test(out)) out = out.replace(/<head[^>]*>/i, (head) => `${head}\n${favicon}`);
    else out = out.replace(/<html[^>]*>/i, (tag) => `${tag}\n<head>\n${favicon}\n</head>`);
  }
  if (!/<html\b[^>]*\blang\s*=/i.test(out)) out = out.replace(/<html\b/i, '<html lang="en"');
  if (!/<head[^>]*>/i.test(out)) out = out.replace(/<html[^>]*>/i, (tag) => `${tag}\n<head></head>`);
  if (!/<meta\b[^>]*\bname\s*=\s*["']viewport["'][^>]*>/i.test(out)) out = out.replace(/<head[^>]*>/i, (head) => `${head}\n<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">`);
  return out;
}

/** `path` in both hosts: a <name>.src.html file inside the output directory (`dir()`), never a link out of it. */
export function readSourcePath(input, dir) {
  const raw = input.trim();
  if (!/\.src\.html?$/i.test(raw)) throw new Error("path must name a <name>.src.html file");
  const outputDir = realpathSync(dir());
  const requested = resolve(outputDir, raw);
  if (lstatSync(requested, { throwIfNoEntry: false })?.isSymbolicLink()) throw new Error(`${requested} must not be a symlink`);
  const source = realpathSync(requested);
  if (source !== outputDir && !source.startsWith(outputDir.endsWith(sep) ? outputDir : `${outputDir}${sep}`)) throw new Error(`${source} must stay inside ${outputDir}`);
  return { html: readFileSync(source, "utf8"), filename: basename(source).replace(/\.src(\.html?)$/i, "$1"), source };
}

/**
 * The page step shared by the Pi tool and the MCP server. Returns null for an ordinary page. A plan source or a kit page
 * becomes the page, renamed from <name>.src.html, with the source kept beside it.
 */
export function renderPageForHost(html, { root, filename, sendBack = false, models = true }) {
  const plan = renderPlanForHost(html, { root, filename, sendBack, models });
  if (plan) return plan;
  const r = renderPage(html, { sendBack, root, models });
  if (!r.kit) return null;
  if (r.errors.length) throw new Error(`The page has ${r.errors.length} error(s); nothing was written:\n${r.errors.map((e) => `- ${e}`).join("\n")}`);
  const page = filename.replace(/\.src(\.html?)$/i, "$1");
  const source = page.replace(/\.html?$/i, ".src.html");
  const warned = r.warnings.length ? `\nWarnings:\n${r.warnings.map((w) => `- ${w}`).join("\n")}` : "";
  return { html: r.html, filename: page, source, kit: true, report: r.report, note: ` Source kept beside it as ${source}; edit it and render again for revisions.${warned}` };
}

/* ── CLI ── */
function openFile(path) {
  const [cmd, args] = process.platform === "darwin" ? ["open", [path]] : process.platform === "win32" ? ["cmd", ["/c", "start", "", path]] : ["xdg-open", [path]];
  spawn(cmd, args, { detached: true, stdio: "ignore" }).unref();
}

async function main() {
  const argv = process.argv.slice(2);
  const flag = (name) => argv.includes(name);
  const value = (name) => { const i = argv.indexOf(name); return i >= 0 ? argv[i + 1] : undefined; };
  const input = argv.find((a, i) => !a.startsWith("-") && !["-o", "--root"].includes(argv[i - 1]));
  if (!input) {
    console.error("usage: node render.mjs page.src.html [-o page.html] [--root <repo>] [--lint] [--open] [--no-check]");
    process.exit(2);
  }
  const output = value("-o") ?? (/\.src\.html?$/i.test(input) ? input.replace(/\.src(\.html?)$/i, "$1") : null);
  if (!output && !flag("--lint")) {
    console.error("name the source <name>.src.html, or pass -o <name>.html");
    process.exit(2);
  }
  const source = readFileSync(input, "utf8");
  const root = value("--root") ?? process.cwd();
  const result = hasPlan(source) ? renderPlan(source, { root }) : renderPage(source, { root });
  const summary = result.summary ?? (result.kit ? "kit inlined" : "no kit marker; written as given");
  for (const w of result.warnings) console.log(`  ⚠ ${w}`);
  for (const e of result.errors) console.log(`  ✗ ${e}`);
  if (result.errors.length) {
    console.log(`✗ ${result.errors.length} error(s), ${result.warnings.length} warning(s); nothing written`);
    process.exit(1);
  }
  const report = result.report ? `\n  ${reportLine(result.report).replaceAll("\n", "\n  ")}` : "";
  if (flag("--lint")) { console.log(`✓ ${summary}${report}`); return; }
  const temp = `${output}.${process.pid}.tmp`;
  // a plan and an ordinary page are written as given; a kit page gets what the hosts add
```

```text file=~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/kit/tags.mjs
// Data tags: the numbers go in, the kit's SVG comes out, on an exact scale that starts at zero.
//   <ve-bars unit="ms" max="9" label="…"><ve-bar value="1" hot>hit</ve-bar>…</ve-bars>   rows in the order written
//   <ve-waffle value="94" note="6 misses" label="…"></ve-waffle>                           100 cells, the first N on
//   <ve-stack unit="k" label="…"><ve-bar value="3.5">SKILL.md</ve-bar>…</ve-stack>        one bar split in proportion
import { esc, kids, textOf } from "./html.mjs";

const CH = 8; // a mono character at 13–14 units, rounded up, for sizing label columns

// "1 ms" and "4 MB" take a no-break space; "3.5k" and "13%" do not.
const withUnit = (v, unit) => (unit ? `${v}${unit.length > 1 ? "\u00a0" : ""}${unit}` : v);

function values(n, { errors, warnings, where }) {
  if (!n.attrs.label) warnings.push(`${where(n)}: add label="…", one sentence a screen reader can read instead of the picture`);
  const rows = [];
  for (const k of kids(n)) {
    if (k.name !== "ve-bar") { errors.push(`${where(k)}: only <ve-bar> belongs in <${n.name}>`); continue; }
    const raw = (k.attrs.value ?? "").trim(), value = Number(raw);
    if (raw === "" || !Number.isFinite(value)) errors.push(`${where(k)}: value="${raw}" is not a number`);
    else if (value < 0) errors.push(`${where(k)}: value="${raw}" is negative; bars start at zero`);
    else rows.push({ raw, value, name: textOf(k).trim(), hot: "hot" in k.attrs });
  }
  if (!rows.length && !kids(n).length) errors.push(`${where(n)}: needs at least one <ve-bar value="…">`);
  return rows;
}

function bars(n, ctx) {
  const rows = values(n, ctx), unit = n.attrs.unit || "";
  let max = Math.max(0, ...rows.map((r) => r.value));
  if (n.attrs.max !== undefined) {
    const m = Number(n.attrs.max);
    if (!Number.isFinite(m) || m <= 0) ctx.errors.push(`${ctx.where(n)}: max="${n.attrs.max}" must be a number above zero`);
    else if (m < max) ctx.errors.push(`${ctx.where(n)}: max="${n.attrs.max}" is below the largest value, ${max}`);
    else max = m;
  }
  if (!rows.length) return "";
  // A shared max means a shared scale, so those charts all use the same fixed columns; others fit their own labels.
  const shared = n.attrs.max !== undefined;
  if (shared) for (const r of rows) {
    if (r.name.length > 9) ctx.errors.push(`${ctx.where(n)}: "${r.name}" is longer than 9 characters, the label column of a shared scale`);
    if (withUnit(r.raw, unit).length > 6) ctx.errors.push(`${ctx.where(n)}: "${withUnit(r.raw, unit)}" is longer than 6 characters, the value column of a shared scale`);
  }
  const labelW = shared ? 9 * CH + 12 : Math.max(...rows.map((r) => r.name.length)) * CH + 12;
  const valueW = shared ? 6 * CH + 8 : Math.max(...rows.map((r) => withUnit(r.raw, unit).length)) * CH + 8;
  // long labels or values widen the drawing, so a bar always has at least 60 units to grow in
  const span = Math.max(240 - labelW - valueW, 60), width = labelW + span + valueW;
  const svg = rows.map((r, i) => {
    const y = 12 + i * 28, w = max ? Math.round((r.value / max) * span * 100) / 100 : 0;
    return `<text y="${y}">${esc(r.name)}</text><rect${r.hot ? ' class="hot"' : ""} x="${labelW}" y="${y - 7}" width="${w}" height="14" rx="2"/><text x="${labelW + w + 8}" y="${y}">${esc(withUnit(r.raw, unit))}</text>`;
  }).join("");
  // a widened chart may grow past the 16rem cap in step, so its labels keep their size
  const cap = width > 240 ? ` style="max-width:${Math.round((width / 240) * 1600) / 100}rem"` : "";
  return `<svg class="ve-bars"${cap} viewBox="0 0 ${width} ${rows.length * 28 - 4}" role="img" aria-label="${esc(n.attrs.label || "")}">${svg}</svg>`;
}

function waffle(n, { errors, warnings, where }) {
  if (!n.attrs.label) warnings.push(`${where(n)}: add label="…", one sentence a screen reader can read instead of the picture`);
  const raw = (n.attrs.value ?? "").trim(), v = Number(raw);
  if (raw === "" || !Number.isInteger(v) || v < 0 || v > 100) { errors.push(`${where(n)}: value="${raw}" must be a whole number from 0 to 100`); return ""; }
  // the first v cells are on, row by row from the top left
  const full = Math.floor(v / 10), part = v % 10, cells = [];
  const on = (x, y, w, h) => w && h && cells.push(`<rect x="${x}" y="${y}" width="${w}" height="${h}" fill="url(#ve-w-on)"/>`);
  const off = (x, y, w, h) => w && h && cells.push(`<rect x="${x}" y="${y}" width="${w}" height="${h}" fill="url(#ve-w-off)"/>`);
  on(0, 0, 100, full * 10);
  on(0, full * 10, part * 10, part ? 10 : 0);
  off(part * 10, full * 10, part ? 100 - part * 10 : 0, part ? 10 : 0);
  off(0, (full + (part ? 1 : 0)) * 10, 100, (10 - full - (part ? 1 : 0)) * 10);
  const y = full * 10 + 5; // the row of the first off cell
  const note = n.attrs.note && v < 100 ? `<path class="ann" d="M104 ${y}H114"/><text x="118" y="${y}">${esc(n.attrs.note)}</text>` : "";
  return `<svg class="ve-waffle" viewBox="0 0 170 100" role="img" aria-label="${esc(n.attrs.label || "")}">${cells.join("")}${note}</svg>`;
}

function stack(n, ctx) {

  if (!rows.length) return "";

export const TAGS = { "ve-bars": bars, "ve-waffle": waffle, "ve-stack": stack };
```

#### `~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/mcp/README.md`

````markdown file=~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/mcp/README.md
# Visual Explainer MCP server

This directory contains the local Model Context Protocol server for visual-explainer.

## Scope

The server is stdio-only. It is meant for MCP hosts that launch a local child process.
It does not start an HTTP listener, handle credentials, call an LLM, or store output outside the local machine.

Rendered files are written only inside the configured output directory. The default is `~/.agent/diagrams/`. Set `VISUAL_EXPLAINER_OUTPUT_DIR` to move that jail to another directory on the same machine; unset keeps the default path byte-identical. A configured jail must resolve to itself, so symlinked jail paths, including macOS `/tmp`, are rejected before anything is created. The default directory follows a symlinked `~/.agent`. Render targets reject existing symlinks and are written through a temporary file rename. Choose a directory only your user can write; avoid world-writable or group-writable shared folders so another local user cannot replace render targets between validation and write. Filenames must be basenames. Paths, traversal, control characters, and symlink targets are rejected.

A page can hold a state-machine model (`<ve-flow>` with a `<script type="text/plain" model>`), which is code the render runs. The server refuses it unless started with `VISUAL_EXPLAINER_RUN_MODELS=1`. With it set, a page's model runs as Node with this server's permissions, importing from the `root` argument or the server's working directory; set it only when every client that can call the render tool is trusted.

## Run from a package install

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "visual-explainer": {
      "command": "visual-explainer-mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

## Run from a checkout

Install dependencies first:

```bash
npm install --no-package-lock
```

Then point the host at the server entry:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "visual-explainer": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["/absolute/path/to/visual-explainer/plugins/visual-explainer/mcp/server.mjs"]
    }
  }
}
```

## Exposed tools

- `visual_explainer_prepare`: returns a recommended visual explanation flow. It does not write files.
- `visual_explainer_render_html`: validates a complete HTML document and writes it to the configured output directory (default `~/.agent/diagrams/`).

Render defaults to `open: false`. Set `open: true` only when you want the server to request a browser or Glimpse window.

## Exposed prompts

The server exposes the bundled command templates as MCP prompts:

- `generate-web-diagram`
- `generate-visual-plan`
- `generate-slides`
- `generate-video`
- `diff-review`
- `plan-review`
- `project-recap`
- `compare`
- `fact-check`
- `state-machine`

Pass `request` to fill the template's `$@` argument.

## Exposed resources

The server exposes read-only resources for the canonical skill, its references, the kit stylesheet, and command templates:

- `visual-explainer://skill/SKILL.md`
- `visual-explainer://references/*.md`
- `visual-explainer://kit/kit.css`
- `visual-explainer://commands/*.md`
````

#### `~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/mcp/server.mjs`

```text file=~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/mcp/server.mjs mode=755
#!/usr/bin/env node
import { spawn } from "node:child_process";
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import { existsSync, lstatSync, mkdirSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, realpathSync, renameSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { homedir } from "node:os";
import { dirname, join, relative, resolve, sep } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { McpServer } from "@modelcontextprotocol/server";
import { serveStdio } from "@modelcontextprotocol/server/stdio";
import * as z from "zod/v4";
import { prepareRenderedHtml, readSourcePath, renderPageForHost, reportLine, reportPage } from "../kit/render.mjs";
import { lookAt, lookLines } from "../kit/look.mjs";

const serverPath = fileURLToPath(import.meta.url);
const mcpDir = dirname(serverPath);
const skillDir = dirname(mcpDir);
const rootDir = join(skillDir, "..", "..");
const packageJson = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(rootDir, "package.json"), "utf8"));

const viewerSchema = z.enum(["browser", "glimpse", "auto"]);
const openStatusSchema = z.enum(["disabled", "unsupported", "dispatched", "failed"]);
const openTargetSchema = z.enum(["browser", "glimpse"]);

const prepareInputSchema = z.object({
  topic: z.string().min(1).describe("What the visual explanation should cover."),
  goal: z.string().optional().describe("What the user wants to understand, decide, or communicate."),
  files: z.array(z.string()).optional().describe("Relevant files or paths the host model should inspect."),
  audience: z.string().optional().describe("Intended audience, such as developer, PM, team, reviewer, or executive."),
}).strict();

const prepareOutputSchema = z.object({
  topic: z.string(),
  goal: z.string().optional(),
  audience: z.string().optional(),
  files: z.array(z.string()),
  recommendedFlow: z.array(z.string()),
});

const renderInputSchema = z.object({
  filename: z.string().min(1).optional().describe("With html: basename filename; .html is appended when missing."),
  html: z.string().min(1).optional().describe("Page source or complete HTML, when you cannot write a path."),
  path: z.string().min(1).optional().describe("Instead of html: a <name>.src.html file in the output directory."),
  root: z.string().min(1).optional().describe("The repository a plan source (<ve-plan> tags) checks its citations against, and a page's <ve-flow> model imports from. Defaults to the server's working directory."),
  open: z.boolean().default(false).describe("Open the written file after rendering. Defaults to false for MCP."),
  viewer: viewerSchema.default("browser").describe("Viewer to use when open is true."),
}).strict();

const renderOutputSchema = z.object({
  path: z.string(),
  viewer: viewerSchema,
  openAttempted: z.boolean(),
  openStatus: openStatusSchema,
  openTarget: openTargetSchema.optional(),
  openError: z.string().optional(),
  fallbackFrom: openTargetSchema.optional(),
  fallbackError: z.string().optional(),
  source: z.string().optional(),
  report: z.object({ figures: z.number(), uncaptioned: z.number(), dataTags: z.number(), flows: z.number(), proseWords: z.number(), machines: z.array(z.string()).optional() }).optional(),
});

const promptArgsSchema = z.object({
  request: z.string().optional().describe("User-supplied prompt arguments. This replaces $@ in the bundled command template."),
}).strict();

const promptFiles = [
  "compare.md",
  "diff-review.md",
  "fact-check.md",
  "generate-slides.md",
  "generate-video.md",
  "generate-visual-plan.md",
  "generate-web-diagram.md",
  "plan-review.md",
  "project-recap.md",
  "state-machine.md",
];

const resourceFiles = [
  { name: "skill", uri: "visual-explainer://skill/SKILL.md", path: "SKILL.md", title: "Visual Explainer Skill", mimeType: "text/markdown" },
  // every reference the skill points to, so a client with no file access can still read them
  { name: "kit-css", uri: "visual-explainer://kit/kit.css", path: "kit/kit.css", title: "Kit stylesheet", mimeType: "text/css" },
  ...(existsSync(join(skillDir, "references")) ? readdirSync(join(skillDir, "references")) : []).filter((file) => file.endsWith(".md")).sort().map((file) => (
    { name: `reference-${file.slice(0, -3)}`, uri: `visual-explainer://references/${file}`, path: `references/${file}`, title: `Reference: ${file}`, mimeType: "text/markdown" }
  )),
];

function readSkillFile(relativePath) {
  return readFileSync(join(skillDir, relativePath), "utf8");
}

function parsePromptFile(relativePath) {
  const text = readSkillFile(relativePath);
  const match = text.match(/^---\n([\s\S]*?)\n---\n?([\s\S]*)$/);
  if (!match) {
    const name = relativePath.split("/").pop()?.replace(/\.md$/, "") ?? relativePath;
    return { name, description: `Visual Explainer prompt from ${relativePath}.`, body: text };
  }

  const frontmatter = match[1];
  const body = match[2];
  const name = frontmatter.match(/^name:\s*(.+)$/m)?.[1]?.trim() ?? relativePath.split("/").pop()?.replace(/\.md$/, "") ?? relativePath;
  const description = frontmatter.match(/^description:\s*(.+)$/m)?.[1]?.trim() ?? `Visual Explainer prompt from ${relativePath}.`;
  return { name, description, body };
}

function outputFilename(input) {
  if (/[\0-\x1f\x7f]/.test(input)) throw new Error("filename must not contain control characters");

  const raw = input.replace(/^@/, "").trim();

  if (!raw) throw new Error("filename is required");
  if (raw.includes("/") || raw.includes("\\")) throw new Error("filename must be a basename, not a path");
  if (raw.includes("..")) throw new Error("filename must not contain '..'");

  return /\.html?$/i.test(raw) ? raw : `${raw}.html`;
}

function resolveOutputDirectory() {
  const configured = process.env.VISUAL_EXPLAINER_OUTPUT_DIR?.trim();
  return {
    path: configured ? resolve(configured) : join(homedir(), ".agent", "diagrams"),
    configured: Boolean(configured),
  };
}

// Checks the nearest existing ancestor, so a rejected directory is never created through a symlink.
function assertResolvesToItself(path) {
  let existing = path;
  // A missing Windows drive or UNC root is its own dirname; stop there and let realpathSync throw.
  while (!lstatSync(existing, { throwIfNoEntry: false }) && dirname(existing) !== existing) existing = dirname(existing);
  const resolved = join(realpathSync(existing), relative(existing, path));
  if (resolved !== path) throw new Error(`${path} must not contain symlinks and must resolve to itself (it resolves to ${resolved})`);
}

function assertOutputPathContained(resolvedDir, outputPath) {
  const resolvedPath = resolve(outputPath);
  const dirPrefix = resolvedDir.endsWith(sep) ? resolvedDir : `${resolvedDir}${sep}`;
  if (resolvedPath !== resolvedDir && !resolvedPath.startsWith(dirPrefix)) {
    throw new Error(`${outputPath} must stay inside ${resolvedDir}`);
  }
}

function writeRenderedFile(outputPath, html) {
  const temporaryPath = `${outputPath}.${process.pid}.${randomUUID()}.tmp`;
  try {
    writeFileSync(temporaryPath, html, { encoding: "utf8", flag: "wx", mode: 0o666 });
    renameSync(temporaryPath, outputPath);
  } catch (error) {
    throw error;
  } finally {
    rmSync(temporaryPath, { force: true });
  }
}

function assertHtmlDocument(html) {
  const trimmed = html.trim();
  if (!trimmed) throw new Error("html is required");

  const start = trimmed.replace(/^\s*<!doctype\s+html\b[^>]*>\s*/i, "").replace(/^(?:<!--[\s\S]*?-->\s*)+/, "");
  if (!/^<html[\s>]/i.test(start) || !/<\/html>\s*$/i.test(trimmed)) {
    throw new Error("html must be a complete HTML document starting with <!doctype html> or <html> and ending with </html>");
  }
}

function runOpener(command, args, openTarget) {
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    const child = spawn(command, args, { detached: true, stdio: "ignore", windowsHide: true });
    let settled = false;

    const settle = (result) => {
      if (settled) return;
      settled = true;
      clearTimeout(timer);
      resolve(result);
    };

    child.once("error", (error) => {
      settle({
        openAttempted: true,
        openStatus: "failed",
        openTarget,
        openError: error.message,
      });
    });

    child.once("exit", (code, signal) => {
      if (code !== 0) {
        settle({
          openAttempted: true,
          openStatus: "failed",
          openTarget,
          openError: code === null ? `opener exited with signal ${signal ?? "unknown"}` : `opener exited with code ${code}`,
        });
      }
    });

    const timer = setTimeout(() => {
      settle({ openAttempted: true, openStatus: "dispatched", openTarget });
    }, 250);

    child.unref();
  });
}

async function openInBrowser(path) {
  if (process.platform === "darwin") return await runOpener("open", [path], "browser");
  if (process.platform === "linux") return await runOpener("xdg-open", [path], "browser");
  if (process.platform === "win32") return await runOpener("cmd", ["/c", "start", "", path], "browser");
  return { openAttempted: false, openStatus: "unsupported", openTarget: "browser" };
}

async function openInGlimpse(path) {
  return await runOpener("glimpseui", ["--width", "1200", "--height", "900", "--title", "Visual Explainer", "--open-links", path], "glimpse");
}

async function openRenderedPage(path, viewer) {
  if (viewer === "browser") return await openInBrowser(path);
  if (viewer === "glimpse") return await openInGlimpse(path);

  const glimpseResult = await openInGlimpse(path);
  if (glimpseResult.openStatus !== "failed") return glimpseResult;

  const browserResult = await openInBrowser(path);
  return {
    ...browserResult,
    fallbackFrom: "glimpse",
    fallbackError: glimpseResult.openError ?? "glimpseui failed",
  };
}

function compact(value) {
  return Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(value).filter((entry) => entry[1] !== undefined));
}

function renderToolResult(message, structuredContent, images = []) {
  return {
    content: [{ type: "text", text: message }, ...images],
    structuredContent: compact(structuredContent),
  };
}

function renderToolError(error) {
  return {
    content: [{ type: "text", text: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) }],
    isError: true,
  };
}

function prepareVisualExplanation(params) {
  const topic = params.topic.trim();
  if (!topic) throw new Error("topic is required");

  const goal = params.goal?.trim();
  const audience = params.audience?.trim();
  const files = params.files?.map((file) => file.trim()).filter(Boolean) ?? [];
  const recommendedFlow = [
    "Choose the page shape with the visual-explainer prompts and skill resources.",
    "Gather and verify the facts yourself; the server does not call an LLM.",
    "Write <name>.src.html in the output directory and call visual_explainer_render_html with path (without file access: html and filename).",
    "The server writes only inside its output directory (default ~/.agent/diagrams/).",
  ];

  const structuredContent = { topic, goal, audience, files, recommendedFlow };
  const message = [
    `Prepared visual explanation for: ${topic}`,
    goal ? `Goal: ${goal}` : undefined,
    audience ? `Audience: ${audience}` : undefined,
    files.length ? `Starting files: ${files.join(", ")}` : undefined,
    "Recommended flow:",
    ...recommendedFlow.map((step, index) => `${index + 1}. ${step}`),
  ].filter(Boolean).join("\n");

  return renderToolResult(message, structuredContent);
}

async function writeRenderedHtml(filenameInput, htmlInput, open, viewer, planRoot, sourcePath) {
  assertHtmlDocument(htmlInput);
  // MCP cannot put the reader's reply into the chat, so plan and kit pages here always copy it instead (no sendBack).
  // a <ve-flow> model runs the repo's code, so a client can only make this server run one when its operator opted in
  const page = renderPageForHost(htmlInput, { root: planRoot, filename: outputFilename(filenameInput), models: process.env.VISUAL_EXPLAINER_RUN_MODELS === "1" });
  // a plan page has its own summary in its note; every other page gets the report
  const report = page ? page.report : reportPage(htmlInput);
  const filename = page?.filename ?? outputFilename(filenameInput);
  const html = prepareRenderedHtml(page ? page.html : htmlInput);
  const { path: outputDir, configured } = resolveOutputDirectory();
  const outputPath = join(outputDir, filename);

  const outputDirStatus = lstatSync(outputDir, { throwIfNoEntry: false });
  if (outputDirStatus?.isSymbolicLink()) throw new Error(`${outputDir} must not be a symlink`);
  if (configured) assertResolvesToItself(outputDir);
  mkdirSync(outputDir, { recursive: true });
  if (configured) assertResolvesToItself(outputDir);
  const resolvedDir = realpathSync(outputDir);
  assertOutputPathContained(resolvedDir, join(resolvedDir, filename));

  const outputStatus = lstatSync(outputPath, { throwIfNoEntry: false });
  if (outputStatus?.isSymbolicLink()) throw new Error(`${outputPath} must not be a symlink`);

  // Keep the source beside the page: revisions and build receipts are small edits to it, then a new render.
  // The source goes first, so a failed write never leaves a new page beside an old source. A source read from path stays as it is.
  const source = sourcePath ?? (page?.source ? join(outputDir, page.source) : undefined);
  if (source && !sourcePath) {
    if (lstatSync(source, { throwIfNoEntry: false })?.isSymbolicLink()) throw new Error(`${source} must not be a symlink`);
    writeRenderedFile(source, htmlInput);
  }
  writeRenderedFile(outputPath, html);
  // a kit page is looked at in a browser, and its sheet comes back with the report, so the agent never scripts its own screenshots
  const looked = page?.kit ? await lookAt(outputPath) : undefined;

  const openResult = open ? await openRenderedPage(outputPath, viewer) : { openAttempted: false, openStatus: "disabled" };
  let message = `Wrote ${outputPath}.`;
  if (openResult.openStatus === "dispatched") {
    message += ` ${openResult.openTarget === "glimpse" ? "Glimpse" : "Browser"} open requested.`;
  } else if (openResult.openStatus === "failed") {
    message += ` ${openResult.openTarget === "glimpse" ? "Glimpse" : "Browser"} open failed: ${openResult.openError ?? "unknown error"}.`;
  } else if (openResult.openStatus === "unsupported") {
    message += " Browser opening is unsupported on this platform.";
  }
  if (openResult.fallbackFrom === "glimpse") {
    message += ` Glimpse fallback reason: ${openResult.fallbackError ?? "unknown error"}.`;
  }
  if (page) message += page.note;
  if (report) message += `\n${reportLine(report)}`;
  if (looked) message += `\n${lookLines(looked).join("\n")}`;
  const images = (looked?.sheets ?? []).map((sheet) => ({ type: "image", data: readFileSync(sheet).toString("base64"), mimeType: "image/png" }));

  return { message, output: compact({ path: outputPath, viewer, ...openResult, source, report }), images };
}

function registerResources(server) {
  for (const resource of resourceFiles) {
    server.registerResource(resource.name, resource.uri, {
      title: resource.title,
      description: `Bundled visual-explainer resource: ${resource.path}`,
      mimeType: resource.mimeType,
    }, async (uri) => ({
      contents: [{ uri: uri.href, mimeType: resource.mimeType, text: readSkillFile(resource.path) }],
    }));
  }

  for (const file of promptFiles) {
    const relativePath = `commands/${file}`;
    const prompt = parsePromptFile(relativePath);
    server.registerResource(`command-${prompt.name}`, `visual-explainer://commands/${file}`, {
      title: `/${prompt.name}`,
      description: prompt.description,
      mimeType: "text/markdown",
    }, async (uri) => ({
      contents: [{ uri: uri.href, mimeType: "text/markdown", text: readSkillFile(relativePath) }],
    }));
  }
}

function registerPrompts(server) {
  for (const file of promptFiles) {
    const prompt = parsePromptFile(`commands/${file}`);
    server.registerPrompt(prompt.name, {
      title: `/${prompt.name}`,
      description: prompt.description,
      argsSchema: promptArgsSchema,
    }, ({ request }) => ({
      messages: [{
        role: "user",
        content: {
          type: "text",
          text: prompt.body.replaceAll("$@", request ?? "").trim(),
        },
      }],
    }));
  }
}

function registerTools(server) {
  server.registerTool("visual_explainer_prepare", {
    title: "Prepare Visual Explainer",
    description: "Plan a visual explanation. Does not call an LLM or write files.",
    inputSchema: prepareInputSchema,
    outputSchema: prepareOutputSchema,
    annotations: { readOnlyHint: true, idempotentHint: true, openWorldHint: false },
  }, async (params) => {
    try {
      return prepareVisualExplanation(params);
    } catch (error) {
      return renderToolError(error);
    }
  });

  server.registerTool("visual_explainer_render_html", {
    title: "Render Visual Explainer HTML",
    description: "Render a page source (path) or HTML to the configured output directory (default ~/.agent/diagrams/). Does not call an LLM.",
    inputSchema: renderInputSchema,
    outputSchema: renderOutputSchema,
    annotations: { readOnlyHint: false, destructiveHint: false, idempotentHint: false, openWorldHint: false },
  }, async ({ filename, html, path, root, open, viewer }) => {
    try {
      if (html !== undefined && path !== undefined) throw new Error("pass html or path, not both");
      if (path !== undefined && filename !== undefined) throw new Error("filename is not allowed with path; the page is named after its source");
      if (path === undefined && (html === undefined || filename === undefined)) throw new Error("pass html with filename, or path");
      const source = path === undefined ? undefined : readSourcePath(path, () => resolveOutputDirectory().path);
      const result = await writeRenderedHtml(source?.filename ?? filename, source?.html ?? html, open, viewer, root ?? process.cwd(), source?.source);
      return renderToolResult(result.message, result.output, result.images);
    } catch (error) {
      return renderToolError(error);
    }
  });
}

export function createServer() {
  const server = new McpServer({ name: "visual-explainer", version: packageJson.version });
  registerResources(server);
  registerPrompts(server);
  registerTools(server);
  return server;
}

function isMainModule() {
  return Boolean(process.argv[1] && realpathSync(process.argv[1]) === serverPath);
}

if (isMainModule()) {
  const handle = serveStdio(createServer);
  console.error("visual-explainer MCP server running on stdio");

  for (const signal of ["SIGINT", "SIGTERM"]) {
    process.on(signal, () => {
      void handle.close().finally(() => process.exit(0));
    });
  }

}
```

```text file=~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/plan/plan.css
/* Plan pages: the Blueprint register from references/style-guide.md, the diagram kit from templates/page.html, and the plan parts.

:root {
  color-scheme: light dark;
  --bg: #0d1520; --surface: #132031; --border: #22324a; --border-bright: #596b87;
  --text: #e3ecf5; --text-dim: #92a6bb; --accent: #ffb547; --accent-dim: rgba(255,181,71,.14);

  --font-body: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', sans-serif;

  --t-label: .75rem; --t-small: .875rem; --t-body: 1rem; --t-lead: 1.25rem; --t-h2: 1.625rem; --t-h1: clamp(2.25rem, 5.5vw, 4rem);
  --s-1: .25rem; --s-2: .5rem; --s-3: .75rem; --s-4: 1rem; --s-5: 1.5rem; --s-6: 2rem; --s-7: 3rem; --s-8: 4.5rem;
  --r-1: 4px; --r-2: 10px;

}
@media (prefers-color-scheme: light) {

    --bg: #f2f6fa; --surface: #ffffff; --border: #d6e0ea; --border-bright: #818f9e;

    --ok: #1c7443; --warn: #776300; --risk: #b0341e; --info: #145f99;

}

.done td { padding: var(--s-2) var(--s-3); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border); vertical-align: top; }
.done td:first-child a { font: 600 var(--t-label) var(--font-mono); margin-right: var(--s-2); }

/* response bar and dialog: the plan's own parts (the shared ones are in kit/reply.js) */
.ve-bar .next { border-color: var(--accent); color: var(--accent); background: var(--surface); }
.r-row.todo { border-color: var(--accent); } .r-row.todo .st { color: var(--accent); } .r-row.changed .st { color: var(--text); }
.verdict { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: var(--s-2); border: 0; padding: 0; }
.verdict label { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--s-2); padding: var(--s-2) var(--s-3); border: 1px solid var(--border-bright); border-radius: var(--r-1); font: 500 var(--t-small) var(--font-mono); cursor: pointer; }
.verdict label:has(input:checked) { border-color: var(--text); background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--text) 8%, var(--surface)); }
.verdict input { accent-color: var(--accent); }
.r-warn { font: 500 var(--t-small) var(--font-mono); color: var(--warn); }
.ve-keys { position: fixed; right: var(--s-5); bottom: 5rem; z-index: 25; background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--border-bright); border-radius: var(--r-1); padding: var(--s-3) var(--s-4); font: var(--t-label)/1.9 var(--font-mono); color: var(--text-dim); box-shadow: 0 12px 32px var(--lift); }

@media (max-width: 40rem) {
  .plan-page { padding: var(--s-6) var(--s-4) 7rem; }
  .c-body { padding-left: var(--s-3); }
  .c-text { flex-basis: 12rem; }
  .c-meta { margin-left: calc(2rem + var(--s-3)); }

}

@media print {
  :root { --bg: #fff; --surface: #fff; --border: #d6e0ea; --border-bright: #818f9e; --text: #0f1a26; --text-dim: #4d6074; --accent: #a34700; --accent-dim: rgba(163,71,0,.12); --ok: #1c7443; --warn: #776300; --risk: #b0341e; --info: #145f99; --node-top: #fff; --grid: transparent; }
  body { background: #fff; }

  .plan-grid { display: block; } .plan-hero { position: static; margin-bottom: var(--s-5); }
  .claim[open] > summary { position: static; box-shadow: none; }
  .frame, .ask, .code, .calls, .mock { break-inside: avoid; }

}
```

```js file=~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/plan/plan.js
/* Plan page runtime. plan/render.mjs inlines it; the page works without it as a static, printable plan.
   Kit (linked highlighting, flow dots, entrance) mirrors templates/page.html. Plan parts: decisions,
   "seen" tracking, data-if, live diff stat, comments, keyboard, saved answers, and the response.
   The comment popover, the dialog, and sending or copying come from kit/reply.js, inlined before it. */
(() => {
  "use strict";
  const R = window.veReply;
  const { $, $$, h, toast } = R;
  const still = matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)").matches;

  /* ── kit: linked highlighting. Hover wins while it lasts; focus comes back after. ── */
  const linked = $$("[data-ref]");
  const refs = (el) => el.dataset.ref.split(" ");
  let hovered = null, focused = null;
  const paint = () => {
    const keys = (hovered || focused)?.dataset.ref.split(" ") ?? [];
    for (const t of linked) t.classList.toggle("is-lit", refs(t).some((k) => keys.includes(k)));
    for (const svg of $$("svg")) svg.classList.toggle("has-lit", !!svg.querySelector(".is-lit"));
  };
  for (const el of linked) {
    el.addEventListener("pointerenter", () => { hovered = el; paint(); });
    el.addEventListener("pointerleave", () => { hovered = null; paint(); });
    el.addEventListener("focus", () => { focused = el; paint(); });
    el.addEventListener("blur", () => { focused = null; paint(); });
  }

  if (!still) {
    /* ── kit: flow dots; the ratio of spawn intervals is the real split ── */
    for (const svg of $$("svg:has([data-flow])")) {
      const layer = $(".ve-dots", svg);
      const routes = $$("[data-flow]", svg).map((p) => ({ p, len: p.getTotalLength(), every: +p.dataset.every, next: 0 }));
      let dots = [], visible = false, running = false;
      const tick = (t) => {
        if (!visible) { running = false; for (const d of dots) d.c.remove(); dots = []; return; }
        for (const r of routes) if (t >= r.next) {
          r.next = t + r.every;
          const c = document.createElementNS(svg.namespaceURI, "circle");
          c.setAttribute("r", 4); c.setAttribute("class", r.p.dataset.flow); layer.append(c);
          dots.push({ c, r, t0: t });
        }
        dots = dots.filter((d) => {
          const s = (t - d.t0) * 0.3;
          if (s > d.r.len) { d.c.remove(); return false; }
          const pt = d.r.p.getPointAtLength(s);
          d.c.setAttribute("cx", pt.x); d.c.setAttribute("cy", pt.y);
          return true;
        });
        requestAnimationFrame(tick);
      };
      new IntersectionObserver(([e]) => { visible = e.isIntersecting; if (!running && visible) { running = true; requestAnimationFrame(tick); } }).observe(svg);
    }
    /* ── kit: entrance; without JS, in print, or under reduced motion everything shows ── */
    document.documentElement.classList.add("js-motion");
    const rise = new IntersectionObserver((entries) => {
      for (const e of entries) if (e.isIntersecting) { rise.unobserve(e.target); e.target.classList.add("in"); }
    }, { rootMargin: "0px 0px -10% 0px" });
    for (const el of $$("main > *")) rise.observe(el);
  }

  /* ── plan ── */
  // a mock keeps its design width and scales down to fit a narrow screen
  for (const host of $$(".mock-host")) {
    const w = parseFloat(host.style.width);
    const fit = () => {
      const room = host.parentElement.clientWidth - 2 * parseFloat(getComputedStyle(host.parentElement).paddingLeft);
      if (room > 0) host.style.zoom = room < w ? (room / w).toFixed(3) : ""; // 0 while its claim is closed
    };
    new ResizeObserver(fit).observe(host.parentElement);
  }

  const asks = $$("fieldset.ask");
  const claims = $$("details.claim");
  const guesses = $$("fieldset.guess");
  if (!claims.length) return;
  const title = ($("h1")?.textContent || document.title).trim().replace(/\s+/g, " ");
  // a revision starts clean, so comments the agent already handled are not sent twice
  const KEY = `ve-plan:${location.pathname}:${document.title}:v${$("main").dataset.v || 1}`;
  const S = { seen: {}, guesses: {}, comments: [] };
```

```text file=~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/plan/render.mjs
const HASH_COMMENTS = new Set(["py", "python", "sh", "bash", "zsh", "shell", "rb", "ruby", "yaml", "yml", "toml", "ini", "dockerfile", "make"]);
const STRING = String.raw`"(?:\\.|[^"\\\n])*"|'(?:\\.|[^'\\\n])*'` + "|`(?:\\\\.|[^`\\\\])*`";

/** Highlighted lines. Tokens never span a returned line, so each line is valid HTML on its own. */
function highlight(code, lang) {
  const l = (lang || "").toLowerCase();
  if (!l || ["text", "plain", "txt", "md", "markdown"].includes(l)) return code.split("\n").map(esc);
  const comment = HASH_COMMENTS.has(l) ? String.raw`#[^\n]*` : l === "sql" ? String.raw`--[^\n]*|\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\/` : String.raw`\/\/[^\n]*|\/\*[\s\S]*?(?:\*\/|$)`;
  const re = new RegExp(`(${comment})|(${STRING})|(\\b\\d[\\d_.]*\\b)|([A-Za-z_$][\\w$]*)`, "g");
  const lines = [""];
  const push = (t, cls) => t.split("\n").forEach((piece, i) => {
    if (i) lines.push("");
    if (piece) lines[lines.length - 1] += cls ? `<span class="tk-${cls}">${esc(piece)}</span>` : esc(piece);

function dedent(text) {
```
