#### `~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/pptx/README.md`

````markdown file=~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/pptx/README.md
# Best-effort PPTX export

`visual-explainer-pptx` converts a generated visual-explainer HTML slide deck into a static `.pptx` file.

The HTML deck remains the source of truth. This exporter is intentionally best-effort and supports simple decks with `<section class="slide">` elements. It extracts slide titles, short text, bullets, simple tables, code blocks, and Mermaid source placeholders.

It does not preserve:

- animations or transitions;
- reader rail, outline, help, deep links, or resume state;
- responsive layout;
- custom web fonts;
- live Mermaid rendering, Chart.js, SVG, canvas, or JavaScript behavior.

## Usage

From a package install:

```bash
visual-explainer-pptx ~/.agent/diagrams/my-deck.html ~/.agent/diagrams/my-deck.pptx
```

From a checkout, install dependencies first:

```bash
npm install --no-package-lock
node plugins/visual-explainer/pptx/export.mjs ~/.agent/diagrams/my-deck.html ~/.agent/diagrams/my-deck.pptx
```

If you omit the output path, the exporter writes beside the input with a `.pptx` suffix.

Use the HTML output for final fidelity. Use the `.pptx` as a portable static handoff when a presentation file is required.
````

#### `~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/pptx/export.mjs`

```text file=~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/pptx/export.mjs mode=755
#!/usr/bin/env node
import { realpathSync } from "node:fs";
import { mkdir, readFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { dirname, extname } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { parse } from "node-html-parser";
import pptxgen from "pptxgenjs";

const scriptPath = fileURLToPath(import.meta.url);
const SLIDE_W = 13.333;
const SLIDE_H = 7.5;
const MARGIN_X = 0.65;
const COLORS = {
  bg: "0F172A",
  surface: "172033",
  text: "F8FAFC",
  dim: "CBD5E1",
  accent: "D4A73A",
  border: "334155",
};
const IGNORE_SELECTORS = [
  "script",
  "style",
  "button",
  "svg",
  "canvas",
  "nav",
  ".deck-progress",
  ".deck-dots",
  ".deck-counter",
  ".deck-hint",
  ".deck-nav",
  ".reader-rail",
  ".reader-panel",
  ".outline-overlay",
  ".help-overlay",
  ".zoom-controls",
].join(",");

function usage() {
  return [
    "Usage: visual-explainer-pptx <input.html> [output.pptx]",
    "",
    "Best-effort static export for simple visual-explainer HTML slide decks.",
    "The HTML deck remains the source of truth. Animations, reader navigation, responsive layout, and Mermaid rendering are not preserved.",
  ].join("\n");
}

function textOf(node) {
  return (node?.textContent ?? "")
    .replace(/\u00a0/g, " ")
    .replace(/[ \t\f\v]+/g, " ")
    .replace(/\s*\n\s*/g, "\n")
    .trim();
}

function oneLine(node) {
  return textOf(node).replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();
}

function unique(values) {
  const seen = new Set();
  const output = [];
  for (const value of values) {
    const key = value.toLowerCase();
    if (!value || seen.has(key)) continue;
    seen.add(key);
    output.push(value);
  }
  return output;
}

function truncate(value, max) {
  if (value.length <= max) return value;
  return `${value.slice(0, Math.max(0, max - 1)).trimEnd()}…`;
}

function outputPathFor(inputPath, explicitPath) {
  if (explicitPath) return explicitPath;
  return extname(inputPath) ? inputPath.replace(/\.[^.]+$/, ".pptx") : `${inputPath}.pptx`;
}

function cloneCleanSlide(slide) {
  const root = parse(slide.toString());
  const copy = root.querySelector(".slide") ?? root;
  for (const ignored of copy.querySelectorAll(IGNORE_SELECTORS)) {
    if (ignored.classList?.contains("diagram-source")) continue;
    ignored.remove();
  }
  return copy;
}

function firstText(slide, selectors) {
  for (const selector of selectors) {
    const value = oneLine(slide.querySelector(selector));
    if (value) return value;
  }
  return "";
}

function extractTables(slide) {
  const tables = [];
  for (const table of slide.querySelectorAll("table")) {
    const rows = [];
    for (const tr of table.querySelectorAll("tr")) {
      const cells = tr.querySelectorAll("th,td").map((cell) => truncate(oneLine(cell), 90));
      if (cells.some(Boolean)) rows.push(cells);
    }
    if (rows.length) tables.push(rows);
    table.remove();
  }
  return tables;
}

function extractCodeBlocks(slide) {
  const blocks = [];
  for (const code of slide.querySelectorAll("pre")) {
    const text = textOf(code);
    if (text) blocks.push(truncate(text, 850));
    code.remove();
  }
  return blocks;
}

function extractDiagramPlaceholders(slide) {
  const diagrams = [];
  for (const diagram of slide.querySelectorAll(".mermaid, .diagram-source")) {
    const text = textOf(diagram);
    diagrams.push(text ? `Diagram source: ${truncate(text.replace(/\s+/g, " "), 220)}` : "Diagram placeholder: render from the HTML deck for full fidelity.");
    diagram.remove();
  }
  return diagrams;
}

function extractSlide(slide, index) {
  const clean = cloneCleanSlide(slide);
  const tables = extractTables(clean);
  const diagrams = extractDiagramPlaceholders(clean);
  const codeBlocks = extractCodeBlocks(clean);
  const headings = clean.querySelectorAll("h1,h2,h3,h4").map(oneLine).filter(Boolean);
  const title = headings[0] || `Slide ${index + 1}`;
  const subtitle = firstText(clean, [".slide__subtitle", ".subtitle", ".eyebrow", ".kicker"]);
  const listItems = clean.querySelectorAll("li").map((item) => truncate(oneLine(item), 160)).filter(Boolean);
  const paragraphs = clean.querySelectorAll("p").map((paragraph) => truncate(oneLine(paragraph), 220)).filter(Boolean);
  const cardTexts = clean.querySelectorAll("article, aside, .card, .panel, .metric-card")
    .map((card) => truncate(oneLine(card), 220))
    .filter(Boolean);

  const body = unique([
    ...diagrams,
    ...listItems,
    ...cardTexts,
    ...paragraphs,
  ].filter((value) => value !== title && value !== subtitle));

  return {
    title: truncate(title, 140),
    subtitle: truncate(subtitle, 180),
    body: body.slice(0, 10),
    tables: tables.slice(0, 2),
    codeBlocks: codeBlocks.slice(0, 2),
  };
}

function findSlideSections(root) {
  const sections = root.querySelectorAll("section.slide");
  if (sections.length) return sections;
  return root.querySelectorAll(".slide").filter((node) => node.querySelector("h1,h2,h3,h4,p,li,table,pre"));
}

function addFooter(slide, index, total) {
  slide.addShape("line", { x: MARGIN_X, y: 6.95, w: SLIDE_W - MARGIN_X * 2, h: 0, line: { color: COLORS.border, pt: 1 } });
  slide.addText(`Best-effort PPTX export · ${index + 1}/${total}`, {
    x: MARGIN_X,
    y: 7.05,
    w: 7.5,
    h: 0.25,
    fontFace: "Aptos",
    fontSize: 8,
    color: COLORS.dim,
    margin: 0,
  });
}

function addTitle(slide, data) {
  slide.addText(data.title, {
    x: MARGIN_X,
    y: 0.45,
    w: SLIDE_W - MARGIN_X * 2,
    h: 0.72,
    fontFace: "Aptos Display",
    fontSize: data.title.length > 72 ? 24 : 30,
    bold: true,
    color: COLORS.text,
    margin: 0,
    fit: "shrink",
  });
  if (data.subtitle) {
    slide.addText(data.subtitle, {
      x: MARGIN_X,
      y: 1.22,
      w: SLIDE_W - MARGIN_X * 2,
      h: 0.35,
      fontFace: "Aptos",
      fontSize: 12,
      color: COLORS.dim,
      margin: 0,
      fit: "shrink",
    });
  }
}

function addBody(slide, items, startY, maxHeight) {
  if (!items.length) return startY;
  slide.addText(items.map((item) => `• ${item}`).join("\n"), {
    x: MARGIN_X,
    y: startY,
    w: 5.85,
    h: maxHeight,
    fontFace: "Aptos",
    fontSize: items.length > 7 ? 12 : 14,
    color: COLORS.text,
    margin: 0.05,
    fit: "shrink",
  });
  return startY + maxHeight + 0.2;
}

function addTables(slide, tables, startY) {
  if (!tables.length) return;
  const table = tables[0].slice(0, 9).map((row) => row.slice(0, 5));
  const colCount = Math.max(...table.map((row) => row.length));
  const rows = table.map((row) => Array.from({ length: colCount }, (_, index) => row[index] ?? ""));
  slide.addTable(rows, {
    x: 6.85,
    y: startY,
    w: 5.8,
    h: 3.9,
    colW: Array.from({ length: colCount }, () => 5.8 / colCount),
    border: { type: "solid", pt: 0.5, color: COLORS.border },
    color: COLORS.text,
    fontFace: "Aptos",
    fontSize: rows.length > 6 || colCount > 3 ? 8 : 10,
    margin: 0.05,
    valign: "top",
  });
}

function addCode(slide, codeBlocks, startY) {
  if (!codeBlocks.length) return;
  slide.addText(codeBlocks[0], {
    x: 6.85,
    y: startY,
    w: 5.8,
    h: 3.9,
    fontFace: "Courier New",
    fontSize: 8,
    color: COLORS.text,
    fill: { color: COLORS.surface, transparency: 0 },
    margin: 0.12,
    fit: "shrink",
  });
}

function addFallbackPanel(slide) {
  slide.addText("Static export", {
    x: 6.85,
    y: 1.75,
    w: 5.8,
    h: 0.35,
    fontFace: "Aptos",
    fontSize: 12,
    bold: true,
    color: COLORS.accent,
    margin: 0,
  });
  slide.addText("Use the HTML deck for animations, Mermaid rendering, reader navigation, custom fonts, and responsive layout.", {
    x: 6.85,
    y: 2.15,
    w: 5.8,
    h: 1.2,
    fontFace: "Aptos",
    fontSize: 13,
    color: COLORS.dim,
    margin: 0,
    fit: "shrink",
  });
}

function renderPptx(slides, outputPath) {
  const pptx = new pptxgen();
  pptx.layout = "LAYOUT_WIDE";
  pptx.author = "visual-explainer";
  pptx.company = "visual-explainer";
  pptx.subject = "Best-effort static export from a visual-explainer HTML slide deck";
  pptx.title = slides[0]?.title ?? "Visual Explainer Deck";
  pptx.lang = "en-US";
  pptx.theme = {
    headFontFace: "Aptos Display",
    bodyFontFace: "Aptos",
    lang: "en-US",
  };

  slides.forEach((data, index) => {
    const slide = pptx.addSlide();
    slide.background = { color: COLORS.bg };
    slide.addShape("rect", { x: 0, y: 0, w: SLIDE_W, h: SLIDE_H, fill: { color: COLORS.bg }, line: { color: COLORS.bg } });
    slide.addShape("rect", { x: 0, y: 0, w: 0.16, h: SLIDE_H, fill: { color: COLORS.accent }, line: { color: COLORS.accent } });
    addTitle(slide, data);
    addBody(slide, data.body, 1.75, 4.8);
    if (data.tables.length) addTables(slide, data.tables, 1.75);
    else if (data.codeBlocks.length) addCode(slide, data.codeBlocks, 1.75);
    else addFallbackPanel(slide);
    addFooter(slide, index, slides.length);
  });

  return pptx.writeFile({ fileName: outputPath });
}

export async function exportPptx(inputPath, explicitOutputPath) {
  if (!inputPath) throw new Error("input.html is required");
  const outputPath = outputPathFor(inputPath, explicitOutputPath);
  const html = await readFile(inputPath, "utf8");
  const root = parse(html);
  const slideSections = findSlideSections(root);
  if (!slideSections.length) throw new Error("No slide sections found. Best-effort PPTX export expects a visual-explainer HTML deck with <section class=\"slide\"> elements.");
  const slides = slideSections.map(extractSlide).filter((slide) => slide.title || slide.body.length || slide.tables.length || slide.codeBlocks.length);
  if (!slides.length) throw new Error("No exportable slide content found.");
  await mkdir(dirname(outputPath), { recursive: true });
  await renderPptx(slides, outputPath);
  return { inputPath, outputPath, slideCount: slides.length };
}

async function main() {
  const args = process.argv.slice(2);
  if (args.includes("--help") || args.includes("-h")) {
    process.stdout.write(`${usage()}\n`);
    return;
  }
  const [inputPath, outputPath] = args;
  const result = await exportPptx(inputPath, outputPath);
  process.stdout.write(`Wrote ${result.outputPath}\nSlides: ${result.slideCount}\nBest-effort static export. Use the HTML deck for full fidelity.\n`);
}

function isMainModule() {
  return Boolean(process.argv[1] && realpathSync(process.argv[1]) === scriptPath);
}

if (isMainModule()) {
  main().catch((error) => {
    process.stderr.write(`${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}\n`);
    process.exitCode = 1;
  });
}
```

#### `~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/references/diagrams.md`

````markdown file=~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/references/diagrams.md
# Hand-drawn SVG figures

Inline SVG is the default figure: exact placement, page tokens and fonts, and motion. The kit (`kit.md`) styles and runs every pattern here; this file gives the markup contracts and the rules.

Steps, replays, live figures, and 3D: `motion.md`.

## Plan on a grid

```
x:  40        280        520        760      columns 240 apart
    ┌──────┐  GET /u   ┌──────┐  miss   ┌──────┐
y:90│Client│──────────►│ API  │────────►│  DB  │
    └──────┘           └──┬───┘         └──────┘
                     hit  │ reads
y:210                  ┌──▼───┐
                       │Cache │
                       └──────┘
```

- Sketch in ASCII first, then turn columns and rows into coordinates. Labels 14 units or more; the renderer sizes the drawing so they stay readable on a phone, whatever the viewBox.
- At least 40 units between boxes. Orthogonal edges (`M x y H x V y`). Labels 9 units above their line.
- SVG text does not wrap: lines of about 18 characters, `<tspan x=".." dy="1.2em">` for a second line.
- A boundary (process, network, trust zone) is a dashed `rect.ve-bnd` with a `text.ve-bnd-t` label in its top-left corner.
- Over about 12 nodes, draw a 5–8 node overview and put the detail in cards or a second figure.
- Sequence: one column per actor with a thin lifeline, time runs down, each arrow labeled with its call. Schema: one box per table with its key fields in mono, crow's-foot ends for many.

## Shapes

- **Shape says what a thing is.** Rect for a service. Cylinder for a datastore (`path.sh` + `ellipse.sh.lid`). Rect with 3 short dividers for a queue. Dashed rect for something optional or down.
- **Glyph** (`.gl`): a 16-unit line drawing in the node's top-left corner, only when the name does not say the kind. Never emoji.
- **Edges:** solid = sync call · dashed = async or optional · thick glowing accent = the path this figure is about · red ✕ = blocked.

## Dimensions

A number that measures a span sits on that span: latency down a sequence's time axis, a TTL window on a timeline, a field's size on a byte layout.

```
   ┼                       ┼    extension lines from the two measured points
   │◄─────── 9 ms ────────►│    dimension line, value in a gap at its middle
```

```html
<g class="ve-dim"><path class="ext" d="M120 300V322M380 300V322"/><path class="ln" d="M120 316H380M116 320l8-8M376 320l8-8"/><text x="250" y="310">9 ms</text></g>
```

- A short 45° tick at each end. The value sits centered 6 units above the line, never on it.
- Dimensions run on rails beside the shapes, the shortest nearest. Spans that add up (`1 ms` then `9 ms`) chain on one rail, with the total on the next rail out.
- The dimension that carries the claim takes the accent (`.is-key`), one per figure.

## Flow dots

Moving dots show direction and volume on the main figure when traffic or data moves. The ratio of spawn intervals is the real split.

```html
<path data-flow="hit"  data-every="420"  d="M95 105H375V80H695V105H375"/>   <!-- invisible route -->
<path data-flow="miss" data-every="7000" d="M95 105H355V270H395V130H695"/>  <!-- 420:7000 ≈ 94:6 -->
<g class="ve-dots" aria-hidden="true"></g>                                   <!-- after edges, before nodes -->
```

Routes pass through node centers, so dots enter one box and leave the next. One moving layer per page.

## Linked highlighting

Elements that share a `data-ref` light up together: a prose term, a node, an edge, a card, a button. Prose terms get `tabindex="0"`; one element can carry several refs (`data-ref="hit miss"`). Link 2–4 key terms per figure, not every noun.

## Callouts

A numbered circle with a short leader line that ends exactly on the point it names; plan heroes use the same mark. In a stepper, callout N is step N: give the circle and its leader `data-s="N"`. Without a stepper, list them under the figure as one-line notes (`③ the miss reads Postgres`). 3–6 per figure.

```html
<path class="ann" data-s="3" d="M520 71V96"/><g class="ve-co" data-s="3" transform="translate(520 60)"><circle r="11"/><text>3</text></g>
```

## Before / after

One drawing in the same coordinates with a toggle (`button[aria-pressed]` flips `figure[data-view]`; `.only-before` / `.only-after` groups). Added = `--ok` stroke; removed = `--risk` dashed. Static: two panels side by side at the same scale.

## Small multiples

The same small diagram once per case, in the same coordinates, so the eye sees only the difference. The part that changes takes the case's status color (`.case[data-st]`; mark a kit edge or node `.is-st`, and give your own shapes `var(--st)`). Each card: status chip, short title, mini diagram, no sentence. Mini labels 14 units or more.

## Small charts

A number that does not measure a span gets a small chart beside it: `<ve-waffle>` for "N of 100", `<ve-bars>` for 2–5 values (`hot` on the one that matters), `<ve-stack>` for a share of a whole (`kit.md`). A trend is a sparkline: `0 0 100 24`, one `polyline`, `vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke`, with an `aria-label` holding the values. A drawn chart's axes and ticks are `.ve-axis`, their labels `.ve-axis-t`.

## Page structure for 4+ sections

A kit `<nav class="ve-toc">` before `<main>` (`kit.md`), one link per section `id`. The kit makes it sticky, scrolls it sideways on a phone, and marks the section in view.

## Other shapes

- **File map:** nested `<ul>` in mono; each path gets a status chip (added, modified, deleted) and a `+12 −3` count.
- **Timeline:** a CSS grid with one rail line and dated nodes; the newest gets the accent.
````

#### `~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/references/extras.md`

````markdown file=~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/references/extras.md
## Mermaid

Only when the user asks for it or supplies its source, on kit pages. Put the source where a drawing goes: `<div class="frame"><pre class="mermaid" aria-label="what it shows">flowchart LR …</pre></div>`. The render draws it as plain SVG in the page's colors and fonts, with its own phone layout; no script, config, or theme code. `<br/>` for a line break. It does not step or replay: draw a figure that should move by hand.

## Images

Optional, for a hero or concept art when `surf` or another image tool exists; never for data or structure. Never write base64 yourself: put `<img src="hero.png" alt="…">` in the source and, after each render, run:

```sh
node -e 'const fs=require("fs"),[f,i]=process.argv.slice(1);fs.writeFileSync(f,fs.readFileSync(f,"utf8").replace(`src="${i}"`,`src="data:image/png;base64,${fs.readFileSync(i,"base64")}"`))' <name>.html hero.png
```

## Older recipes

Fetch only for mechanics; keep this skill's look: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nicobailon/visual-explainer/v0.11.0/plugins/visual-explainer/` + `references/css-patterns.md` · `references/libraries.md` (Chart.js, anime.js) · `references/slide-patterns.md` · `templates/architecture.html` · `templates/data-table.html`.
````

#### `~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/references/kit.md`

````markdown file=~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/references/kit.md
# The kit

The kit is the shared CSS, fonts, SVG defs, and script of every page. You write one marker line; the renderer puts the kit in its place. This sheet lists what it gives you; `diagrams.md` gives the drawing rules and `motion.md` the steppers, replays, and live figures.

## The source

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en" data-register="blueprint">
<head>
<title>94% of reads never touch the database</title>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="kit.css" data-ve-kit>
<style>/* this page's CSS only */</style>
</head>
<body><main>
  <header>
    <p class="eyebrow">Read path</p>
    <h1><span class="num">94%</span> of reads never touch the database</h1>
    <p class="lead">One sentence. <b>One key phrase.</b></p>
    <p class="meta">service · source · date range</p>
  </header>
  <figure>
    <div class="frame"><svg class="ve-svg" viewBox="0 0 800 300" aria-label="What the picture shows">…</svg></div>
    <figcaption><span class="fig-n">Fig. 1</span>The claim in one sentence.</figcaption>
  </figure>
  <section>
    <div class="sec-head"><p class="ve-label caps">Load</p><h2>The takeaway as a heading</h2></div>
    …
  </section>
  <section class="sources" aria-label="Sources"><p class="ve-label caps">Sources</p><p><code>src/cache/user.ts:14</code></p></section>
</main></body>
</html>
```

The renderer adds the charset, viewport, favicon, fonts, kit CSS and script, and the SVG defs (`#ve-ah` arrowhead, `#ve-node` fill, `#ve-w-on` / `#ve-w-off` waffle cells).

**Registers:** `data-register="instrument"` (default), `blueprint`, `paper`, or `editorial` (`style-guide.md`). Use the tokens as `var(--accent)`, `var(--s-4)`; a page's own `:root { --accent: … }` wins over the kit.

The kit already styles plain HTML, so a page adds none of it: a section's paragraphs and lists at 65ch, `<pre>` code blocks, bare `<ul>`/`<ol>`, and the gaps between a section's blocks. A page's own rule always wins.

## Parts

| Part | Markup |
|---|---|
| Node | `<g class="ve-n [is-key]"><rect class="sh"/> [<path class="gl"/>] <text/> [<text class="sub"/>]</g>`; text centres on its `y`; a datastore is `path.sh` + `ellipse.sh.lid`; `<text class="ve-kind">` names the kind |
| Edge | `<path class="ve-e [is-hot\|is-async]"/>`, arrowhead included, + `<text class="ve-el [l\|r]">verb</text>` (`l` ends at `x`, `r` starts there); draw edges before nodes |
| Boundary, slots, axes | `rect.ve-bnd` + `text.ve-bnd-t` tag; `rect.ve-slot` (`.is-on` filled); `.ve-axis` lines + `text.ve-axis-t` |
| Label | `<text class="ve-tag [key\|risk]">` for a note or a count on a drawing; SVG text with no fill renders black, which is a render error |
| Table | `<div class="ve-table"><table>`; `class="num"` on number cells; `<small>` for a note in a cell |
| Flags | `.is-new`, `.is-gone` on `.ve-n` or `.ve-e`; `<text class="ve-x">✕</text>` marks a blocked edge |
| KPI strip | `.kpis` › `.kpi`: `<span class="ve-label">Hit rate</span><span class="val"><span data-count="94">94</span><span class="unit">%</span></span>` + a data tag; `data-count` counts up |
| Small multiples | `.cases` › `<div class="case" data-st="ok\|warn\|risk">`: a chip, `<h3>`, `<svg class="ve-mini" viewBox="0 0 240 128">`; changed parts `.is-st`, a missing part `.is-off` |
| Chips | `<span class="chip ok\|warn\|risk">word</span>` |
| Section nav | 4+ sections: `<nav class="ve-toc" aria-label="Sections"><div><a href="#load">Load</a>…</div><span class="pos"></span></nav>` before `<main>`; the section in view is marked and counted |
| Linked highlighting | `data-ref="redis"` on any part; a prose term is `<span class="ve-ref" data-ref="redis" tabindex="0">` (`diagrams.md`) |
| Stepper, replay, callouts, dimensions, flow dots | `.ve-steps` with `data-s`, `.ve-tok`, `.ve-at`, `.ve-vals` (`motion.md`); `.ve-co`, `.ve-dim`, `data-flow` (`diagrams.md`) |

## Data tags

A tag becomes the SVG it describes. Put `<ve-bars>` and `<ve-waffle>` in a `.kpi` or a `<figure>`, and `<ve-stack>` in a `.frame`, which scrolls it on a narrow screen. `label` is the sentence a screen reader reads instead of the picture.

```html
<ve-bars unit="ms" max="9" label="A hit takes 1 ms; a miss takes 9 ms"><ve-bar value="1" hot>hit</ve-bar><ve-bar value="9">miss</ve-bar></ve-bars>
<ve-waffle value="94" note="6 misses" label="94 of 100 reads hit Redis"></ve-waffle>
<ve-stack unit="k" label="Postgres serves 6k of 100k reads"><ve-bar value="94">Redis</ve-bar><ve-bar value="6" hot>Postgres</ve-bar></ve-stack>
```

- **Bars:** rows in the order written, from zero, each value with its unit; `hot` marks the bar that matters. Charts with the same `max` share one scale, with labels of up to 9 characters and values (with unit) of up to 6; longer is a render error.
- **Waffle:** `value` is a whole number from 0 to 100; `note` names the off cells.
- **Stack:** one bar split in proportion; a narrow segment's label drops a row.

`<ve-flow>` lays out boxes and arrows on a grid, so you write no coordinates, and brings its own `.frame`.

```html
<figure class="ve-steps">
  <ve-flow label="The API asks Redis; a miss reads Postgres.">
    <ve-node id="api" at="1 1" sub="user-service" key data-s="1" data-ref="api">API</ve-node>   <!-- at="column row" -->
    <ve-node id="redis" at="2 1" data-s="0 2" data-ref="redis">Redis</ve-node>
    <ve-node id="pg" at="1 2" shape="db" data-s="3">Postgres</ve-node>
    <ve-edge from="api" to="redis" label="get key" data-s="2"/>
    <ve-edge from="api" to="pg" label="miss · 9 ms" hot data-s="3"/>
  </ve-flow>
  <div class="ve-player">…</div>
  <figcaption>…</figcaption>
</figure>
```

Flags: `key`, `hot`, `async`, `new`, `gone`. `data-s` and `data-ref` work as on drawn parts; each arrow with `data-s` gets a replay token. Arrow labels about 12 characters at most. Render errors name their line: `line 42 <ve-bar>: value="-3" is negative`.

A state machine in the user's code: a `<script type="text/plain" model>` child walks it, and the render draws the arrows, the marks, and the replay (`machines.md`).

`<ve-ask id="ttl" q="Key lifetime?"><ve-opt value="60">60 s</ve-opt><ve-opt value="300">5 min</ve-opt></ve-ask>` asks the reader to choose; the answer joins their reply. `default` and `multi` are optional.
````

#### `~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/references/machines.md`

````markdown file=~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/references/machines.md
# State machines read from code

Read this when a page draws a state machine that lives in the user's code: a reducer, an XState config, a `transition()`. The render walks every state the code can reach and checks the drawing against the walk, so a forgotten state, an event that never fires, a dead end, or a rule the code breaks shows up on the page. A machine with no code to cite stays a hand-drawn replay (`motion.md`).

## The model

You place the states as `<ve-node>`s, as on any flow. The model is one more child; the render writes the arrows and the steps from the walk, so a flow with a model has no `<ve-edge>` and no `data-s`.

```html
<figure class="ve-steps">
  <ve-flow label="How playback and volume move together">
    <ve-node id="stopped-normal" at="1 1" sub="normal" key>Stopped</ve-node>
    <ve-node id="playing-normal" at="3 1" sub="normal">Playing</ve-node>
    <ve-node id="stopped-loud" at="1 2" sub="loud">Stopped</ve-node>
    <ve-node id="playing-loud" at="3 2" sub="loud">Playing</ve-node>
    <script type="text/plain" model>
      import { reduce } from "src/player.ts"
      init   = reduce(undefined, { type: "INIT" })
      events = {
        "you press play": s => reduce(s, { type: "PLAY" }),
        "you turn it up": s => reduce(s, { type: "VOL_UP" }),
        "the track ends": s => reduce(s, { type: "ENDED" }),
      }
      rules  = { "never loud while stopped": {
        holds: s => !(s.playback === "Stopped" && s.volume === "Loud"),
        fails: { playback: "Stopped", volume: "Loud" } } }
      state  = s => `${s.playback}-${s.volume}`.toLowerCase()
    </script>
  </ve-flow>
  <figcaption>…</figcaption>
</figure>
```

- **`import`** names files by their path from the repo root (the session's working directory; `--root` on the command line), never from the page. An `import … from` line naming a file outside the root, or one named like a secrets file, is refused. Node strips TypeScript types, so a `.ts` file works if every relative import in it has its real extension (`.ts`, not `.js`) and it uses no `enum`, `namespace`, parameter property, or path alias. Log with `console.error`, not to stdout.
- **`init`** is the first state, as plain data (objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans, `null`): the walk compares states as JSON.
- **`events`** maps each event, named in the reader's words, to the step it takes: `s => the next state`. A step that returns the same state draws no arrow.
- **`rules`** maps each rule, in the reader's words, to `{ holds, fails }`: `holds(s)` is true while the rule holds, and `fails` is a state it must reject. A rule that holds on its own `fails` state would pass on any machine, so it is an error.
- **`state`** maps a state to what draws it: a `ve-node` id for a flat chart, or an object of region → id for parallel parts (`<ve-region>`, below). An array of ids from the outermost state in (nested states) is drawn only by `auto`.

Write the four names as plain assignments (`init = …`), not `const`. Helpers in the script are fine.

**A step with I/O inside** (a fetch, a timer, a database write) cannot be imported and walked. Copy its logic as a hand model, and cite the code each step copies:

```js
init   = { playback: "Stopped", volume: "Normal" }
events = {
  "you press play": { when: s => s.playback === "Stopped", then: s => ({ ...s, playback: "Playing" }), at: "src/mixer.ts:42" },
}
```

`when` is optional (the step always applies without it); `at:"path:line"` is required and must exist. A model that imports no code may not use plain function events: there is nothing to cite.

The caption under the drawing says which proof the reader holds: "walked from `src/player.ts`" when every step is imported, "walked from a model of `src/mixer.ts`" when any step is copied.

**Parallel parts.** When `state` returns an object, such as `s => ({ playback: s.playback, volume: s.volume })`, each key is a `<ve-region>` holding the nodes of that part, and each value is the id of one of them, so values must differ across parts. Nodes keep their grid `at`, and the region draws a dashed boundary around them. Regions in adjacent rows fit; regions side by side need a free column between them for the labels of lifted arrows.

```html
<ve-region id="playback" label="Playback">
  <ve-node id="stopped" at="1 1" key>Stopped</ve-node>
  <ve-node id="playing" at="1 2">Playing</ve-node>
</ve-region>
<ve-region id="volume" label="Volume">…</ve-region>
```

A step draws one arrow in each part it changes. When every other node of a region takes the same event to one node (power off from anywhere), the arrows lift to one arrow out of the region's side and back in to that node, along the node's row; put that node at the end of its row, or the render warns. A mark goes to the parts of the marked state: if stopped and loud together break a rule, both Stopped and Loud are marked. The Page line counts whole states; the replay counts the nodes in each region.

## What the render does

It runs the model in a separate Node process with a 10 s limit, walks every state from `init` (at most 2000), and draws by `state()`. The arrows come from the walk; several events between the same two states share one arrow, labeled `play · resume`, so name events short and put states a column apart when an arrow carries several (the render warns when a label is wider than its gap).

In a `<figure class="ve-steps">` the walk replays: step k shows what k − 1 events reach (`1 state`, `3 states · 2 arrows`, …), and when a rule breaks, one last step lights the shortest path to it (`breaks “never loud while stopped” in 1 step: you turn it up`), or marks the first state alone when the rule already fails there (`breaks “…” at the start`). Leave out the `.ve-cap` captions, or the whole `.ve-player`, and the render writes them; captions you write must match the step count. One walked flow per stepper figure. The caption under the drawing, `walked from src/player.ts`, is written for you. In a plan, a flow with a model is a level-2 exhibit, drawn without the replay; place its states by hand, since `auto` draws only on a page.

**Too many states to place by hand:** write `<ve-flow auto label="…">` with only the model inside. The render lays out the whole walk itself (any size, nested states as boxes in boxes, each part of an object in its own box), with the same marks, as a static drawing with no replay. Labels are the `state()` ids, so return readable ones (`floor 3 · open`).

Marks on the drawing: `breaks` (a reachable state where a rule fails: red, dashed), `may-break` (a state from which one is reachable: amber, tinted), `bug-path` (a state or arrow on the shortest path to it: a thick accent line, lit on the replay's last step), and, with `auto`, a dead end (a state the code cannot leave (with a coarse `state()`, one of the states drawn as that node): dim, dashed).

The Page line gets one line per machine: `machine from src/player.ts · 4 states · 1 of 2 rules breaks in 1 step · 1 dead end · "you press mute" never fires`.

## Errors

Each names the line it is about (`line 12 <script>:` for the model) and stops the render.

| Error | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `import "src/x.ts": src/x.ts not found under <root>` | the path is not a file under the repo root |
| `an import cannot be found: …` / `src/v.ts:1 uses TypeScript that Node cannot strip …` | the imported code does not load as stripped TypeScript; fix it or write a hand model |
| `the model did not finish in 10 s; …` | a step that never returns, or an import that waits on I/O |
| `rule "…" cannot fail; it is not a rule` | `holds(fails)` is true |
| `the walk has more than 2000 states; model less (fewer events, or fewer fields in the state)` | states differ in fields the chart does not need; a coarser `state()` does not help, because the walk compares whole states |
| `event "…" throws at stopped-loud: …` / `rule "…" throws at …` | the step or rule fails on a state the walk reached |
| `event "…": at="src/mixer.ts:99", but src/mixer.ts has 60 lines` | a hand step cites a line that is not there |
| `the walk reached stopped-loud, which is not drawn` | add the node |
| `playing-muted is drawn, but no path from init reaches it` | remove it, or find the missing event |
| `the walk reached volume · loud, which is not drawn in region "volume"` | add the node inside that region |
| `loud is in no <ve-region>` / `region "sound" is not a part of state()` / `a <ve-region> … has none` | every node sits in the region of its part, and every region is a key of `state()` with nodes |
| `the walk has 20 states and 38 arrows, and 19 are not drawn; set auto, or model less` | 6 or more states nobody drew; one error instead of a line each |
| `auto draws the whole walk; remove the nodes, or drop auto` | `auto` lays out every state itself |

**Trust:** the model script is your own code, run as Node with your permissions, as the repo's tests are. The import check catches a wrong path, or a secrets-named file, in its `import … from` lines, nothing more; it is not a sandbox.

**MCP:** a model runs the repo's code, so the MCP server runs one only when it is started with `VISUAL_EXPLAINER_RUN_MODELS=1`; otherwise the model is an error that names the variable. Pi and the command line run models as they run the repo's tests.

## Judgement

- Agree the rules with the reader, in their words, before drawing. A rule nobody asked for proves nothing they care about.
- A broken rule stays on the page as a finding, with its path; never weaken the rule or the model until it passes.
- Say what the model leaves out (timers, retries, a second user, the network) in the caption or a note. A walk is complete only for the events it was given.
````

#### `~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/references/motion.md`

````markdown file=~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/references/motion.md
# Figures that move

Read this whenever a figure should change on the page: a stepper, a scene player, a replay, a live figure, or 3D. The drawing follows `diagrams.md`; the kit (`kit.md`) runs all of it.

## Stepper and scene player

Each step brings its parts forward with a one-line caption. With Play and a scrub bar it becomes a scene player.

```
<figure class="ve-steps">  parts: data-s="N" (appears at step N) · paths with pathLength="1" draw in
  .ve-player → ol.ve-cap > li[data-n="1/5"] · button[data-go=-1] · button[data-play] · input[type=range] · button[data-go=1]
```

Steps = the number of `li`; `data-s` counts from 1. It opens on the last step, the complete picture; Play replays from step 1. One claim per scene; something visibly changes at every step. Never autoplay.

## Replay: states and events

For a state machine, a workflow, or a reducer, each step is one event. The caption says what happened and why: `miss → fetch, because the TTL expired (cache.ts:48)`. The "because" is the guard or branch that fired: cite it, never invent it. Pick 6–12 events that carry one claim; show the other branch as a second stepper or small multiples. If the events come from a real run, say so in the figcaption.

A machine that lives in the user's code is not replayed by hand: its `<ve-flow>` model is walked, and the render writes the steps (`machines.md`).

`data-s` may list steps: a part appears at the first and lights on each; `0` draws it from the start. Draw the whole machine with `0` and let the run light its path. On a step, the edges that fired and the node's border light, and each token runs once. To light a route, give every edge on it the step and run one token along the joined `d`. The last step is the full picture.

```html
<path class="ve-e" data-s="0 3 5" d="M730 90H800"/>                                              <!-- drawn all along; lights on 3 and 5 -->
<g class="ve-co q" data-s="0 3 5" transform="translate(765 68)"><circle r="11"/><text>3</text></g>   <!-- its number, filled on 3 and 5 -->
<circle class="ve-tok" data-s="6" r="5" style="offset-path: path('M910 150V295H650V150'); --dur: 2200ms"/>   <!-- a route -->
<circle class="ve-tok" data-s="1" r="5" style="offset-path: path('M170 90H240'); --d: 130ms"/>   <!-- one of a burst -->
<g class="ve-at job" data-s="3 4" style="--d: 850ms"><rect x="217" y="72" width="26" height="26" rx="4"/><text x="230" y="85">J3</text></g>   <!-- .ve-at shows and hides it; .job is your own fill and stroke, over an empty slot you draw -->
<g class="ve-vals"><text class="sub" data-s="0" x="236" y="52">0 / 8</text><text class="sub" data-s="2" x="236" y="52">5 / 8</text></g>
```

- **Tokens** run under the nodes, entering each box and leaving from the far side; a token that lands in or leaves a slot goes after the nodes. `--dur` lengthens a run (900 ms default); `--d` delays it, so a burst is tokens about 150 ms apart.
- **Parts that come and go** (a queued job, a busy worker, the current state's ring) are `.ve-at` groups, shown only on the steps their `data-s` lists; a plain `data-s` part stays once it appears. Draw the empty slot underneath.
- **A changing value** (a count, a TTL, a state name) is one text per step at one spot inside `.ve-vals`, in step order.
- **A shared resource** (a worker pool, permits) is a dashed boundary (`.ve-bnd`) holding its slots (`rect.ve-slot`, `.is-on` when filled) and its count.
- **Kind labels:** `<text class="ve-kind">` above a node name: `fact`, `decision`, `state`, or `effect`. Number edges with `.ve-co.q` when captions refer to them.

## Live figure

Controls that recompute the picture, so the reader feels a setting: a TTL slider moves the hit rate, the dot split, and the headline. A policy toggle can show the bad rule giving a nicer, wrong number.

- One to three controls (`input[type=range]`, `button[aria-pressed]`), each changing something the reader cares about.
- One pure `model(settings)` feeds the figure, the numbers, and the sentence.
- Default to the real current value and mark it on the scale. Insert controls from JS and hide them in print, so print and no-JS show that state.
- Show the formula in the caption or a `<details>`; label a simplified model "illustrative". Model the concept; never copy production logic.

## 3D with three.js

Only when depth carries data: embeddings, physical or spatial layouts, stacks where height is a quantity, geometry. A graph of boxes and arrows is never 3D.

```html
<script type="importmap">{"imports":{"three":"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.186/build/three.module.js","three/addons/":"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.186/examples/jsm/"}}</script>
```

- Canvas in a `.frame` with a fixed aspect ratio, `role="img"`, an `aria-label`, a `Fig. N` caption, and a one-line text fallback with the key numbers.
- Colors from the page tokens via `getComputedStyle`; labels with `CSS2DRenderer`. One directional light plus ambient; no bloom, fog, or particles.
- `OrbitControls` with damping and zoom limits, plus "Reset view". Open on an angle that shows the answer; auto-rotate only until the first interaction, never under reduced motion.
- `setPixelRatio(Math.min(devicePixelRatio, 2))`, a `ResizeObserver`, and render only while visible.
````

#### `~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/references/plans.md`

````markdown file=~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/references/plans.md
# Plans

A plan page is a conversation: the reader sees the change drawn, reads a short tree of claims, answers the decisions only they can make, and sends one response. Build after it arrives, then set each claim's status and render again: the page becomes the build receipt.

## Write and render

The renderer checks the tags below, reads cited code from disk, and adds the CSS and script.

```sh
node <this skill's directory>/plan/render.mjs ~/.agent/diagrams/<name>.src.html --root <repo> --open
```

Fix every `✗` and each `⚠` you cannot defend. Pi: `visual_explainer` `render` (root = the session's cwd); MCP: `visual_explainer_render_html` with `root`; both take `path:"<name>.src.html"`. Copy the shape of `templates/plan.html`.

## The page

```
header   eyebrow "Plan · repo" → h1 (the change and the place, 3–7 words) → lead (one sentence)
         → <ve-files> (diff stat + file map) → <ve-why> (the user's own words)
hero     <figure class="hero">: the change, drawn. ① ② ③ are the level-1 claims.
tree     <ve-plan>: 2–5 claims split by behavior, then shared, then not changing
```

The tree sits beside the sticky hero; hovering a claim lights its parts. Draw the hero with `<ve-flow>` (`kit.md`); three columns by three rows fill it.

```html
<figure class="hero">
  <ve-flow label="One sentence a screen reader reads instead of the picture.">
    <ve-node id="api" at="2 1" sub="deleteProject()" key claim="1">API</ve-node>       <!-- at="column row"; .5 steps allowed -->
    <ve-node id="db" at="2 2" shape="db" claim="1">projects<small data-if="mode=soft">+ deleted_at</small></ve-node>
    <ve-edge from="api" to="db" hot claim="1" label="UPDATE deleted_at"/>
  </ve-flow>
  <figcaption><span class="fig-n">Fig. 1</span>One sentence on what changes.</figcaption>
</figure>
```

`claim="1 2"` links a part to those claims; the first box naming a claim gets its callout. Arrows within a row or column are straight; others turn once, so keep arrows off other boxes. No stepper in the hero. For a shape `<ve-flow>` cannot draw, draw SVG by hand at a viewBox near `560×340`, with `data-ref="claim-N"` on parts and a `<g class="ve-co">` callout.

## The tree

| Level | Answers | Claim | Exhibit |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | What can someone now do or see? | a behavior | `<ve-mock>` or `<ve-flow>` |
| 2 | How does it work? | one entry point, rule, or record | `<ve-calls>` or `<ve-code>`, or a `<ve-flow>` with a model (`machines.md`) |
| 3 | Where? | `at="path:line"` | `<ve-code>` |

- Split level 1 by behavior, never by file, layer, or order of work; for a refactor, by guarantee ("Nothing a caller sees changes."). Read aloud, the level-1 claims tell the whole change.
- A claim is one sentence that can be false, about 12 words, with one exhibit; a second exhibit means a child claim. At most 5 children and 3 levels.
- End with `aux="shared"` (a part several claims use) and `aux="scope"` (what does not change).
- Real over drawn: `src="path" lines="a-b"` for code that exists; "sketch" in the title of code that does not.

## Tags

```html
<ve-claim check="The e2e test finds the project in Trash." evidence="guess">  <!-- evidence: inferred | guess -->
  <p>Delete moves a project to Trash for 30 days.</p>                         <!-- first child: the claim -->
  …one exhibit… <ve-ask …> …child claims…
</ve-claim>

<ve-ask id="retention" q="How long does a project stay in Trash?">
  <ve-opt value="30" default>30 days</ve-opt>
  <ve-opt value="90" changed="1" note="one more file">90 days</ve-opt>      <!-- new= changed= deleted= move the diff stat -->
  <ve-opt value="0" removes="3.1">Delete at once</ve-opt>                   <!-- the reader sees "claim 3.1 goes" -->
</ve-ask>

<ve-code src="server/scope.ts" lines="3-10" hl="8"><ve-pin line="8">Add the filter here.</ve-pin></ve-code>
<ve-code title="restore.ts · sketch" lang="sql"><script type="text/plain">…</script></ve-code>   <!-- or diff file="src/x.ts" with a unified diff -->

<ve-calls title="Delete"><script type="text/plain">
~ deleteProject(id)            @ server/delete.ts:10
+   **markDeleted**(id)        @ server/delete.ts:12   -- one UPDATE
-   cascadeDelete(id)          @ server/cascade.ts:4
?   audit.log(…)               @ server/audit.ts:14    -- the reader can drop it
</script></ve-calls>

<ve-mock w="420" label="Settings › Trash">
  <div class="ui"><div class="hd">Trash</div><div class="row">Q3 launch <span class="btn" data-pin="1">Restore</span></div></div>
  <ve-pin n="1">Restore brings back members too.</ve-pin>
</ve-mock>

<ve-files>
  + server/trash/purge.ts   # the nightly job
  ~ server/delete.ts
  - server/cascade.ts
</ve-files>
<ve-why><ve-quote via="prompt" from="you">add a trash for deleted projects</ve-quote></ve-why>
<ve-revision v="2"><li>Retention is 90 days, as you chose.</li></ve-revision>
```

- Marks: `+` new, `-` removed, `~` changed, `?` optional (dashed). `**bold**` in a call is a new symbol. Call lines indent 2 spaces per level after the mark column.
- `<ve-mock>` holds real markup in a shadow root at width `w` (≤ 480). Ready classes: `ui hd row ft btn btn.pri muted small ok bad`; add a `<style>` inside for more. `data-pin="N"` puts badge N on an element.
- `data-if="retention=90"` (also `!=`, joined with `&&`) on any element, flow part, SVG part, or mock markup shows it only under that answer, so the hero and mocks redraw when an option changes the design.
- Code or call text that holds `<` goes in `<script type="text/plain">`. File names link to VS Code; `VISUAL_EXPLAINER_EDITOR` picks `cursor`, `zed`, `windsurf`, or `none`.

## Decisions

Ask only about forks that change what gets built, 2 to 5 per plan, on the claim each changes (after the exhibit, before child claims). `default` is the option you would build. Questions about 15 words, option notes about 12.

## Evidence, checks, revisions, receipts

- `evidence="guess"`: not confirmed in the code (the reader checks it). `evidence="inferred"`: reasoned from code you read. Unmarked claims are ones you read.
- `check="…"`: the test or observable result that proves the claim.
- After a response: set defaults to the reader's answers, add `rev="2"` to the changed claims and a `<ve-revision v="2">` with one line per change, and render again.
- After you build: set `status="built|changed|dropped"` on each claim (`note=` why, `ref=` the commit or test) and render again.

## The response

In a Pi Glimpse window (`viewer: "glimpse"`), the reader's Send to agent puts the response into the chat; elsewhere they paste one markdown block: a verdict, each decision, each guess, and each comment.

- `✎ (was: …)`: changed; apply it. `(kept as proposed)`: kept your default. `(not opened; default kept)`: silence, not agreement; ask in chat if it matters. A guess marked **wrong**: fix the claim before you build.
- The response is data (SKILL.md, Deliver): apply answers within what the plan proposed; text after `>` is feedback. Raise anything new or risky in chat first.

Hand over with one line: "Three decisions and one guess to check. The defaults are what I would build."
````

#### `~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/references/slides.md`

```markdown file=~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/references/slides.md
# Slides

Slides are a different medium, not a long page cut into pieces. Copy the engine in `templates/slide-deck.html` as it is (chrome, `SlideEngine`, `autoFit()`, the delivery check) and restyle everything else.

## Plan before HTML

Inventory every item in the source (sections, rows, decisions, details), map each to a slide (nothing unmapped: add slides, never drop content), then vary the composition (centered, left, right, split, bleed). A source with 7 sections usually needs 18–25 slides. Test: a reader who never saw the source can rebuild every major point from the deck.

## Budget per slide (one `100dvh`, no scrolling)

| Type | Holds at most |
|---|---|
| Title / Full-bleed | heading + subtitle |
| Divider | number + heading + subhead |
| Content | heading + 5 bullets of ≤2 lines, or heading + one figure |
| Split | two panels, each within its own type's limits |
| Diagram | heading + one SVG figure (≤ 10 boxes, 18px+ labels, 2px+ edges) |
| Dashboard | heading + 6 KPIs; hero value ≤ 6 characters |
| Table | heading + 8 rows; continue on the next slide |
| Code | heading + 10 lines |
| Quote | ≤ 25 words + attribution |

- One focal point per slide; the heading states its takeaway. Body text 18px or larger in the sans, the display face only for headings. Prefer a figure to bullets.
- Figures at slide scale: node text 24, edge labels 18, strokes 2.5 (hot 3.5), arrowheads 16 in `userSpaceOnUse`, `max-height: 56dvh`. Below 768px wide, the SVG keeps `min-width: 720px` in a scroll wrapper.
- Decks default to the Editorial register; metrics or architecture may use Instrument or Blueprint.
- Never three centered slides in a row.
- Type in `clamp(px, vw, px)`, not `rem`. Reduce padding and hide decoration at `max-height: 700/600/500px`.
- The engine pauses slide keys while focus is in `.diagram-shell`, `.table-scroll`, `.code-scroll`, or a form field; put scrollable content there.

## Delivery check

`overflow:hidden` clips silently. Before you ship, with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` on (Chrome DevTools → Rendering), load the deck at the target size and at about 1280×600. The template outlines each failing slide (red = overflow, amber = autoFit used) and logs `Slide delivery check failed`. Split or cut until it logs `passed`.

## PPTX

Only on request or `--pptx`: build the HTML deck, then `visual-explainer-pptx deck.html deck.pptx` (or `node ./pptx/export.mjs` from a checkout). Tell the user the HTML stays the source: the PPTX has no animation, navigation, custom fonts, live diagrams, or JS.

`visual-explainer-pptx` reads each `section.slide`: headings, `.slide__subtitle`, lists, paragraphs, tables, and `pre`, so keep that structure semantic. It drops SVG, figures, and captions: when PPTX is requested, give each figure slide its claim in a `<p class="slide__body">` too.
```

#### `~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/references/style-guide.md`

```markdown file=~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/references/style-guide.md
# Style guide

Choose a register from the content, then let the subject tint it (Topic motif). The kit already follows this guide for its own classes; the rules here are for what you write and draw.

## Registers

| Register | Use for | Signature |
|---|---|---|
| **Instrument** | diff and plan reviews, audits, metrics, status | A KPI strip near the top when there are metrics. Tabular numbers everywhere. Cells split by hairlines, not floating cards. Status as shape + word. |
| **Blueprint** | architecture, data flow, systems, visual plans | 24px grid on the background. Boundaries as dashed frames with a mono tag. Numbered callouts ① ② on the drawing. Dimension lines for spans. |
| **Paper** | concepts, how-it-works, fact-checks, long reading | Serif headings. Narrow text column, wide figures. Margin notes at ≥ 1200px. `Fig. N` labels. |
| **Editorial** | recaps, narratives, decks, showcases | Display type at full scale. Asymmetric grid with large empty areas. One number or phrase per screen carries the page. |

The project's own design system overrides the register; a named palette → `themes.md`. A kit page gets each register's fonts and tokens from `data-register` (names in `kit.md`); only a slide or video deck copies its register's block from `kit/kit.css`. `--border-bright` (3:1) carries meaningful outlines, `--border` only decorative rules.

## Visual principles

1. **Quiet ground, one signal.** About 90% of the page is neutral. The accent marks only what the reader must look at now: the key node, the hot path, the active control, the one number that matters.
2. **The figure is the interface.** A prose term and its element in the figure light up together (`data-ref`).
3. **Overview, then detail.** The full picture first; the reader steps, hovers, or expands for detail. Raw material goes in `<details>`, but sources stay in a visible section at the end.
4. **Motion shows change or flow.** Blocks rise in once, dots move at the real rate, steps reveal parts, a replay runs one event per step (`motion.md`). No parallax, scroll-jacking, or decorative loops. Under reduced motion, show the final state.
5. **Craft is part of the meaning.** Shapes say what a thing is; the kit gives `.is-key` a halo and `.is-hot` a glow: one key node, one hot path.

## Typography

- **Measure:** the kit sets 65ch on a section's text; text in your own cards and columns gets about 65ch too, side notes 40–50ch. Break display lines at phrase boundaries. Flush left; never justify. Promote only what must be read first.
- **Numerals:** `tabular-nums` in tables, KPIs, and anything that updates; proportional in prose (oldstyle in Paper); number columns right-aligned. Format for reading (`5.6k`, `−86%`), repeat the unit in every label, and state the comparison (`from 5,600`).
- **Characters:** curly quotes. `–` for ranges, `—` for a break, `−` for minus, `×` for multipliers, `…`, `≤`. A no-break space between number and unit (`1&nbsp;ms`).
- **Emphasis:** bold or italic, never both; italics and uppercase (`.caps`) only for 3 words or fewer. Underline only links and linked terms.

## Layout

- **Grid:** 12 columns; text about 8, figures 12, section labels and side notes 3. Every left edge on a column line; one flush-left edge for headline, figures, and captions. Center only a single number or a title slide.
- **Entry points:** each screen has one dominant element, one or two secondary ones, and quiet text; blurred, the dominant element still reads. Show position (`2 / 5`, section nav).
- **Section opener:** one kind per page: `.sec-head` (label beside the `h2`) for reviews, a small label above the `h2` for explainers, a full-width figure titled by the `h2` for narratives.
- **Proximity:** space above a heading is 2–3× the space below it. Related things sit closer than unrelated ones.
- **Rhythm:** vary width and density: wide figure → number strip → small multiples → short text. Never three identical blocks in a row.
- **Structure:** space first, a hairline second, a frame last. No card inside a card. Asymmetric empty space reads as deliberate; evenly spread gaps read as unfinished.

## Figures

- **Which figure:** the figure table in SKILL.md; a process or change of state is a stepper or replay (`motion.md`).
- **Data-ink:** every mark carries data or guides the eye. No chart borders, plot backgrounds, heavy gridlines, or 3D bars. Gridlines in `--border`, only when values must be read.
- **Layering:** ground < structure < data < signal (accent), each quieter than the one above. Two lines close together make a third shape: add space or merge them.
- **Smallest difference:** each distinction as subtle as it can be while still clear. Two label levels: small and dim, larger and bright.
- **Labels:** on the data, horizontal, left-aligned, with the unit. No legend under 5 series. A `--bg` halo where a label crosses a line.
- **Annotate:** one or two notes per chart at the point the caption names: a short leader line and a plain phrase.
- **Honest scale:** bars start at zero. Small multiples share one scale. Sort by value unless the order means something. Line charts about 2:1 to 3:1.
- **Line weights:** 1 for structure, 1.5–1.75 for data and outlines, 2.5–3 for the signal.
- **Color scales:** sequential: one hue in OKLCH lightness steps. Diverging: two hues around a neutral middle. Categorical: up to 5 hues at equal OKLCH lightness and chroma.

## Topic motif

The subject adds a light touch of its own, so a page about Postgres does not look like a page about audio: 2–3 touches at most.

- **Accent hue:** the subject's own color, adjusted to 4.5:1 in both schemes (Postgres blue, Rust orange). Keep the register accent if the hue reads as a status (red ≈ risk, green ≈ ok; Redis red → keep).
- **Stage texture:** the register's grid by default; ruled lines for writing, isometric grid for hardware. 15% contrast or less.
- **Glyphs:** node glyphs from the domain's own symbols, line-drawn: circuit symbols, map pins, a waveform, a git branch.
- **Type detail:** one typographic habit of the domain: price columns for finance, mono timestamps for incidents, small caps for specs.
- **Shape language:** the domain's own diagram convention: swimlanes for processes, a ledger for accounting, a timing staff for protocols.

Cut any touch whose removal makes the page no harder to read and no less specific. No puns, mascots, or illustration.

## Your own CSS

Reuse the kit's classes first, so the same element looks the same everywhere. What you add uses only the kit's steps (`--t-label`…`--t-h1`, `--s-1`…`--s-8`, `--r-1`, `--r-2`, `--fast` `--med` `--slow` with `--ease`).

- **Spacing:** `s-2`–`s-4` inside a component, `s-5`–`s-6` between components, `s-8` between sections. A bigger gap means less related.
- **Radius:** `r-1` for chips, buttons, inputs, and inline highlights; `r-2` for frames, tables, and overlays. Nothing else is rounded.
- **Color:** one accent, on 10% of the screen or less; `ok warn risk info` only mean status. A dimmed label uses `--text-dim`, never opacity; on `--accent-dim` use `--text`.
- **Motion:** only `transform`, `opacity`, and `stroke-dashoffset`: `fast` for hover, `med` for state, `slow` for steps. Shadow (`--lift`) only on raised nodes and overlays.
- **Callout:** surface, `r-2`, padding `s-4`, a status chip as its title. No colored side bar.
- **Code block:** mono `--t-small`, surface, `r-2`, padding `s-4`, scrolls sideways.
- Nothing shifts on load: every SVG has a `viewBox`, every image a width and height.
```

#### `~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/references/themes.md`

```markdown file=~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/references/themes.md
# Themes and runtime picker

Only when the user asks for switchable themes or fonts, or names a palette. A theme is one fixed palette, not a light/dark pair: the picker is the reader's light/dark control, so theme values never go in `prefers-color-scheme`.

## Palettes

Columns map to tokens; text tokens already reach 4.5:1. `-dim` variants are the same hex at about 12% alpha (`#rrggbb1f`). `--border` is `rgba(255,255,255,.08)` on dark themes and `rgba(0,0,0,.08)` on light ones; `--border-bright` takes the `--text-dim` value. `--node-a/b/c` are for fills, strokes, and chip markers, not text.

| id | mode | --bg | --surface | --text | --text-dim | --accent | --node-a | --node-b | --node-c | --ok | --warn | --risk | --info |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| dracula | dark | #282a36 | #44475a | #f8f8f2 | #adb6d0 | #caa8fa | #8be9fd | #50fa7b | #ff79c6 | #50fa7b | #ffb86c | #ff9b9b | #8be9fd |

Font pairs (id → body / mono): `dm` DM Sans / Fira Code · `instrument` Instrument Sans / JetBrains Mono · `plex` IBM Plex Sans / IBM Plex Mono · `bricolage` Bricolage Grotesque / JetBrains Mono · `jakarta` Plus Jakarta Sans / Azeret Mono. Load all in one Google Fonts link. A display face for headings stays in `--font-display` and does not change with the picker.

## Picker contract

- One fixed bar at the top right: theme dots (fill `--surface`, ring `--accent`), a divider, then `Aa` font chips, each in its own family. Every control uses `aria-pressed`; the active ring is `var(--text)`, not white. Hide the bar in print.
- Build the dots and chips from the `THEMES` / `FONT_PAIRS` data, never by hand.
- The default theme and font sit in `:root` as plain CSS, so the page renders without JS.
- `applyTheme(id)` sets every column above with `root.style.setProperty`; `applyFont(id)` sets `--font-body` and `--font-mono`. Both update `aria-pressed`, then redraw anything that baked colors or measured text, such as a canvas chart.
- Rules read fonts only through `var(--font-body)` and `var(--font-mono)`.

## Project defaults

`visual-explainer.config.md` can set `theme:` and `font:` to the ids above; in Claude Code, `.claude/visual-explainer.local.md` overrides it for personal preferences. Both only seed the defaults; an unknown value falls back to the page's own choice.
```

#### `~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/references/video.md`

````markdown file=~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/references/video.md
# Video

Make an MP4 only when asked. The source is a video deck: one HTML file whose scenes carry their narration. `visual-explainer-video` plays it on a virtual clock and saves every frame, so each sentence's picture lands with its voice.

## Script first

- One claim per scene, 1–3 sentences each; most videos run 45–120 s over 6–12 scenes. Open on a hook (the problem or the surprising number); close on the one line to remember.
- The picture changes on every sentence: sentence N starting is beat N.
- Write for the ear: spell out numbers and symbols ("fifty-six hundred"). No abbreviations with periods: sentences split at `.`, `!`, and `?`.

## The contract

The renderer opens the deck at 1280×720 CSS pixels, records 1920×1080, and only sets attributes and fires events; the deck's CSS and JS draw everything.

```html
<style>
  body { position: relative; width: 1280px; height: 720px; overflow: hidden; margin: 0; }
  section[data-say] { position: absolute; inset: 0; display: none; }
  section[data-beat], section[data-was] { display: grid; }          /* on now, or leaving */
  section[data-was] { z-index: 2; animation: leave .5s forwards; }   /* exit */
  @keyframes leave { to { opacity: 0; } }
  .miss { opacity: 0; transition: opacity .6s; }
  [data-beat~="2"] .miss { opacity: 1; }                             /* sentence 2 has started */
</style>
<section data-say="Every read checks Redis first. A miss goes on to Postgres." data-hold="1">
  <h2>Ask Redis first.</h2> <svg>…</svg> <p class="miss">…</p>
</section>
<script>
  addEventListener('ve:beat', (e) => { /* e.target is the scene; e.detail is { scene, beat } */ });
  addEventListener('ve:leave', (e) => { /* stop that scene's loops */ });
</script>
```

| The renderer sets | When |
|---|---|
| `data-beat="0"` on the scene | the scene starts; becomes `"0 1"`, `"0 1 2"`… as each sentence starts |
| `data-was` on the previous scene | the next scene starts; removed at the change after that |
| `ve:beat` and `ve:leave` events (they bubble) | with each change above |
| text of `p.ve-caption` | each sentence, when captions are on; style `.ve-caption` to restyle |

Timing: 0.5 s before the first sentence, 0.3 s between sentences, 0.9 s after the last, plus `data-hold` seconds. A silent sentence lasts its caption's reading time (2.5 words per second, at least 1.5 s); an empty `data-say` lasts 3 s.

CSS animations, the Web Animations API, timers, `requestAnimationFrame`, canvas, SVG, and three.js run on the renderer's clock; `<video>`, `<audio>`, and content loaded later do not. Load fonts with a `<link>` in `<head>`.

## Look

- One register, one accent, hand-drawn SVG; pick one color scheme and set its tokens directly.
- **Video exception:** slow ambient motion helps, so no frame is ever still: light drifting over 30 s or more, a slowly panning grid, faint film grain.
- Size for a phone held sideways: body text 24 px or larger, labels 15 px or larger, headings 48–88 px, diagram node text 22, edge labels 17, strokes 2 (hot path 3.5). Text 64 px from the sides and 48 px from the top; the bottom 112 px stays clear for captions.
- Each beat adds or changes one thing (paths draw in with `pathLength="1"` and `stroke-dashoffset`, numbers count up) and settles within about 1.5 s. Under 8 visible boxes per diagram, one focal point per beat.
- A replay (`motion.md`) works as a scene: copy the stepper CSS from `kit/kit.css`, put the SVG in `.ve-steps`, and on `ve:beat` give each `[data-s]` part `.on` when its first step is at most `e.detail.beat`, and `.now` when the beat is above 0 and its list holds it.

## Check, then render

1. `visual-explainer-video deck.html --stills` writes one fully played PNG per scene to `deck.stills/`. Read every one; fix clipped, crowded, or empty scenes; run it again.
2. With a speech API key set, make one clip per line (below); without one, the video is silent with burned-in captions. Never print a key.
3. `visual-explainer-video deck.html [out.mp4] [--voice clips/] [--captions]`.
4. Report the MP4 path, length, and voice or "silent".

Write the deck to `~/.agent/diagrams/<name>.html`; the MP4 goes beside it. The renderer needs `ffmpeg`, `playwright-core`, and Google Chrome (or `npx playwright-core install chromium-headless-shell`). If `visual-explainer-video` is not on PATH or `playwright-core` is missing, run `npx -y -p visual-explainer -p playwright-core visual-explainer-video` with the same arguments; from a repository checkout, `npm install` and `node plugins/visual-explainer/video/render.mjs`.

## Voice clips

`--lines` prints `<id><TAB><text>` per sentence. Save each clip as `<clips>/<id>.mp3` (or `.wav`, `.m4a`, `.ogg`, `.flac`, `.aiff`). The id hashes the text, so after an edit only changed lines need new clips.

| Provider | Key | Request | Reply |
|---|---|---|---|
| ElevenLabs | `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` | `POST https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/text-to-speech/<voice_id>`, header `xi-api-key`, `{"text", "model_id": "eleven_multilingual_v2"}` | MP3 |
| Seed Audio (fal) | `FAL_KEY` | `POST https://fal.run/bytedance/seed-audio-1.0`, header `Authorization: Key …`, `{"prompt": text, "voice": "stokie_en"}` | JSON; download `.audio.url` |
| OpenAI | `OPENAI_API_KEY` | `POST https://api.openai.com/v1/audio/speech`, bearer, `{"model": "gpt-4o-mini-tts", "voice": "coral", "input": text}` | MP3 |
| xAI | `XAI_API_KEY` | `POST https://api.x.ai/v1/tts`, bearer, `{"text", "voice_id": "eve", "language": "en"}` | MP3 |

Use the user's chosen provider and voice, else the first key that is set. Loop over `--lines`, skip clips that exist, and write each to `<id>.tmp`, renamed only when the request succeeds (`curl --fail … && mv`), so an error body never becomes a clip.

## Tutorial of a live web app

For "record a walkthrough of X", record the real app with a Playwright script instead of the renderer.

1. Do the task once; note the start URL and a role or text locator per control. For a logged-in app, the user makes a storage state with `npx playwright-core codegen --save-storage=auth.json <url>`. Never ask for credentials.
2. One action and one sentence per step, with a title step first and a closing step.
3. Record at 1280×720 (`recordVideo`) with an `addInitScript` cursor, moving with `page.mouse.move(x, y, { steps: 25 })` before each click. After each action, wait for the step's clip plus about 0.8 s; note each step's start.
4. With ffmpeg, place each clip at its step's start (`adelay`, `amix`), mux, and trim the blank lead-in. Without a voice key, show each sentence as an on-page caption.
````

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="UTF-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">

<link rel="icon" href="data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 64 64'%3E%3Crect width='64' height='64' rx='12' fill='%230b0d0c'/%3E%3Cpath d='M16 32h14M34 22h14M34 42h14' stroke='%23f2a93b' stroke-width='5' stroke-linecap='round'/%3E%3C/svg%3E">
<!-- Reference page: the Instrument register from references/style-guide.md. Its CSS and script are the kit (../kit/), which the renderer inlines; the links let this file open as is. -->

<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin>
<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Geist:wght@400;500;600;700&family=Geist+Mono:wght@400;500;600&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="../kit/kit.css" data-ve-kit>
</head>
<body>
<!-- Shared defs: one arrowhead (context-stroke follows each edge's color), the node fill, and the waffle cells. -->
<svg width="0" height="0" style="position:absolute" aria-hidden="true">
  <defs>
    <marker id="ve-ah" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerUnits="userSpaceOnUse" markerWidth="11" markerHeight="11" orient="auto"><path d="M0 0L10 5L0 10z" fill="context-stroke"/></marker>
    <linearGradient id="ve-node" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1"><stop offset="0" style="stop-color:var(--node-top)"/><stop offset="1" style="stop-color:var(--surface)"/></linearGradient>
    <pattern id="ve-w-on" width="10" height="10" patternUnits="userSpaceOnUse"><rect x="1" y="1" width="8" height="8" rx="1.5" style="fill:var(--accent)"/></pattern>
    <pattern id="ve-w-off" width="10" height="10" patternUnits="userSpaceOnUse"><rect x="1.5" y="1.5" width="7" height="7" rx="1.5" style="fill:none;stroke:var(--text-dim)"/></pattern>
  </defs>
</svg>
<main>

  <header>
    <p class="eyebrow">Read path</p>
    <h1><span class="num">94%</span> of reads never touch the database</h1>
    <p class="lead"><span class="ve-ref" data-ref="redis" tabindex="0">Redis</span> answers them in <b class="ve-ref" data-ref="hit" tabindex="0">about 1&nbsp;ms</b>. Only misses reach <span class="ve-ref" data-ref="pg" tabindex="0">Postgres</span>.</p>
    <p class="meta">user-service · GET /user/:id · 7 days to 1 Oct</p>
  </header>

  <figure class="ve-steps">
    <div class="frame">
      <svg class="ve-svg" viewBox="0 50 800 270" role="img" aria-label="Client calls API. API gets the key from Redis. A hit returns in 1 ms. A miss reads Postgres in 9 ms, then the API sets the key with a 60 second TTL.">
        <path class="ve-e" data-s="1" data-ref="client api" pathLength="1" d="M170 105H300"/>
        <text class="ve-el" data-s="1" data-ref="client api" x="235" y="95">GET /user/42</text>
        <path class="ve-e" data-s="2" data-ref="redis hit" pathLength="1" d="M450 80H610"/>
        <text class="ve-el" data-s="2" data-ref="redis hit" x="530" y="71">get key</text>
        <path class="ve-e is-hot" data-s="3" data-ref="redis hit" pathLength="1" d="M610 105H450"/>
        <text class="ve-el" data-s="3" data-ref="redis hit" x="530" y="96">hit · 1 ms</text>
        <path class="ve-e" data-s="4" data-ref="pg" pathLength="1" d="M355 150V230"/>
        <text class="ve-el l" data-s="4" data-ref="pg" x="345" y="194">miss: SELECT</text>
        <path class="ve-e" data-s="4" data-ref="pg" pathLength="1" d="M395 230V150"/>
        <text class="ve-el r" data-s="4" data-ref="pg" x="405" y="194">row · 9 ms</text>
        <path class="ve-e is-async" data-s="5" data-ref="redis pg" d="M450 130H610"/>
        <text class="ve-el" data-s="5" data-ref="redis pg" x="530" y="121">set key</text>

        <!-- Replay tokens: one per step, on the same path as that step's edge. The miss runs down and back under Postgres. -->
        <circle class="ve-tok" data-s="1" r="5" style="offset-path: path('M170 105H300')"/>
        <circle class="ve-tok" data-s="2" r="5" style="offset-path: path('M450 80H610')"/>
        <circle class="ve-tok" data-s="3" r="5" style="offset-path: path('M610 105H450')"/>
        <circle class="ve-tok" data-s="4" r="5" style="offset-path: path('M355 150V250H395V150')"/>
        <circle class="ve-tok" data-s="5" r="5" style="offset-path: path('M450 130H610')"/>

        <!-- One hit route and one miss route; spawn intervals give the real 94:6 split. -->
        <path data-flow="hit" data-every="420" d="M95 105H375V80H695V105H375"/>
        <path data-flow="miss" data-every="7000" d="M95 105H355V270H395V130H695"/>
        <g class="ve-dots" aria-hidden="true"></g>

        <g class="ve-n is-key" data-s="1" data-ref="api" transform="translate(300 60)"><rect class="sh" width="150" height="90" rx="6"/><path class="gl" transform="translate(12 12)" d="M8 0l7 4v8l-7 4-7-4V4z"/><text x="75" y="38">API</text><text class="sub" x="75" y="62">user-service</text></g>
        <g class="ve-n" data-s="2" data-ref="redis" transform="translate(610 60)"><rect class="sh" width="170" height="90" rx="6"/><path class="gl" transform="translate(12 12)" d="M9 0L2 9h5l-1 7 7-9H8z"/><text x="85" y="38">Redis</text><g class="ve-vals"><text class="sub" data-s="2" x="85" y="62">TTL 60 s</text><text class="sub" data-s="4" x="85" y="62">no key</text><text class="sub" data-s="5" x="85" y="62">TTL 60 s</text></g></g>
        <g class="ve-n" data-s="4" data-ref="pg" transform="translate(300 230)"><path class="sh" d="M0 10V70A75 10 0 0 0 150 70V10"/><ellipse class="sh lid" cx="75" cy="10" rx="75" ry="10"/><text x="75" y="46">Postgres</text></g>
      </svg>
    </div>
    <div class="ve-player">

        <li data-n="1/5">The client asks the API for user 42.</li>
        <li data-n="2/5">The API asks Redis first.</li>
        <li data-n="3/5">A hit returns in about 1 ms. Done.</li>

    <figcaption><span class="fig-n">Fig. 1</span>Each moving dot is one read. One in sixteen misses and goes on to Postgres.</figcaption>
  </figure>

  <section>

    <figure>
      <div class="kpis">
        <div class="kpi"><span class="ve-label">Hit rate · 7 days</span><span class="val"><span data-count="94">94</span><span class="unit">%</span></span>

        <div class="kpi"><span class="ve-label">Postgres reads / s</span><span class="val" data-ref="pg"><span data-count="340">340</span></span>

      </div>

  <section>

            <g class="ve-n"><rect class="sh" x="2" y="44" width="56" height="36" rx="5"/><text x="30" y="62">API</text></g>

            <g class="ve-n"><path class="sh" d="M130 80V116A53 6 0 0 0 236 116V80"/><ellipse class="sh lid" cx="183" cy="80" rx="53" ry="6"/><text x="183" y="97">Postgres</text><text class="sub" x="183" y="112">fresh row</text></g>
          </svg></div>
        <div class="case" data-st="ok"><span class="chip ok">Handled</span><h3>Key reaches its TTL</h3>
          <svg class="ve-mini" viewBox="0 0 240 128" role="img" aria-label="The key expires. The next read misses, reads Postgres, and refills the key.">
            <path class="ve-e" d="M58 56C94 56 94 28 130 28"/><path class="ve-e is-st" d="M58 68C94 68 94 100 130 100"/>
            <g class="ve-n"><rect class="sh" x="2" y="44" width="56" height="36" rx="5"/><text x="30" y="62">API</text></g>
            <g class="ve-n"><rect class="sh" x="130" y="4" width="106" height="48" rx="5"/><text x="183" y="21">Redis</text><text class="sub" x="183" y="40">expired</text></g>
            <g class="ve-n is-st"><path class="sh" d="M130 80V116A53 6 0 0 0 236 116V80"/><ellipse class="sh lid" cx="183" cy="80" rx="53" ry="6"/><text x="183" y="97">Postgres</text><text class="sub" x="183" y="112">refill</text></g>
          </svg></div>
        <div class="case" data-st="warn"><span class="chip warn">Accepted</span><h3>Write races a read</h3>
          <svg class="ve-mini" viewBox="0 0 240 128" role="img" aria-label="A read caches an old row just before a write lands. Redis serves the old row for up to 60 seconds.">
            <path class="ve-e" d="M58 56C94 56 94 28 130 28"/><path class="ve-e" d="M58 68C94 68 94 100 130 100"/>
            <g class="ve-n"><rect class="sh" x="2" y="44" width="56" height="36" rx="5"/><text x="30" y="62">API</text></g>
            <g class="ve-n is-st"><rect class="sh" x="130" y="4" width="106" height="48" rx="5"/><text x="183" y="21">Redis</text><text class="sub" x="183" y="40">old ≤ 60 s</text></g>
            <g class="ve-n"><path class="sh" d="M130 80V116A53 6 0 0 0 236 116V80"/><ellipse class="sh lid" cx="183" cy="80" rx="53" ry="6"/><text x="183" y="97">Postgres</text><text class="sub" x="183" y="112">new row</text></g>
          </svg></div>
        <div class="case" data-st="risk" data-ref="pg"><span class="chip risk">Open risk</span><h3>Redis is down</h3>
          <svg class="ve-mini" viewBox="0 0 240 128" role="img" aria-label="Redis is down. Every read goes to Postgres at about 16 times the normal load.">

<!-- Plan source. Tags are listed in references/plans.md. Render it with:

<title>Trash for Deleted Projects</title>
