```text file=~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/templates/plan.html
<body>

<header>
  <p class="eyebrow">Plan · plot-app</p>
  <h1>Trash for Deleted Projects</h1>
  <p class="lead">Delete stops being final. A project waits in <b>Trash for 30 days</b>, then a nightly job removes it.</p>
  <ve-files>
    + migrations/0042_trash.sql   # deleted_at and an index
    + server/trash/purge.ts       # the nightly job
    + web/trash/TrashView.tsx     # the new view
    ~ server/projects/delete.ts   # UPDATE, not DELETE
    ~ server/projects/scope.ts    # skips trashed rows
    - server/projects/cascade.ts  # no longer used
  </ve-files>
  <ve-why>
    <ve-quote via="prompt" from="you">add a trash for deleted projects. people delete the wrong one and then email support</ve-quote>
    <ve-quote via="support" from="ticket #4182" at="Sep 30">I deleted Q3 launch by mistake. Is there any way to get it back?</ve-quote>
  </ve-why>
</header>

<!-- The hero is the answer as a picture. claim="N" links a box or arrow to claim N; the first box naming a claim gets its numbered callout. -->
<figure class="hero">
  <ve-flow label="Settings sends DELETE to the API. The API now sets deleted_at on the projects row instead of a cascade delete. The new Trash view lists trashed projects and restores them. A new nightly purge job deletes rows older than 30 days and their files.">
    <ve-node id="settings" at="1 1" sub="Delete project">Settings</ve-node>
    <ve-node id="api" at="2 1" sub="deleteProject()" key claim="1">API</ve-node>
    <ve-node id="cascade" at="3 1" sub="removed" gone>Cascade</ve-node>
    <ve-node id="trash" at="1 2" sub="new view" new claim="1 2">Trash</ve-node>
    <ve-node id="projects" at="2 2" sub="+ deleted_at" shape="db" claim="1">projects</ve-node>
    <ve-node id="purge" at="2 3" sub="nightly" new claim="3">Purge job</ve-node>
    <ve-node id="files" at="3 3" claim="3">Files<small data-if="files=purge">purged</small><small data-if="files=keep">kept</small></ve-node>
    <ve-edge from="settings" to="api" label="DELETE"/>
    <ve-edge from="api" to="cascade" gone/>
    <ve-edge from="api" to="projects" hot claim="1" label="UPDATE deleted_at"/>
    <ve-edge from="projects" to="trash" claim="1" label="lists"/>
    <ve-edge from="trash" to="projects" new claim="2" label="restore"/>
    <ve-edge from="purge" to="projects" async new claim="3" label="DELETE &gt; 30 d"/>
    <ve-edge from="purge" to="files" async new claim="3" label="files" data-if="files=purge"/>
  </ve-flow>

  <figcaption><span class="fig-n">Fig. 1</span>Delete becomes an UPDATE. A nightly job does the real delete.</figcaption>
</figure>

<ve-plan>

  <ve-claim check="The e2e test deletes a project and finds it in Trash with 30 days left.">
    <p>Delete moves a project to Trash for 30 days.</p>
    <ve-mock w="420" label="Settings › Trash">
      <div class="ui">
        <div class="hd">Trash <small>2 projects</small></div>
        <div class="row"><span><b>Q3 launch</b><br><span class="muted small">Deleted by Dana · <span data-if="retention=30">29</span><span data-if="retention=7">6</span><span data-if="retention=90">89</span> days left</span></span><span class="btn" data-pin="1">Restore</span></div>
        <div class="row"><span><b>Old roadmap</b><br><span class="muted small">Deleted by you · 3 days left</span></span><span class="btn">Restore</span></div>
      </div>
      <ve-pin n="1">Restore brings back members and tasks too. See claim 2.</ve-pin>
    </ve-mock>
    <ve-ask id="retention" q="How long does a project stay in Trash?">
      <ve-opt value="30" default>30 days</ve-opt>
      <ve-opt value="7">7 days</ve-opt>
      <ve-opt value="90">90 days</ve-opt>
    </ve-ask>

    <ve-claim>
      <p>Delete sets <code>deleted_at</code>. It removes no rows.</p>
      <ve-calls title="Delete">
<script type="text/plain">
~ deleteProject(id, userId)            @ server/projects/delete.ts:10
+   **markDeleted**(id, now)           @ server/projects/delete.ts:12   -- one UPDATE
-   cascadeDelete(id)                  @ server/projects/cascade.ts:4
?   audit.log("project.trashed")       @ server/audit.ts:14             -- strike it if not wanted
</script>
      </ve-calls>
    </ve-claim>

    <ve-claim evidence="guess" check="The scope test passes with a trashed project in the fixture.">

        <ve-pin line="8">Add <code>AND p.deleted_at IS NULL</code> here. I found no read that skips this scope, but I did not open all 14 callers.</ve-pin>

<script type="text/plain">
UPDATE projects SET deleted_at = NULL
WHERE id = $1 AND deleted_at IS NOT NULL
RETURNING id;   -- no row back: already purged, tell the user
</script>

      <ve-opt value="admins" changed="1" note="one more permission check">The owner and workspace admins</ve-opt>
    </ve-ask>
  </ve-claim>

  <ve-claim check="A project trashed 31 days ago is gone after the job runs.">
    <p>A nightly job deletes projects older than 30 days.</p>
    <ve-calls title="Purge">
<script type="text/plain">
+ **purgeTrash**(now)                    @ server/trash/purge.ts:5
+   select ids where deleted_at < now − 30 d
+   cascadeDelete(id)                    @ server/projects/cascade.ts:4   -- reused, not changed
+   files.remove(keys)                   @ server/files/store.ts:12
</script>

      <ve-code src="server/files/store.ts" lines="12-17">
        <ve-pin line="15">Batches of 1,000 keys, the S3 limit for one request.</ve-pin>
      </ve-code>

  <ve-claim aux="shared">

    <ve-code title="migrations/0042_trash.sql · sketch" lang="sql">
<script type="text/plain">
ALTER TABLE projects ADD COLUMN deleted_at timestamptz;
CREATE INDEX projects_trash ON projects (deleted_at) WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL;
</script>

  <ve-claim aux="scope">
```

```text file=~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/templates/slide-deck.html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="UTF-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
<title>API Gateway Redesign — Reference Deck</title>
<link rel="icon" href="data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 64 64'%3E%3Crect width='64' height='64' rx='12' fill='%23111111'/%3E%3Cpath d='M18 44V20h16a8 8 0 0 1 0 16H18' fill='none' stroke='%23ff6e50' stroke-width='5'/%3E%3C/svg%3E">
<!-- Reference deck in the Editorial register. Copy ENGINE, CHROME, and DELIVERY CHECK as they are; restyle the rest. -->
<script>document.documentElement.classList.add('js');</script>
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin>
<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Instrument+Sans:wght@400;500;600&family=Instrument+Serif&family=JetBrains+Mono:wght@500;600&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">
<style>
  :root {
    color-scheme: light dark;
    --font-display: 'Instrument Serif', Georgia, serif; /* headings only; reading text stays sans */
    --font-body: 'Instrument Sans', 'Segoe UI', sans-serif;
    --font-mono: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace;
    --bg: #fbfbf9; --surface: #f1f0ec; --border: #e2e0da; --border-bright: #8c8a85;
    --text: #111111; --text-dim: #5a5853; --accent: #cc3418; --accent-dim: rgba(204,52,24,.12);
    --ok: #1d7443; --risk: #a01d48;
  }
  @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
    :root {
      --bg: #0f0f0f; --surface: #1a1a19; --border: #2b2a28; --border-bright: #696763;
      --text: #f2f0eb; --text-dim: #a4a19b; --accent: #ff6e50; --accent-dim: rgba(255,110,80,.14);
      --ok: #6cc492; --risk: #f57fa2;
    }
  }
  * { margin: 0; padding: 0; box-sizing: border-box; }
  body { font-family: var(--font-body); color: var(--text); background: var(--bg); overflow: hidden; -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased; }
  ::selection { background: var(--accent-dim); }

  /* ===== ENGINE ===== */
  .deck { height: 100dvh; overflow-y: auto; scroll-snap-type: y mandatory; scroll-behavior: smooth; }
  .slide {
    height: 100dvh; scroll-snap-align: start; overflow: hidden; position: relative; isolation: isolate;
    display: flex; flex-direction: column; justify-content: center; gap: clamp(16px, 2.5vh, 28px);
    padding: clamp(40px, 7vh, 88px) clamp(32px, 8vw, 128px);
    transition: opacity .6s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1), transform .6s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1);
  }
  .js .slide { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(32px); }
  .slide.visible { opacity: 1; transform: none; }
  .js .slide .reveal { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(12px); transition: opacity .5s, transform .5s; }
  .slide.visible .reveal { opacity: 1; transform: none; }
  .slide.visible .reveal:nth-child(2) { transition-delay: .08s; }
  .slide.visible .reveal:nth-child(3) { transition-delay: .16s; }
  .slide.visible .reveal:nth-child(4) { transition-delay: .24s; }

  /* ===== DELIVERY CHECK: reduced motion doubles as the fit test ===== */
  @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
    .deck { scroll-behavior: auto; }
    .slide, .slide .reveal { opacity: 1 !important; transform: none !important; transition: none !important; }
    .slide[data-slide-check] { outline: 4px solid var(--risk); outline-offset: -4px; }
    .slide[data-slide-check="auto-fit"] { outline-color: var(--accent); }
    .slide[data-slide-check]::after {
      content: attr(data-slide-check-label); position: absolute; top: 12px; left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%);
      z-index: 20; padding: 6px 10px; border-radius: 4px; color: var(--bg); background: var(--risk); font: 600 12px/1.2 var(--font-mono); pointer-events: none;
    }
    .slide[data-slide-check="auto-fit"]::after { background: var(--accent); }
  }

  /* ===== CHROME ===== */
  .deck-progress { position: fixed; top: 0; left: 0; height: 2px; background: var(--accent); z-index: 100; transition: width .3s; pointer-events: none; }
  .deck-dots {
    position: fixed; right: clamp(12px, 2vw, 24px); top: 50%; transform: translateY(-50%); z-index: 100;
    display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: flex-end; gap: 4px; padding: 6px; width: 32px;
    max-height: min(70dvh, 560px); overflow-y: auto; border-radius: 10px;
    background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--bg) 70%, transparent); backdrop-filter: blur(6px); transition: width .2s;
  }
  .deck-dots:hover, .deck-dots:focus-within { align-items: stretch; width: min(260px, calc(100vw - 32px)); border: 1px solid var(--border); }
  .deck-dot {
    display: grid; grid-template-columns: 8px minmax(0,1fr); align-items: center; gap: 0; width: 20px; min-height: 24px;
    padding: 6px; border: 0; border-radius: 4px; background: transparent; color: var(--text-dim);
    font: 500 12px/1.2 var(--font-mono); text-align: left; cursor: pointer;
  }
  .deck-dot::before { content: ''; width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 50%; background: currentColor; opacity: .55; justify-self: center; }
  .deck-dot-label { max-width: 0; overflow: hidden; opacity: 0; white-space: nowrap; text-overflow: ellipsis; transition: max-width .2s, opacity .2s; }
  .deck-dots:hover .deck-dot, .deck-dots:focus-within .deck-dot { gap: 10px; width: 100%; }
  .deck-dots:hover .deck-dot-label, .deck-dots:focus-within .deck-dot-label { max-width: 200px; opacity: 1; }
  .deck-dot:hover { color: var(--text); }
  .deck-dot[aria-current="true"] { color: var(--accent); }
  .deck-dot[aria-current="true"]::before { opacity: 1; transform: scale(1.4); }
  .deck-dot:focus-visible, .deck-panel__button:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px; }
  .deck-counter, .deck-hints { position: fixed; bottom: clamp(12px, 2vh, 24px); z-index: 100; font: 500 12px var(--font-mono); color: var(--text-dim); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
  .deck-counter { right: clamp(16px, 2vw, 28px); }
  .deck-hints { left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%); transition: opacity .5s; white-space: nowrap; }
  .deck-hints.faded { opacity: 0; pointer-events: none; }
  .deck-overlay { position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: 200; display: none; place-items: center; padding: 24px; background: rgba(0,0,0,.45); backdrop-filter: blur(4px); }
  .deck-overlay.open { display: grid; }
  .deck-panel { width: min(560px, 86vw); max-height: 80dvh; overflow: auto; padding: 16px 12px; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 10px; background: var(--bg); font-family: var(--font-mono); box-shadow: 0 24px 64px rgba(0,0,0,.25); }
  .deck-panel:focus { outline: none; }
  .deck-panel__header { margin: 2px 10px 10px; font-size: 12px; letter-spacing: .08em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--text-dim); }
  .deck-panel__button { display: flex; gap: 12px; width: 100%; padding: 8px 10px; border: 0; border-radius: 4px; background: transparent; color: inherit; font: 14px/1.3 var(--font-body); text-align: left; cursor: pointer; }
  /* Accent text on its own tint drops under 4.5:1; the tint carries the state, the text stays --text. */
  .deck-panel__button:hover, .deck-panel__button[aria-current="true"] { background: var(--accent-dim); color: var(--text); }
  .deck-panel__number { min-width: 22px; font: 500 12px/1.6 var(--font-mono); color: var(--text-dim); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
  .deck-help-row { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; gap: 24px; padding: 7px 10px; font-size: 13px; }
  .deck-help-row kbd { padding: 2px 8px; border: 1px solid var(--border-bright); border-radius: 4px; font: inherit; }

  /* ===== SKIN: restyle freely ===== */
  .slide__hero { font: 400 clamp(56px, 11vw, 148px)/.92 var(--font-display); letter-spacing: -.035em; text-wrap: balance; max-width: 12ch; }
  .slide__heading { font: 400 clamp(32px, 5vw, 60px)/1.05 var(--font-display); letter-spacing: -.02em; text-wrap: balance; max-width: 28ch; }
  .slide__body { font-size: clamp(18px, 2vw, 24px); line-height: 1.45; color: var(--text-dim); max-width: 38ch; text-wrap: pretty; }
  .slide__label { font: 600 clamp(12px, 1.2vw, 14px) var(--font-mono); letter-spacing: .08em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--accent); }
  .slide__meta { display: flex; gap: 24px; padding-top: 16px; border-top: 1px solid var(--border); font: 500 clamp(12px, 1.2vw, 14px) var(--font-mono); color: var(--text-dim); }
  .slide--title { justify-content: flex-end; }
  .slide__number { position: absolute; right: clamp(32px, 8vw, 128px); top: 6vh; font: clamp(120px, 24vw, 300px)/.8 var(--font-display); color: var(--accent); }

  .slide__kpis { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 2fr 1fr 1fr; gap: 1px; background: var(--border); border-block: 1px solid var(--border); }
  .kpi { background: var(--bg); padding: clamp(16px, 3vh, 32px) clamp(12px, 2vw, 28px) clamp(16px, 3vh, 32px) 0; min-width: 0; }
  .kpi + .kpi { padding-left: clamp(12px, 2vw, 28px); }
  .slide__kpi-val { font: 400 clamp(44px, 6vw, 80px)/1 var(--font-display); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; white-space: nowrap; }
  .kpi:first-child .slide__kpi-val { font-size: clamp(72px, 12vw, 168px); color: var(--accent); letter-spacing: -.03em; }
  .slide__kpi-val small { font: 500 .3em var(--font-mono); color: var(--text-dim); letter-spacing: 0; }
  .slide__kpi-label { margin-top: 12px; font: 500 clamp(12px, 1.2vw, 14px) var(--font-mono); color: var(--text-dim); }
  .slide__kpi-label b { color: var(--ok); font-weight: 600; }

  @media (max-height: 600px) { .slide { padding: 24px clamp(24px, 6vw, 64px); } .slide__number { display: none; } }
  @media (max-height: 500px) { .deck-dots { display: none; } }
  @media (max-width: 768px) { .slide__kpis { grid-template-columns: 1fr; } .kpi + .kpi { padding-left: 0; } }
</style>
</head>
<body>
<div class="deck">

  <section class="slide slide--title">
    <p class="slide__label reveal">Engineering review</p>
    <h1 class="slide__hero reveal">The gateway moves to the edge</h1>
    <p class="slide__meta reveal"><span>API platform</span><span>Q1 review</span></p>
  </section>

  <section class="slide slide--divider">
    <span class="slide__number" aria-hidden="true">01</span>
    <p class="slide__label reveal">The problem</p>
    <h2 class="slide__heading reveal">Every request waits on one process.</h2>
    <p class="slide__body reveal">Rate limits, auth, and routing all run in a single proxy. One slow upstream stalls everything.</p>
  </section>

  <section class="slide slide--dashboard">
    <h2 class="slide__heading reveal">Two weeks in, p50 latency is down 81%</h2>
    <div class="slide__kpis reveal">
      <div class="kpi"><div class="slide__kpi-val">8<small> ms</small></div><div class="slide__kpi-label">p50 latency · <b>−81%</b></div></div>
      <div class="kpi"><div class="slide__kpi-val">99.99<small>%</small></div><div class="slide__kpi-label">uptime · <b>+0.4</b></div></div>
      <div class="kpi"><div class="slide__kpi-val">0</div><div class="slide__kpi-label">cascade outages · from 3</div></div>
    </div>
  </section>

</div>

<script>
  // ===== DELIVERY CHECK (copy as is) =====
  function autoFit() {
    document.querySelectorAll('.slide__kpi-val').forEach(function(el) {
      if (el.scrollWidth > el.clientWidth) {
        el.style.transform = 'scale(' + el.clientWidth / el.scrollWidth + ')'; el.style.transformOrigin = 'left top';
        el.closest('.slide').setAttribute('data-auto-fit', 'KPI value');
      }
    });
    document.querySelectorAll('.slide--quote blockquote').forEach(function(el) {
      var len = el.textContent.trim().length;
      if (len > 150) {
        el.style.fontSize = Math.max(16, Math.round(parseFloat(getComputedStyle(el).fontSize) * Math.max(.5, 150 / len))) + 'px';
        el.closest('.slide').setAttribute('data-auto-fit', 'quote');
      }
    });
  }
  function checkSlideOverflow() {
    var failures = [];
    document.querySelectorAll('.slide').forEach(function(slide, i) {
      var excess = Math.ceil(slide.scrollHeight - slide.clientHeight), fit = slide.getAttribute('data-auto-fit');
      if (excess > 1 || fit) {
        slide.setAttribute('data-slide-check', excess > 1 ? 'overflow' : 'auto-fit');
        slide.setAttribute('data-slide-check-label', excess > 1 ? 'OVERFLOW — split or reduce (' + excess + 'px)' : 'AUTO-FIT USED — review budget (' + fit + ')');
        failures.push('Slide ' + (i + 1) + ': ' + (excess > 1 ? 'vertical overflow ' + excess + 'px' : 'autoFit: ' + fit));
      } else {
        slide.removeAttribute('data-slide-check'); slide.removeAttribute('data-slide-check-label');
      }
    });
    if (failures.length) console.error('Slide delivery check failed. ' + failures.join(' | ') + '. Split or reduce content; autoFit is only a safety net.');
    else console.info('Slide delivery check passed: no vertical overflow or autoFit fallback.');
    return failures;
  }
  function finishSlideRender() {
    autoFit();
    if (!matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches) return;
    (document.fonts ? document.fonts.ready : Promise.resolve()).then(function() { requestAnimationFrame(checkSlideOverflow); });
  }

  // ===== ENGINE (copy as is) =====
  function SlideEngine() {
    this.deck = document.querySelector('.deck');
    this.slides = [].slice.call(document.querySelectorAll('.slide'));
    this.current = 0; this.total = this.slides.length;
    this.storeKey = ['visual-explainer:slide-deck', location.pathname, document.title, this.total].join(':');
    this.buildChrome(); this.bindEvents(); this.observe(); this.restore(); this.update();
  }
  SlideEngine.prototype.titleOf = function(i) {
    var el = this.slides[i].querySelector('.slide__hero,.slide__heading,blockquote');
```

```js file=~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/video/driver.js
// Injected before deck scripts by render.mjs.
// 1. Virtual time: timers, requestAnimationFrame, performance.now, Date, and every CSS or Web
//    Animation advance only when the renderer moves the clock, so a slow frame never drops or skews time.
// 2. Scene state: __ve.cue() sets the attributes and events that the deck's own CSS and JS react to.
(() => {
  let now = 0, nextId = 1, frames = new Map(), cur = -1, caption = null;
  const timers = new Map();
  const owned = new WeakMap(); // Animation the renderer runs -> virtual ms of its last sync
  const epoch = Date.now();
  performance.now = () => now;
  Date.now = () => epoch + now;
  // new Date() and Date() read the virtual clock too; explicit arguments behave natively.
  window.Date = new Proxy(Date, {
    construct: (D, args, nt) => Reflect.construct(D, args.length ? args : [epoch + now], nt),
    apply: (D) => new D(epoch + now).toString(),
  });
  window.setTimeout = (fn, ms, ...args) => { const id = nextId++; timers.set(id, { at: now + Math.max(0, +ms || 0), fn, args }); return id; };
  window.setInterval = (fn, ms, ...args) => { const every = Math.max(1, +ms || 0), id = nextId++; timers.set(id, { at: now + every, fn, args, every }); return id; };
  window.clearTimeout = window.clearInterval = (id) => { timers.delete(id); };
  window.requestAnimationFrame = (cb) => { const id = nextId++; frames.set(id, cb); return id; };
  window.cancelAnimationFrame = (id) => { frames.delete(id); };

  // The renderer owns only the passage of time. It holds a running animation paused (natively) and moves it
  // itself; the page's own pause(), finish(), and cancel() hand it back to the page, and play() returns it.
  const { pause, play } = Animation.prototype;
  // Setting currentTime completes the pause now, so a rate change pending from reverse() applies before the next sync.
  const own = (a) => { pause.call(a); a.currentTime = a.currentTime; owned.set(a, now); };
  for (const m of ['pause', 'finish', 'cancel']) {
    const native = Animation.prototype[m];
    Animation.prototype[m] = function () { owned.delete(this); return native.call(this); };
  }
  Animation.prototype.play = function () { play.call(this); own(this); };
  // Take each running animation from now. Runs after every callback that could start one, so an animation
  // started by a timer at 100 ms counts from 100 ms, not from the next frame. Paused ones stay with the page.
  const adopt = () => { for (const a of document.getAnimations()) if (a.playState === 'running') own(a); };
  // Move each owned animation on by the virtual time since its last sync at its current rate, from where it
  // is, so a seek or rate change by the page counts from when the page made it.
  const sync = () => {
    for (const a of document.getAnimations()) {
      const t0 = owned.get(a);
      if (t0 === undefined || a.playState !== 'paused') continue; // the page's, or replayed by it (adopt takes it)
      const rate = a.playbackRate, t = a.currentTime + (now - t0) * rate;
      owned.set(a, now);
      // finish() fires finish and animationend events, which a paused animation never would.
      if (rate > 0 ? t >= a.effect.getComputedTiming().endTime : rate < 0 && t <= 0) a.finish();
      else a.currentTime = t;
    }
  };
  // Run due timers in order, each at its own time and seeing animations at that time.
  const advance = (target) => {
    if (target < now) throw new Error(`clock cannot go back: ${target} < ${now}`);
    for (;;) {
      let id = null, due = null;
      for (const [k, t] of timers) if (t.at <= target && (!due || t.at < due.at)) { id = k; due = t; }
      if (!due) break;
      now = due.at;
      if (due.every) due.at += due.every; else timers.delete(id);
      sync();
      if (typeof due.fn === 'function') due.fn(...due.args); else (0, eval)(String(due.fn));
      adopt();
    }
    now = target;
    sync();
  };

  const scenes = () => [...document.querySelectorAll('[data-say]')];
  const fire = (el, type, detail) => el.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent(type, { bubbles: true, detail }));

  window.__ve = {
    scenes: () => scenes().map((s) => ({ lines: s.dataset.say.trim().split(/(?<=[.!?])\s+/).filter(Boolean), hold: +s.dataset.hold || 0 })),

    // At `at` ms, scene i is on with sentences 1..beat started: data-beat="0 1 … beat", so CSS can match
    // [data-beat~="2"]. The scene before it keeps data-was until the next change, for its exit animation.
    cue(at, i, beat, text, captions) {
      advance(at);
      const list = scenes(), next = list[i];
      if (i !== cur) {
        for (const s of list) s.removeAttribute('data-was');
        const prev = list[cur];
        if (prev) { prev.removeAttribute('data-beat'); prev.setAttribute('data-was', ''); fire(prev, 've:leave', { scene: cur }); }
        cur = i;

        document.head.prepend(Object.assign(document.createElement('style'), { textContent:

      }
      caption.textContent = captions ? text : '';
      adopt();
    },

    // One video frame at `target` ms.
    tick(target) {
      advance(target);
      const batch = frames;
      frames = new Map();
      adopt();
      for (const cb of batch.values()) { cb(now); adopt(); }
      sync();
    },
  };
})();
```

```text file=~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/video/media.mjs
import { execFileSync, spawn } from "node:child_process";
import { createHash } from "node:crypto";
import { readdirSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { join, parse } from "node:path";

const RATE = 48000;
const WPS = 2.5; // caption reading speed in words per second
const AUDIO = /\.(mp3|wav|m4a|aac|ogg|opus|flac|aiff?)$/i;

// A narration line's clip is <id>.<ext> in the voice folder. The id hashes the text, so an edited
// line needs a new clip and an unchanged line keeps its old one.
export const lineId = (text) => createHash("sha256").update(text).digest("hex").slice(0, 12);

// Line text -> mono 16-bit PCM. Every line must have a clip.
export function loadVoice(dir, lines) {
  // Only finished audio files count, so a leftover download such as <id>.tmp never stands in for a clip.
  const files = new Map(readdirSync(dir).filter((f) => AUDIO.test(f)).map((f) => [parse(f).name, join(dir, f)]));
  const missing = [...new Set(lines)].filter((t) => !files.has(lineId(t)));
  if (missing.length) {
    throw new Error(`${missing.length} line(s) have no clip in ${dir}. Make <id>.mp3 (or .wav) for each:\n${missing.map((t) => `  ${lineId(t)}\t${t}`).join("\n")}`);
  }
  const decode = (file) => {
    try { return execFileSync("ffmpeg", ["-v", "error", "-i", file, "-f", "s16le", "-ac", "1", "-ar", String(RATE), "pipe:1"], { maxBuffer: 1 << 30, stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"] }); }
    catch (e) { throw new Error(`Not a readable audio clip: ${file}\n${e.stderr?.toString().trim()}`); }
  };
  return new Map([...new Set(lines)].map((t) => [t, decode(files.get(lineId(t)))]));
}

// Seconds a line lasts: its clip, or the time a viewer needs to read it as a caption.
export const lineLength = (text, pcm) => (pcm ? pcm.length / 2 / RATE : Math.max(1.5, text.split(/\s+/).length / WPS));

// Lay each clip at its start time on one silent track and write a WAV file.
export function writeTrack(file, clips, total) {
  const data = Buffer.alloc(Math.ceil(total * RATE) * 2);
  for (const { at, pcm } of clips) pcm.copy(data, Math.round(at * RATE) * 2);
  const head = Buffer.alloc(44);
  head.write("RIFF", 0); head.writeUInt32LE(36 + data.length, 4); head.write("WAVE", 8);
  head.write("fmt ", 12); head.writeUInt32LE(16, 16); head.writeUInt16LE(1, 20); head.writeUInt16LE(1, 22);
  head.writeUInt32LE(RATE, 24); head.writeUInt32LE(RATE * 2, 28); head.writeUInt16LE(2, 32); head.writeUInt16LE(16, 34);
  head.write("data", 36); head.writeUInt32LE(data.length, 40);
  writeFileSync(file, Buffer.concat([head, data]));
}

// ffmpeg reading JPEG frames on stdin at a constant rate.
export function encoder(out, { fps, audio }) {
  const args = ["-y", "-v", "error", "-f", "image2pipe", "-c:v", "mjpeg", "-framerate", String(fps), "-i", "pipe:0"];
  if (audio) args.push("-i", audio, "-map", "0:v", "-map", "1:a", "-c:a", "aac", "-b:a", "192k");
  args.push("-vf", "scale=trunc(iw/2)*2:trunc(ih/2)*2", "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "medium", "-tune", "animation", "-crf", "18", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p", "-movflags", "+faststart", out);
  const ff = spawn("ffmpeg", args, { stdio: ["pipe", "inherit", "inherit"] });
  let failure = null;
  const exited = new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    ff.on("error", reject);
    ff.on("close", (code) => (code === 0 ? resolve() : reject(new Error(`ffmpeg exited with code ${code}`))));
  });
  exited.catch((e) => { failure = e; });
  ff.stdin.on("error", () => {}); // EPIPE once ffmpeg has exited; its exit code carries the failure
  return {
    async write(buf) {
      if (failure) throw failure;
      // A drain never comes from an ffmpeg that has exited, so wait on either.
      if (!ff.stdin.write(buf)) await Promise.race([new Promise((r) => ff.stdin.once("drain", r)), exited]);
    },
    async done() { ff.stdin.end(); await exited; },
    kill() { ff.kill("SIGKILL"); },
  };
}

export function requireFfmpeg() {
  try { execFileSync("ffmpeg", ["-version"], { stdio: "ignore" }); }
  catch { throw new Error("ffmpeg is not on PATH. Install it first, for example: brew install ffmpeg"); }
}

export const duration = (file) => Number(execFileSync("ffprobe", ["-v", "error", "-show_entries", "format=duration", "-of", "csv=p=0", file]).toString());
```

```text file=~/.ai/skills/visual-explainer/video/render.mjs mode=755
#!/usr/bin/env node
import { existsSync, mkdtempSync, renameSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { createRequire } from "node:module";
import { homedir } from "node:os";
import { basename, dirname, join, resolve } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath, pathToFileURL } from "node:url";
import { parseArgs } from "node:util";
import { duration, encoder, lineId, lineLength, loadVoice, requireFfmpeg, writeTrack } from "./media.mjs";

const DRIVER = fileURLToPath(new URL("./driver.js", import.meta.url));
const FRAME = { x: 0, y: 0, width: 1280, height: 720, scale: 1.5 }; // 1920×1080 output
const LEAD = 0.5, GAP = 0.3, TAIL = 0.9, BARE = 3; // pacing in seconds around and between lines
const USAGE = `Usage: visual-explainer-video <deck.html> [out.mp4] [options]

Renders a video deck (<section data-say> scenes) to a 1920×1080 MP4 on a virtual clock, so
every frame lands on time. See references/video.md.

Options:
  --lines          Print "<id><TAB><text>" for each narration line, then stop.
  --voice <dir>    Narrate with <dir>/<id>.mp3 (or .wav, .m4a, .ogg, .flac, .aiff). Without it
                   the video is silent with captions.
  --captions       Burn in captions with a voice too.
  --stills         Write one PNG per scene, fully played and captioned, to <name>.stills/, then stop.
  --fps <n>        Frames per second (default 30).`;

async function main() {
  const { values, positionals } = parseArgs({
    allowPositionals: true,
    options: { lines: { type: "boolean" }, voice: { type: "string" }, captions: { type: "boolean" }, stills: { type: "boolean" }, fps: { type: "string" }, help: { type: "boolean", short: "h" } },
  });
  if (values.help || !positionals.length) return console.log(USAGE);
  if (positionals.length > 2) throw new Error(`Too many arguments: ${positionals.slice(2).join(" ")}\n\n${USAGE}`);
  const home = (p) => resolve(p.replace(/^~(?=\/)/, homedir()));
  const input = home(positionals[0]);
  if (!existsSync(input)) throw new Error(`No such file: ${input}`);
  const stem = input.replace(/\.[^./]+$/, "");
  const out = home(positionals[1] ?? `${stem}.mp4`);
  const fps = Number(values.fps ?? 30);
  if (!Number.isInteger(fps) || fps < 1 || fps > 120) throw new Error("--fps must be a whole number from 1 to 120");

  if (values.lines) {
    const scenes = await withDeck(input, ({ scenes }) => scenes);
    for (const text of new Set(scenes.flatMap((s) => s.lines))) console.log(`${lineId(text)}\t${text}`);
    return;
  }
  if (values.stills) return await withDeck(input, (deck) => stills(deck, `${stem}.stills`));
  if (!existsSync(dirname(out))) throw new Error(`Output folder does not exist: ${dirname(out)}`);
  requireFfmpeg();
  const voice = values.voice ? home(values.voice) : null;
  await withDeck(input, (deck) => render(deck, { out, fps, voice, captions: values.captions || !voice }));
  console.log(`wrote ${out} (${duration(out).toFixed(1)} s)`);
}

// Opens the deck at 1280×720 CSS pixels with driver.js injected, and passes it to fn.
async function withDeck(input, fn) {
  let chromium;
  try {
    ({ chromium } = await import("playwright-core"));
  } catch (e) {
    if (e.code !== "ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND") throw e;
    // playwright-core is an optional peer, so only people who make videos download it.
    throw new Error("playwright-core is not installed. Run: npx -y -p visual-explainer -p playwright-core visual-explainer-video <deck.html> …\nWith a global install, run npm install -g playwright-core once. In a repository checkout, run npm install first.");
  }
  let browser;
  try {
    browser = await chromium.launch();
  } catch (e) {
    if (!/Executable doesn't exist/.test(e.message)) throw e;
    try {
      browser = await chromium.launch({ channel: "chrome" });
    } catch {
      const { version } = createRequire(import.meta.url)("playwright-core/package.json");
      throw new Error(`No browser found. Install Google Chrome, or run: npx playwright-core@${version} install chromium-headless-shell`);
    }
  }
  try {
    const ctx = await browser.newContext({ viewport: { width: 1280, height: 720 }, deviceScaleFactor: 1.5, reducedMotion: "no-preference" });
    await ctx.addInitScript({ path: DRIVER });
    const page = await ctx.newPage();
    const errors = [];
    page.on("pageerror", (e) => errors.push(e.message));
    await page.goto(pathToFileURL(input).href, { waitUntil: "networkidle" });
    await page.evaluate(() => document.fonts.ready);
    const failed = () => { if (errors.length) throw new Error(`The deck threw: ${errors[0]}`); };
    failed();
    const scenes = await page.evaluate(() => __ve.scenes());
    if (!scenes.length) throw new Error(`${basename(input)} has no <section data-say> scenes.`);
    const cdp = await ctx.newCDPSession(page);
    // The clip scale re-rasterizes at 1.5×; without it a CDP screenshot comes back at 1280×720.
    const shot = async (format = "jpeg") =>
      Buffer.from((await cdp.send("Page.captureScreenshot", { format, clip: FRAME, ...(format === "jpeg" && { quality: 92, optimizeForSpeed: true }) })).data, "base64");
    return await fn({ page, scenes, shot, failed });
  } finally {
    await browser.close();
  }
}

// Stills show each scene's last sentence as a caption, so captions can be checked against the layout.
async function stills({ page, scenes, shot, failed }, dir) {
  // A fresh, uniquely named folder per run: no stale files, no clash with another run.
  const part = mkdtempSync(`${dir}.partial-`);
  try {
    let t = 0;
    for (const [i, s] of scenes.entries()) {
      for (let b = 0; b <= s.lines.length; b++) {
        await page.evaluate(([i, b, t, text]) => { __ve.cue(t, i, b, text, true); __ve.tick(t + 1500); }, [i, b, t, s.lines[b - 1] ?? ""]);
        t += 1500;
      }
      await page.evaluate((t) => __ve.tick(t), t += 3000);
      failed();
      writeFileSync(join(part, `scene-${String(i + 1).padStart(2, "0")}.png`), await shot("png"));
    }
    // Replace the previous stills only once every new one exists.
    rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
    renameSync(part, dir);
  } finally {
    rmSync(part, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
  console.log(`wrote ${scenes.length} stills to ${dir}`);
}

async function render({ page, scenes, shot, failed }, { out, fps, voice, captions }) {
  const clips = voice ? loadVoice(voice, scenes.flatMap((s) => s.lines)) : null;
  // Scene start, then each line in turn; a line's beat starts when its clip starts.
  const cues = [], track = [];
  let t = 0;
  for (const [i, s] of scenes.entries()) {
    cues.push({ t, scene: i, beat: 0, text: "" });
    let at = t + LEAD;
    for (const [j, text] of s.lines.entries()) {
      cues.push({ t: at, scene: i, beat: j + 1, text });
      if (clips) track.push({ at, pcm: clips.get(text) });
      at += lineLength(text, clips?.get(text)) + GAP;
    }
    t = (s.lines.length ? at - GAP + TAIL : t + BARE) + s.hold;
  }

  // One fresh folder beside the output holds the voice track and the partial MP4. The MP4 is renamed
  // into place on success, so a failed render keeps the last good one and two renders never share files.
  const partDir = mkdtempSync(join(dirname(out), ".ve-partial-"));
  const part = join(partDir, basename(out));
  let enc = null;
  try {
    const frames = Math.ceil(t * fps);
    const audio = clips ? join(partDir, "voice.wav") : null;
    if (audio) writeTrack(audio, track, frames / fps); // as long as the video, so neither stream ends early
    enc = encoder(part, { fps, audio });
    let next = 0, shown = 0;
    for (let f = 0; f < frames; f++) {
      // Each cue runs at its own time between frames, so what it starts is timed from the cue.
      const due = [];
      while (next < cues.length && cues[next].t <= f / fps) due.push(cues[next++]);
      await page.evaluate(([due, ms, captions]) => {
        for (const c of due) __ve.cue(c.t * 1000, c.scene, c.beat, c.text, captions);
        __ve.tick(ms);
      }, [due, (f / fps) * 1000, captions]);
      failed();
      await enc.write(await shot());
      const pct = Math.floor(((f + 1) / frames) * 10) * 10;
      if (pct > shown) { shown = pct; console.log(`rendered ${pct}%`); }
    }
    await enc.done();
    renameSync(part, out);
  } catch (e) {
    enc?.kill();
    throw e;
  } finally {
    rmSync(partDir, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
}

main().catch((e) => {
  console.error(e.message);
  process.exit(1);
});
```

#### `~/.ai/skills/worktree-quick/SKILL.md`

````markdown file=~/.ai/skills/worktree-quick/SKILL.md
---
name: worktree-quick
description: Create or destroy a code-only git worktree for a PR, branch, or new task (fetch + checkout, copies env, yarn install; no DB/ports/seed). Use when the user runs /worktree-quick, "worktree quick", "quick worktree", "code-only worktree", "checkout this PR in a worktree", "/worktree-quick add dark mode", or wants a disposable worktree to start a task or review a PR/branch without a second local stack. Do NOT use for a full seeded env on alternate ports — that is /monorepo-worktree.
---

# /worktree-quick

Code-only worktree: `git fetch` + `git worktree add`, then copy `.env*` and `yarn install` (own `node_modules`; husky postinstall wires pre-push). Yarn is mandatory on every worktree, create or reuse; never symlink `node_modules` from primary. No Postgres/Redis, no port remaps, no seed, no serve. Use `/monorepo-worktree` for a runnable second stack.

## Commands

| User says                                              | Action                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------- |
| `/worktree-quick 1234` / `pr 1234` / PR URL            | Fetch that PR, add worktree                  |
| `/worktree-quick feature/foo` / `branch …`             | Fetch that ref, add worktree                 |
| `/worktree-quick add dark mode` / `new …` / `task …`   | New branch from current HEAD for that task   |
| `/worktree-quick destroy 1234` / `remove` / `teardown` | Remove the quick worktree + `quick/*` branch |
| `/worktree-quick list`                                 | Show quick worktrees only                    |

User arguments: `$ARGUMENTS`

## Fast path

Script: `~/.ai/skills/worktree-quick/scripts/quick-worktree.sh`, run from inside the target git repo or with `REPO_ROOT` set. Agents are non-interactive: always pass `--yes` on destroy, and use `--force` only if the worktree is dirty and the user wants it discarded.

```bash
~/.ai/skills/worktree-quick/scripts/quick-worktree.sh 1234                              # PR number, #N, pr N, or PR URL
~/.ai/skills/worktree-quick/scripts/quick-worktree.sh pr 1234
~/.ai/skills/worktree-quick/scripts/quick-worktree.sh https://github.com/org/repo/pull/1234
~/.ai/skills/worktree-quick/scripts/quick-worktree.sh feature/foo                       # branch or ref
~/.ai/skills/worktree-quick/scripts/quick-worktree.sh create origin/fix-types my-review
~/.ai/skills/worktree-quick/scripts/quick-worktree.sh new "add dark mode toggle"        # new task from current HEAD
~/.ai/skills/worktree-quick/scripts/quick-worktree.sh task "fees page polish"
~/.ai/skills/worktree-quick/scripts/quick-worktree.sh list                              # destroy / list
~/.ai/skills/worktree-quick/scripts/quick-worktree.sh destroy 1234 --yes
~/.ai/skills/worktree-quick/scripts/quick-worktree.sh destroy --name pr-1234 --yes
~/.ai/skills/worktree-quick/scripts/quick-worktree.sh destroy --all --yes
```

## What the script does (create)

1. Resolve repo root (`REPO_ROOT` or cwd git main worktree).
2. Fetch the ref: PRs use `git fetch origin pull/N/head` (works for forks; `gh pr view` is optional metadata); branches use `git fetch origin <ref>`, then `origin/<ref>` or the local ref.
3. Tasks (`new …` / `task …` / multi-word description / unresolved single token): branch from **current HEAD**; no fetch.
4. `git worktree add -b quick/<slug> ../worktrees/<repo>-quick-<slug> <sha>`. The local branch is always `quick/<slug>` because the same branch cannot be checked out in two worktrees.
5. Write a `worktree-quick` marker in the worktree git dir (not the working tree; do not commit it).
6. Copy `.env`, `.env.local`, and `apps/{web-crm,web-funnel,server-crm}/.env.local` from primary as-is (no port/DB rewrite).
7. `yarn install` in the worktree (own `node_modules`; husky postinstall creates `.husky/_` so pre-push runs). Remove a leftover `node_modules` symlink first.

## What the script does (destroy)

1. Resolve target by PR number, slug, `--name`, `--path`, or `--all`.
2. Refuse the primary checkout, `.worktree-slot` (full-stack) worktrees, and anything that is not `*-quick-*` / `.worktree-quick`.
3. `git worktree remove` (retry `--force` only if asked).
4. Delete the local `quick/*` branch unless `--keep-branch` or it is checked out elsewhere. No ports, no Redis, no `DROP DATABASE`.

## Agent checklist

1. Parse `$ARGUMENTS`: `list` / `destroy|remove|teardown` / PR / branch / **task description**. If missing, **ask**.
2. `cd` to the repo the user is talking about; do not guess a different project.
3. For a task, run `…/quick-worktree.sh new "<description>"`. Do not hand-roll `git worktree add` unless the script is missing.
4. Do not create `dbname_wtN`, rewrite ports, seed, or start serve. The script copies env and runs `yarn install`; wait for it. If you reuse an existing path, remove a leftover `node_modules` symlink, then `(cd "<path>" && yarn install)` and wait for exit 0.
5. After create, report **path**, **branch**, **sha**, PR URL if any, and the destroy command. If the user also asked for work in the worktree, do it in that path. After destroy, run `list` / `git worktree list` and confirm the path is gone.
6. If the user then asks to run the app, stop and point them at `/monorepo-worktree`: a quick worktree has no port remap, so serving it (even just `web-income`) takes primary's `4202`/`3000`/… and makes slots' vite drift to random ports (slot income lives on `income.futurewholesale.local:{WEB_PORT}`, seeded via `database:seed-income`).
````

#### `~/.ai/skills/worktree-quick/scripts/quick-worktree.sh`

```bash file=~/.ai/skills/worktree-quick/scripts/quick-worktree.sh mode=755
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# quick-worktree.sh — Code-only git worktree for a PR or branch.
# Copies .env*, then yarn install (own node_modules; husky postinstall
# wires pre-push — do not skip yarn). Do not symlink node_modules.
# No DB, no Redis, no port remaps, no seed, no serve.
#
# Usage:
#   ./quick-worktree.sh [create] <pr|branch|url> [name]
#   ./quick-worktree.sh [new|task] <what to work on>
#   ./quick-worktree.sh destroy <pr|name|path|task> [--yes] [--force] [--keep-branch]
#   ./quick-worktree.sh list
#
# Examples:
#   ./quick-worktree.sh 1234
#   ./quick-worktree.sh pr 1234
#   ./quick-worktree.sh feature/foo
#   ./quick-worktree.sh https://github.com/org/repo/pull/1234
#   ./quick-worktree.sh create origin/fix-types my-review
#   ./quick-worktree.sh new add dark mode toggle
#   ./quick-worktree.sh task fees page polish
#   ./quick-worktree.sh destroy 1234 --yes
#   ./quick-worktree.sh destroy --name pr-1234 --yes
#   ./quick-worktree.sh list
#
# Env:
#   REPO_ROOT   Pin the primary checkout (otherwise cwd git repo)
#   GIT_REMOTE  Remote to fetch from (default: origin)

set -euo pipefail

REMOTE="${GIT_REMOTE:-origin}"
YES=0
FORCE=0
KEEP_BRANCH=0
ACTION=""
TARGET=""
CUSTOM_NAME=""
NAME_FLAG=""
PATH_FLAG=""
ALL=0
FORCE_TASK=0
TASK_TITLE=""

usage() {
  sed -n '2,26p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'
  exit 1
}

die() {
  echo "ERROR: $*" >&2
  exit 1
}

# --- parse args ---
POSITIONAL=()
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    create|setup)
      ACTION="create"
      shift
      ;;
    new|task|work)
      ACTION="create"
      FORCE_TASK=1
      shift
      ;;
    destroy|remove|teardown|rm|clean)
      ACTION="destroy"
      shift
      ;;
    list|ls)
      ACTION="list"
      shift
      ;;
    --name)
      NAME_FLAG="${2:-}"
      [[ -n "${NAME_FLAG}" ]] || usage
      shift 2
      ;;
    --path)
      PATH_FLAG="${2:-}"
      [[ -n "${PATH_FLAG}" ]] || usage
      shift 2
      ;;
    --all)
      ALL=1
      shift
      ;;
    --keep-branch) KEEP_BRANCH=1; shift ;;
    --force) FORCE=1; shift ;;
    --yes|-y) YES=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help) usage ;;
    --)
      shift
      break
      ;;
    -*)
      die "unknown flag: $1"
      ;;
    *)
      POSITIONAL+=("$1")
      shift
      ;;
  esac
done

join_positional() {
  local start="$1"
  local i=0 s=""
  i="${start}"
  while [[ "${i}" -lt ${#POSITIONAL[@]} ]]; do
    if [[ -n "${s}" ]]; then
      s="${s} "
    fi
    s="${s}${POSITIONAL[$i]}"
    i=$((i + 1))
  done
  printf '%s' "${s}"
}

if [[ ${#POSITIONAL[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
  if [[ "${POSITIONAL[0]}" == "pr" || "${POSITIONAL[0]}" == "branch" || "${POSITIONAL[0]}" == "ref" ]]; then
    if [[ ${#POSITIONAL[@]} -lt 2 ]]; then
      die "${POSITIONAL[0]} requires a number or ref"
    fi
    TARGET="${POSITIONAL[0]} ${POSITIONAL[1]}"
    if [[ ${#POSITIONAL[@]} -gt 2 ]]; then
      CUSTOM_NAME="$(join_positional 2)"
    fi
  elif [[ ${#POSITIONAL[@]} -gt 1 && "${FORCE_TASK}" -eq 0 ]]; then
    TARGET="${POSITIONAL[0]}"
    CUSTOM_NAME="$(join_positional 1)"
    if [[ "${TARGET}" != *'/'* && ! "${TARGET}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "${TARGET}" != http* ]]; then
      TARGET="$(join_positional 0)"
      CUSTOM_NAME=""
      FORCE_TASK=1
    fi
  else
    TARGET="$(join_positional 0)"
  fi
fi

if [[ -z "${ACTION}" ]]; then
  if [[ -z "${TARGET}" && -z "${PATH_FLAG}" && "${ALL}" -eq 0 ]]; then
    ACTION="list"
  else
    ACTION="create"
  fi
fi

slugify() {
  echo "$1" \
    | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' \
    | sed -E 's#^origin/##; s#^refs/heads/##; s#^refs/pull/##; s#/head$##' \
    | tr '/:#' '---' \
    | tr -cs 'a-z0-9._-' '-' \
    | sed -E 's/^-+//; s/-+$//; s/-+/-/g' \
    | cut -c1-48
}

extract_pr() {
  local raw="$1"
  raw="$(echo "${raw}" | sed -E 's/^#//')"
  if echo "${raw}" | grep -Eq 'github\.com/.+/pull/[0-9]+'; then
    echo "${raw}" | sed -E 's#.*github\.com/.+/pull/([0-9]+).*#\1#'
    return 0
  fi
  if echo "${raw}" | grep -Eq '^[Pp][Rr][-/ ]?[0-9]+$'; then
    echo "${raw}" | sed -E 's/^[Pp][Rr][-/ ]?//'
    return 0
  fi
  if echo "${raw}" | grep -Eq '^[0-9]+$'; then
    echo "${raw}"
    return 0
  fi
  return 1
}

resolve_primary() {
  if [[ -n "${REPO_ROOT:-}" && -d "${REPO_ROOT}" ]]; then
    (cd "${REPO_ROOT}" && pwd)
    return 0
  fi
  local main_wt
  main_wt="$(git worktree list --porcelain 2>/dev/null | awk '/^worktree /{print $2; exit}')"
  if [[ -n "${main_wt}" && -d "${main_wt}" ]]; then
    echo "${main_wt}"
    return 0
  fi
  if git rev-parse --show-toplevel >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    git rev-parse --show-toplevel
    return 0
  fi
  die "cannot resolve repo root. cd into a git repo or set REPO_ROOT."
}

PRIMARY="$(resolve_primary)"
REPO_NAME="$(basename "${PRIMARY}")"
WORKTREES_ROOT="$(dirname "${PRIMARY}")/worktrees"

is_primary() {
  local candidate="$1"
  local a b
  a="$(cd "${candidate}" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)" || return 1
  b="$(cd "${PRIMARY}" && pwd -P)"
  [[ "${a}" == "${b}" ]]
}

marker_file() {
  local path="$1" gitdir
  if gitdir="$(git -C "${path}" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir 2>/dev/null)"; then
    if [[ -f "${gitdir}/worktree-quick" ]]; then
      echo "${gitdir}/worktree-quick"
      return 0
    fi
  fi
  if [[ -f "${path}/.worktree-quick" ]]; then
    echo "${path}/.worktree-quick"
    return 0
  fi
  return 1
}

is_quick_worktree() {
  local path="$1"
  [[ -f "${path}/.worktree-slot" ]] && return 1
  marker_file "${path}" >/dev/null && return 0
  local base
  base="$(basename "${path}")"
  [[ "${base}" == "${REPO_NAME}-quick-"* ]] && return 0
  return 1
}

assert_not_primary() {
  local path="$1"
  if is_primary "${path}"; then
    die "refusing to operate on the primary checkout: ${path}"
  fi
}

assert_quick_or_die() {
  local path="$1"
  assert_not_primary "${path}"
  if ! is_quick_worktree "${path}"; then
    die "refusing to touch non-quick worktree: ${path} (no quick marker; expected ${REPO_NAME}-quick-*)"
  fi
}

marker_get() {
  local path="$1" key="$2" file
  file="$(marker_file "${path}")" || return 1
  awk -F= -v k="${key}" '$1==k {print substr($0, index($0,$2)); exit}' "${file}"
}

list_quick_paths() {
  git -C "${PRIMARY}" worktree list --porcelain | awk '/^worktree /{print $2}' | while IFS= read -r p; do
    [[ -n "${p}" ]] || continue
    if is_quick_worktree "${p}"; then
      echo "${p}"
    fi
  done
}

cmd_list() {
  local found=0
  printf '%-56s %-28s %-10s %s\n' "PATH" "BRANCH" "SOURCE" "REF"
  printf '%-56s %-28s %-10s %s\n' "----" "------" "------" "---"
  while IFS= read -r p; do
    [[ -n "${p}" ]] || continue
    found=1
    local branch source ref
    branch="$(git -C "${p}" rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo "?")"
    source="$(marker_get "${p}" source 2>/dev/null || echo "?")"
    ref="$(marker_get "${p}" ref 2>/dev/null || git -C "${p}" rev-parse --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo "?")"
    printf '%-56s %-28s %-10s %s\n' "${p}" "${branch}" "${source}" "${ref}"
  done < <(list_quick_paths)
  if [[ "${found}" -eq 0 ]]; then
    echo "(no quick worktrees for ${REPO_NAME})"
  fi
}

# Same env files as the primary checkout, copied as-is (no port/DB rewrite —
# this is not a second stack). Missing sources are a warning, not a failure.
copy_env_files() {
  local primary="$1" wt="$2"
  copy_one_env() {
    local src="$1" dest="$2"
    if [[ -f "${src}" ]]; then
      mkdir -p "$(dirname "${dest}")"
      cp "${src}" "${dest}"
      echo "  copied ${src#"${primary}"/}"
    else
      echo "  WARN: missing ${src}"
    fi
  }
  copy_one_env "${primary}/.env" "${wt}/.env"
  copy_one_env "${primary}/.env.local" "${wt}/.env.local"
  copy_one_env "${primary}/apps/web-crm/.env.local" "${wt}/apps/web-crm/.env.local"
  copy_one_env "${primary}/apps/web-funnel/.env.local" "${wt}/apps/web-funnel/.env.local"
  copy_one_env "${primary}/apps/server-crm/.env.local" "${wt}/apps/server-crm/.env.local"
}

# Yarn installs a real node_modules in the worktree. Drop a leftover symlink
# from older setup so install does not write into the primary tree.
drop_node_modules_symlink() {
  local dest="${1}/node_modules"
  if [[ -L "${dest}" ]]; then
    rm -f "${dest}"
    echo "  removed leftover node_modules symlink"
  fi
}

write_marker() {
  local path="$1" gitdir
  gitdir="$(git -C "${path}" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir)"
  cat > "${gitdir}/worktree-quick" <<EOF
kind=quick
repo=${REPO_NAME}
source=${SOURCE}
pr=${PR_NUM}
ref=${RESOLVED_SHA}
upstream=${UPSTREAM_REF}
branch=${BRANCH_NAME}
url=${SOURCE_URL}
task=${TASK_TITLE}
created=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
EOF
}

resolve_task() {
  local desc="$1"
  desc="$(echo "${desc}" | sed -E 's/^(new|task|work|on)[[:space:]]+//')"
  [[ -n "${desc}" ]] || die "task mode requires a description (e.g. 'new add dark mode')"
  SOURCE="task"
  TASK_TITLE="${desc}"
  TITLE="${desc}"
  UPSTREAM_REF="$(git -C "${PRIMARY}" rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)"
  RESOLVED_SHA="$(git -C "${PRIMARY}" rev-parse HEAD)"
  SOURCE_URL=""
  PR_NUM=""
}

resolve_create_target() {
  local raw="$1"
  PR_NUM=""
  SOURCE=""
  SOURCE_URL=""
  UPSTREAM_REF=""
  RESOLVED_SHA=""
  TITLE=""
  TASK_TITLE=""

  if [[ "${FORCE_TASK}" -eq 1 ]]; then
    resolve_task "${raw}"
    return 0
  fi

  local maybe_pr
  if maybe_pr="$(extract_pr "${raw}")"; then
    SOURCE="pr"
    PR_NUM="${maybe_pr}"
    git -C "${PRIMARY}" fetch "${REMOTE}" "pull/${PR_NUM}/head"
    RESOLVED_SHA="$(git -C "${PRIMARY}" rev-parse FETCH_HEAD)"
    UPSTREAM_REF="pull/${PR_NUM}/head"
    if command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      TITLE="$(gh pr view "${PR_NUM}" --json title --jq .title 2>/dev/null || true)"
      SOURCE_URL="$(gh pr view "${PR_NUM}" --json url --jq .url 2>/dev/null || true)"
      local head
      head="$(gh pr view "${PR_NUM}" --json headRefName --jq .headRefName 2>/dev/null || true)"
      if [[ -n "${head}" && "${head}" != "null" ]]; then
        UPSTREAM_REF="${head}"
      fi
    fi
    return 0
  fi

  SOURCE="branch"
  local ref="${raw}"
  if git -C "${PRIMARY}" fetch "${REMOTE}" "${ref}" 2>/dev/null; then
    if git -C "${PRIMARY}" rev-parse --verify --quiet "${REMOTE}/${ref}^{commit}" >/dev/null; then
      UPSTREAM_REF="${REMOTE}/${ref}"
      RESOLVED_SHA="$(git -C "${PRIMARY}" rev-parse "${REMOTE}/${ref}^{commit}")"
      return 0
    fi
    if git -C "${PRIMARY}" rev-parse --verify --quiet "FETCH_HEAD^{commit}" >/dev/null; then
      UPSTREAM_REF="${ref}"
      RESOLVED_SHA="$(git -C "${PRIMARY}" rev-parse "FETCH_HEAD^{commit}")"
      return 0
    fi
  fi
  if git -C "${PRIMARY}" rev-parse --verify --quiet "${ref}^{commit}" >/dev/null; then
    UPSTREAM_REF="${ref}"
    RESOLVED_SHA="$(git -C "${PRIMARY}" rev-parse "${ref}^{commit}")"
    return 0
  fi
  if [[ "${raw}" == *'/'* || "${raw}" == *':'* ]]; then
    die "cannot resolve '${raw}' as a PR number or git ref (tried fetch ${REMOTE} ${ref})"
  fi
  resolve_task "${raw}"
}

cmd_create() {
  local raw="${TARGET}"
  [[ -n "${raw}" ]] || die "create requires a PR, branch, or task description. Usage: quick-worktree.sh <pr|branch|new …>"

  resolve_create_target "${raw}"

  local slug
  if [[ -n "${CUSTOM_NAME}" ]]; then
    slug="$(slugify "${CUSTOM_NAME}")"
  elif [[ -n "${NAME_FLAG}" ]]; then
    slug="$(slugify "${NAME_FLAG}")"
  elif [[ "${SOURCE}" == "pr" ]]; then
    slug="pr-${PR_NUM}"
  elif [[ "${SOURCE}" == "task" ]]; then
    slug="$(slugify "${TASK_TITLE}")"
  else
    slug="$(slugify "${raw}")"
  fi
  [[ -n "${slug}" ]] || die "could not derive a worktree name from '${raw}'"

  local wt_path="${WORKTREES_ROOT}/${REPO_NAME}-quick-${slug}"
  BRANCH_NAME="quick/${slug}"

  if [[ -d "${wt_path}" ]]; then
    die "worktree path already exists: ${wt_path}"
  fi
  if git -C "${PRIMARY}" show-ref --verify --quiet "refs/heads/${BRANCH_NAME}"; then
    die "local branch already exists: ${BRANCH_NAME} (destroy it first or pass a different name)"
  fi

  mkdir -p "${WORKTREES_ROOT}"
  git -C "${PRIMARY}" worktree add -b "${BRANCH_NAME}" "${wt_path}" "${RESOLVED_SHA}"
  write_marker "${wt_path}"

  echo "Copying env from primary..."
  copy_env_files "${PRIMARY}" "${wt_path}"
  drop_node_modules_symlink "${wt_path}"
  echo "yarn install (husky postinstall wires pre-push)..."
  (cd "${wt_path}" && yarn install)

  echo "═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
  echo " Quick worktree (env + yarn install — no db / seed / serve)"
  echo "═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
  echo "  repo:     ${PRIMARY}"
  echo "  path:     ${wt_path}"
  echo "  branch:   ${BRANCH_NAME}"
  echo "  source:   ${SOURCE}${PR_NUM:+ #${PR_NUM}}"
  echo "  ref:      ${RESOLVED_SHA}"
  echo "  upstream: ${UPSTREAM_REF}"
  if [[ "${SOURCE}" == "task" && -n "${TASK_TITLE}" ]]; then
    echo "  task:     ${TASK_TITLE}"
  elif [[ -n "${TITLE}" ]]; then
    echo "  title:    ${TITLE}"
  fi
  if [[ -n "${SOURCE_URL}" ]]; then
    echo "  url:      ${SOURCE_URL}"
  fi
  echo "═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
  echo "cd ${wt_path}"
  echo "Destroy: $0 destroy ${slug} --yes"
}

resolve_destroy_path() {
  if [[ -n "${PATH_FLAG}" ]]; then
    local p="${PATH_FLAG}"
    if [[ "${p}" != /* ]]; then
      p="$(cd "${p}" 2>/dev/null && pwd)" || die "path not found: ${PATH_FLAG}"
    fi
    echo "${p}"
    return 0
  fi

  local key="${NAME_FLAG:-${TARGET}}"
  [[ -n "${key}" ]] || return 1
  key="$(echo "${key}" | sed -E 's/^(new|task|work|on)[[:space:]]+//')"

  local maybe_pr
  if maybe_pr="$(extract_pr "${key}")"; then
    local p
    p="${WORKTREES_ROOT}/${REPO_NAME}-quick-pr-${maybe_pr}"
    if [[ -d "${p}" ]]; then
      echo "${p}"
      return 0
    fi
    while IFS= read -r cand; do
      [[ -n "${cand}" ]] || continue
      local pr
      pr="$(marker_get "${cand}" pr || true)"
      if [[ "${pr}" == "${maybe_pr}" ]]; then
        echo "${cand}"
        return 0
      fi
    done < <(list_quick_paths)
  fi

  local slug
  slug="$(slugify "${key}")"
  local p="${WORKTREES_ROOT}/${REPO_NAME}-quick-${slug}"
  if [[ -d "${p}" ]]; then
    echo "${p}"
    return 0
  fi

  # Allow passing the full directory basename or an existing worktree path
  if [[ -d "${key}" ]]; then
    (cd "${key}" && pwd)
    return 0
  fi

  return 1
}

destroy_one() {
  local wt_path="$1"
  assert_quick_or_die "${wt_path}"

  local branch
  branch="$(marker_get "${wt_path}" branch || true)"
  if [[ -z "${branch}" ]]; then
    branch="$(git -C "${wt_path}" rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)"
  fi

  echo "Removing worktree: ${wt_path}"
  rm -f "${wt_path}/.worktree-quick"
  if [[ "${FORCE}" -eq 1 ]]; then
    git -C "${PRIMARY}" worktree remove --force "${wt_path}" \
      || { rm -rf "${wt_path}"; git -C "${PRIMARY}" worktree prune; }
  else
    git -C "${PRIMARY}" worktree remove "${wt_path}" \
      || die "worktree remove failed (dirty?). Re-run with --force"
  fi
  git -C "${PRIMARY}" worktree prune

  if [[ "${KEEP_BRANCH}" -eq 0 && -n "${branch}" && "${branch}" == quick/* ]]; then
    if git -C "${PRIMARY}" show-ref --verify --quiet "refs/heads/${branch}"; then
      if git -C "${PRIMARY}" worktree list --porcelain | awk '/^branch /{print $2}' | grep -qx "refs/heads/${branch}"; then
        echo "Leaving branch ${branch} (still checked out elsewhere)"
      else
        git -C "${PRIMARY}" branch -D "${branch}"
        echo "Deleted branch ${branch}"
      fi
    fi
  fi
}

cmd_destroy() {
  local paths=()
  if [[ "${ALL}" -eq 1 ]]; then
    while IFS= read -r p; do
      [[ -n "${p}" ]] && paths+=("${p}")
    done < <(list_quick_paths)
    [[ ${#paths[@]} -gt 0 ]] || die "no quick worktrees to destroy"
  else
    local p
    p="$(resolve_destroy_path)" || {
      echo "Could not resolve destroy target '${NAME_FLAG:-${TARGET:-}}'." >&2
      echo "Known quick worktrees:" >&2
      cmd_list >&2
      exit 1
    }
    paths+=("${p}")
  fi

  echo "Will destroy:"
  local p
  for p in "${paths[@]}"; do
    echo "  ${p}"
    assert_quick_or_die "${p}"
  done

  if [[ "${YES}" -ne 1 ]]; then
    die "refusing to destroy without --yes (non-interactive). Re-run with --yes."
  fi

  for p in "${paths[@]}"; do
    destroy_one "${p}"
  done

  echo "Remaining worktrees:"
  git -C "${PRIMARY}" worktree list
}

case "${ACTION}" in
  list) cmd_list ;;
  create) cmd_create ;;
  destroy) cmd_destroy ;;
  *) usage ;;
esac
```

### OpenCode-only skills

Kept apart from `skills/` because OpenCode also scans `~/.claude/skills`, so a shared name would collide.

### Command assets

Extra references for commands. `*/scripts` are symlinks into `oc_skills`.

### Workflows

Grok workflows (rhai).

#### `~/.ai/workflows/peer-review.rhai`

```rust file=~/.ai/workflows/peer-review.rhai
// peer-review — plan → implement → specialist review → adversarial verify →
// independent triage → fix → optional delta re-review. Improves on the
// peer-review skill with fail-closed verification, implementer/judge
// separation, early exit, and budget-aware round structure.

let meta = #{
    name: "peer-review",
    description: "Peer-reviewed build: plan, implement, parallel specialists, adversarial verify findings, independent triage, fix, optional delta re-review",
    when_to_use: "When you want /peer-review quality (plan+implement+multi-specialist rounds) with adversarial verification and no implementer-as-judge bias",
    phases: [
        #{ title: "Resolve", detail: "task / PRD / issue into a bound spec" },
        #{ title: "Plan", detail: "structured plan with consumer map, authZ, failure modes" },
        #{ title: "Implement", detail: "build against the plan; record files touched" },
        #{ title: "Review", detail: "parallel specialists (7 actionable + architecture advisory)" },
        #{ title: "Verify", detail: "independent skeptics prove each finding is real" },
        #{ title: "Triage", detail: "fresh judge accepts / rejects / defers confirmed findings only" },
        #{ title: "Fix", detail: "implement accepted changes; type-harden soft-fails" },
        #{ title: "Re-review", detail: "optional delta pass on fixed files only" },
        #{ title: "Summary", detail: "durable report + deferred list + architecture advisory if needed" },
    ],
};

// ── Schemas ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

let plan_schema = #{
    "type": "object",
    "required": ["goal", "approach", "files", "consumer_map", "invariants", "authz", "failure_modes", "out_of_scope", "open_questions", "implementation_steps"],
    "properties": #{
        "goal": #{ "type": "string" },
        "approach": #{ "type": "string" },
        "files": #{ "type": "array", "items": #{ "type": "string" }, "maxItems": 40 },
        "consumer_map": #{ "type": "string" },
        "invariants": #{ "type": "string" },
        "authz": #{ "type": "string" },
        "failure_modes": #{ "type": "string" },
        "out_of_scope": #{ "type": "string" },
        "open_questions": #{ "type": "string" },
        "implementation_steps": #{ "type": "array", "items": #{ "type": "string" }, "maxItems": 20 },
    },
};

let implement_schema = #{
    "type": "object",
    "required": ["summary", "files_touched", "build_ok", "notes"],
    "properties": #{
        "summary": #{ "type": "string" },
        "files_touched": #{ "type": "array", "items": #{ "type": "string" }, "maxItems": 60 },
        "build_ok": #{ "type": "boolean" },
        "notes": #{ "type": "string" },
    },
};

let findings_schema = #{
    "type": "object",
    "required": ["findings", "summary"],
    "properties": #{
        "summary": #{ "type": "string" },
        "findings": #{
            "type": "array",
            "maxItems": 6,
            "items": #{
                "type": "object",
                "required": ["title", "severity", "file", "observation", "why", "suggested_change"],
                "properties": #{
                    "title": #{ "type": "string" },
                    "severity": #{ "type": "string" },
                    "file": #{ "type": "string" },
                    "line": #{ "type": "string" },
                    "observation": #{ "type": "string" },
                    "why": #{ "type": "string" },
                    "suggested_change": #{ "type": "string" },
                },
            },
        },
    },
};

let arch_schema = #{
    "type": "object",
    "required": ["verdict", "note"],
    "properties": #{
        "verdict": #{ "type": "string" },
        "note": #{ "type": "string" },
    },
};

let verdict_schema = #{
    "type": "object",
    "required": ["real", "reason", "evidence"],
    "properties": #{
        "real": #{ "type": "boolean" },
        "reason": #{ "type": "string" },
        "evidence": #{ "type": "string" },
    },
};

let triage_schema = #{
    "type": "object",
    "required": ["decisions"],
    "properties": #{
        "decisions": #{
            "type": "array",
            "maxItems": 24,
            "items": #{
                "type": "object",
                "required": ["index", "decision", "reasoning"],
                "properties": #{
                    "index": #{ "type": "integer" },
                    "decision": #{ "type": "string" },
                    "reasoning": #{ "type": "string" },
                    "implementation_note": #{ "type": "string" },
                },
            },
        },
    },
};

let fix_schema = #{
    "type": "object",
    "required": ["summary", "files_touched", "build_ok", "applied", "rejected_during_apply"],
    "properties": #{
        "summary": #{ "type": "string" },
        "files_touched": #{ "type": "array", "items": #{ "type": "string" }, "maxItems": 60 },
        "build_ok": #{ "type": "boolean" },
        "applied": #{ "type": "array", "items": #{ "type": "string" }, "maxItems": 24 },
        "rejected_during_apply": #{
            "type": "array",
            "maxItems": 12,
            "items": #{
                "type": "object",
                "required": ["title", "reason"],
                "properties": #{
                    "title": #{ "type": "string" },
                    "reason": #{ "type": "string" },
                },
            },
        },
    },
};

let summary_schema = #{
    "type": "object",
    "required": ["report_markdown"],
    "properties": #{
        "report_markdown": #{ "type": "string" },
    },
};

// ── Args ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

let task = if args == () { () } else { args.task };
if task == () {
    pause("verification", "Pass args.task — free-form description, a PRD path, or a GitHub issue (#42 / URL). Optional: args.rounds (1 or 2, default 2), args.base (git base branch).");
}

let max_rounds = 2;
if args != () && args.rounds != () {
    // Rhai has no int parse from arbitrary; accept number only.
    if type_of(args.rounds) == "i64" || type_of(args.rounds) == "f64" {
        if args.rounds == 1 { max_rounds = 1; }
        if args.rounds == 2 { max_rounds = 2; }
    }
}

let base_branch = "main";
if args != () && args.base != () && type_of(args.base) == "string" && args.base != "" {
    base_branch = args.base;
}

const MAX_VERIFY = 12;
const MAX_FINDINGS_PER_SPECIALIST = 6;

// ── Helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

fn trimmed(s) {
    if type_of(s) == "string" {
        s.trim();
        s
    } else {
        ""
    }
}

// Canned validate_only outputs are small fixed objects — never assume arrays exist.
fn as_array(x) {
    if x == () { return []; }
    if type_of(x) == "array" { return x; }
    []
}

fn as_string(x) {
    if x == () { return ""; }
    if type_of(x) == "string" { return x; }
    json_encode(x)
}

fn severity_rank(sev) {
    let s = trimmed(sev);
    if s == "blocker" || s == "BLOCKER" || s == "critical" || s == "CRITICAL" { return 4; }
    if s == "major" || s == "MAJOR" || s == "high" || s == "HIGH" { return 3; }
    if s == "minor" || s == "MINOR" || s == "medium" || s == "MEDIUM" { return 2; }
    1
}

fn merge_files(a, b) {
    let out = [];
    for p in a {
        let seen = false;
        for q in out {
            if q == p { seen = true; }
        }
        if !seen { out.push(p); }
    }
    for p in b {
        let seen = false;
        for q in out {
            if q == p { seen = true; }
        }
        if !seen { out.push(p); }
    }
    out
}

fn files_prompt_block(files) {
    let block = "";
    let i = 0;
    for f in files {
        if i > 0 { block += "\n"; }
        block += "- ";
        block += f;
        i += 1;
    }
    if block == "" { block = "(no files listed — discover via git status / git diff against base)"; }
    block
}

fn findings_prompt_block(findings) {
    let block = "";
    let i = 0;
    for f in findings {
        block += "\n### INDEX ";
        block += i.to_string();
        block += " — ";
        block += f.title;
        block += "\n- Specialty: ";
        block += f.specialty;
        block += "\n- Severity: ";
        block += f.severity;
        block += "\n- File: ";
        block += f.file;
        if f.line != () && f.line != "" {
            block += ":";
            block += f.line;
        }
        block += "\n- Observation: ";
        block += f.observation;
        block += "\n- Why: ";
        block += f.why;
        block += "\n- Suggested change: ";
        block += f.suggested_change;
        block += "\n";
        i += 1;
    }
    block
}

fn shared_review_rules() {
    let s = "";
    s += "SHARED RULES:\n";
    s += "1. Use read_file / grep / git tools to inspect the ACTUAL code. Do not answer from memory.\n";
    s += "2. Read every listed file fully (not just hunks). For wiring/dual-path issues, also read consumers outside the list.\n";
    s += "3. Stay in your specialty. Skip issues owned by other specialists unless inseparable.\n";
    s += "4. Do not modify code. Review only.\n";
    s += "5. Be specific: file path, line if possible, concrete change. Vague advice is invalid.\n";
    s += "6. Respect OUT OF SCOPE in the plan — do not raise those.\n";
    s += "7. Empty findings is valid ONLY after you read the code and found nothing in your specialty. Summary must say clean.\n";
    s += "8. Cap at 6 findings. Prefer highest severity. Severity: blocker | major | minor | nit.\n";
    s += "9. Never invent issues to fill the quota.\n";
    s
}

fn specialty_body(name) {
    if name == "correctness" {
        let s = "";
        s += "SPECIALTY: Correctness / plan-fit / edge cases\n";
        s += "Review ONLY for: plan vs implementation mismatches; logic bugs; edge cases; off-by-one; null derefs; race/async ordering; incomplete error handling that is pure correctness; missing cleanup; wrong status codes; copy-paste bugs.\n";
        s += "Do NOT deep-dive: injection/auth catalogs, silent-fallback catalogs, R1-R10 checklists, unused-import/dead-symbol cleanup, extract-to-shared DRY, or test-suite design.\n";
        return s;
    }
    if name == "security" {
        let s = "";
        s += "SPECIALTY: Security / authZ / secrets\n";
        s += "Review ONLY for: injection (SQL/NoSQL/command/XSS/template); missing/weak auth; thin tenant checks without assignment/role gates; over-broad procedures; identity vs capability conflation; auth fail-open; secrets/PII in logs or responses; env names in user errors; cross-tenant leakage; missing input validation; crypto/session/JWT issues.\n";
        s += "Do NOT deep-dive: performance, soft-type hardening (except fail-open auth), test coverage, plan-fit nits.\n";
        return s;
    }
    if name == "silent" {
        let s = "";
        s += "SPECIALTY: Silent failure / soft types (\"just make it work\")\n";
        s += "Prefer hard failures with clear errors over wrong-state continuation unless intentional graceful degradation.\n";
        s += "Flag: empty catch; catch that logs and continues as success; .catch(()=>undefined|null|[]|{}); try/catch returning success defaults; fire-and-forget where failure must surface.\n";
        s += "Flag fallbacks that should hard-fail: critical config defaults; empty arrays/objects when required data missing; || [] / ?? {} papering; optional chains on required paths; mock/stale production fallbacks; parse→silent default; retry that succeeds with empty data.\n";
        s += "Soft types root cause: for every fallback, name the exact hard type + validation boundary. Never suggest any / as any / double cast / blanket ! / @ts-ignore.\n";
        s += "Flag: optional fields that should be required; Partial for loaded entities; unvalidated JSON deep in domain; empty success when absence is error.\n";
        s += "For each finding: (1) what happens on failure today (2) what should happen (3) soft-type root cause + hard type (4) concrete fix without more defaults.\n";
        return s;
    }
    if name == "recurring" {
        let s = "";
        s += "SPECIALTY: Recurring PR failure patterns R1-R10\n";
        s += "Walk checklist; flag production failure modes as blocker/major.\n";
        s += "R1 Soft success (looks ACTIVE/ready while broken). R2 Write-only / incomplete E2E wiring (UI→API→DB→read→export pipelines→import→jobs). R3 App-only invariants/races (need DB unique/transactions). R4 Thin authZ/tenant/secret boundaries. R5 Form hydration/mount wipes. R6 Dual-path inconsistency (CRM vs funnel, twin transformers). R7 Envelope casts / partial updates null omitted fields / type lies. R8 Tests that don't protect failure modes. R9 UX recovery missing. R10 Reinvention / arbitrary design tokens / incomplete a11y.\n";
        s += "For R2/R6 read consumers outside the touched list. In Why, name the production failure mode. Prefer DB constraints, existing auth helpers, hard preflight throws, full consumer wiring — not more ?? defaults.\n";
        return s;
    }
    if name == "testing" {
        let s = "";
        s += "SPECIALTY: Testing gaps\n";
        s += "Review ONLY missing/weak tests. Do not redesign product logic except to name the assertion that would catch a bug.\n";
        s += "Flag: new branches without tests; modified behavior without updated tests; happy-path-only fixtures; tests that no-op green when fixtures missing; missing failure-path assertions; contract changes without e2e/integration updates.\n";
        s += "Prefer at least one test that would FAIL if a silent-success or write-only bug returned. For each: where test lives, what to assert, what bug it catches.\n";
        return s;
    }
    if name == "deadcode" {
        let s = "";
        s += "SPECIALTY: Dead code / unused / stale comments\n";
        s += "Remove refactor leftovers. Prove unused with grep/read — do not guess.\n";
        s += "Flag unused imports (named/default/type-only/unneeded side-effect); unused locals/params/private helpers/types/constants; exports/re-exports with no in-repo consumers (unless intentional public package API); dead/unreachable branches; assigned-never-read vars; leftover feature-flag/env reads.\n";
        s += "Flag stale/useless comments to DELETE: narrating removed behavior (used to/previously/was/no longer/removed X/old path); large commented-out blocks; JSDoc contradicting current signatures; TODOs already done or pointing at deleted code; leftover section banners; obvious narrating comments from this change with no non-obvious intent.\n";
        s += "Do NOT flag: symbols used via types/decorators/DI/reflection; WHY/invariant/security comments that still apply; WIP with active TODO+issue; broad cleanups outside this change's blast radius.\n";
        s += "Severity: unused import=nit; dead private helper/misleading stale comment=minor/major; stale comment contradicting auth/security=major/blocker. Each finding needs proof of zero refs (or quote) + exact delete.\n";
        return s;
    }
    if name == "duplication" {
        let s = "";
        s += "SPECIALTY: Duplication / extract-to-shared\n";
        s += "Flag repeated logic only when ALL hold: (1) >=3 real occurrences after this change (2) would realistically be used more (3) stable enough to name (4) extraction reduces drift risk.\n";
        s += "Scope of shared home from fan-out: 3+ in one file => private helper; 3+ in one feature/module => module utils/helpers; 3+ across one app => app shared module; 3+ across apps/FE+BE domain => existing libs/ package; near-match existing helper => extend/reuse, no parallel utility.\n";
        s += "Always include occurrence count, file:line list, proposed symbol+path, params vs identical core. Search the repo, not only touched files.\n";
        s += "Do NOT flag: only 2 weak lookalikes; intentional test-fixture dup; trivial one-liners; similar control flow with different business meaning; huge unrelated DRY refactors.\n";
        s += "Severity: easy local 3-copy=minor/nit; drifting copies or dual-path same domain rule=major; reinvented existing helper=major. Suggested change = concrete signature + home path, not 'consider DRY'.\n";
        return s;
    }
    "SPECIALTY: general review\n"
}

fn make_review_prompt(specialty, plan_json, files_block, round_label, focus_note) {
    let p = "";
    p += "You are an independent specialist code reviewer for ONE concern only.\n";
    p += "You have no prior context. Review what you see. You do not know about other specialists or other rounds.\n\n";
    p += "ROUND: ";
    p += round_label;
    p += "\n\n";
    p += specialty_body(specialty);
    p += "\n";
    p += shared_review_rules();
    p += "\n## The plan (JSON)\n";
    p += plan_json;
    p += "\n\n## Files implemented / in scope\n";
    p += files_block;
    p += "\n\n";
    if focus_note != "" {
        p += "## Focus for this pass\n";
        p += focus_note;
        p += "\n\n";
    }
    p += "Return structured findings for your specialty only. line may be empty string if unknown.\n";
    p
}

fn make_arch_prompt(plan_json, files_block) {
    let p = "";
    p += "You are performing an ARCHITECTURE SENSE-CHECK only. Advisory. Conservative.\n";
    p += "Question: Does the way this is implemented actually make sense as it is now?\n\n";
    p += "Use read_file / grep to inspect the plan, listed files, and surrounding codebase patterns (similar features, helpers, layering).\n\n";
    p += "STANCE — default to fine:\n";
    p += "- Most working designs that fit local patterns are fine.\n";
    p += "- Only speak when there is a VERY CLEAR better path that fits this codebase, or the approach is CLEARLY poor (wrong layer, fights abstractions, parallel system for something already solved).\n";
    p += "- Style prefs, micro-opts, naming bikesheds are NOT findings. Preferable-but-not-clearly-better is NOT a finding. Silence/fine is correct when acceptable.\n\n";
    p += "CRITICAL:\n";
    p += "- Never demand a rewrite or re-architecture.\n";
    p += "- Never emit severity findings for triage.\n";
    p += "- Keep notes short (half page max). If fine: verdict fine and note empty string.\n\n";
    p += "Verdict enum: fine | clear-better-path | poor-fit\n\n";
    p += "## Plan (JSON)\n";
    p += plan_json;
    p += "\n\n## Files\n";
    p += files_block;
    p += "\n";
    p
}

fn make_verify_prompt(f) {
    let p = "";
    p += "You are an adversarial skeptic. Your job is to REFUTE review findings unless the shipped code independently proves them.\n";
    p += "Default real=false. Set real=true ONLY with concrete evidence you inspected yourself (file:line + what the code does).\n";
    p += "Missing evidence, ambiguity, or 'probably' => real=false.\n";
    p += "Use read_file / grep. Do not trust the finding text alone.\n";
    p += "If the finding is true but severity is inflated, still real=true and note that in reason.\n";
    p += "If the finding misreads out-of-scope, intentional tradeoff in the plan, or already-fixed code, real=false.\n\n";
    p += "FINDING TO VERIFY:\n";
    p += "Title: ";
    p += f.title;
    p += "\nSpecialty: ";
    p += f.specialty;
    p += "\nSeverity: ";
    p += f.severity;
    p += "\nFile: ";
    p += f.file;
    if f.line != () && f.line != "" {
        p += "\nClaimed line: ";
        p += f.line;
    }
    p += "\nObservation: ";
    p += f.observation;
    p += "\nWhy it matters: ";
    p += f.why;
    p += "\nSuggested change: ";
    p += f.suggested_change;
    p += "\n\nReturn: real (bool), reason (short), evidence (file:line quotes or concrete code behavior; empty string if unreal).\n";
    p
}

// ── Phase: Resolve ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

phase("Resolve");
log("Resolving task into a bound spec");

let resolve_prompt = "";
resolve_prompt += "Resolve the user's peer-review task into a single clear specification document.\n\n";
resolve_prompt += "INPUT (verbatim):\n";
resolve_prompt += json_encode(task);
resolve_prompt += "\n\nRules:\n";
resolve_prompt += "1. If INPUT is a filesystem path that exists, read the file and treat it as the PRD/spec.\n";
```
