#### `~/.ai/dsh-plugins/sql-explorer/index.js`

```js file=~/.ai/dsh-plugins/sql-explorer/index.js mode=600
/**
 * Host half of the Session SQL Explorer.
 *
 * It answers one question for the browser: which PostgreSQL database does the
 * Session currently work against? The answer comes from the Session's working
 * directory: a `/monorepo-worktree` checkout carries `.worktree-slot` (the
 * slot number and `DATABASE_URL`), and any other project carries a
 * `DATABASE_URL` in a dotenv file. Queries run through the `psql` client so
 * the plugin needs no database driver of its own.
 */
import { execFile } from 'node:child_process';
import { existsSync } from 'node:fs';
import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import path from 'node:path';

export const name = 'sql-explorer';
export const inject = ['webServer', 'agents', 'workingDirectory'];

const ROUTE_PREFIX = '/sql-explorer';
const ENV_FILES = ['.env', '.env.local', '.env.development', '.env.development.local'];
const MAX_BODY_BYTES = 1024 * 1024;
const MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES = 32 * 1024 * 1024;
const DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000;
const CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000;
const CSV_NULL = '<NULL>';
const ROW_STATEMENTS = new Set(['select', 'with', 'values', 'table', 'show', 'explain', 'fetch']);

/** A failure that already carries the HTTP status the browser should see. */
class ExplorerError extends Error {
  constructor(status, message, extra = {}) {
    super(message);
    this.status = status;
    this.extra = extra;
  }
}

/**
 * Register the Session database routes.
 * @param ctx Host context carrying the web server, Agent registry, and working directories.
 */
export function apply(ctx) {
  /** Per-Session manual connection overrides, kept in memory only. */
  const overrides = new Map();
  ctx.effect(() => ctx.webServer.register({
    kind: 'prefix',
    path: ROUTE_PREFIX,
    handler: (req, res) => {
      handle(ctx, overrides, req, res).catch((error) => sendError(res, error));
    },
  }), 'sql-explorer: Session database routes');
}

/**
 * Dispatch one request to its route.
 * @param ctx Host context.
 * @param overrides Manual connection overrides by Session id.
 * @param req Node request.
 * @param res Node response.
 */
async function handle(ctx, overrides, req, res) {
  if (req.headers['x-dsh-sql-explorer'] !== '1') {
    throw new ExplorerError(403, 'Missing the SQL Explorer request header.');
  }
  if (req.method === 'OPTIONS') {
    throw new ExplorerError(405, 'Cross-origin requests are not supported.');
  }
  const url = new URL(req.url ?? '/', 'http://127.0.0.1');
  const route = url.pathname.slice(ROUTE_PREFIX.length);

  if (req.method === 'GET' && route === '/target') {
    const sessionId = requiredSessionId(url.searchParams.get('sessionId'));
    const context = await sessionContext(ctx, overrides, sessionId);
    send(res, 200, { cwd: context.cwd, target: publicTarget(context.target) });
    return;
  }

  if (req.method === 'GET' && route === '/ping') {
    const sessionId = requiredSessionId(url.searchParams.get('sessionId'));
    const context = await sessionContext(ctx, overrides, sessionId);
    const info = await ping(context.target);
    send(res, 200, { target: publicTarget(context.target), connection: info });
    return;
  }

  if (req.method === 'GET' && route === '/schema') {
    const sessionId = requiredSessionId(url.searchParams.get('sessionId'));
    const context = await sessionContext(ctx, overrides, sessionId);
    const schema = await readSchema(context.target);
    send(res, 200, { target: publicTarget(context.target), schema });
    return;
  }

  if (req.method === 'POST' && route === '/query') {
    const body = await readJson(req);
    const sessionId = requiredSessionId(body.sessionId);
    const sql = requireSql(body.sql);
    const limit = normalizeLimit(body.limit);
    const context = await sessionContext(ctx, overrides, sessionId);
    const result = await runQuery(context.target, sql, limit);
    send(res, 200, result);
    return;
  }

  if (req.method === 'POST' && route === '/connect') {
    const body = await readJson(req);
    const sessionId = requiredSessionId(body.sessionId);
    const raw = requireSql(body.url).trim();
    const target = buildTarget(raw, {
      source: 'manual',
      slot: null,
      envFile: null,
      cwd: contextCwd(ctx, sessionId),
      override: true,
    });
    await ping(target);
    overrides.set(sessionId, { url: raw, at: new Date().toISOString() });
    send(res, 200, { target: publicTarget(target) });
    return;
  }

  if (req.method === 'DELETE' && route === '/connect') {
    const sessionId = requiredSessionId(url.searchParams.get('sessionId'));
    overrides.delete(sessionId);
    const context = await sessionContext(ctx, overrides, sessionId);
    send(res, 200, { target: publicTarget(context.target) });
    return;
  }

  throw new ExplorerError(404, `Unknown SQL Explorer route ${req.method} ${route}.`);
}

// ── Session → database ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/**
 * Resolve the Session's working directory and database target.
 * @param ctx Host context.
 * @param overrides Manual connection overrides by Session id.
 * @param sessionId Live Session id.
 * @returns `{ cwd, target }`.
 */
async function sessionContext(ctx, overrides, sessionId) {
  const cwd = contextCwd(ctx, sessionId);
  const override = overrides.get(sessionId);
  if (override !== undefined) {
    return {
      cwd,
      target: buildTarget(override.url, {
        source: 'manual',
        slot: null,
        envFile: null,
        cwd,
        override: true,
      }),
    };
  }
  return { cwd, target: await detectTarget(cwd) };
}

/**
 * Read the working directory of a live Session.
 * @param ctx Host context.
 * @param sessionId Session id sent by the browser.
 * @returns Absolute working directory.
 */
function contextCwd(ctx, sessionId) {
  const agent = ctx.agents.get(sessionId);
  if (agent === undefined) {
    throw new ExplorerError(409, 'This Session is not live, so its database cannot be resolved. Open the Session and reopen the SQL Explorer tab.');
  }
  try {
    return ctx.workingDirectory.get(agent.session);
  } catch (error) {
    throw new ExplorerError(500, `Could not read this Session's working directory: ${errorText(error)}`);
  }
}

/**
 * Find the database the checkout uses: the nearest `.worktree-slot` marker plus
 * the nearest `DATABASE_URL` in a dotenv file.
 * @param cwd Session working directory.
 * @returns Public target plus a server-only connection string.
 */
async function detectTarget(cwd) {
  const searched = [];
  let dir = path.resolve(cwd);
  let marker;
  for (let depth = 0; depth < 8; depth += 1) {
    if (marker === undefined) marker = await readSlotMarker(dir);
    for (const file of ENV_FILES) {
      const envFile = path.join(dir, file);
      const raw = await readEnvValue(envFile, 'DATABASE_URL');
      if (raw === undefined) continue;
      const target = buildTarget(raw, {
        source: marker === undefined ? 'dotenv' : `worktree slot ${marker.slot}`,
        slot: marker?.slot ?? null,
        envFile,
        cwd,
        override: false,
      });
      if (marker?.dbName != null && marker.dbName !== target.database) {
        target.warning = `The .worktree-slot marker names ${marker.dbName}, but ${envFile} points at ${target.database}. Using the connection URL.`;
      }
      return target;
    }
    searched.push(dir);
    const parent = path.dirname(dir);
    if (parent === dir) break;
    dir = parent;
  }
  throw new ExplorerError(
    422,
    `No DATABASE_URL found for this Session. Looked in ${searched.join(', ')}. Set one in .env, or enter a connection URL in the panel.`,
    { searched },
  );
}

/**
 * Read the worktree slot marker written by the monorepo-worktree setup script.
 * @param dir Candidate directory.
 * @returns `{ slot, dbName }` when the marker exists.
 */
async function readSlotMarker(dir) {
  let text;
  try {
    text = await readFile(path.join(dir, '.worktree-slot'), 'utf8');
  } catch (error) {
    if (error?.code === 'ENOENT') return undefined;
    throw error;
  }
  const fields = Object.fromEntries(text
    .split(/\r?\n/)
    .map((line) => line.split('='))
    .filter((pair) => pair.length === 2)
    .map(([key, value]) => [key.trim(), value.trim()]));
  const slot = Number.parseInt(fields.SLOT ?? '', 10);
  return {
    slot: Number.isFinite(slot) ? slot : null,
    dbName: fields.DB_NAME ?? null,
  };
}

/**
 * Read one key from a dotenv file without executing it.
 * @param file Absolute dotenv path.
 * @param key Variable name.
 * @returns The unquoted value, or undefined when absent.
 */
async function readEnvValue(file, key) {
  let text;
  try {
    text = await readFile(file, 'utf8');
  } catch (error) {
    if (error?.code === 'ENOENT' || error?.code === 'EISDIR') return undefined;
    throw error;
  }
  for (const raw of text.split(/\r?\n/)) {
    const line = raw.trim();
    if (line === '' || line.startsWith('#')) continue;
    const eq = line.indexOf('=');
    if (eq === -1) continue;
    const name = line.slice(0, eq).replace(/^export\s+/, '').trim();
    if (name !== key) continue;
    let value = line.slice(eq + 1).trim();
    if ((value.startsWith('"') && value.endsWith('"')) || (value.startsWith("'") && value.endsWith("'"))) {
      value = value.slice(1, -1);
    }
    value = value.replace(/\$\{([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\}/g, (_, ref) => process.env[ref] ?? '');
    return value === '' ? undefined : value;
  }
  return undefined;
}

/**
 * Turn a PostgreSQL URL into the target the panel shows and psql receives.
 * @param raw Connection URL.
 * @param meta Detection metadata.
 * @returns Public target fields plus `connectionString`.
 */
function buildTarget(raw, meta) {
  let url;
  try {
    url = new URL(raw);
  } catch {
    throw new ExplorerError(422, `"${raw}" is not a valid PostgreSQL connection URL.`);
  }
  if (url.protocol !== 'postgres:' && url.protocol !== 'postgresql:') {
    throw new ExplorerError(422, `Expected a postgres:// URL, received ${url.protocol}//.`);
  }
  const database = decodeURIComponent(url.pathname.replace(/^\//, ''));
  if (database === '') {
    throw new ExplorerError(422, 'The connection URL has no database name.');
  }
  const connection = new URL(url.toString());
  connection.search = '';
  const host = url.hostname === '' ? 'localhost' : url.hostname;
  const port = url.port === '' ? '5432' : url.port;
  const user = url.username === '' ? undefined : decodeURIComponent(url.username);
  return {
    database,
    host,
    port,
    user: user ?? null,
    source: meta.source,
    slot: meta.slot,
    envFile: meta.envFile,
    cwd: meta.cwd,
    override: meta.override,
    display: `${url.protocol}//${url.username}${url.password === '' ? '' : ':••••'}@${host}:${port}/${database}`,
    connectionString: connection.toString(),
  };
}

/**
 * Drop the credential-bearing field before answering the browser.
 * @param target Resolved target.
 * @returns The target without `connectionString`.
 */
function publicTarget(target) {
  const { connectionString: _connectionString, ...rest } = target;
  return rest;
}

// ── psql ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/**
 * Locate the psql client for this Host process.
 * @returns Absolute path or the plain command name.
 */
function resolvePsql() {
  const candidates = [
    process.env.SQL_EXPLORER_PSQL,
    '/opt/homebrew/bin/psql',
    '/usr/local/bin/psql',
    '/usr/bin/psql',
    '/opt/local/bin/psql',
  ];
  for (const candidate of candidates) {
    if (typeof candidate === 'string' && candidate !== '' && existsSync(candidate)) return candidate;
  }
  return 'psql';
}

/**
 * Run one statement with psql.
 * @param connectionString libpq URL.
 * @param sql Statement text.
 * @param options `csv` output and timeout.
 * @returns Raw process result.
 */
function runPsql(connectionString, sql, options = {}) {
  const { csv = true, timeoutMs = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS } = options;
  const args = ['-X', '-v', 'ON_ERROR_STOP=1', '-v', 'VERBOSITY=verbose'];
  if (csv) args.push('--csv', '-P', `null=${CSV_NULL}`, '-P', 'footer=off', '-P', 'pager=off');
  else args.push('-t', '-A', '-P', 'pager=off');
  args.push('-c', sql, connectionString);
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    execFile(resolvePsql(), args, {
      timeout: timeoutMs,
      maxBuffer: MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES,
      encoding: 'utf8',
      windowsHide: true,
      env: { ...process.env, PGCONNECT_TIMEOUT: '5', PGAPPNAME: 'dsh-sql-explorer' },
    }, (error, stdout, stderr) => {
      resolve({ error, stdout: stdout ?? '', stderr: stderr ?? '' });
    });
  });
}

/**
 * Check the connection and read server facts.
 * @param target Resolved target.
 * @returns Connection facts.
 */
async function ping(target) {
  const sql = "SELECT json_build_object('database', current_database(), 'user', current_user, 'serverVersion', current_setting('server_version'), 'server', coalesce(inet_server_addr()::text, 'local'))";
  const result = await runPsql(target.connectionString, sql, { csv: false, timeoutMs: CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS });
  if (result.error !== null) throw psqlFailure(result, 502);
  const facts = parseJsonOutput(result.stdout);
  return facts;
}

/**
 * Read every schema, table, and column visible to this connection.
 * @param target Resolved target.
 * @returns `{ database, serverVersion, schemas }`.
 */
async function readSchema(target) {
  const sql = `
WITH namespaces AS (
  SELECT n.oid, n.nspname
  FROM pg_namespace n
  WHERE n.nspname NOT IN ('pg_catalog', 'information_schema')
    AND n.nspname NOT LIKE 'pg_toast%'
    AND n.nspname NOT LIKE 'pg_temp%'
)
SELECT json_build_object(
  'database', current_database(),
  'serverVersion', current_setting('server_version'),
  'schemas', coalesce((
    SELECT json_agg(json_build_object(
      'name', ns.nspname,
      'tables', coalesce((
        SELECT json_agg(json_build_object(
          'name', c.relname,
          'kind', c.relkind,
          'estimatedRows', CASE WHEN c.reltuples < 0 THEN NULL ELSE c.reltuples::bigint END,
          'columns', coalesce((
            SELECT json_agg(json_build_object(
              'name', a.attname,
              'type', format_type(a.atttypid, a.atttypmod),
              'nullable', NOT a.attnotnull,
              'default', pg_get_expr(d.adbin, d.adrelid)
            ) ORDER BY a.attnum)
            FROM pg_attribute a
            LEFT JOIN pg_attrdef d ON d.adrelid = a.attrelid AND d.adnum = a.attnum
            WHERE a.attrelid = c.oid AND a.attnum > 0 AND NOT a.attisdropped
          ), '[]'::json)
        ) ORDER BY c.relname)
        FROM pg_class c
        WHERE c.relnamespace = ns.oid AND c.relkind IN ('r', 'p', 'v', 'm', 'f')
      ), '[]'::json)
    ) ORDER BY ns.nspname)
    FROM namespaces ns
  ), '[]'::json)
)`.trim();
  const result = await runPsql(target.connectionString, sql, { csv: false, timeoutMs: DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS });
  if (result.error !== null) throw psqlFailure(result, 502);
  return parseJsonOutput(result.stdout);
}

/**
 * Run a user statement and shape it for the results grid.
 * @param target Resolved target.
 * @param sql User statement.
 * @param limit Optional row cap for row-returning statements.
 * @returns Result payload.
 */
async function runQuery(target, sql, limit) {
  const statement = sql.trim().replace(/[\s;]+$/, '');
  if (statement === '') throw new ExplorerError(400, 'The statement is empty.');
  const capped = applyLimit(statement, limit);
  const started = Date.now();
  let result = await runPsql(target.connectionString, capped.sql);

  if (result.error !== null && capped.limited) {
    // A wrapped statement can fail where the user's own statement succeeds
    // (for example a data-modifying CTE). Report the real statement instead.
    const direct = await runPsql(target.connectionString, statement);
    if (direct.error === null) {
      result = direct;
    } else {
      throw psqlFailure(direct, 400);
    }
  }
  if (result.error !== null) throw psqlFailure(result, 400);

  const durationMs = Date.now() - started;
  const keyword = leadingKeyword(statement);
  if (!ROW_STATEMENTS.has(keyword)) {
    return {
      kind: 'command',
      command: lastNonEmptyLine(result.stdout),
      columns: [],
      rows: [],
      rowCount: 0,
      durationMs,
      limited: false,
      statement,
    };
  }
  const parsed = parsePsqlRows(result.stdout);
  if (parsed.kind === 'command') {
    return {
      kind: 'command',
      command: parsed.command,
      columns: [],
      rows: [],
      rowCount: 0,
      durationMs,
      limited: false,
      statement,
    };
  }
  return {
    kind: 'rows',
    command: null,
    columns: parsed.columns,
    rows: parsed.rows,
    rowCount: parsed.rows.length,
    durationMs,
    limited: capped.limited,
    limit,
    statement,
  };
}

/**
 * Wrap a row-returning statement in a LIMIT when the panel asked for one.
 * @param sql Stripped statement.
 * @param limit Row cap, 0 for none.
 * @returns `{ sql, limited }`.
 */
function applyLimit(sql, limit) {
  if (!Number.isInteger(limit) || limit <= 0) return { sql, limited: false };
  if (!['select', 'with', 'values', 'table'].includes(leadingKeyword(sql))) return { sql, limited: false };
  return {
    sql: `SELECT * FROM (\n${sql}\n) AS __dsh_sql_explorer_sub LIMIT ${limit}`,
    limited: true,
  };
}

/**
 * Classify a statement by its first keyword, skipping comments.
 * @param sql Statement text.
 * @returns Lowercase keyword, or an empty string.
 */
function leadingKeyword(sql) {
  let text = sql;
  for (;;) {
    text = text.replace(/^\s+/, '');
    if (text.startsWith('--')) {
      const end = text.indexOf('\n');
      text = end === -1 ? '' : text.slice(end + 1);
      continue;
    }
    if (text.startsWith('/*')) {
      const end = text.indexOf('*/');
      text = end === -1 ? '' : text.slice(end + 2);
      continue;
    }
    break;
  }
  const match = /^([A-Za-z]+)/.exec(text);
  return match === null ? '' : match[1].toLowerCase();
}

/**
 * Shape psql's stderr into a user-facing failure.
 * @param result Raw psql result.
 * @param status HTTP status for a query rejection.
 * @returns ExplorerError.
 */
function psqlFailure(result, status) {
  const stderr = result.stderr.trim();
  if (result.error?.code === 'ENOENT') {
    return new ExplorerError(500, `The psql client was not found. Install PostgreSQL or set SQL_EXPLORER_PSQL to its path.`);
  }
  if (result.error?.killed === true || result.error?.code === 'ETIMEDOUT') {
    return new ExplorerError(408, `The statement did not finish within ${Math.round(DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS / 1000)}s and was cancelled.`);
  }
  if (result.error?.code === 'ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_STDIO_MAXBUFFER' || /maxBuffer/i.test(String(result.error?.message))) {
    return new ExplorerError(413, 'The result is too large to display. Add a LIMIT or narrow the query.');
  }

  const verbose = /ERROR:\s+([0-9A-Z]{5}):\s*([^\n]*)/.exec(stderr);
  if (verbose !== null) {
    return new ExplorerError(status, verbose[2].trim(), {
      sqlState: verbose[1],
      ...collectPsqlDetails(stderr),
    });
  }
  const plain = /ERROR:\s+([^\n]*)/.exec(stderr);
  if (plain !== null) {
    return new ExplorerError(status, plain[1].trim(), collectPsqlDetails(stderr));
  }
  if (/psql:\s*error:/.test(stderr) || result.error !== null) {
    return new ExplorerError(502, stderr === '' ? errorText(result.error) : stderr.split('\n')[0].trim());
  }
  return new ExplorerError(status, 'The statement failed without a message.');
}

/**
 * Pull DETAIL, HINT, and the offending line out of psql's verbose stderr.
 * @param stderr psql stderr text.
 * @returns Extra error fields.
 */
function collectPsqlDetails(stderr) {
  const detail = /^DETAIL:\s+([^\n]*)/m.exec(stderr);
  const hint = /^HINT:\s+([^\n]*)/m.exec(stderr);
  const line = /^LINE\s+(\d+):\s+([^\n]*)/m.exec(stderr);
  const extra = {};
  if (detail !== null) extra.detail = detail[1].trim();
  if (hint !== null) extra.hint = hint[1].trim();
  if (line !== null) {
    extra.line = Number.parseInt(line[1], 10);
    extra.context = line[2].trim();
  }
  return extra;
}

/**
 * Parse one JSON object psql printed in tuples-only mode.
 * @param stdout Process output.
 * @returns Parsed object.
 */
function parseJsonOutput(stdout) {
  const text = stdout.trim();
  if (text === '') throw new ExplorerError(502, 'The database returned no data.');
  try {
    return JSON.parse(text);
  } catch {
    throw new ExplorerError(502, 'The database returned data this panel could not read.');
  }
}

/** Command tags psql prints instead of a result set. */
const COMMAND_TAG = /^(?:INSERT\s+\d+\s+\d+|UPDATE\s+\d+|DELETE\s+\d+|MERGE\s+\d+|COPY\s+\d+|CREATE\s+[A-Z][A-Z ]*|ALTER\s+[A-Z][A-Z ]*|DROP\s+[A-Z][A-Z ]*|TRUNCATE\s+TABLE|BEGIN|COMMIT|ROLLBACK|SAVEPOINT|RELEASE|SET|RESET|GRANT|REVOKE|VACUUM|ANALYZE|REFRESH\s+MATERIALIZED\s+VIEW|DISCARD\s+[A-Z]+)$/;

/**
 * Parse psql CSV output into either a result set or a command tag.
 * @param stdout Process output.
 * @returns `{ kind: 'rows', columns, rows }` or `{ kind: 'command', command }`.
 */
function parsePsqlRows(stdout) {
  const text = stdout.replace(/\r\n/g, '\n').replace(/[\r\n]+$/, '');
  if (text === '') return { kind: 'command', command: '' };
  const records = parseCsv(text);
  if (records.length === 0) return { kind: 'command', command: '' };
  if (records.length === 1 && records[0].length === 1) {
    const line = records[0][0].trim();
    if (COMMAND_TAG.test(line)) return { kind: 'command', command: line };
  }
  const columns = records[0];
  const rows = records.slice(1).map((cells) => cells.map((cell) => (cell === CSV_NULL ? null : cell)));
  return { kind: 'rows', columns, rows };
}

/**
 * Parse RFC 4180 CSV, including quoted commas and newlines.
 * @param text CSV text.
 * @returns Records.
 */
function parseCsv(text) {
  const records = [];
  let record = [];
  let field = '';
  let quoted = false;
  let index = 0;
  while (index < text.length) {
    const char = text[index];
    if (quoted) {
      if (char === '"') {
        if (text[index + 1] === '"') {
          field += '"';
          index += 2;
          continue;
        }
        quoted = false;
        index += 1;
        continue;
      }
      field += char;
      index += 1;
      continue;
    }
    if (char === '"') {
      quoted = true;
      index += 1;
      continue;
    }
    if (char === ',') {
      record.push(field);
      field = '';
      index += 1;
      continue;
    }
    if (char === '\n') {
      record.push(field);
      records.push(record);
      record = [];
      field = '';
      index += 1;
      continue;
    }
    field += char;
    index += 1;
  }
  if (field !== '' || record.length > 0) {
    record.push(field);
    records.push(record);
  }
  return records;
}

// ── Request helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/**
 * Read a JSON request body with a hard size cap.
 * @param req Node request.
 * @returns Parsed body.
 */
async function readJson(req) {
  const chunks = [];
  let size = 0;
  for await (const chunk of req) {
    size += chunk.length;
    if (size > MAX_BODY_BYTES) throw new ExplorerError(413, 'The request body is too large.');
    chunks.push(chunk);
  }
  const text = Buffer.concat(chunks).toString('utf8');
  if (text === '') return {};
  try {
    return JSON.parse(text);
  } catch {
    throw new ExplorerError(400, 'The request body must be JSON.');
  }
}

/**
 * Require a Session id.
 * @param value Candidate value.
 * @returns The Session id.
 */
function requiredSessionId(value) {
  if (typeof value !== 'string' || value === '') throw new ExplorerError(400, 'Missing sessionId.');
  return value;
}

/**
 * Require a non-empty statement string.
 * @param value Candidate value.
 * @returns The statement.
 */
function requireSql(value) {
  if (typeof value !== 'string' || value.trim() === '') throw new ExplorerError(400, 'Missing SQL text.');
  return value;
}

/**
 * Normalize the row cap sent by the panel.
 * @param value Candidate value.
 * @returns 0 for no cap, otherwise 1–10000.
 */
function normalizeLimit(value) {
  if (value === undefined || value === null) return 0;
  const number = Number(value);
  if (!Number.isFinite(number) || number < 0) return 0;
  return Math.min(Math.floor(number), 10_000);
}

/**
 * Write one JSON response.
 * @param res Node response.
 * @param status HTTP status.
 * @param payload JSON payload.
 */
function send(res, status, payload) {
  const body = JSON.stringify(payload);
  res.writeHead(status, {
    'content-type': 'application/json; charset=utf-8',
    'cache-control': 'no-store',
    'content-length': Buffer.byteLength(body),
  });
  res.end(body);
}

/**
 * Write a failure response.
 * @param res Node response.
 * @param error Thrown value.
 */
function sendError(res, error) {
  if (res.headersSent) {
    res.destroy();
    return;
  }
  if (error instanceof ExplorerError) {
    send(res, error.status, { error: { message: error.message, ...error.extra } });
    return;
  }
  const message = errorText(error);
  console.error(`[sql-explorer] ${message}`);
  send(res, 500, { error: { message } });
}

/**
 * Render an unknown thrown value as text.
 * @param error Thrown value.
 * @returns Message text.
 */
function errorText(error) {
  if (error instanceof Error) return error.message;
  if (typeof error === 'string') return error;
  return 'Unknown failure';
}

/**
 * Read the last non-empty stdout line, which is psql's command tag.
 * @param stdout Process output.
 * @returns The tag, or an empty string.
 */
function lastNonEmptyLine(stdout) {
  const lines = stdout.split(/\r?\n/).map((line) => line.trim()).filter((line) => line !== '');
  return lines.length === 0 ? '' : lines[lines.length - 1];
}
```

## Hyprland (Arch)

Hyprland + hyprpaper config and Arch bootstrap scripts. All blocks here are `os=linux`.

```sh
python3 /tmp/dotfiles extract --only ~/.config/hypr   # or a full extract
~/.config/hypr/install.sh                            # generic / non-NVIDIA
~/.config/hypr/install-nvidia.sh                     # NVIDIA: runs install.sh, then the driver stack
```

Run as your normal user; the scripts call `sudo` when needed.

**What the scripts do**

- Sync pacman, install Hyprland + ecosystem (hyprpaper, hypridle, hyprlock, hyprshot, waybar, swaync, wofi,
  thunar, xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland, qt wayland), pipewire + wireplumber, brightnessctl, playerctl, firefox,
  polkit-gnome, base-devel + git.
- Bootstrap `paru` if no AUR helper exists, then AUR: `pyprland`, `spotify`, `claude-desktop`.
- Add the `dynamic-cursors` plugin via `hyprpm` (loaded by `hyprland.conf`).
- Enable user services `pipewire`, `pipewire-pulse`, `wireplumber`; create `~/Pictures` and `~/Screenshots`.
- `install-nvidia.sh` also installs `nvidia-dkms nvidia-utils libva-nvidia-driver egl-wayland linux-headers`, adds
  `nvidia nvidia_modeset nvidia_uvm nvidia_drm` to `MODULES` in `/etc/mkinitcpio.conf` (rebuilds initramfs), and
  writes `/etc/modprobe.d/nvidia.conf` with `options nvidia_drm modeset=1 fbdev=1`.

**After install**

1. Reboot (NVIDIA: the DKMS module and `nvidia_drm.modeset=1` take effect at boot).
2. Put a wallpaper at the path in `hyprpaper.conf` (currently `/home/sp00nes/Pictures/arch-linux_upscaled.png`).
3. Create `~/.config/theme/colors-hyprland.conf`; `hyprland.conf` sources it on line 1 for border colors.
4. Install WezTerm (`$terminal`); the scripts do not.
5. Monitors are hardcoded (`eDP-1`, `HDMI-A-1`, `HDMI-A-2`); edit the `monitor=` lines for other setups.

**Keybinds** (`SUPER` is the mod key)

| Bind | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `SUPER + C` | Terminal |
| `SUPER + E` | File manager (thunar) |
| `SUPER + B` | Firefox |
| `SUPER + X` | Spotify |
| `SUPER + space` | wofi launcher |
| `SUPER + Q` | Kill active window |
| `SUPER + F` | Fullscreen |
| `SUPER + V` | Float + center window |
| `SUPER + S` | Toggle `magic` special workspace |
| `SUPER + N` | pypr toggle term |
| `SUPER + T` | pypr toggle taskbar |
| `SUPER + 1..0` | Switch workspace |
| `SUPER + SHIFT + 1..0` | Move window to workspace |
| `SUPER + SHIFT + M` | Exit Hyprland |
| `Print / CTRL+Print / ALT+Print` | Window / region / active-output screenshot |

Volume, brightness, and media keys go through `wpctl`, `brightnessctl`, and `playerctl`.

#### `~/.config/hypr/claude-first-launch.sh`

```bash file=~/.config/hypr/claude-first-launch.sh mode=755 os=linux eol=none
#!/bin/bash

# Toggle to the special workspace named "magic"
hyprctl dispatch togglespecialworkspace magic

# Launch Claude in the background so the script can continue
claude-desktop &

# Store the PID of claude-desktop
CLAUDE_PID=$!

# Wait for Claude window to appear
# This checks if any window with Claude class exists
while ! hyprctl clients | grep -q "class: Claude"; do
  # Check if the process is still running
  if ! kill -0 $CLAUDE_PID 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "Claude process terminated unexpectedly"
    exit 1
  fi
  sleep 0.1
done

# Give it a moment to apply window rules
sleep 0.5

# Toggle back to regular workspace
hyprctl dispatch togglespecialworkspace magic
```

#### `~/.config/hypr/install.sh`

```bash file=~/.config/hypr/install.sh mode=755 os=linux
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install everything required by this Hyprland config on Arch Linux.
# Generic version - no GPU-vendor packages. For NVIDIA, run install-nvidia.sh.
# Run as your normal user (not root). Sudo will be requested when needed.

set -euo pipefail

if [[ $EUID -eq 0 ]]; then
    echo "Run this script as a regular user, not root." >&2
    exit 1
fi

if ! command -v pacman &>/dev/null; then
    echo "pacman not found - this script targets Arch Linux." >&2
    exit 1
fi

echo ":: Syncing package databases"
sudo pacman -Sy --noconfirm

# --- Official repo packages ---------------------------------------------------
PACMAN_PKGS=(
    # Hyprland core + ecosystem
    hyprland
    hyprpaper
    hypridle
    hyprlock
    hyprshot
    xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland
    qt5-wayland
    qt6-wayland

    # Bar / notifications / launcher / file manager
    waybar
    swaync
    wofi
    thunar

    # Audio / brightness / media keys
    pipewire
    pipewire-pulse
    pipewire-alsa
    wireplumber
    pavucontrol
    brightnessctl
    playerctl

    # Apps referenced by keybinds
    firefox

    # Misc utilities used by config / scripts
    polkit-gnome
    xdg-user-dirs
    git
    base-devel
)

echo ":: Installing official packages"
sudo pacman -S --needed --noconfirm "${PACMAN_PKGS[@]}"

# --- AUR helper ---------------------------------------------------------------
if ! command -v paru &>/dev/null && ! command -v yay &>/dev/null; then
    echo ":: No AUR helper found - bootstrapping paru"
    tmpdir=$(mktemp -d)
    git clone https://aur.archlinux.org/paru-bin.git "$tmpdir/paru-bin"
    (cd "$tmpdir/paru-bin" && makepkg -si --noconfirm)
    rm -rf "$tmpdir"
fi

if command -v paru &>/dev/null; then
    AUR_HELPER=paru
else
    AUR_HELPER=yay
fi

# --- AUR packages -------------------------------------------------------------
AUR_PKGS=(
    pyprland          # pypr (scratchpads / dropdowns referenced in binds)
    spotify           # bound to SUPER+X
    claude-desktop    # used by claude-first-launch.sh + window rules
)

echo ":: Installing AUR packages with $AUR_HELPER"
"$AUR_HELPER" -S --needed --noconfirm "${AUR_PKGS[@]}"

# --- Hyprland plugin: dynamic-cursors -----------------------------------------
# hyprland.conf does: hyprctl plugin load .../dynamic-cursors.so
echo ":: Setting up hyprpm and dynamic-cursors plugin"
hyprpm update || true
if ! hyprpm list 2>/dev/null | grep -q dynamic-cursors; then
    hyprpm add https://github.com/VirtCode/hypr-dynamic-cursors
fi
hyprpm enable dynamic-cursors || true
hyprpm reload || true

# --- Wallpaper / screenshot dirs ---------------------------------------------
mkdir -p "$HOME/Pictures" "$HOME/Screenshots"
if [[ ! -f "$HOME/Pictures/arch-linux_upscaled.png" ]]; then
    echo ":: NOTE: $HOME/Pictures/arch-linux_upscaled.png is missing - hyprpaper will fail until you add it."
fi

# --- Services -----------------------------------------------------------------
systemctl --user enable --now pipewire pipewire-pulse wireplumber || true

cat <<'EOF'

Done (generic install).

If this machine has an NVIDIA GPU, also run:
    ./install-nvidia.sh

Next steps:
  * Drop your wallpaper at ~/Pictures/arch-linux_upscaled.png (or edit hyprpaper.conf).
  * Make sure ~/.config/theme/colors-hyprland.conf exists (sourced by hyprland.conf).
  * Log in via a Wayland session and start Hyprland.
EOF
```

#### `~/.config/hypr/install-nvidia.sh`

```bash file=~/.config/hypr/install-nvidia.sh mode=755 os=linux
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# NVIDIA install on top of the generic Hyprland setup.
# Runs install.sh first, then layers on NVIDIA-specific packages and tweaks
# matching the env vars in hyprland.conf.
# Run as your normal user (not root). Sudo will be requested when needed.

set -euo pipefail

if [[ $EUID -eq 0 ]]; then
    echo "Run this script as a regular user, not root." >&2
    exit 1
fi

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" &>/dev/null && pwd)"

# --- Run the generic installer first ------------------------------------------
if [[ -x "$SCRIPT_DIR/install.sh" ]]; then
    echo ":: Running generic install.sh"
    "$SCRIPT_DIR/install.sh"
else
    echo "install.sh not found next to this script - aborting." >&2
    exit 1
fi

# --- NVIDIA packages ----------------------------------------------------------
NVIDIA_PKGS=(
    nvidia-dkms
    nvidia-utils
    libva-nvidia-driver
    egl-wayland
    linux-headers
)

echo ":: Installing NVIDIA packages"
sudo pacman -S --needed --noconfirm "${NVIDIA_PKGS[@]}"

# --- Early KMS in mkinitcpio --------------------------------------------------
# Needed for proper Wayland + NVIDIA behaviour.
MKINIT=/etc/mkinitcpio.conf
if [[ -f "$MKINIT" ]] && ! grep -Eq '^MODULES=.*nvidia' "$MKINIT"; then
    echo ":: Adding nvidia modules to $MKINIT"
    sudo sed -i -E 's/^(MODULES=\()([^)]*)\)/\1\2 nvidia nvidia_modeset nvidia_uvm nvidia_drm)/' "$MKINIT"
    sudo sed -i -E 's/  +/ /g; s/\( /(/' "$MKINIT"
    sudo mkinitcpio -P
fi

# --- nvidia-drm modeset kernel param -----------------------------------------
# Sets nvidia_drm.modeset=1 via a modprobe.d drop-in (works regardless of bootloader).
MODPROBE_FILE=/etc/modprobe.d/nvidia.conf
if [[ ! -f "$MODPROBE_FILE" ]] || ! grep -q 'nvidia_drm modeset=1' "$MODPROBE_FILE"; then
    echo ":: Writing $MODPROBE_FILE"
    echo 'options nvidia_drm modeset=1 fbdev=1' | sudo tee "$MODPROBE_FILE" >/dev/null
fi

cat <<'EOF'

Done (NVIDIA install).

Reboot before launching Hyprland so the DKMS module is in the running kernel
and nvidia_drm.modeset=1 takes effect.
EOF
```

## The dotfiles tool

Python 3 stdlib only. `extract` writes this block to `~/.local/bin/dotfiles` like any other file.

#### `~/.local/bin/dotfiles`

````python file=~/.local/bin/dotfiles mode=755
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""dotfiles: one markdown file holds every config.

Fenced blocks in dotfiles.md are read by kind:
  ```lang file=~/path [mode=NNN] [eol=none] [os=darwin|linux]   one file (mode omitted = 644)
  ```text links      lines of `<link> -> <target>`; symlinks to create
  ```text roots      lines of `<dir> [!exclude-glob ...]`; refresh adds new files found here

Commands:
  extract   write files + symlinks for this OS (refuses to clobber; --force moves old aside)
  status    show what differs between the md and the live machine (exit 1 if anything does)
  refresh   pull live file contents back into the md; add new files under roots
"""
import argparse
import fnmatch
import os
import re
import sys
import tempfile

DEFAULT_MD = os.path.expanduser('~/projects/dot-config/dotfiles.md')
FENCE = re.compile(r'^(`{3,})(\S*)(.*)$')
JUNK = ('.DS_Store', '__pycache__', '*.pyc', 'node_modules')
BACKUP_SUFFIX = '.pre-dotfiles'
PLATFORM = 'darwin' if sys.platform == 'darwin' else 'linux'


class Block:
    def __init__(self, start, end, lang, words, attrs, body_lines):
        self.start, self.end = start, end  # line index of opening / closing fence
        self.lang, self.words, self.attrs = lang, words, attrs
        self.body_lines = body_lines

    @property
    def kind(self):
        if 'file' in self.attrs:
            return 'file'
        if 'links' in self.words:
            return 'links'
        if 'roots' in self.words:
            return 'roots'
        return None

    @property
    def path(self):
        return self.attrs['file']

    def content(self):
        if not self.body_lines:
            return ''
        text = '\n'.join(self.body_lines)
        return text if self.attrs.get('eol') == 'none' else text + '\n'

    def for_this_os(self):
        return self.attrs.get('os', PLATFORM) == PLATFORM


def parse(text):
    lines = text.split('\n')
    blocks, i = [], 0
    while i < len(lines):
        m = FENCE.match(lines[i])
        if not m:
            i += 1
            continue
        fence, lang, rest = m.groups()
        j = i + 1
        while j < len(lines) and lines[j] != fence:
            j += 1
        if j == len(lines):
            sys.exit(f'dotfiles: line {i + 1}: unclosed fence {fence}')
        words = [w for w in rest.split() if '=' not in w]
        attrs = dict(w.split('=', 1) for w in rest.split() if '=' in w)
        blocks.append(Block(i, j, lang, words, attrs, lines[i + 1:j]))
        i = j + 1
    return lines, blocks


def render(path, content, lang, mode=None, os_name=None):
    """Fenced block for one file. Fence is longer than any backtick run inside."""
    if ' ' in path:
        raise ValueError(f'path with spaces not supported: {path}')
    longest = max((len(r) for r in re.findall(r'`+', content)), default=0)
    fence = '`' * max(3, longest + 1)
    info = [f'{fence}{lang}', f'file={path}']
    if mode:
        info.append(f'mode={mode}')
    if os_name:
        info.append(f'os={os_name}')
    if content == '':
        body = []
    elif content.endswith('\n'):
        body = content[:-1].split('\n')
    else:
        body = content.split('\n')
        info.append('eol=none')
    return [' '.join(info), *body, fence]


def read_text(path):
    with open(path, 'rb') as f:
        raw = f.read()
    if b'\0' in raw:
        raise SystemExit(f'dotfiles: {path}: binary file, cannot embed')
    try:
        return raw.decode('utf-8')
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        raise SystemExit(f'dotfiles: {path}: not UTF-8, cannot embed')


def file_mode(path):
    mode = format(os.stat(path).st_mode & 0o777, 'o')
    return None if mode == '644' else mode


def lang_for(path):
    name = os.path.basename(path)
    ext = os.path.splitext(name)[1].lstrip('.')
    by_ext = {'md': 'markdown', 'sh': 'bash', 'py': 'python', 'ts': 'ts', 'js': 'js', 'json': 'json',
              'lua': 'lua', 'toml': 'toml', 'yml': 'yaml', 'yaml': 'yaml', 'conf': 'ini', 'rhai': 'rust'}
    by_name = {'.zshrc': 'zsh', '.gitconfig': 'ini', 'dotfiles': 'python'}
    return by_name.get(name) or by_ext.get(ext, 'text')


def link_lines(block):
    out = []
    for raw in block.body_lines:
        line = raw.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith('#'):
            continue
        link, sep, target = line.partition(' -> ')
        if not sep:
            sys.exit(f'dotfiles: bad links line (want "<link> -> <target>"): {raw}')
        out.append((link.strip(), target.strip()))
    return out


def root_lines(block):
    out = []
    for raw in block.body_lines:
        parts = raw.split()
        if parts and not parts[0].startswith('#'):
            out.append((parts[0], [p[1:] for p in parts[1:] if p.startswith('!')]))
    return out


def expand(path):
    return os.path.expanduser(path)


def link_target(target):
    return expand(target) if target.startswith('~') else target


def selected(path, only):
    return not only or any(expand(path).startswith(expand(p)) for p in only)


def file_state(block):
    dest = expand(block.path)
    if os.path.islink(dest) or not os.path.isfile(dest):
        return 'missing' if not os.path.lexists(dest) else 'conflict'
    if read_text(dest) != block.content():
        return 'modified'
    if file_mode(dest) != block.attrs.get('mode'):
        return 'mode'
    return 'ok'


def link_state(link, target):
    dest = expand(link)
    if os.path.islink(dest):
        return 'ok' if os.readlink(dest) == link_target(target) else 'conflict'
    return 'conflict' if os.path.lexists(dest) else 'missing'


def move_aside(dest):
    backup = dest + BACKUP_SUFFIX
    if os.path.lexists(backup):
        sys.exit(f'dotfiles: backup already exists, remove it first: {backup}')
    os.rename(dest, backup)
    return backup


def cmd_extract(args):
    _, blocks = parse(read_text(args.md))
    files = [b for b in blocks if b.kind == 'file' and (args.all_os or b.for_this_os()) and selected(b.path, args.only)]
    links = [(l, t) for b in blocks if b.kind == 'links' and (args.all_os or b.for_this_os())
             for l, t in link_lines(b) if selected(l, args.only)]

    todo_files = [(b, file_state(b)) for b in files]
    todo_links = [(l, t, link_state(l, t)) for l, t in links]
    clobber = [b.path for b, s in todo_files if s in ('modified', 'conflict')] + \
              [l for l, _, s in todo_links if s == 'conflict']
    if clobber and not args.force and not args.dry_run:
        print('dotfiles: these exist and differ (re-run with --force to move them aside as *' + BACKUP_SUFFIX + '):')
        for p in clobber:
            print('  ' + p)
        sys.exit(1)

    for b, state in todo_files:
        dest = expand(b.path)
        if state == 'ok':
            continue
        if args.dry_run:
            print(f'{state:9} {b.path}')
            continue
        if state in ('modified', 'conflict'):
            print(f'backup    {move_aside(dest)}')
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(dest), exist_ok=True)
        with open(dest, 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='') as f:
            f.write(b.content())
        os.chmod(dest, int(b.attrs.get('mode', '644'), 8))
        print(f'wrote     {b.path}')

    for link, target, state in todo_links:
        dest = expand(link)
        if state == 'ok':
            continue
        if args.dry_run:
            print(f'{state:9} {link} -> {target}')
            continue
        if state == 'conflict':
            print(f'backup    {move_aside(dest)}')
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(dest), exist_ok=True)
        os.symlink(link_target(target), dest)
        print(f'linked    {link} -> {target}')


def new_files(blocks):
    known = {expand(b.path) for b in blocks if b.kind == 'file'}
    found = []
    for b in blocks:
        if b.kind != 'roots' or not b.for_this_os():
            continue
        for root, excludes in root_lines(b):
            base = expand(root)
            if not os.path.isdir(base):
                sys.exit(f'dotfiles: root missing: {root}')
            for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(base):
                rel_dir = os.path.relpath(dirpath, base)

                def skip(name):
                    rel = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(rel_dir, name))
                    return any(fnmatch.fnmatch(name, j) for j in JUNK) or \
                        any(fnmatch.fnmatch(rel, e) or fnmatch.fnmatch(name, e) for e in excludes) or \
                        os.path.islink(os.path.join(dirpath, name))

                dirnames[:] = sorted(d for d in dirnames if not skip(d))
                for name in sorted(filenames):
                    full = os.path.join(dirpath, name)
                    if not skip(name) and full not in known:
                        found.append(root.rstrip('/') + '/' + os.path.relpath(full, base))
    return found


def cmd_status(args):
    _, blocks = parse(read_text(args.md))
    dirty = False
    for b in blocks:
        if b.kind == 'file' and b.for_this_os():
            state = file_state(b)
            if state != 'ok':
                dirty = True
                print(f'{state:9} {b.path}')
        elif b.kind == 'links' and b.for_this_os():
            for link, target in link_lines(b):
                state = link_state(link, target)
                if state != 'ok':
                    dirty = True
                    print(f'{state:9} {link} -> {target}')
    for path in new_files(blocks):
        dirty = True
        print(f'new       {path}')
    if not dirty:
        print('clean')
    sys.exit(1 if dirty else 0)


def common_depth(a, b):
    n = 0
    for x, y in zip(a.split('/'), b.split('/')):
        if x != y:
            break
        n += 1
    return n


def cmd_refresh(args):
    lines, blocks = parse(read_text(args.md))
    file_blocks = [b for b in blocks if b.kind == 'file' and b.for_this_os()]
    missing = [b for b in file_blocks if not os.path.isfile(expand(b.path))]
    if missing and not args.prune:
        print('dotfiles: live file missing (restore it, or re-run with --prune to drop its block):')
        for b in missing:
            print('  ' + b.path)
        sys.exit(1)

    # replacements: (start, end_inclusive) -> new lines; applied bottom-up
    edits, updated, removed = [], 0, 0
    for b in file_blocks:
        if b in missing:
            start = b.start - 2 if b.start >= 2 and lines[b.start - 2] == f'#### `{b.path}`' else b.start
            edits.append((start, b.end + 1 if b.end + 1 < len(lines) and lines[b.end + 1] == '' else b.end, []))
            removed += 1
            continue
        dest = expand(b.path)
        new = render(b.path, read_text(dest), b.lang, file_mode(dest), b.attrs.get('os'))
        if new != lines[b.start:b.end + 1]:
            edits.append((b.start, b.end, new))
            updated += 1

    added = new_files(blocks)
    for path in reversed(added):  # same-anchor inserts stack, so insert last-first to keep order
        anchor = max(file_blocks, key=lambda b: (common_depth(b.path, path), b.end))
        dest = expand(path)
        block = render(path, read_text(dest), lang_for(path), file_mode(dest), anchor.attrs.get('os'))
        edits.append((anchor.end + 1, anchor.end, ['', f'#### `{path}`', '', *block]))

    for start, end, new in sorted(edits, key=lambda e: (e[0], e[1]), reverse=True):
        lines[start:end + 1] = new

    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(args.md)))
    with os.fdopen(fd, 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='') as f:
        f.write('\n'.join(lines))
    os.replace(tmp, args.md)
    print(f'updated {updated}, added {len(added)}, removed {removed}')
    for path in added:
        print(f'  added {path}')


def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog='dotfiles', description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    sub = p.add_subparsers(dest='cmd', required=True)
    e = sub.add_parser('extract', help='write files and symlinks from the md')
    e.add_argument('--only', action='append', default=[], metavar='PATH_PREFIX', help='limit to paths under this prefix (repeatable)')
    e.add_argument('--force', action='store_true', help='move differing files/links aside as *' + BACKUP_SUFFIX)
    e.add_argument('--dry-run', action='store_true')
    e.add_argument('--all-os', action='store_true', help='include blocks marked for another OS')
    s = sub.add_parser('status', help='diff the md against the live machine')
    r = sub.add_parser('refresh', help='pull live files back into the md')
    r.add_argument('--prune', action='store_true', help='drop blocks whose live file is gone')
    for sp in (e, s, r):
        sp.add_argument('md', nargs='?', default=DEFAULT_MD)
    args = p.parse_args()
    {'extract': cmd_extract, 'status': cmd_status, 'refresh': cmd_refresh}[args.cmd](args)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
````
